commits.message:
gateway: a reply of several requests tells the last one's prompt, bills them all

Claude Code reads a reply's input, cache_creation and cache_read as how
full its conversation is. A reply more than one upstream request made
summed all three across them. In the bridge: Claude Code's own
ToolSearch/WebSearch going on into the answering message, a TUI message
written after its call was told (lateUsage), a cut stream's retry
(b42ff722). Each later request re-sends what the earlier one had, so the
reporter's TaskStop reply after a ToolSearch said cache_read 1,154,857
(577,009 + 577,848) and cache_creation 829 (253 + 576) for a ~577k
conversation, and Claude Code compacted early. 12 of their 30 replies
after ToolSearch were about 2x.

The translated route summed the same way across its tries (#5115): the
empty reply asked again (#667), a loop's re-ask (#1359), a cut reply's
continuation (#853), and search.go's web search rounds. The Anthropic
passthrough has no in-reply fold; each try is its own call.

Usage.after (claude_subscription.go) replaces plus at these joins: the
client is told the last request's input, cache writes and cache reads,
and every request's output and reasoning (all of it was streamed). The
earlier requests' prompts go in Deferred, which the ledger bills
(billed()) and no encoder tells. Usage.restart makes a later request's
prompt counts replace the earlier's, a zero too, so a later request that
reads nothing from the cache isn't told, or billed again, the earlier's
reads. Cache writes are last-only for the client as well: the later
request reads what the earlier wrote, so summed they count it twice.
ggbdpq's #5115 analysis named the translated route's case; no code of
theirs was used.

Tests (usage_last_prompt_test.go), on the reporter's numbers:
- TestClaudeOwnCallReplyTellsLastPrompt: bridge, told 6/576/577848,
  billed 8/829/1154857; and a second request that missed the cache.
- TestClaudeTUILateMessagePromptNotTold: interactive mode's late message.
- TestRetriedReplyTellsLastPrompt: Gemini three reasoning-only replies
  then an answer, Chat and Anthropic clients; ledger has all four.
- TestLaterTryZeroCacheReadNotTold: a continuation and a search round
  whose later request reads 0 from the cache.
Tests that pinned the summed client numbers now pin the last request's
and check the billed sum (CachePartialUpdateMatrix, Probe1717 zero split,
cut stream retry, own WebSearch, search rounds, StreamCutUsage renamed
TestStreamCutUsageTellsLastTry).

Run (mote, Go 1.26.8, -tags nogui):
- The new tests on origin/main ca77a9ea8: red, the client told
  8/829/1154857 (the report's numbers), prompt_tokens 2,000,000 for
  four 500k tries.
- Broken by hand: restart dropped -> TestClaudeCutStreamGoesOnInRetry
  and the cache-missed case red (reads billed twice); after() put back
  to plus -> 12 tests red; restart on the translated tries dropped ->
  TestLaterTryZeroCacheReadNotTold red (cache reads 200 billed, 111
  told). The last one was green before that test was added.
- go test ./internal/gateway/ whole: ok except
  TestClaudeInternalMessagesKeepCacheWrites, which pinned the sum and
  was updated after; that test with the usage, cache, search,
  continuation and TUI tests then ok (61.8s).
- go vet ./internal/gateway for darwin, linux and windows; gofmt clean.
- The full suite runs after the push (mote's suite lock held 3h+ by
  another session).

Not tried: a real Claude Code account or the real TUI, the reporter's
session, a real Gemini/translated provider, Windows or Linux runs of
the package.

Reported-by: sleepy_shibe (Discord)

provider: Grok's mover min is 0.2.5 (plugins#818)

opencode-grok-auth 0.2.5 (plugins 5bbdb826) stops telling a user to add
the account again when xAI answers 401 "Authentication required" on a
token Grok Build left as it was and that hasn't expired. That refusal
isn't xAI's verdict on the token (which reads "Invalid or expired
credentials (... upstream=...)"), and it passed by itself within minutes
in the report. The plugin now answers it as a 503 with Retry-After: 60
and X-Magpie-Sign-In: kept, so the gateway rests the account briefly and
fails over (failOther, as for any kept 401 or 503); a real verdict is
still 401 "sign in again". A 401's wait on `grok models` is capped at
15s (was the 30s exec timeout).

npm has 0.2.5: `npm view --prefer-online
@magpie-community/opencode-grok-auth time` gives 2026-11-07T01:58:19Z.
The publish run's npm job is red only for middleware-think-tags 0.1.2
(E404, not its trusted publisher); grok 0.2.5 published in it.

Run: go test ./internal/provider/ on mote, ok (125s); gofmt -l clean.
The plugin side ran its package tests (mote), the repo bun test (Linux
VM, 6571 pass) and check.mjs grok; its body has the hand-breaks.

Not tried: a real "Authentication required" 401 (could not provoke
one), a revoked real token, a Grok Build renewal slower than 15s.

Reported-by: zane668

sessions: an Antigravity app conversation's folder is its summary row's workspace

The Antigravity app's Sessions tab put every conversation under "No
folder". Since 24dc1651b the app reader reads each conversation's row of
~/.gemini/antigravity/conversation_summaries.db for its title, and the
row's workspace_uris (a JSON list of file:// URIs) was already parsed into
the row's folder for agy, but parseAntigravity never set it as the
session's folder. It now does: the first local workspace URI, the same
rule as agy (agyFolder, including Windows drive and UNC forms). A row with
"[]", and a conversation with no row, still have no folder.

The antigravity parse version goes to 2: a parse kept in the Sessions
cache has the same row revision (agyRev already holds the folder) and
would otherwise keep its empty folder until the conversation changed.

Sibling, agy (the Antigravity CLI tab): already sets the folder from the
same column, for transcripts and row-only conversations (TestAgy*); no
change. A transcript with no row has no folder there, as before.

Shapes: workspace_uris and raw_summary as this Mac's agy writes them
(read only; ["file:///<project>"]); the fixture's paths are made up.

Run (mote): go test -tags nogui ./internal/sessions ./internal/usage ok;
GOOS=linux go vet -tags nogui and GOOS=windows go vet ./internal/sessions
ok; gofmt clean; GUI sessions-folder-list, -paging and -delete in
Chromium (34 pass) and WebKit (17 pass).

Broken by hand: with the old antigravity_app.go and sessions.go,
TestAntigravityAppFolder reads "" for both conversations with a workspace,
and TestAntigravityAppParseBeforeFolderReadAgain keeps the old parse.

Not tried: a real Antigravity app summaries database with workspace rows
(this Mac's app data folder has no conversations); the reporter's own
data; Windows paths beyond agyFolder's existing unit test.

Reported-by: zane668

gateway: a full window of some models only rests that model (plugins#817)

A subscription account that fails with a window full rests until that
window renews (restAfter's "window" branch). The rest was always on the
account (restKey), whatever the window counted. Now, when every full
window that counts the model counts some models only (Allowance.Pooled,
the same reading a quota refusal already narrows by), the model rests
(restID), and its siblings in their own windows still answer. A full
window of the whole account rests the account as before.

zane668's ZCode Start Plan gift account: GLM-5.3's daily bucket was
spent, and the plugin passed its 200 "exceed quota limit" on as it came.
The gateway read that as a 502 that did not stream (failOther), the
window branch took GLM-5.3's full bucket, and the account rested ~22h.
GLM-5.3-Flash, with its own bucket 71% left and a weekend bucket unused,
was skipped by every group. zcode 0.1.53 now says that answer as a 429
(failQuota, which pooled already narrowed). This change is for any
plugin or built-in whose failure isn't worded as quota while a
per-model window is full.

Checked the reporter's reading before changing anything: spentUp runs
only on the forcedGift and freeGift paths, and the plain path returns
done(kept(res)). failure(502, "... did not stream: exceed quota limit")
is failOther. pooled is computed for failQuota only, and the window
branch set modelBackoff false and kept restKey.

TestScopedWindowFullRestsTheModelOnly builds the allowance through
PluginAllowanceForTest from the plugin's startUsage windows as the
report read them (GLM-5.3 100%, Flash 29%, the weekend bucket 0%):
- the 502 that did not stream rests GLM-5.3 alone till its reset, and
  Flash not;
- the plugin's new 429 1005 does too;
- with a whole-account plan window full as well, or alone, the account
  rests and Flash with it.
Not changed: the Codex out-of-credit branch's window. Its credits are
the account's.

Run at 93c258ef9 on mote: go vet ./internal/gateway ok; go test -run
'Rest|Window|Pool|Quota|Spent|Narrow|Renew|ZCode|Zcode|Backoff|Fail'
./internal/gateway ok (70.8s). Broken by hand: windowModel left out of
the restID condition, and the 502 subtest fails ("rests
zcode@me@zcode (model ""), want the model alone"). The 429 subtest
passes either way (pooled already covered it), as a guard.

Not tried: a live ZCode account with a spent bucket. The full suite
runs after the push.

Reported-by: zane668

gateway: an account its vendor restricted isn't asked again while it rests

leowang (Discord #help, 11-07) had two Antigravity accounts that Google
suspended for a Terms of Service violation. Their usage rows read
"tried 23, answered 0, 23 account restricted by the vendor" and 22/0/22.
2e58f85e4 (v0.1.3110) reads that 403 as failRestricted and rests the
account restrictedRest (2h), and the comment promises one refused request
per account per two hours. But when the model has no other account,
restLast keeps a lone resting candidate ("there is no other") and
probeOne keeps the resting one back soonest. So every request still went
to Google, alternating between the two accounts. The same held for every
failRestricted refusal (WorkBuddy 11140, ZCode 3012, a Codex risk block).

restAfterMarked now keeps the vendor's words with a restricted rest.
restrictedHeld gives them again, with the refusal's status, when the
last candidate of a request is an account resting for that reason. This
mirrors verifyHeld: nobody is asked, the try is marked restricted so the
panel keeps saying why, and the rest isn't taken anew, including in a
strictly kept conversation. When the rest ends (or Unrest), the account
is asked once again. A refusal of the request's content (Antigravity's
400 high-risk text, or its 429 on agent prompts, failPrompt) rests
nothing and still asks.

Run (mote, macOS 27):
- go test -count=1 -timeout 45m ./internal/gateway: ok
- the new tests (restricted_held_test.go) and -run
  'TestAntigravitySuspended|TestRiskRefusal|TestWorkBuddyRestricted|
  TestPluginRestrictedAccountSkipped|TestZCodeStartPlanBlockRestsRestricted|
  Restricted|Verif': ok
- gofmt -l, go vet ./..., GOOS=linux go vet -tags nogui ./...,
  GOOS=windows go vet ./...: clean
Broken by hand:
- On the old gateway.go/routing.go,
  TestSuspendedAccountsNotAskedWhileTheyRest is red ("turn 2: 403 ...
  asked [u1]") and TestRestrictedLoneAccountNotAskedWhileItRests is red
  ("request 2 ... asked [acct-1 acct-1]").
  TestContentRefusalStillAsksTheAccount passes on both.
- With the !heldRestricted rest guard replaced by true,
  TestSuspendedStrictConversationKeepsItsRest is red ("turn 3 moved the
  rest").
Not tried:
- A real suspended Google account. The fixture is the 403 body from
  2e58f85e4's test.
- A restricted rest still lives in memory only (rests.json keeps ladder
  rests), so a restart asks each such account once more. Not changed.

Reported-by: 小李 (Discord)

sessions: Antigravity's conversations take their title from conversation_summaries.db

The Antigravity desktop app's Sessions tab read every row as "(no
prompt)". The app keeps its step payloads encrypted, and the reader only
read their metadata, so no title was ever found. The app's language
server (the same code as agy) writes a row per conversation into
~/.gemini/antigravity/conversation_summaries.db: title once one is made,
and preview (the first request) from the start. The app reader now reads
that row, the same way agy's reader does, with title as the session's
name and preview as its prompt, and reparses when the row changes.

Sibling, agy: a row-only conversation with no title yet (the real row on
this Mac, agy 1.4.12: title "", preview "hi") was not listed at all; it
now shows its preview. A summaries database made before preview was a
column is still read (falls back to title only). The rows cache is kept
per database, since both readers now read one each.

Run (mote): go test -tags nogui ./internal/sessions ./internal/usage ok;
GOOS=linux go vet -tags nogui and GOOS=windows go vet ./internal/sessions
ok; gofmt clean. DDL in the test is from Antigravity 2.29.0's
language_server, started in a sandbox HOME on mote, which created
conversation_summaries.db on first start.

Broken by hand: with the old agy.go, antigravity_app.go and sessions.go,
TestAntigravityAppTitle fails ("before a title: \"\", want the preview")
and TestAgyRowOnlyPreview finds no session. With the preview-less
fallback query removed, TestAgyRowsWithoutPreview fails (rows map[] ok
false).

Not tried: a real Antigravity app database with summary rows (this Mac's
app data has none to read, and its files were only read); app versions
older than 2.29.0, which may keep summaries in agyhub_summaries_proto.pb
instead. workspace_uris is not used as the app session's folder.

usage: WorkBuddy's credits a day count each pool, adding up to Total credits (yapechan)

yapechan on Discord (#feedback, 11-07, WorkBuddy China): the card's
"Credits used per day" read 今天 0 for 积分 and 额外积分 and 今天 34.06
for 积分合计, so the total wasn't the two pools' sum.

Since the plugin's 0.2.22/0.2.24 the card has both pools set aside,
Credits and Extra credits, and Total credits, the two together, as the
window that stops the account. noteDailyCredits takes a window set aside
for a counted window's breakdown when that window used at least as much
over the same span (the CodeArts rule, ec3111d87), and the total always
does, so both pools were marked Part and counted nothing; they still
showed because they had days from before 0.2.22. The card's figures
themselves (x / 500, y / 2900, x+y / 3400) were right; only the days were.

Now pools set aside that together grant what a counted window grants
(poolsOfWhole: two or more, same unit, limits summing to its limit) are
that whole's pools: each counts its own days beside the whole's, and is
shown even with none. A bucket that is only part of its whole (CodeArts'
基础积分 under 总积分) stays its breakdown. Both WorkBuddy builds send the
same shape, so workbuddy-ai is covered too. Days already counted can't be
split again: today's 34.06 stays on the total alone.

TestDailyCreditsPoolsOfWhole (new): the plugin's current card for
CN_FREE_SUMMARY's shape, the extra credits moving alone, then the plan's,
then both: Credits 20 + Extra credits 28 = Total credits 48; and a
CodeArts-like card with two buckets that don't make up its whole shows
总积分 alone.

Reported-by: yapechan

routing: a provider set to Use first goes ahead of the others Smart weighs it with

hzh_1119 on Discord: ChatGPT Pro and Business now come with monthly API
credit, and they want an OpenAI API key spent before the ChatGPT
subscription where both serve a model, the subscription taking over
after. Smart had no way to say so: an API key tells no allowance, so it
went after every account with room, in every model's found group
(auto/<model>). The only way round was a group set to In order with its
members dragged, one group at a time, which nothing pointed to.

A provider row's right-click has Use first (provider/usefirst,
provider.SetUseFirst, Provider.UseFirst, copied onto its accounts by
accountSettings, kept by the editor's Save). Its keys and accounts are
routes.Seat.Lead, and Smart (leadFirst) puts those not all but used up
ahead of every other seat, each side in Smart's own order. A resting one
is passed over as before, so a 429 insufficient_quota (out of credit) or
a failure moves the request on to the subscription. Off by default;
within one provider nothing changes. The Routing page says why the first
went first (Weighed.UseFirst, firstWhy) and doesn't call the one behind
it "renewing later" (behindWhy). The menu shows a tick when it is on.
Free quota by expiry orders its paid seats with Smart and so follows it;
other strategies don't read it. The core's script budget is met by
cutting three Providers-page comments in app.js, no raise.

Run (on mote via mote-run, at da548b454 = origin/main):
- go test ./internal/routes ./internal/provider: ok. ./internal/gui: ok
  but TestMainWindowCorners/macOS_26_SDK, red the same on a fresh
  origin/main da548b454 checkout (#3949, macOS 27).
- go test -run 'TestUseFirstLeadsTheGroup|TestRoutingGroups'
  ./internal/gateway: ok.
- node --test use-first.test.cjs (new: 40 cases, Chromium and WebKit,
  1100 and 420 wide, en zh zh-TW ja de) and provider-find.test.cjs
  (its menu now lists Use first): 52 pass.
- i18n-keys, i18n-en-no-cjk, routing-behind-why: pass but i18n-keys'
  "a plugin's words are its own", red the same on origin/main
  (#5327, #5426, #5482; none of its keys are this change's).
- GOOS=linux and GOOS=windows go vet -tags nogui ./...: ok. gofmt -l: none.

Broken by hand:
- Lead left out of weighRouted's seat: TestUseFirstLeadsTheGroup red
  (served from ksub with api set to Use first).
- Smart without leadFirst: TestSmartLeadFirst red
  ([plus pro api ...], want api first).
- firstWhy's Use first case off: use-first.test.cjs's Routing cases red

Not tried: a real ChatGPT account beside a real OpenAI key with API
credit; the 429 insufficient_quota fallthrough is from the fake

Reported-by: shangyuan0818 (Discord)

agent tests: the WSL probe test has a timeout(1) where macOS has none (#5570)

TestWSLProbeLooksPastWindowsCommand runs the distro probe in the host's
/bin/sh, and the probe asks a command's version under `timeout 10`.
A distro has timeout (coreutils); macOS 26.2 has none (mote's macOS
27.2 has one), so the ver: line was "sh: timeout: command not found", no version,
and the test was red on every macos-latest run since it landed in
f9a88c4fb (42279775186, 42285312651, 42292490462, 42295916081), not
intermittently. The probe itself is right. The test now puts a stand-in
timeout on PATH when /usr/bin/timeout is missing, and its failure prints
the probe's output.

Run (mote, macOS 27): go test -count=3 -run TestWSLProbe ./internal/agent,
ok, with the injection below and the stand-in renamed to match.
Broken by hand: mote has /usr/bin/timeout, so the probe's `timeout 10`
was renamed `timeoutx 10` in the test: with no stand-in it is red as on
CI (Has bin:pi, Versions empty; out shows "timeoutx: command not
found"), green with the stand-in.
Not tried: a macos-latest (macOS 26) runner itself; this Mac is 26.2 and
has no /usr/bin/timeout, which is the cause.

Fixes #5570

gateway tests: big compaction bodies aren't held to the 30s unrouted stop (#5571)

TestCompactionOverByteCapSlowFitting (and its siblings through cappedOn)
send bodies up to 42MB. magpie's work on one before its first route takes
~0.6s, ~9s under -race on a loaded Mac, and on a loaded ubuntu runner
under -race past unroutedUnknown's 30s: the request was stopped with 504
"held this request for 30s without routing" after 65s of test, the CI
goroutine dump in parseRequest. Not a product bug: without -race the
same work is well under a second. cappedOn now lifts the two unrouted

gateway, provider, cli: search APIs marked mix are asked together, their pages merged (#2845)

A search asked the search APIs in order and gave the model the first
one's pages. On #2845's 80-query benchmark no single API was best on
both sets. The deduplicated union of two or three APIs' pages scored
higher than the best single API and lost no query (60-query set: 108 to
114-117 of 120, sign test p <= 0.03).

Off by default. When two or more search APIs are marked mix
(SearchAPI.Mix), they are asked first, at once (askSearchAPIsTogether).
Each uses its own keys and timeouts, as when it is asked alone
(askSearchAPIKeys). Their pages go to the model in turn: each API's
first page in the saved order, then each one's second. A page an
earlier API already gave is left out by its address (pageKey). One
that fails or finds nothing leaves the others' pages. When none finds
anything, the APIs not mixed are asked in order. With fewer than two
mixed APIs on and ready, a search runs in order as before. No text
says which API found a page, so what a vendor sees reads as before.

MixSearchAPIs marks the vendors named (two or more, set up, each once)
and clears the rest; none clears all. SetSearchAPI keeps the mark, as
it keeps off, since Settings sends an edit without it. Backup copies
the whole entry, so the mark carries over. CLI: magpie search mix
<api>,<api>, magpie search mix off, and magpie search lists a mixed
one as mix. docs/subsystems/gateway-routing.md has a section on it.

An agent that cancels its request before it is answered is logged 499
"the agent canceled the request": a person stops the reply, or sends the
next message while it is coming and Claude Desktop cancels it and asks
again, or Codex takes a subagent's report (#2398). The gateway already
says nobody failed (no rest, no reroute: TestCanceledRequestRestsNobody),
but Record.Failed is a status >= 400 or an error, so every page counted
it as a failure: the Requests card's "N failed" and success share, its
Failed filter, the CSV's error column, the Routing page's "errors your
agent saw", the Context page's error rate, the failed colour in the
Requests list, Routing and Recent calls, and the OTLP export's error
status. A Claude Desktop session on 2026-10-27 had four, each a message
sent mid-reply; #2398 had 91 of a day's 92 failures.

usage.CanceledBy tells the agent's cancel (499 with AgentCanceled) from
magpie's own limit on a request it asked of itself, logged 499 too and
still a failure (#2318). The cancel is logged with an error type of its
own, agent_canceled (usage.CanceledErrType, set in failedWith), so the
record says what it was and nothing guesses it from a 499, as #2398
asked. Record.Canceled reads the type, and a record logged before it by
its status and message, so the old log reads the same with nothing
migrated. A middleware's usage rows carry the type, so a module can tell
the cancel from magpie's own limit, which its rows (no error text)
couldn't.

Record.Failed leaves the cancel out; Totals counts it apart (Canceled, in
count and plus); RetriedRequest and the first-token and speed sums ask
Answered, so a canceled request is timed nowhere, as before; Codex's
memory of the last model still skips it. Routes and Recent calls say
canceled (set as a route is done and as a day's history is read, so old
days read the same); the Routing totals and the Context page's errors
leave it out. Ledger rows say canceled, and the pages show it muted, in neither the
failed nor the answered colour: the Requests list and its detail ("499 ·
canceled"), the Requests card ("N canceled", the success share of the requests not
canceled), the overview tile, the Routing page (a "gone" outcome, no
speed) and Recent calls (muted). New strings are in zh, zh-TW, ja and de.

The OTLP export: the records the gateway gives its observers for a
request and its try carry the type too (canceledAs), and a root span's
error.type follows Record.Failed, so a canceled request's span and its
try's go with status code 499, no error and no error.type.
TestOTelWaterfallFailureAndCancellation's canceled case held two failed
spans (the try the vendor refused as the agent left is recorded canceled,
as the request is); it now holds neither failed, both 499 and no

provider: a Claude model on Copilot has its 1-hour cache write priced as Copilot bills it, at the 5-minute write (#3435)

Copilot bills a cache write at one price however long it is kept. Its
copilot_usage counts a 1-hour write as the cache_write a 5-minute one
is, and GitHub's "Models and pricing for GitHub Copilot"
(docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-billing/models-and-pricing)
lists one "Cache write" price per Claude model, no 1-hour tier (Opus
5.5: input $4, cached input $0.20, cache write $5, output $20). magpie
gave every Claude model's list price Anthropic's 1-hour write, 2x input
(catalog.OneHourFor), so copilot/claude-opus-5.5 was priced at $8 per
million for an hour's write where Copilot bills $5: on the reporter's
request, $0.125456 against Copilot's own $0.078443.

A Copilot price (tariffOf, cacheWritesAlike) now has no 1-hour write of
its own, so an hour's write is billed as a 5-minute one
(catalog.Price.OneHour), its tiers alike, copied as they may be the
catalog's. This holds for a call read after Copilot was signed out too
(tariffOf's unknown-provider path, MakerPrice), which the reporter's
patch left at 2x. A price the user gave for a Copilot model keeps the
1-hour write they gave, and one they left out isn't filled with 2x input
(userPrice, so UserBasePriceIn reads it alike). Every other provider is
as before: Anthropic, Bedrock, Vertex and relays bill the hour at 2x, so
the rule is scoped to Copilot's id, not taken off every non-Anthropic
provider. Usage rows are priced as they are read (Record.CostAt), so
calls already recorded read at the new price too. docs/reference.md and
ModelPrice's comment say so.

magpie runs) plays the Dock flap: 29 frames of 512x512 RGBA, each
handed to the Dock tile as an NSImage made on a Go thread. A Go thread
has no autorelease pool, so the NSCGImageSnapshotRep that

frames of about 37 flaps.

get a pool each (same class; their objects are small).

web: the page's API answers its own origin only, not a page on another port or a sibling subdomain

With browser access on (Settings > Browser access, or magpie web), the
sign-in cookie magpie_web_<port> is SameSite=Lax, which a browser sends
with any same-site request: another port of 127.0.0.1 or of the LAN
address, or a sibling name behind the same reverse proxy. apiFramed
refused Origin null, frames and cross-site, but not same-site, and /api
decodes JSON from any Content-Type. So such a page could POST a stdio MCP
server to /api/library/servers/save (text/plain, no-cors) and start it
with /api/library/mcp/check: code run as the user.

webOwnPage (in webHandler, behind webGuard, /api/ only) now judges every
write (all methods but GET/HEAD/OPTIONS) with net/http's
CrossOriginProtection: Sec-Fetch-Site same-origin or none passes, any
other value is refused; from a browser without Sec-Fetch-Site, Origin must
be absent or name the request's Host (or MAGPIE_PUBLIC_URL, for a proxy
that rewrites Host). Any /api request, a GET too, whose Sec-Fetch-Site is
same-site or cross-site is refused, so no GET route with a side effect
(GET /api/import/{id} reads once and deletes) is another page's to call,
without auditing each one. A Sec-Fetch-Site same-origin with an Origin
that doesn't match the Host passes: the browser compared the origins
itself, and nginx's default proxy_set_header Host $proxy_host would
otherwise break every write behind it. The desktop window's /api is served
in-process over no port with no cookie, so it isn't wrapped and its
headers are unchanged. No Content-Type rule: every write the page makes
goes through api() as application/json, but multipart and text/plain are
both CORS-safelisted, so the rule would add nothing the origin check
doesn't already give.

remote magpie: a moved remote is looked for again, and is sent its key only after it proves it holds it

fe61503e6 had a Remote magpie whose address didn't dial look for it on
the old address's /24 and this computer's private /24s, and sent GET
/v1/models, signed with the provider's gateway key (Authorization,
x-api-key and the provider's own headers), to every address that took
the connection at the port. On a café's or hotel's network, or with the
other computer off, anything listening there got the key in clear and,
by answering {"data":[]}, became the provider: the failed request and
every later one went to it. 18a9a2d88 turned the look off.

Now an address that takes the connection is first asked to prove it
holds the key, with nothing keyed sent:

- B POSTs {"nonce": 32 random bytes hex, "key_id": sha256(key) hex} to
  /v1/magpie/prove (provider.RemoteProvePath), no key, no provider
  headers, no proxy, no redirects (proves in remote_moved.go).
- A (gateway's remote_prove.go) finds the enabled gateway key with that
  sha256 (access.ProveSecret: constant-time compares over every key,
  the legacy settings sharing key too, then Check, so an off, expired
  or orphaned issued key has none) and answers
  HMAC-SHA256(key, "magpie-prove-v1\n" nonce "\n" address), the address
  being the one the connection reached it at (http.LocalAddrContextKey);
  404 when no key matches. A host that relays B's nonce to A elsewhere
  gets a proof for A's address, which B, checking against the address it
  dialled with hmac.Equal, refuses.
- Only after that does isRemote ask /v1/models with the key, as before.
- The route goes through lanGuard like OIDC's trade (proveAsked: POST,
  exact path, no gateway key): from another machine only while shared,
  past the allow list and rebinding check; corsGuard still judges its
  Origin, the handler refuses anything fromBrowser, and an unknown id
  from another machine counts against tooManyAuthFails. readOnlyRoutes
  lists it (it carries no key and answers none).

  one long-poll per Remote magpie. On a new tag it fetches the list
  through the same RefetchTaking, so catalog.Touched rewrites the
  agents' configs. A magpie from before answers at once with no ETag; it
  is left to the 10m schedule and asked again after an hour. A Remote
  magpie whose user set its list to "off" is not followed. The schedule
  stays as the fallback.

plugin host: a plugin's redirect to another origin is sent none of its key headers (#5508)

Bun follows any redirect anywhere and, on a hop to another origin, drops
only Authorization and Cookie. Checked on Bun 1.4.2 before the change:
x-api-key, x-goog-api-key and a custom header reached a second local
server on each of 301, 302, 303, 307 and 308. So a vendor (or anything
answering at its URL) that redirected elsewhere got a plugin's key
headers, and an https vendor's redirect to http was followed.

host.js now applies provider.KeepsCredentials' rule (c57a5f7f5) at the
one place every plugin fetch leaves, `sent`:
- `followed` sends each hop with redirect "manual" and follows a 3xx
  itself only to the first request's origin (scheme, host, port), or
  http to https on the same host and default ports (`sameOrigin`, a
  port of provider.SameOrigin), at most 10 ("stopped after 10
  redirects", as Go's). Any other 3xx is given back to the plugin as it
  came, Location included.
- A bare request (no body, only accept/user-agent-like headers,
  BARE_HEADERS) still follows a redirect anywhere, as a download handed
  to a CDN does; it carries nothing of the plugin's.
- 301/302 on POST and 303 become GET with the body and its headers
  dropped; 307/308 send the body again, and a stream body that can't be
  sent twice makes the 3xx the answer.
- A fetch asked with redirect "manual" or "error" (mimo, cursor,
  gcp-ai and others do) goes out as it was asked.

Paths this covers, all of which reach globalThis.fetch and so `sent`:
- the gateway's request to a plugin account: Provider.do → the
  account's transport → plugin.Fetch → host "fetch" → fetchAs → the
  loader's fetch, or the host's fetch when the loader has none. A 3xx
  the host gives back reaches the caller as the vendor sent it.
- plugin.Fetch from the check-ins (MiniMax, Qoder, Trae, WorkBuddy) and
  the models/usage/check/decide reads through plugins.go.
- the plugin's own hooks: sign-in authorize/callback, models, usage,
  checkin, chat.headers, gateway request hooks, and pi.js's extensions
  (its watchFetch wraps the host's fetch).
- proxied ones: a provider's or account's own proxy (via / init.proxy),
  magpie's global proxy, the SOCKS bridge (netproxy.ForBun) and the LAN
  direct rule. Each hop is sent by `hop` (the old `sent`), so each picks
  its own proxy for its own host.
Not covered, filed as #5520: Bun.fetch (read-only and non-configurable
in Bun 1.4.2, so it can't be wrapped; no community plugin calls it), and
a library on node:http that follows redirects itself. node:http,
node:http2 and WebSocket follow none. The Go side needs nothing more:
Provider.do already hands a plugin account's request to its transport,
which doesn't follow.

Docs: provider-plugins.md (the rule, what isn't covered, the test) and
gateway-routing.md's list of what follows KeepsCredentials.

browser: magpie in Docker uses the host's own browser, through a key the page hands out

noahhrreion ran magpie in a container and its Magpie Browser never
connected. The host's Chrome dials ws://127.0.0.1:3425/v1/magpie/browser/
extension, which reaches the container from the bridge (172.17.0.1). That
is not loopback, so the gateway refused it (403). The browser MCP also
refused every caller from elsewhere, and the hub marked the browser
HereOnly. The extension's folder under the container's HOME can't be
loaded by the host's browser either.

Nothing is opened to the network without a key:

- The extension takes a gateway key: its popup has a Gateway key field,
  and config.js carries KEY (extension 0.1.7). From another computer the
  extension connects only with ?key= of a gateway key that is on, and
  only from the extension's own Origin (checked first). Loopback is
  unchanged, and a page's origin, null, a keyless call or a rebound Host
  are all still refused (TestBrowserExtensionOnlyFromItsOrigin).
- A browser that connects with a key belongs to that key. Sessions are
  tagged key:<id>/... (browserOwner, keyedSession), and a remote caller's
  session is forced to its own key's whatever it names. The relay filters
  every lookup (forSession, all, choose) through browserConn.serves. The
  browser MCP admits a remote caller only with a gateway key; a web page
  is refused as before.
- The key the page makes is recorded as this magpie's own browser's: its
  id goes in settings.Dir()/browser-key, written temp-and-rename. This
  goes by where the key came from, not by its name. A browser connecting
  with it serves this computer's sessions too, so agents inside the
  container use it as they would one on loopback. A record that can't be
  read names no key, so no keyed browser is this computer's.
- Router: magpie mcp browser is HubServer.Keyed. A visitor from
  elsewhere gets it only with a key (HubVisitor.Key), and hubCall names
  its session key:<id>/..., so it reaches only that key's browser.
- GUI: a page whose browser can't reach magpie's folders (InContainer, or
  a page from another computer) is "away". The Magpie Browser sheet's
  button then reads Download the extension. It does a POST to
  /api/library/browser/extension with the page's origin, which answers a
  zip pointed at that origin (3430 passes the gateway's routes on) and
  holding the recorded key's secret. The key is made the first time and
  reused while it is on. The steps (unzip, chrome://extensions, Developer
  mode, Load unpacked) are shown in every language. It is a POST so that
  a link from another site can't mint a key.
- Docs: reference.md (Docker), subsystems/library.md and mcp-router.md,
  and site docker.html in en, zh and ja.

sessions: a Codex prompt's title is read from its head, not its whole text decoded

cxFastPrompt decoded each user message's whole text with json.Unmarshal
to take its first 160 runes for a title. A pasted log or file made all
of it again (512MB on a cold read of a year of real Codex history,

gateway: a vendor's redirect to another origin is sent no provider key

Go's http.Client follows up to 10 redirects to any host, https to http
included, and on a hop to another domain drops only Authorization,
Cookie and WWW-Authenticate. So a vendor (or anything answering at its
URL) that redirected elsewhere got x-api-key, x-goog-api-key, api-key
and a provider's own headers sent there; Authorization too when only
the port differed, and all of them in the clear on an https to http
hop on the same host.

The class is fixed where the requests leave:
- provider.KeepsCredentials is a CheckRedirect that follows a redirect
  only to the request's own origin (scheme, host, port; or http to
  https on the same host and default ports), at most 10, and gives any
  other 3xx back as the answer (http.ErrUseLastResponse).
- provider.Keyed(c) is a copy of c with c's own CheckRedirect, then
  KeepsCredentials. Provider.do, the choke point of every p.Do, sends
  through it, and every http.DefaultClient.Do in internal/provider that
  carries a credential is Keyed(http.DefaultClient).Do. A copy per
  call, since netproxy.Install sets the default client's transport at
  run time. Left alone: Grok's public download, Antigravity's version
  URL and cline.go's unsigned read.
- the gateway's client (s.client, every vendor call), the Codex relay's
  and the Codex websocket's take KeepsCredentials, and so does
  chatgpt_api's siwcClient.

The native route needs nothing more: the vendor's 3xx comes back to
the caller as it came, Location included, and the caller decides.
Translated routes don't follow either, rather than following with
credentials stripped: it is the rule search_api.go had already (#1580),
no vendor magpie speaks to was found redirecting its API to another
origin, a stripped request elsewhere would only fail with a confusing
401, and the vendor-URL downloads (video, images) are fetched unsigned
through vendorClient, so they are not affected.

Authorization, x-api-key, x-goog-api-key, api-key and a custom header;

sessions: a Claude session's calls list grows to the rate its file was read at

claudeCall appended each call to st.Calls, and append grows a long list
by about a quarter at a time, so a session's calls were copied through

calls the rest of the file is likely to hold at the rate read so far

the same way; a packed file, whose offsets run past its size, is left to
append.

update: the Windows app asks where to install, the first time

The Windows exe opened from Downloads (or the Desktop, or temp)
installed itself into %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\magpie without a word.
Now, the first time, with nothing installed yet, Windows' task dialog
asks "Install magpie in this folder?". It shows the folder and offers
Install, Change… and Cancel, in the tray's language (en, zh, zh-TW,
ja, de).

- Change… opens the system folder picker. A picked folder gets
  "magpie" added unless it is already named that (update.InstallDir).
- A folder other than the default is recorded at HKCU\Software\magpie
  InstallLocation. So the next exe downloaded replaces the copy there
  in place and asks nothing (installed(), forwards()).
- Cancel runs the exe where it is, as a portable copy, and nothing is
  recorded.
- Uninstall forgets the record (update.ForgetInstallDir, a new System
  step).
- The shortcut, App Paths, autostart, magpie://, the PATH entry and
  self-update already take the running exe's folder, so they follow
  the choice.

Program Files and other folders only an administrator can write to
are refused in the dialog (update.Installable test-writes and maps a
permission error to ErrNeedsAdmin). They are not elevated into.
magpie installs per user (HKCU Run, the user's PATH), and its
self-update replaces the exe without elevation (CanElevate is false on
Windows). So an admin folder would make every update fail, or would
need a UAC prompt on each one. A downloads folder is refused too.
Refusing is the simplest correct choice: it costs a user nothing they
had before, and keeps updates silent. Any folders the test-write made
are removed again.

Docs: gui-shell.md, "Where Windows installs magpie".

NEKO-CwC asked, after v0.1.3141, why a custom API-key Responses relay's
400/413/422 is still turned into context_length_exceeded when the relay
never said so. It shouldn't be. tooLongUnsaid read any provider's
400/413/422 that said nothing of length, for a request 1.2 times past the
model's window, as "prompt is too long". That rule came from three
vendors' refusals in b3ab3e42e (v0.1.735, 10-03): Devin's 502 "capacity
issues", Qoder's 400 "Error in upstream response" and WorkBuddy's 400
"Invalid request parameters". #711 (v0.1.808) then kept the 413 case for
Factory's byte cap. 978284dd6 (v0.1.3141) had already scoped the 5xx to
Devin. The 4xx half still applied to every provider.

Now:
- unsaidStatus lists who gets the inference, keyed by the id of the
  plugin that serves the vendor (all of them are retired as built-ins),
  never by the provider's id, which a user's own provider can share:
  devin 500/502/503/504; qoder, qoder-cn, workbuddy, workbuddy-ai
  400/413/422; factory 413. unsaidOverflows replaces busyOverflows.
- Every other provider's failure reaches the client with its own status
  and words: custom and by-address providers, API-key relays, OpenAI,
  Anthropic, other plugins. Transport failures are never inferred
  (unchanged since 978284dd6).
- An upstream that says it overflowed (tooLongRe, overflow codes) is
  still passed on as an overflow. A 400/422 whose own words say the
  request is too long (saysLength, #4420) is still read past half the
  window for any vendor, because the vendor named the cause.
- The single call site in serve runs for every client route (Responses,
  Codex's /responses, Chat, Messages) and every upstream protocol, held
  or streamed, before anything is sent. Mid-stream SSE errors were never
  inferred.

routing: a dsh fork's requests are named by the reply its client was given (#5491)

dsh's chat and messages routes send no session id, so Routing and Context
found a dsh session by the hash of the conversation's opening. A fork
repeats its source's opening, so every request the fork made showed under
the source, and the fork's name never appeared.

Flandern1211's patch, ported:
- The gateway keeps the id of the reply it gave the client
  (Route.ResponseID). It is set from clientResponseID in the same update
  that marks the route done, so a poll that sees Done also sees the id,
  with no race against the usage ledger. When magpie translates, it is
  the id after translation, e.g. chatcmpl-…, not the upstream's msg_….
- sessions reads dsh's replayState.response.responseId into
  Session.ResponseIDs. Only main files are read, only replies served by
  the gateway, and only the fork's own replies after its session/end-seed
  (seedLength for version 1).
- Routing (pricedRoutes) and Context (joinConvs) look up a finished
  request by its reply id first, then by its opening. A request logged
  before this keeps the opening's session.

Changed from the patch:
- A reply id names a session over the opening only when the opening is
  that session's own, or a session it was forked from, or the opening is
  unknown. Vendors' ids can repeat: an encoder keeps the upstream's id,
  and Ollama's is chatcmpl-<0..999>. Without the guard, two unrelated
  conversations could swap names. Session.ForkOf comes from the fork
  header's parentSession, isSeeded and delegationDepth 0, which is how
  dsh's buildForkSeed writes it. ownerOf walks that chain, so a fork of a
  fork works too.
- Poll cost: dsh never writes down some reply ids (a title call, a
  refused turn). Under the patch, each such id made Routing list every
  session again every 2s, for as long as the route was on the page. Now
  an id is waited for only up to a minute (convsKept) after its request
  ended (looseKeys). After that the regular one-minute rebuild covers it.
- A page whose loose routes carry only a reply id still builds the map
  (looseRoute).
- The patch's synthetic fork headers gain parentSession, as dsh writes
  them.
- docs/subsystems/gateway-routing.md describes the reply-id join.

Tests:
- TestDshForkNamedByTheReplyTheGatewayGave sends dsh 0.2.0-rc.2's real
  captured completions request (testdata/dsh-gateway) through
  gateway.New() twice, to an Anthropic-only upstream, so the reply is
  translated. It writes the source's real session file with the first
  client id, and a fork shaped like dsh's buildForkSeed output with the
  second. It then checks that pricedRoutes and contextOf put each request
  under its own session, and an old route without an id under the source.
- TestDshForkOfARealSessionListsItsOwnReplies forks the real fixture
  session: the fork lists only its own reply and ForkOf, the source
  keeps [c1].
- TestDshReplyIDOfAnotherConversationNamesNoOne covers the guard.
- TestRoutingWaitsForAReplyIDOnlyAWhile covers the poll bound.
- The patch's own tests: TestDoneRouteKeepsTheClientResponseID (json and
  stream), TestDshResponseIDs*, TestRoutingTellsAForkByItsReply,
  TestContextTellsAForkByItsReply.

Cause: none found in magpie. The bytes are read by stdlib crypto/tls, and
every conn wrapper on the path only passes them through, so a record whose
MAC fails was mangled before it reached us: by the gateway or a box between
(the system proxy route, a TLS-inspecting middlebox). HTTP/2 meets it far
more than one-off clients do: one long-lived connection carries every
stream, plus magpie's health pings (netproxy.HTTP2Health), so a gateway
that interleaves its writes racily breaks it.

- Provider.HTTP1 ("HTTP version" row, "HTTP/1.1 only" tick, under the
  editor's Advanced; shown for a provider of the user's own at an https://
  address, the same set InsecureTLS takes). Via adds netproxy.WithHTTP1 for
  its own base URLs' hosts; Dispatch sends those over its HTTP/1.1 copy.
  Another host, and a request made for another provider (With), keep HTTP/2.
  Save refuses it on a preset's; a save that leaves the key out keeps it.
- With no setting: a TLS record error read on an HTTP/2 reply (h2Watch) or
  round trip marks the host:port, and Dispatch speaks HTTP/1.1 to it for 6
  hours. Go's transport already drops the broken connection. Zero-config
  default otherwise unchanged.
- Advanced opens by itself when the tick is set. No note under the row
  (the core script budget, not raised).

A first start (or one after the session caches are gone) reads every
Claude Code transcript to count calls. On a real 21 GB history this
allocated 14.6 GB and ran 460 GCs. Three things made most of what was
thrown away right after:

- ccWithoutContent made a new copy of each reply line with its content
  set to null (82 MB), and gjson.GetBytes copied the content to find it
  (27 MB). ccDecode now builds the stripped line in a pooled buffer and
  finds the content through an unsafe.String view, with no copy.

  made a decoder for each one (29 MB). A string with no escapes and valid
  UTF-8 is now taken as its bytes. Anything else still goes to
  json.Unmarshal, which writes U+FFFD for bad bytes.
- writeCalls made a new Patches list for each frame (1 GB). It now reuses
  one list from a pool and clears it before putting it back, so the pool
  keeps no reference to the call state.

draws nothing, and the Sessions turn keeps only the reply.

URL, or a bare Anthropic or Gemini source that starts as a PNG, JPEG,
GIF or WebP does, 1 KiB or more, with no escapes) for a short ref
before the caps apply.

  keep their pictures in keptImages. It is memory only and bounded:
  128 MiB, least recently used first, and the same picture is kept
  once. dataImage reads a ref back to the data: URL. A ref whose
  picture has gone draws nothing.

library: a skill whose app left its own link on a deleted version follows the version on disk

tjhhhh_84378 on Discord (11-06): ego lite updated from 0.6.2.5 to 0.6.2.7,
deleted Versions/0.6.2.5, and left its own ~/.local/share/ego/
active_version_dir naming it. The library's ego-browser, brought in since
dccfefdf7 (#2635), links to ego's ~/.local/share/ego/ego-skills ->
active_version_dir/Resources/ego-skills/ego-browser, so the whole chain led
nowhere and the skill was lost, while 0.6.2.7 had it complete.

Who owns which link: ~/.local/share/ego/ego-skills, active_version_dir and
the framework's Versions/* are ego's; magpie only reads them. magpie writes
the library's own link (library/skills/ego-browser) and the agents' links
to it. The stale pointer is ego's, but magpie lost the skill with a newer
version on disk.

557f51dbf mended a library link that points straight into Versions/<old>,
but movedVersion looked only at the link's own target: for ego-skills the
first missing part is not a version name, so nothing was found.

followMovedSkills (skill_moved.go) now, for a dangling library link whose
target isn't in a version folder, follows the links on the way as far as
they are there (linkedEnd) and asks movedVersion of where they end:
Current/current/latest when that leads to the skill, else the highest
version beside the deleted one with a SKILL.md there. The library links to
that folder, and keeps the app's steady link as the new Source.Via. Once
the steady link leads to a SKILL.md again (ego or the user mended it), the
library links through it once more and Via is cleared. ego's links are
never written. With no other version on disk the link is kept as it was
and the skill is shown missing, as before.

Old imports: a skill linked straight into Versions/<old> was already
mended by 557f51dbf; one linked through ego's link (since dccfefdf7) is
mended by this on the next read of the Library page or the next sync. No
re-import needed. Agents that read ~/.agents/skills directly still see
ego's own entry there, which is the user's/ego's and is left alone.

plugin: TestStopLetsARenewalEnd waits for the renewal to start and the stopped host to end, not for 300ms and Restart (#2743)

The test was red on main two ways, each from a timing assumption:

- "the renewal never started" (line 54, 60s): the load call that starts
  the renewal had a fixed 300ms context. When the call is not written to
  the host within those 300ms (a slow get, a busy writer), it is given up
  on before it is sent, the plugin never reaches auth.refresh, and no
  wait helps. Now the call's context is cancelled only once the
  renewal's log shows it started.
- "kept ... not the renewed token" (line 61, CI at 84ad780b6): a
  given-up call keeps its slot until its abort is written to the host
  (callAborting). If Restart runs before that write, the host is busy,
  retire stops it in the background, and Restart returns at once; the
  test then read plugin-auth.json while the renewal was still running.
  The product is right: the background stop still lets the renewal end
  and saves the token. The test now waits on the stopped host's dead
  channel. It also waits until magpie has heard the host's "renewing"
  event, so a host output read late can't count as no renewal.

otherwise Windows' address on the one WSL adapter whose network holds

probes use it: agent's parseProbe (distro.Gateway, what place writes into
agents) and wslrun's (Tool.Host, a 127.0.0.1 proxy handed to a WSL CLI),

net (OnWSLNet), so agents there get the WSL key.

writes the new gateway into wsl.json and keeps 192.168.9.1 in Was. The
startup SyncCatalog then rewrites Pi's provider block (baseUrl and apiKey)

first probe after it runs, and its agents' files at the next sync after

commits.message:
fix(bedrock): forward Codex agent messages that carry encrypted content intact (#50457)

* fix(bedrock): forward Codex agent messages that carry encrypted content intact

Codex multi-agent v2 sends worker messages as agent_message items whose
encrypted_content block only the model server can decrypt. Bedrock Mantle and
Bedrock Runtime used to 400 on agent_message, so LiteLLM rewrote every one into
assistant text, pasting the ciphertext into the prompt and dropping the sender
and recipient. Bedrock now decrypts these items itself, so the rewrite left the
recipient model reading an opaque token instead of its task.

Agent messages with an encrypted_content block now go to Bedrock untouched on
both endpoints. The Bedrock configs declare supports_encrypted_agent_messages,
and the shared normalizer keys off that flag so the two cannot drift. Mantle's
/v1/responses route for open-weight models still rejects agent_message in any
form, so it keeps the old rewrite. Plaintext-only agent messages keep the
rewrite on every route.

* fix(bedrock): only keep worker messages locked for OpenAI GPT models

Gemma and Grok on Mantle's OpenAI route never lock Codex worker messages, so
Codex puts plain text in the locked slot and Bedrock rejected it with
invalid_encrypted_content once the route alone decided to forward it intact.
Decide from the model instead, and restore the full-value rewrite assertion.

fix(router): pin /v1/responses requests for prompt caching affinity (#50321)

* fix(router): pin /v1/responses requests for prompt caching affinity

* fix(router): pin previous_response_id turns and keep native tools in the Responses pin key

A Responses turn that continues a stored response now goes to the deployment
that answered it, unless that deployment already failed this request. Native
Responses tools are hashed into the pin key as sent instead of converted, so
two requests with different native tools no longer share a pin and a native
request no longer logs a false dropped-tool warning. The pin keeps its
cacheable deployment ids in a sorted tuple so loggers can serialize request
metadata.

* fix(router): leave a Responses request with a malformed tool to the provider

* fix(router): keep the Responses prompt cache pin out of logged metadata

The pre-call check now keeps the pin in a router-owned in-flight store and
puts only a random token in litellm_metadata, so loggers that ship metadata
never see the routing key or deployment ids. The store is shared across check
instances, so turning prompt_caching off and on at runtime keeps pinning, and
a retry drops its previous attempt's token. The skipped-input debug log now
names only the error type.

* fix(router): apply the prompt caching pin after tag, region and pre-call filters, and leave it on retries

The prompt caching check no longer narrows the candidates inside the callback
filters. It names the deployment it prefers, and the router core applies that
preference at the pinned deployment step, after tag, region, pre-call and plugin
filters, only when the deployment is still a candidate. A pin can no longer
send a request to a deployment its tags do not allow.

A retry skips the pin when the pinned deployment was already tried in this
request, read from the retry breadcrumbs in both metadata buckets and the
excluded and retry-skipped ids. When the retry count outruns the breadcrumbs
the check stands down, so a pinned deployment that keeps failing is not
retried on every attempt.

* test(router): list the prompt caching check as an in-memory cache caller

The check's in-flight Responses pins live in a process-local InMemoryCache, so it opens no Redis span and needs no key family, like the other in-memory callers

* fix(router): pin a lone healthy deployment, free every in-flight Responses pin, and clear a reused metadata dict's retry records

* test(router): lift test cooldowns through the cooldown store's evict_local

* fix(router): key Responses tools like their chat twin and drop the pin token after success

A Responses function tool now hashes only the function fields it sent, so a chat request and a Responses request with the same tool share one pin. The success event also removes the pin token from the caller's metadata dict.

* test(router): cover untyped tool parameters and custom tool grammars in the Responses pin key

fix(router): count embedding batches per input in pre-call checks (#49851)

* fix(router): count embedding batches per input in pre-call checks

Embedding input lists went through the Responses input transform, which
calls .get() on each item, so every list-input /embeddings call logged
"failed to count tokens" and skipped the context window check. Lists of
texts, token IDs or token ID lists now count as their longest input,
since an embedding model's context window applies to each input on its
own

* fix(router): keep empty and boolean input lists on the Responses count path

An empty list carries no embedding evidence, and counting it as a zero
token batch skipped the instructions and tools of an empty Responses
input. Boolean lists are not token IDs

* fix(router): honor disable_token_counter for token ID embedding input

Text inputs already counted as zero through token_counter when token
counting is disabled, while token ID inputs were still measured by
length and could be rejected. The router reads the flag through its
dynamic config like its other process settings

* refactor(router): type the embedding count helper with a read-only sequence and final locals

* fix(router): count embedding batches per input on the media-free text projection

The per-input count now runs on the text projection from the embedding
media split, so data URIs a deployment embeds as media keep the media
path and only text items are checked against the context window. A
caption next to an image is checked on its own, and a text-only
deployment still counts an image data URI as text

* fix(router): keep embedding images out of the pre-call count only on image backends, and skip tokenizing inputs that fit by bytes

Media leaves the embedding count only when every deployment in the group declares image embedding input, so a text-only backend still counts a data URI as text and an image backend outside the TPM media list no longer gets a false 400. A text no longer than the smallest window in UTF-8 bytes counts as its byte length without the tokenizer, since a token is never shorter than a byte.

* fix(router): keep embedding images out of the pre-call count when any backend in the group embeds images

Mark Cohere embed-english-light-v3.0 as embedding images, as its v3 siblings are.

* fix(router): check embedding text batches only with an exact OpenAI tokenizer

litellm's default tokenizer counts non-English text several times higher than
non-OpenAI embedding providers do, so counting batches with it refused inputs
the provider accepts. Text batches on those groups now stay unchecked as at the
merge base, without the error log. Main's per-provider media split and the
cost map are restored, so strings and embedding media keep main's path.

* fix(router): count long embedding batches in slices so chat counts do not wait behind them

A text batch is now tokenized in slices of 65,536 characters, each its own offloaded call, so the FIFO count limiter can serve a chat count between slices. The no-OpenAI-tokenizer rule for text lists moved into the pre-call check, so RoutingContext.count_pre_call_check_tokens counts a text list by its longest text.

* fix(router): read embedding media off the event loop and wait on the count limiter in the fairness test

feat(proxy): mixed Codex model picker and LiteLLM routing on native codex routes (#49408)

* feat(proxy): mixed Codex model picker and LiteLLM routing on native codex routes

The native Codex catalog now lists the key's other chat and responses models after
ChatGPT's, within Codex's catalog size limit, and drops the ETag so the merged list
refreshes on Codex's timer. A request for a model configured by exact name on another
provider goes through /v1/responses without the ChatGPT bearer or account header,
while ChatGPT names and wildcard-only matches keep the subscription passthrough.
Reasoning items another provider produced are dropped before forwarding to ChatGPT.

* fix(proxy): keep Codex's picker from turning reasoning off for LiteLLM models

Codex fills a missing default_reasoning_level with effort "none" when a model is picked in /model, while
`codex -m <model>` sends no effort at all. A thinking-only provider model then answers 400. On the native
/backend-api/codex/responses route, drop effort "none" for a LiteLLM model whose catalog entry names no
default, so the provider applies its own default exactly as `codex -m` does

* fix(proxy): harden Codex mixed-model routing on the native ChatGPT routes

Keep the ChatGPT credentials out of hook raw headers on the inner /v1/responses
request, route to LiteLLM and merge LiteLLM catalog rows only for keys that may
call /v1/responses, drop unpersisted reasoning ids on the passthrough when store
is not true, keep any slug the caller's ChatGPT account lists on the subscription
via a shared account catalog cache, and keep X-Models-Etag for keys whose catalog
added no LiteLLM rows. The guide covers the new behavior and the /v1 wildcard
precedence over a catch-all deployment.

* fix(proxy): keep Codex's native route on the subscription when the account list is unknown

A name OpenAI lists for the caller's ChatGPT account now goes to LiteLLM only when the
account's list is known and leaves it out. A failed catalog read is remembered for 60 s and
the Codex version comes only from a User-Agent whose product matches the originator header.

The merged catalog serves a stable ETag digest of OpenAI's ETag and the key's LiteLLM rows,
and /responses replaces X-Models-Etag with the same value, memoized per key for 300 s, so
Codex stops refetching or dropping its catalog cache.

LiteLLM-routed native replies wrap their reasoning with the model id, so an OpenAI or Azure
blob is dropped before chatgpt.com and unwrapped for LiteLLM, and the chat-completions bridge
decodes wrapped thinking blocks with their signature.

The access-group recipe uses chatgpt/ model names so /v1 routing does not change, and the
native route checks the chatgpt/ form of a name the key holds only through that group. A
none reasoning effort is dropped only under drop_params. The guide covers app tools, every
routing case, and the ETag, and the catalog logs how many models the byte limit left out.

* fix(fireworks_ai): move Codex additional_tools items into tools on the Responses API

* fix(proxy): keep Codex native turns working when the key's model listing fails

A listing callback that raises no longer turns chatgpt.com's catalog or
responses answer into a 500. The catalog keeps upstream's body and ETag, and
responses keep upstream's X-Models-Etag.

Under drop_params, a `none` reasoning effort is now dropped only when a
candidate deployment does not explicitly support it, so an alias to a model
like openai/gpt-5.4 keeps it.

The account slug list and its unavailable marker are keyed on the account id
plus the caller's ChatGPT Authorization header, so a failed fetch with one
bearer cannot turn off LiteLLM routing for another caller on the same account.

The auth step checks the Codex route before importing the Codex module.

* fix(proxy): keep Codex model switches working across LiteLLM providers

On the Codex native route, a LiteLLM model now gets only the encrypted reasoning every deployment it can route to is able to decrypt, so ChatGPT or another deployment's blobs no longer make xAI answer 400

Codex additional_tools items are hoisted into tools for every provider except the OpenAI API, and namespace tools become flat tools named mcp__docs__search, the shape xAI accepts

A JWT caller's models ETag is cached on a hash of its LiteLLM credential, so ChatGPT turns stop rebuilding the catalog rows

* fix(proxy): keep Codex namespace tool calls intact across LiteLLM providers

Fireworks and Bedrock Mantle accept Codex namespace tools natively, so the
native route now hoists them without flattening, like OpenAI and Azure and
the chat completions bridge. Other native Responses providers still get
flat names, now built with the bridge's namespace_tool_name_map, and each
function_call they return gets its tool name and namespace back in the
non-streaming body and in streamed output_item.added, output_item.done,
and completed/incomplete/failed events. Every other event passes through
unchanged

* fix(proxy): bridge Codex turns for providers whose Responses API rejects Codex tools

Codex sends its freeform exec tool as a custom tool on every turn, and xAI's
Responses API answers 422 for custom, namespace and additional_tools shapes.
On the Codex native route, a model whose deployments include a native
Responses provider other than OpenAI, Azure, Fireworks or Bedrock Mantle now
asks for the chat completions bridge with use_chat_completions_api, which
already turns custom and namespace tools into functions, hoists
additional_tools, and puts the namespace back on each returned call

OpenAI and Azure still get the request unchanged, and Fireworks and Bedrock
Mantle still get it on their own Responses API with additional_tools hoisted.
The route's namespace flattening and the response-side namespace restore are
removed, since no path sends flattened names anymore

* fix(proxy): drop reasoning ids a Codex turn's LiteLLM target cannot resolve

A reasoning item another deployment produced, replayed with store false and no blob the
target can decrypt, now reaches the target as its readable summary without id or status,
and is dropped when nothing readable is left. OpenAI answered 400 on the status field and
404 on the id for a glm-5p3 item replayed whole to an openai deployment. Same-deployment
replays and stored conversations keep the item whole

* refactor(codex): reach encrypted reasoning stripping through the router registry

The Codex route read Router.optional_callbacks and imported EncryptedContentAffinityCheck from
litellm.router_utils, which the router surface fence forbids outside the router. RouterRegistry
gains decryptable_reasoning(model_group, request_input, targets), which keeps the same rule: with
encrypted content affinity on for the group, reasoning one target can decrypt stays, otherwise
every target must decrypt it

* fix(proxy): keep Codex's priority tier off LiteLLM rows in the native model catalog

* fix(proxy): drop Codex's none effort for an alias whose native entry names no default

* fix(proxy): start a native Codex alias at its pinned reasoning effort and build the catalog off the event loop

* test(proxy): map the pinned reasoning efforts field in the router registry stub

* fix(proxy): honor admin-only /v1/responses and keep Codex's default tier off native aliases

Codex native routes now send a key to LiteLLM only when admin_only_routes allows it,
a native alias with configured service tiers starts with no tier picked, and the
account slug cache declares its Redis key family.

* fix(proxy): check the key's tool allowlist on native Codex LiteLLM turns and additional_tools items

* fix(proxy): check vector store grants on file_search tools inside additional_tools items

A Responses request can define file_search inside an additional_tools input item, which the native Codex route hoists for LiteLLM-served models and OpenAI runs as is on /v1/responses. The vector store check now reads those tools in both strict and legacy modes. The input item scan uses a Mapping guard instead of a pydantic error per item, since auth now runs it on every list input.

* fix(proxy): apply the proxy-wide allowed_routes to LiteLLM models on native Codex routes

* fix(proxy): cap native Codex account catalog reads per LiteLLM caller before rate limits apply

* fix(guardrails): check additional_tools items next to top-level function tools in tool_policy

ToolPolicyGuardrail read tools from the request body only when no top-level
function tool existed, so a blocked tool defined in an additional_tools item
reached Fireworks once the Responses transform moved the item into tools after
the pre-call hooks. Check every list on each request, including namespace
members inside items.

* fix(router): serve decryptable_reasoning from the Rust core's optional checks

The merge with main removed the Python router core, so the registry's host has no
optional_callbacks and no routing context, and native Codex requests with encrypted
reasoning raised RustCoreUnsupported. The filter now lives with the optional checks,
which own both. The ported pinned_reasoning_efforts field gets a test on the Rust core

Also give the static litellm.Router a declared constructor. Since the Python core was
deleted a bare __init__ assignment reads as RustCore's, so every Router(model_list=...)
is a type error and make lint fails on main. TYPE_CHECKING only, no runtime change

* fix(proxy): check the budget of a saved alias target on native Codex LiteLLM turns

Native /backend-api/codex/responses binds {endpoint}, so auth skipped the key's or team's model_group_alias and read budgets on the requested name, while the later /v1/responses handoff served the target unchecked. Auth now resolves the alias on a turn that routes to LiteLLM, as it does on /v1, and leaves ChatGPT-only names on the subscription. Also makes the tool_policy tests build a real ToolPolicyRegistry and type their fixtures.

* fix(proxy): keep a name the ChatGPT account lists on the subscription despite a saved alias

* fix(codex): keep LiteLLM keys off ChatGPT, enforce tool policy on namespaces and pin reasoning on aliases

Auth no longer asks ChatGPT for the account's model list when the bearer is
missing or is the LiteLLM key, so a key sent as the bearer never reaches it.

tool_policy now reads the members of a top-level namespace, which is where
the native route's hoist puts them.

A global alias now reads encrypted content affinity from its target group.

A non-list top-level tools value and a non-string function name now reach the
provider, which refuses them, instead of raising a 500.

The catalog ETag no longer depends on the order a process iterates priced
service tiers in, so workers and pods agree on it.

* fix(proxy): list a team's models in the order the team set them

get_team_models built the names in a set, so each process listed a team key's models in its own hash order and the native Codex catalog sent a different row order and ETag from each worker

* fix(proxy): apply JWT route policy before native Codex routes serve LiteLLM models

A standard JWT caller now gets a LiteLLM model on /backend-api/codex/models
and /backend-api/codex/responses only when the JWT auth flow would admit a
direct /v1/responses call for that model, so team_allowed_routes,
admin_allowed_routes and RBAC route limits hold on the handoff too.

The Fireworks Responses transform also leaves additional_tools input items
in place when the tools param is not a list, instead of raising while hoisting

* fix(fireworks): hoist additional_tools when tools is a tuple

litellm.responses passes a tuple tools argument through to the Fireworks
transform unchanged, so the non-list guard skipped hoisting and left the
additional_tools item in the input. Treat tuples like lists and cover both
shapes in the drop_params merge test

fix(responses): map streamed flex_unavailable errors to 429 not 500 (#50336)

* fix(responses): map streamed flex_unavailable errors to 429 not 500

When OpenAI has no flex capacity, a service_tier flex request fails with type
resource_unavailable / code flex_unavailable. Non-streamed, this arrives as HTTP
429 and litellm raises RateLimitError. Streamed /v1/responses delivers the same
error as an in-stream event, and neither field was in _ERROR_CODE_HTTP_STATUS, so
it defaulted to 500 InternalServerError.

The HTTP status then depended only on stream: one provider outage looked like a
429 or a 500. The 500 reads as a server error in metrics and alerting, and callers
that retry on 429 do not retry it.

Map both resource_unavailable and flex_unavailable to 429 so the streamed path
matches the non-streamed path.

Fixes #49736

* test(responses): cover streamed flex outage end to end for error and response.failed events

Streams the flex_unavailable payload from #49736 through litellm.aresponses with an injected client and asserts a 429 RateLimitError for both in-stream event kinds, matching the non-streamed path

* test(responses): drop explanatory comment from flex status mapping test

* test(integration): cover streamed flex outage status on responses and chat bridge

Drives the flex_unavailable payload from #49736 through a real proxy as an in-stream error event and as response.failed. The native /v1/responses stream fails with rate_limit_exceeded and logs 429, and the chat bridge answers a 429 throttling error, where both reported a 500 before the mapping fix

fix(chatgpt): forward text and max_output_tokens to the Codex backend (#38086)

* fix(chatgpt): keep text and accept string input for the Codex backend

Two request-side defects stop chatgpt/* serving structured output or a string
input.

The allowlist at the end of transform_responses_api_request omits "text". The
chat-to-responses bridge translates response_format into text.format, so the
allowlist discards strict schemas silently and the backend answers with prose
instead of JSON. The backend does honour text.format when it receives it.

Separately the backend rejects a bare string input with
{"detail": "Input must be a list"}, while the Responses API itself accepts
either shape, so the string needs wrapping before it is sent.

Both are request-shaping only, so neither depends on the streaming work in
#31332 or #34095, though those two block the same call and have to be in place
to observe this one end to end.

The "text" case was reported in #24356 and closed by the stale bot without a
fix.

Signed-off-by: Alexander Chernov <alexander@chernov.it>

* fix(chatgpt): annotate the input coercion for the type-discipline gate

The LIT002 budget counts mutable-collection construction, and wrapping the
string input builds a list and a dict, which put the total two over its
ceiling. Both constructions are the wire payload this backend requires, so the
list cannot be replaced with an immutable equivalent; annotate the line with a
reason instead, matching the convention used elsewhere in the tree.

LIT005 freezes reasonless suppressions at zero, so the reason is required
rather than decorative.

Signed-off-by: Alexander Chernov <alexander@chernov.it>

* refactor(chatgpt): bind the coerced input instead of rebinding the parameter

Greptile flagged the parameter rebinding and the explanatory comments against
the repo conventions in CLAUDE.md, which bans rebinding a function parameter
(LIT011) and keeps comments to suppressions, TODOs and genuinely complex logic

Bind a Final local for the coerced input rather than reassigning `input`, and
drop both prose comments; the rationale lives in the commit and the PR body
rather than duplicated at the call site. The mutable-ok suppression stays,
since it is the allowed kind and the list is still constructed

Behaviour is unchanged: 24 tests pass, and the same 4 fail with only the
provider file reverted to base

Signed-off-by: Alexander Chernov <alexander@chernov.it>

* fix(chatgpt): forward max_output_tokens to the Codex backend and return incomplete non-stream responses

The Codex backend accepts and enforces max_output_tokens, so the allowlist now keeps it
instead of dropping it. A structured-output request could otherwise stream until the
backend gave up, ignoring the caller's max_tokens.

A capped request ends with response.incomplete, so the non-stream SSE aggregator now
treats that event as terminal and returns the partial response instead of an error.
