fix(anthropic)!: do not surface server_tool_use as client tool_calls (#48385)

* fix(anthropic): do not surface server_tool_use as client tool_calls

Anthropic server-executed tools (web search, tool search, code execution)
were returned in chat completions tool_calls with srvtoolu_ ids, so
OpenAI-protocol agent clients treated them as pending work and re-invoked
the model until their recursion limit.

Move them to provider_specific_fields.server_tool_calls on both the
non-streaming and streaming paths. History replay, the /v1/responses
bridge and the /v1/messages streaming guardrail read that field, so
multi-turn reconstruction, web_search_call output items and the
guardrail's fail-closed check on server tool blocks keep working.

* fix(responses): return Claude web_fetch calls as web_search_call open_page items

* fix(responses): keep Claude server web calls without a result as hosted items

A non-streamed Claude turn that calls web_search or web_fetch next to a
client tool can return the server call before its result. Build an
in_progress web_search_call for it, so the Responses bridge no longer
returns it as a client function_call

* fix(anthropic): keep pending server calls native and hide server calls from client tool paths

Replaying a server call that has no result yet now sends it back as
server_tool_use, so Anthropic accepts the next turn. The tool permission
guardrail checks server calls again and rewrite mode removes a denied one.
The /v1/messages adapter keeps Claude's server blocks, and the Responses
bridge never returns a server call as a client function_call.

* fix(anthropic): let guardrails, tool usage, tracing, and Responses replay see Claude's server calls

Claude's server tool calls moved out of tool_calls into provider_specific_fields.server_tool_calls,
so every reader of tool_calls stopped seeing them. The chat guardrail handler now passes them to
output guardrails and writes rewrites back to server_tool_calls (stream and non-stream), tool usage
and registry discovery count them, otel, Datadog and the Logs Tools panel list them, and a pending
Claude web search or fetch item replayed to /v1/responses goes back to Anthropic as its own
server_tool_use instead of running again

* fix(anthropic): let guardrails and loggers read Claude's server tool calls again

Guardrails, tool policies, tracing loggers and the Responses guardrail
translation read only client tool calls after server calls moved to
provider_specific_fields. They now read server calls first, then client
calls, through one shared helper, and the Responses guardrail treats
Claude's web_search_call items as web_search or web_fetch calls.
Non-streaming splits server calls by block type, as streaming does.

* fix(anthropic): keep Claude server calls visible to guardrails, redaction and tracing

A guardrail rewrite of a Claude server call now also updates its hosted web_search_calls copy,
streamed or not. Redaction with message logging off hides server call arguments and hosted web
call actions on chat and Responses. Pillar and Pangea scan server calls, transform-mode streaming
guardrails keep server call chunks, and OTEL v2 Responses spans list Claude's web calls.

* fix(anthropic): keep the legacy hook view of streamed /v1/messages web search after the main merge

Main's legacy post-call hooks see Claude's server call as tool_use with its search results first. The streamed /v1/messages response now keeps that view while native scans keep server_tool_use.

* fix(guardrails): let Cisco AI Defense scan Claude's web calls on Responses

Claude's web search and fetch now come back from /v1/responses as web_search_call items, so Cisco AI Defense reads and clears their query or URL the way it did for the old function_call arguments. The helpers that read and rewrite those items move to the shared guardrail utils so the Responses guardrail handler and Cisco use one copy.

* test(guardrails): inject Pillar's HTTP client and type the Cisco web call actions

* test(guardrails): type the fake Pillar client like its Protocol

* fix(anthropic): keep a pending server call and its thinking when the turn also waits on a client tool

Only a turn with no client tool_use is a paused turn. A tool_use turn that also started web_fetch or
web_search still needs that call and its thinking replayed, or Claude loses the fetch result

* fix(guardrails): scan replayed Claude server calls and hosted web calls

Request guardrails now see and rewrite server_tool_calls replayed in chat
messages. Cato and Purview scan Claude web_search and web_fetch calls on
Responses output, and a function tool call with an extra custom key is no

* fix(anthropic): apply streamed guardrail tool call rewrites to their own block when a server tool call follows

* test: type the new guardrail test helpers with litellm's tool call types instead of Any

* test: narrow the remaining new test helper parameters from bare dict and object

* fix(anthropic): keep server calls in Responses streams, guardrail masks, OTEL and Logs

Streamed /v1/responses now emits Claude's tool search and paused web search calls, text guardrail masks rewrite replayed server calls, OTEL gen_ai messages and the Logs pretty view list server calls next to client calls, and integration tests read server calls from server_tool_calls

feat(proxy): hash UI passwords with PBKDF2 in FIPS mode (#49874)

* feat(proxy): hash UI passwords with PBKDF2 in FIPS mode

A FIPS OpenSSL refuses scrypt, so every password write fails there and
nobody can sign in with a password. When OpenSSL enforces FIPS, passwords
now use PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 at 600k iterations with a salt from OpenSSL's
DRBG, stored as "pbkdf2:" plus base64 of salt and key. Any other row is
refused with one error log and left as it is, and the boot migration does
nothing, because FIPS mode is for new deployments.

PBKDF2 at 600k takes about five times as long as scrypt, so in FIPS mode the
five request paths run it on one thread instead of the event loop. A single
thread keeps a login burst from using up a CPU quota, which is what stalls
the loop with asyncio.to_thread. A login that queued for that thread asks the
throttle again before it answers, so a burst of guesses can't get past a block
that the failures ahead of it just set.

The breached password check is off in FIPS mode, because it runs the
password through SHA-1.

A standard OpenSSL reads False at every new branch, so standard mode keeps
scrypt, inline, on the same rows.

Resolves LIT-8425

* fix(proxy): take FIPS logins one at a time and recheck the throttle first

A login that waited for the KDF thread asked the throttle again only after
deriving, so a burst for one user kept that thread busy long after the user
was blocked. Logins now wait for their turn on a lock and ask the throttle
when it comes, so a blocked login costs no PBKDF2 and only one login at a time
holds a place in the KDF queue. Password changes and invite claims no longer
wait behind a whole burst of logins.

* fix(proxy): keep PBKDF2 rows on a standard boot and warn when FIPS skips the breach check

A standard boot treated a pbkdf2: row as plaintext and hashed its text, so the
real password stopped working and the old row text signed in. The migration now
leaves a row of that exact shape alone. Any other pbkdf2: text still migrates.

FIPS mode now logs a warning when it skips a breach check that is turned on.

The one-thread test no longer depends on timing, and the new test variables are
annotated Final.

* fix(proxy): keep the breached password check on in FIPS mode

* fix(proxy): choose the password KDF from fips_mode instead of the host OpenSSL

* test(proxy): fake the scrypt probe in the FIPS fixture now that the gate checks scrypt

fix(bedrock): forward the per-turn-control beta to Bedrock Invoke (#43086)

* fix(bedrock): forward the per-turn-control beta to Bedrock Invoke

Claude Code sends `anthropic-beta: per-turn-control-2026-07-01` together
with a mid-conversation `role: system` message carrying a message-level
`output_config` (for example an effort change). The beta header config
mapped the beta to null for `bedrock`, so LiteLLM dropped it while
keeping the message in place on models flagged
`supports_mid_conversation_system`, and Bedrock Invoke rejected the turn
with "messages.N.output_config: Extra inputs are not permitted".

Direct Bedrock InvokeModel probes with a synthetic request show Claude
Opus 5.5 accepts that message shape only with this beta, and that Claude
Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 4.6, Opus 4.8, Opus 5, and Sonnet 5 accept the beta on
a plain request, so map it to itself for `bedrock`. `bedrock_converse`
is unchanged.

* fix(rust): allow the per-turn-control beta on bedrock in the Rust beta table

The Rust table must match litellm/anthropic_beta_headers_config.json cell for cell, and the JSON now maps the beta for bedrock. Also type the new Bedrock Invoke test.

* fix(bedrock): forward per-turn-control on Bedrock Invoke only where the cost map flags the model

Bedrock InvokeModel accepts per-turn-control-2026-07-01 on Claude 4.5 and newer and answers 400 invalid beta flag
on Claude 3 Haiku. Released proxies load the beta map from main, so forwarding it in the bedrock row would turn
Claude 3 Haiku requests on every running release from 200 into 400. Keep that row null and forward the client's
beta from the Invoke transformation when a new claude-per-turn-control cost map rule sets supports_per_turn_control.

* fix(bedrock): keep the per-turn-control beta through the messages handler filter on Bedrock Invoke

The /v1/messages handler filtered client betas against the beta map before the
Bedrock Invoke config could add per-turn-control back for models the cost map
flags, so the beta never reached Bedrock. Provider configs now name betas their
model accepts beyond the beta map, and the handler filter keeps those

* fix(bedrock): keep a deployment's per-turn-control flag on that deployment

supports_per_turn_control is now deployment-scoped, so a deployment's opt-in or opt-out no longer changes the beta forward for other deployments of the same Bedrock model. The forward reads the deployment's own model_info first, then the model map.

This uses the SDK's existing convention for background reads (`getSessionTurn`'s `showErrors: false`, `useProjectSession`). - **The rest of the pattern:** the 3 `POST /sessions` 500s were a `kortix.yaml` parse error, already fixed by #11641, which prod v0.15.0 carries. fix(kortixd): Claude Code sessions no longer break at Anthropic's 32 MB request cap (#11943) ## Summary A Claude subscription session (`claude-agent/*`) that reads screenshots no longer breaks for good at Anthropic's 32 MB request cap. Claude Code puts every image a tool returned inside a `tool_result` block and resends them all on every step. The sandbox LLM proxy's image window read only top-level content parts, so it counted none of them. With the real `claude` binary, the request grew by ~4.8 MB per 15 screenshot reads. After ~100 reads it passed 32 MB, and every later turn of that session failed with "Request too large (max 32MB)". Claude Code resends its history, so only a new session recovered. Now the proxy window counts images nested in `tool_result` and in Responses `function_call_output`. feat(agents): every agent gets its session ids; a subagent reads its parent's conversation (#11940)

## Summary

A subagent used to start from its parent's written summary alone ("Write
a complete prompt: the subagent sees nothing of this conversation").
That summary is lossy, and the subagent guessed the rest. Now every
agent's system prompt names its ids (`session_id`, `project_id`,
`parent_session_id`, `space_id`) and the command that reads any of them:
`kortix sessions log <session_id> -n 50`. A subagent reads its parent's
conversation itself when the brief leaves something out. The API now
lets a session read every session up its spawn chain, read-only.

## Demo

No UI. The proof is a real parent → child run on the local stack, with
real Platinum boxes:

1. The parent session holds the code word `HERON-7319`. It starts a
separate subagent whose prompt does not contain the word.
2. In the child box: `echo $KORTIX_PARENT_SESSION_ID` printed the
parent's id, and `kortix sessions log $KORTIX_PARENT_SESSION_ID -n 5`
printed the parent's conversation. The child reported `HERON-7319`.
3. Second run: the parent was made another user's private session before
the child read it. `kortix sessions log $KORTIX_PARENT_SESSION_ID` →
`parent_exit=0`. `kortix sessions log <an unrelated private session>` →
`unrelated_exit=1`, "not found in any project you can access".

## What is affected

- **Every pi agent** (root, separate subagent, in-session subagent,
workflow agent): a new `## Session ids` section in the system prompt.
The ids are fixed for a session, so the prompt cache is unchanged.
- **The `agent` tool and `workflow` text:** "write the task and the
facts it depends on; the subagent reads this conversation with `kortix
sessions log` when your prompt leaves something out; never paste the
conversation". A fork is told how to read what its parent says after the
fork.
- **Box env:** new `KORTIX_PARENT_SESSION_ID` (the `parent_session_id`
column, else `metadata.spawned_by_session`), set on every (re)provision.
- **Session read access (IAM):** a session-bound credential now reads
the sessions that spawned its session, at any depth up to 8, on two read
routes only: `GET …/sessions/:id` and `GET …/sessions/:id/log`
(`spawnAncestorRead`). It gets reader standing only (`isOwner: false`,
no lifecycle or sharing rights). Every other route still answers `404`,
so a child cannot prompt its parent or answer the parent's permission
requests. Only the server-written spawn link
(`metadata.spawned_by_session`) counts. A person-set `parent_session_id`
grants nothing. Hidden private channels still hide.
- **CLI `kortix sessions log`:** when the box refuses the live read
(`403`, a child reading its parent), the fallback note now says "the
live turn is not open to this credential" instead of "its sandbox is not
answering".
- **Not affected:** migrations, billing, the daemon port gate (a child
still cannot open its parent's box: the live read stays `403`), human
access rules, mobile, desktop.

## Verification

| Check | Result | What it proves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pnpm test -- --db-only integration-session-ancestor-read` (new, 7
tests) | PASS | child reads its private parent (another user's) as
reader, not owner; a write route never sees the parent; grandchild reads
up the chain; sibling stays hidden; a person-set `parent_session_id`
grants nothing; parent still owns child; a human who cannot see the
parent still cannot |
| Same suite with `isSpawnAncestor` forced to `false` | FAIL (2 tests) |
the tests catch the missing rule |
| `bun test src/__tests__/pi-harness.test.ts` (kortixd) | 241 pass |
incl. new test: root prompt carries session/project/parent/space ids; an
in-session subagent names the main conversation as parent |
| `pi-cloud-subagent.test.ts`, `pi-team-tasks.test.ts` | 60 + 8 pass |
subagent spawn bodies unchanged |
| `tsgo` api, kortixd, cli; `eslint` on changed API files | 0 errors | |
| Local e2e, real boxes (Demo steps 1–3) | PASS | env var reaches the
box; the read works for another user's private parent; an unrelated
private session stays `not found` |
| `curl` as the child's session token, parent = another user's private
session | PASS | `GET …/sessions/<parent>` `200`, `GET …/<parent>/log`
`200`, `POST …/<parent>/prompts` `404`, `GET …/<parent>/prompts` `404`;
another user's unrelated private session `404` |

The system-prompt section runs in a box only after deploy: cloud boxes
run the released kortixd. It is covered by the harness test locally, and
I check it on dev after the deploy.

## Risks and rollback

- The new read path runs one memoized recursive query (60 s TTL) only
when the ordinary rules refuse a row to a session token. Human requests
never run it.
- A subagent can now read its parent's whole conversation. The parent
chose to start it, and the child already acts within the same project
for the same person, so I judged this inside the existing trust
boundary.
- Rollback: revert this PR. No data or schema changes.

to create session`, and the infra sweep filed it.

The window is expected and ends by itself, so it is not an error to page
on. This PR makes it a typed, retryable outcome on both sides, following
the existing pattern for expected 503s (`request_deadline`,
`git_mirror_unavailable`): the API answers `503 deploy_in_progress` with
`Retry-After`, and `handleApiError` toasts it without capturing it. The
next not-mixed-version-safe migration hits old tasks that carry this
code, so they answer the typed 503.

I chose this reading after the first attempt blocked as "no code defect"
and intake said to decide: the playbook asks for a typed, non-paging
outcome for an expected state instead of no change. I did not change the
migration policy (expand/contract): that is the owner's decision.

fix(api): lifecycle status writes are compare-and-set; stale webhooks never undo newer billing state (#11932)

## Summary

Fifteen lifecycle status writers read a row, checked its status in code,
then wrote `UPDATE … WHERE id = ?`. A concurrent writer in that gap was
overwritten: a cancelled account deletion kept running, a merged change
request read `closed`, a deleted session's box came back `active`, a
revoked connector account came back `active`. This PR makes each of them
one compare-and-set transition (`WHERE status IN (allowed from)`, 0 rows
= lost race, answered as 409 or a no-op). It also fixes the Stripe,
RevenueCat, Enterprise and invite writers that let an old or late event
undo newer state, adds `NOT VALID` CHECKs to nine status columns that
accepted any string, and adds a lint rule so a blind status write cannot
come back.

## Demo

No user-visible screen changes: every fix is an API status write. The
terminal run of the real routes against the worktree stack is in
Verification.

## What is affected

- **Sessions and sandboxes (preview proxy, every proxied request).**
Traffic no longer moves a session into `running`: a session parked after
a turn error, a failed session, a provisioning session and a deleted
session keep their status. The proxy heal of a `stopped`/`error` box
never revives a row a delete archived or a restart claimed. "Mark
errored" applies only to an `active` row.
- **Change requests.** Close and reopen answer `409` when a merge
committed first; the request stays `merged`. A merge that raced a close
is recorded as merged (the code is on the base branch).
- **Project access requests.** Approve claims the request before it
grants the role. An approve and a reject that race: one wins, the loser
answers `409` and grants nothing.
- **Review items (web, Slack, Teams, bulk).** A verdict decides an open
item once. A second verdict answers `409` (web), "was already decided"
(Slack/Teams), or `already_resolved` (bulk). `acted_by` and `feedback`
keep the first decider.
- **Kortix Capture.** An admin's deny sticks against a racing enroll
call: no device token is minted for a denied computer.
- **Connector accounts.** A revoke records `revokedAt` and expires the
account's pending OAuth sessions. An in-flight OAuth callback, device
poll or Composio finalize that started before the revoke stores nothing
(`connection_revoked`). A sign-in a person starts after the revoke, a
pasted credential, a restore and a machine pairing still reconnect.
- **Apps.** `deleted` is terminal for a runtime. The idle reaper's final
`stopped` lands only on its own `stopping` claim, so a wake that started
the box meanwhile wins. A wake lease never takes a `stopping` row; it
waits for the stop, then wakes.
- **Provider transitions.** Cancel and supersede bump `lease_epoch`, so
the runner still driving the row can no longer write `building`/`ready`
over the terminal state.
- **Account deletion.** A cancel after the worker claimed the request
answers `409 "Account deletion is already running and can no longer be
cancelled"` (was: success, or `400`). Immediate deletion claims the
request first. Closure cancels every live Stripe subscription of every
customer of the account (Enterprise contract subscriptions included) and
ends the active contract. `payment_status = 'deleted'` is terminal
inside the SQL statement: the closure's own
`customer.subscription.deleted` no longer sets it back to `active`.
- **Stripe webhooks.** A subscription event re-reads the live
subscription before it writes, so event order no longer matters (one
extra `subscriptions.retrieve` per event). `invoice.payment_failed` runs
under the account lock and ignores a subscription that is not the
account's current one. A late `checkout.session.completed` for an ended
subscription activates nothing and does not turn auto top-up back on.
- **RevenueCat.** Expiration and the other downgrade events are ignored
for a Stripe-billed account, a closed account, another product, or an
expiration older than the last grant.
- **Enterprise.** Creating an offer while a contract is active is
refused for every collection mode. Withdrawing an offer expires its open
Checkout sessions (a paid one blocks the withdraw with `409`). Contract
status and `enterprise_entitled` are written in one transaction.
- **Invites.** Re-accepting an accepted invite applies nothing
(`already_accepted: true`): no roles, no SCIM groups. An expired invite
is refused before any grant.
- **Database.** Migration `20261106140140429_lifecycle_status_checks`:
nine `NOT VALID` CHECKs (`account_deletion_requests.status`,
`credit_accounts.payment_status` / `trial_status`,
`project_trigger_executions.status` / `run_status`,
`project_snapshot_archives.status`, `project_git_connections.status`,
`chat_thread_participants.status`, `cli_device_grants.status`). Each set
is every value a writer in the repo writes plus every value a live row
holds on dev, staging and prod (read-only `GROUP BY` probe), so an old
row stays updatable. Catalog-only; no table scan.
- **Not affected:** no new status value, no enum change, no route added
or removed, no SDK or web change, no kortixd change.
`stripe_subscription_status` gets no CHECK (Stripe owns that set and
adds to it).

## Verification

All on the branch tree (merged with `dev` at `80b383ff97`), worktree
stack `state-guarded-writes`.

| Real routes, worktree stack: `POST /v1/account/cancel-deletion` after

## Risks and rollback

Every resize restarts the stream and sends each viewer a new `hello`, and each viewer answers with its own size again. Two viewers of different sizes therefore resize the desktop back and forth. Every round shows a black frame until the next keyframe. - **Fix:** a patch to voxl (`apps/sandbox/voxl/size-owner.patch`) lets one viewer size the desktop: - The first viewer to ask owns the size. - A viewer that acts on the desktop (pointer, click, scroll, key) takes it over. - When the owner leaves, the next viewer that asked takes it. - The other viewers watch the desktop scaled. - **Release:** the binary ships as prerelease `voxl-47bb94ec4d25-kortix.3`. - **Upstream:** the same change is proposed as tembo/voxl#86. Linear: KRTX-4362. ## Demo No video: a recording of a black flash once a second shows the symptom, not the fix. feat(goals): goal state moves to the API; only a verifier can mark done (#11910) ## Summary This PR moves a goal's state from the agent-writable front matter of `GOAL.md` into two new API tables, `project_goals` and `project_goal_events`, and adds `/v1/projects/:projectId/goals` routes that own every state change. A person pauses, resumes, stops, restarts and answers a goal. The goal's owner session activates it, waits on a question, reports progress, requests verification and hands over. Only the goal's current verifier session, which never owned it, marks it `done`, with one result per criterion. Every goal heartbeat passes an admission check (flag, pause, state, daily wake cap, credits) before a turn starts, and a leader-only reconciler job repairs heartbeats, adopts or blocks a failed owner, and re-sends prompts that did not queue. The `kortix goals` CLI, the `kortix-goals` skill, `@kortix/sdk`, the web Goals page and the TUI all switch to these routes; `GOAL.md` stays as the goal's brief and `evidence/` as its artifacts. Before this change an owner session could write `state: done` and an invented verifier into `GOAL.md`, and the web page showed the goal as verified. The `goals` flag stays off by default. A control socket that opened but never got `auth_ok` stayed open-but-offline until the next worker restart. | `paused` is part of the persisted attachment record. fix(ci): failed promotes resume, gates survive rehearsals, dev deploys retry failed surfaces (#11924) ## Summary The delivery workflows had states that a failure left half-done with no automatic way out. This PR makes each one either resume on a rerun or refuse up front: - Promote to Production resumes after a failed staging build, deploy or `/health` proof. Before, a rerun refused the already-merged SHA, and the only way out (`ref=staging`) skipped the staging proof. - A waiting release gate can no longer be replaced by a rehearsal dispatch. A cancelled current-head gate reruns once. - `:latest` moves only after prod serves the version. `:stable` accepts only a version with a published GitHub Release. - A rollback and a release no longer roll prod at the same time. - Deploy Dev retries a surface whose last roll failed, and it corrects stale "Not live on dev yet" comments. - A branch dispatch of Deploy Dev no longer migrates the dev database. - The docs no longer tell anyone to re-add the `preview` label to redeploy. Removing the label deletes the environment and its Postgres volume. ## Demo This PR changes workflows, scripts and docs only. No screen changes, so no video. The workflow changes cannot run on a laptop. The unit tests below drive the two changed scripts on temporary git repos with stubbed `gh`/`curl`. ## What is affected - **Release operators.** promote.yml, build-staging.yml, deploy-staging.yml (run name only), tests-release.yml, rerun-failed-once.yml, deploy-prod.yml, promote-self-host-stable.yml, rollback-prod.yml. - **Everyone who deploys dev.** deploy-dev.yml detect-changes and two job conditions, plus announce-dev-live.sh. - **Migration authors.** check-migration-order.sh gets `--pr ` and `--head `. The pre-push hook is unchanged. - **Preview users.** A dispatch input `run_tests` (default `true`, so behavior is unchanged without it). - **Docs.** kortix-release, kortix-rollback, contributing, preview-environments.md, MIGRATIONS.md, and one learnings entry (its enforcement line). - **Not affected.** No app code, no migration, no IAM role or secret, no ECS task definition, and no prod or staging data. ## Per change: what fails, and what happens now | Change | Failure path before | Now | |---|---|---| | promote.yml resume | Build, deploy or health fails after the staging merge. Staging moved and no release PR exists. A rerun exits "already merged". | The plan finds the merged `promote/dev-` PR. While its merge is the staging tip, the run skips the merge. It skips the build when the 3 staging manifests passed, deploys only when staging does not serve the SHA, and always repeats the 8-read `/health` proof. If staging moved past the merge, the run refuses and names `ref=staging`. | | promote.yml deploy lookup | `find_run deploy-staging.yml "$T0"` had no SHA filter. It could wait on another run, or on one GitHub replaced. | The lookup matches the merge SHA through the new `run-name` of deploy-staging. A replaced run ends `cancelled`, the step fails, and a rerun resumes. | | promote.yml re-promote | The old head's gate run held `tests-release-staging`, so the new head waited 30 min (2026-11-06). | Not-completed gate runs on `release/vX.Y.Z` with an older `head_sha` are cancelled before approval. | | build-staging concurrency | A cherry-pick push to staging cancelled the build that promote dispatched. | Dispatched builds use group `build-staging-sha-` and are never cancelled. Pushes still supersede pushes. | | tests-release concurrency | A rehearsal dispatch replaced a waiting release-PR gate. The required check ended `cancelled`, and rerun-once ignored it. | PR gates and rehearsals use separate groups. `rehearsal-guard` fails a rehearsal while any PR gate is queued or running. The api/browser jobs need it. Residual: a gate approved after the guard passed can overlap a running rehearsal. | | rerun-failed-once | Only `failure` reran. | A `cancelled` release-PR gate reruns once when it is an open release PR's current head and no other gate run on that head is active or green. A run cancelled before any job ran reruns whole. A run the workflow token approved gets no `workflow_run` event, so a pending one cancelled before it started still needs a manual rerun. That case is documented in the header. | | deploy-prod `:latest` | `:X.Y.Z` and `:latest` moved at retag, before migrate, the ECS roll and the live check. | `:X.Y.Z` still moves at retag, because ECS rolls that tag. `:latest` moves with `:prod` in `promote-prod-channel`, which needs `verify-live-version`. | | promote-self-host-stable | Accepted any version with a `:X.Y.Z` image. | Requires a published, non-draft GitHub Release `vX.Y.Z`. deploy-prod creates it only after deploy-ecs, verify-live-version and frontend-auth-proof. | | rollback-prod | Separate concurrency group, so it could race a release roll. The header said `--ref dev`, which `environment: prod` refuses. The skill described a `:latest` retag and a rollback PR that do not exist. | Group `deploy-prod`. A waiting run of either workflow replaces the other's waiting run, which is the newer intent. The header says `--ref prod`, and a first step states the ref requirement. The plan prints the migrations newer than the target and warns on DROP/RENAME/ALTER TYPE/SET NOT NULL. It does not refuse. The skill describes the real 4 steps and what undoes a rollback. | | deploy-dev detect-changes | Every surface diffed against the API `/health` commit. A web, gateway or CLI roll that failed while the API rolled was never retried. | `scripts/ci/deploy-dev-changes.sh` diffs each surface against the commit it serves: API `/v1/health`, gateway `/health/live`, web `/api/health`, CLI tag `dev-latest`. apps_router and terraform use the API commit, as before. An unknown commit builds only that surface (fail-safe). The announce base is the oldest served commit among the surfaces this run builds. The filters stay in deploy-dev.yml. | | deploy-dev branch dispatch | `migrate-db` and `deploy-api-ecs` ran on `--ref ` and applied branch migrations to the dev DB. | Both require `refs/heads/dev`. | | announce-dev-live.sh | A "Not live on dev yet" comment outside the next range stayed forever. | A live run checks the 30 most recently updated merged PRs into dev. When every surface serves a commit that contains a PR's merge commit (compare `ahead`/`identical`), the stale comment becomes "Live on dev". | | migration order before merge | A PR into dev runs no CI, and `gh pr merge` runs no hook. A branch pushed before dev got a newer migration merged out of order. | `sh scripts/check-migration-order.sh --pr ` fetches origin/dev and the PR head and checks them. The contributing skill runs it before every merge that adds a migration. No new workflow triggers on PRs into dev, so `tests/unit/sandbox-workflow.test.ts` still holds. The push-to-dev "Migrations are sequential" job stays the backstop. | | preview redeploy | Docs said "re-add the label". Removing the label runs teardown and deletes the sandbox and its Postgres volume. | Docs give `gh workflow run deploy-preview.yml -f pr_number= -f run_tests=false`. The new input defaults to `true`. | | MIGRATIONS.md | Claimed `singleTransaction: true` and "nothing was applied" on failure. Claimed previews share the dev DB. Had no staging row. | Per-file transactions, matching `RUNNER_TRANSACTION_MODE`. Preview has its own DB (`preview-up`). Staging row added. CI-gate triggers corrected. | ## Verification All commands ran in `/work/Projects/kortix/suna-delivery-state-fixes` on 0dd05fffd5 (merged with origin/dev eb67dcb8dc). | Check | Result | What it proves | |---|---|---| | `actionlint` (all workflows) | PASS, exit 0 | The changed YAML and expressions parse. shellcheck is not installed, so embedded scripts were not shellchecked. | | `bash -n` on announce-dev-live.sh and deploy-dev-changes.sh, `sh -n` on check-migration-order.sh | PASS | The scripts parse. | | `vitest unit/deploy-dev-changes.test.ts` (new, 5 tests) | PASS | A failed web roll rebuilds the web while the API is current. An unknown base builds. The real deploy-dev.yml filter block parses into 6 surfaces. | | `vitest unit/announce-dev-live.test.ts` (10, 2 new) | PASS | A stale "Not live" comment outside the range is corrected only when every surface contains the merge and the run is live. | | `vitest unit/migration-order-guard.test.ts` (10, 2 new) | PASS | `--head` catches a branch that sorted last at push time and sorts out of order after dev moved. | | `vitest unit/deploy-concurrency.test.ts` (9, 2 new) | PASS | rollback-prod and deploy-prod share group `deploy-prod`, and the header says `--ref prod`. | | `vitest unit/sandbox-workflow.test.ts` (29, assertions added) | PASS | Resume wiring, SHA-pinned deploy lookup, run-name, build-staging groups, split tests-release groups plus the guard, the cancelled-rerun rule, superseded-head cancel, and the `run_tests` input. No PR-into-dev trigger was added. | | The other workflow tests (app-runtime, dev-channel-promotion, web-ecs, ecs-deploy-worker, image-build-speed, rerun-identity, gate-setup-budgets, shard, prod-deploy-trust, release-record, deploy-banner-timeouts, preview-sticky-comment, cosign, aws-env-action, ecs-stabilize-budget, skills-layout, no-docs-tree) | PASS | Nothing else that pins these files broke. | Not verified: every promote, staging, release-gate, prod, rollback and `:stable` path. Those run only in CI against staging or prod and need the owner's approval to dispatch. The failure walkthrough above is reasoning, not a run. ## Risks and rollback - `promote-self-host-stable` now refuses versions whose release job failed (no GitHub Release). This is intended. A version like that needs its release job rerun first. - Self-hosts that track `:latest` now get a release only after the live check, which is minutes later than before. - A waiting `deploy-prod` run can be replaced by a rollback dispatch, and the other way round. Both are deliberate prod actions, and the newer one wins. - A Deploy Dev `changed` run can build more than before when a surface's served commit is old and its paths changed since. It never builds less than a surface needs. - Rollback: revert this squash commit. No state migrates. ## Reviewer focus 1. `.github/workflows/promote.yml`, plan step and "Build and deploy staging": check the resume condition (the merged promote PR's merge equals the staging tip) and that the `/health` proof always runs. 2. `.github/workflows/rerun-failed-once.yml`: check the `cancelled` rules (current head only, no other active or green run) and the full rerun when no job ran. 3. `.github/workflows/deploy-dev.yml` detect-changes plus `scripts/ci/deploy-dev-changes.sh`: check the per-surface bases and the announce base.

fix(artifacts): comments stay mapped with a leading space; read-only viewers never see a stale co-edited doc (#11916)

## Summary

Third round of the Artifact audit (after kortix-ai/CompanyOS#11911 and
kortix-ai/CompanyOS#11912). Two of these are bugs found while verifying
the first two PRs in a browser. Everything stays behind the existing
`artifacts` and `artifact_comments` flags.

**One leading space unmapped every comment in a doc**

- **What a person saw:** they pressed Enter, typed a space, then text.
Every comment highlight in the doc disappeared, and "Comment" on any new
selection failed.
- **Why:** the editor keeps the paragraph's leading space, but Markdown
cannot write it, so the file holds the text without it.
`docMarkdownPositions` aligned the doc's text with the Markdown all or
nothing. One mismatch made the whole map null, and both the highlights
and new anchors read that map.
- **Fix:** the alignment skips whitespace present on one side only (a
leading or trailing space). Any other difference still means another
text, and no map.

**A read-only viewer could see an old version of a co-edited doc for up
to 10 minutes**

- **What a person saw:** an agent wrote a doc (`publish`, a Files write)
while no editor had it open. A viewer without write access then saw the
old text.
- **Why:** only a leader (an editor tab) merges an outside edit into the
shared doc, and a viewer never leads. With no editor open, the shared
doc kept the old text until its state was reset after 10 idle minutes.
- **Fix:** a viewer shows the shared doc only while it is not behind the
file (`viewerMayGoLive`). That means an editor holds the live lease, or
the last flush is the file version the viewer knows. Otherwise it shows
the file, which already follows later file versions. It asks every 3 s
and goes live again once an editor opens and catches the doc up.
  - A live viewer checks again 8 s after the file moves.
- A file the Files mount re-versioned with the same text also reads as
behind. The viewer then shows that same text, without live edits, until
an editor opens.
- **Also fixed:** the text that highlights, carets and new anchors map
against now comes from what the current editor shows. An editor being
replaced can no longer write its old Markdown over it.

**Smaller fixes**

- **Activity sentence order:** Activity lines were built as "name +
verb" with a space, which is wrong in Japanese. Each language now has
one sentence pattern: "Ada saved a version", "Adaがバージョンを保存しました".

Phosphor names.

viewer's "Open full page" and Close sit in a `ButtonGroup`, as the
design system asks.

feat(apps): a silent or crashing watcher can wake a repair agent (#11907) ## Summary The app-based events plan promised two things for a watcher that stops: - **Repair:** "wakes a repair agent when the watcher goes silent". - **Crash alerts:** "a crash that keeps coming back alerts the App's work triggers". Neither existed. A silence alert reached only people. When an always-on App used its 3 restarts in an hour, keep-alive wrote one log line and stopped. Now Kortix writes three events about an App to the App's event log: | Event | When | `data` | | --- | --- | --- | | `kortix.app.silent` | A trigger's `expect_event_within` passed and its silence alert opened | `trigger`, `last_heard_at`, `expect_event_within_seconds` | | `kortix.app.crashed` | An always-on App stopped 3 times in an hour, and keep-alive stopped restarting it | `restarts`, `within_seconds` | | `kortix.app.recovered` | The App posted again, or its machine answers ready again | `trigger` and `cause: silence`, or `cause: crash` | Rules for these events: - One reaches only a `type: app` trigger whose event is that exact name (`on: { event: kortix.app.silent, app: status-watch }`). An `event: "*"` trigger never gets one. - Each is written once per episode. - None counts as the App posting: they never stamp `last_event_at`. - With no listener, the App's log keeps the event as `unmatched`, and the reason names the trigger to add. - An App cannot post these names. The test route can, so a person or agent can prove a repair trigger: `kortix apps events emit kortix.app.silent --wait`. A spent restart budget also opens a `crash` alert on the App's work triggers. Like a silence alert, it is sent whatever the `notification_center` flag says. The next keep-alive pass that finds the App ready ends it. Each restart is now a `supervisor_restarted` event of the release. One cleanup: an App's own events no longer write skipped rows to the triggers that listen to `kortix.app.*`. **Also in this PR:** `kortix_schedules test` on an App event automation now sends a real test event (`kortix apps events emit --wait`) instead of a dry run. The plan's part F asked for this. It reports the outcome (fired, skipped and why, pending), the session it started, and the fix when no trigger listens. Other automations keep the dry run. **Reliability fixes after Strix's review** (c1ee94a44c). Strix found no security issue and listed these defects: - The crash verdict is per App, not per machine. On an App with two machines, a healthy machine no longer clears what a crashed one raised on every pass. - A crash episode ends when every machine is ready again. A second crash inside the same hour is a new `kortix.app.crashed` event; before, it reused the first event's id and was deduplicated. - Stopping an App ends its crash streak (with no `recovered` event), because keep-alive no longer checks a stopped App. - A repair trigger with its own `expect_event_within` raises no silence alert. Kortix's events never count as the App posting, so that alert could never clear. ## Demo No UI changes. The API and DB evidence is in Verification. fix(ci): verify the gitleaks release archive before it runs (KRTX-4321) (#11894)

Closes KRTX-4321

## Review in 60 seconds

- **Both CI secret scanners now verify the gitleaks release before it
runs.** `.github/workflows/secret-scan.yml` and
`.github/workflows/security-scan.yml` downloaded the release tarball and
executed the extracted binary with no integrity check, while the release
publishes `gitleaks_<v>_checksums.txt`. Each install step now fetches
that manifest, requires the archive be listed in it, and runs `sha256sum
-c` before `tar` extracts anything — a bad archive fails the job instead
of scanning with an unverified binary (CWE-494).
- **A new unit test executes the real `run:` block** of both steps
against a local fixture release: the genuine archive installs and runs,
and a tampered archive, a missing manifest and a manifest entry with a
TAB separator each fail before or instead of running the binary. The TAB
case carries the archive's own correct digest, so only the `grep`
listing guard rejects it — deleting either `grep -q` line turns the
suite red (mutation-checked: `Tests 2 failed | 6 passed (8)`). The suite
is red on the trunk workflows for the stated reason.
- **Feedback cycle:** the G9 item on head `367e192` was that no test
pinned the `grep -q` listing guard; the unlisted-archive case was
rejected by `sha256sum -c --ignore-missing` ("no file was verified")
instead. That case is replaced by the TAB-separator case, which pins the
guard.

**Risk:** low — the steps gain one release download and a checksum check
inside a CI job; no runtime code, no schema, no API. The only way it
breaks is if gitleaks stops publishing `gitleaks_<v>_checksums.txt`, and
then the job fails loudly instead of silently trusting the download.
- **Scope is the two install steps only:** `gitleaks git` / `gitleaks
detect` and their exit codes are untouched, so detection results do not
change — only whether the binary that produces them was verified.

Self-review: 4 items found and fixed

## Summary

The gitleaks binary decides whether a committed secret blocks a release,
so its own integrity sits inside the boundary it enforces. Before this
change, the blocking PR secret gate and the history scan both did `curl
… | tar` and ran the extracted binary with no check at all — a corrupted
or substituted download would scan happily and could pass a secret
commit, or fail for the wrong reason.

Both install steps now follow one verify-then-extract shape:

```sh
base="https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/releases/download/v${GITLEAKS_VERSION}"
archive="gitleaks_${GITLEAKS_VERSION}_linux_x64.tar.gz"
curl -sSfL "${base}/gitleaks_${GITLEAKS_VERSION}_checksums.txt" -o checksums.txt
grep -q " ${archive}$" checksums.txt
curl -sSfL "${base}/${archive}" -o "${archive}"
sha256sum -c --ignore-missing checksums.txt
tar -xzf "${archive}" gitleaks
```

`set -euo pipefail` is added to the `secret-scan.yml` step so a failed
`grep` or `sha256sum` actually aborts it.

The issue's Proposed change asks exactly this: "Fetch `checksums.txt`
and run `sha256sum -c` before extraction in both places". It also says
"reuse the installer's verify pattern where a signature exists" — the
existing `scripts/install.sh` additionally verifies a Sigstore bundle,
but that covers *our* releases signed by
`scripts/ci/cosign-sign-blob.sh`. gitleaks publishes no `.bundle` or
`.sig` next to `checksums.txt` (checked: 404), so the checksum is the
strongest artifact available there.

## Security & data review

- **Boundary:** the scanner now verifies its own binary, so a tampered
or corrupt release can no longer scan unnoticed (CWE-494). This is the

gitleaks publishes no Sigstore bundle, so this is the strongest artifact
available; the issue's Proposed change asks for the checksum
specifically.
- **Fails closed:** a missing manifest, an unlisted archive or a digest
mismatch aborts the job before `tar` runs.

- **Risk:** if gitleaks changes the manifest's filename or line format

— the job stops instead of scanning unverified — and the fixture tests
make that format a test-time contract.
- **Risk:** one extra small download per job run.
- **Rollback:** revert this commit; nothing else to undo.

improve(ios): run simulator tests with pnpm ios:test (#194298)

## What Problem This Solves

Running iOS app tests from a terminal needs a long, hand-built `xcodebuild` command, and a mistyped suite name in `-only-testing` silently runs nothing and still exits 0.

## User Impact

No app change. Developers and agents get one command, `pnpm ios:test`, that runs the iOS app tests on a simulator with the same flags as CI and reports a short, trustworthy result.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `pnpm ios:test` runs the `OpenClaw` scheme (`OpenClawTests` and `OpenClawLogicTests`). `pnpm ios:test TalkModeManagerTests` or `Target/Suite[/test]` selectors run fewer; `OpenClawUITests` selectors use their own scheme. `IOS_SIM` picks a simulator by name or UDID; otherwise a booted iPhone, then the first available one.
- It runs the same project preparation as `ios:gen`, then `xcodebuild test` with CI's flags (`-parallel-testing-enabled NO`, `-collect-test-diagnostics never`) and the `apps/ios/build/DerivedData` path `ios:run` already uses. Output goes to a log file, as in CI, so simulator log forwarding cannot stall timed tests.
- It prints each failure (test ID and the first lines of the message), the pass/fail/skip counts, and the log and `.xcresult` paths in `apps/ios/build/TestResults`. When the build fails, it prints the compiler errors instead of "0 tests".
- `xcodebuild` ignores `-only-testing` selectors that match no test. `findUnmatchedSelectors` in `scripts/lib/ios-test-results.mjs` (the existing xcresult parser) compares the selectors with the result tree, and `ios:test` fails when a selector ran nothing. It matches on node URLs, so Swift Testing suites with display names still match their type name.
- `apps/ios/README.md` documents the command.

## Evidence

- `pnpm ios:test` (whole `OpenClaw` scheme) on an iPhone 17 simulator: 3m19s, 1343 passed, 3 skipped, 2 failed. Both failures are existing source-text tests that are red on `main` and not in any CI list (`RootTabsSidebarRegressionTests` "sidebar has one agent selector…", `WatchApprovalTransportSourceGuardTests` "retry reset matches the exact active attempt"); this PR does not touch them.
- Misspelled suite plus real selectors (a Swift Testing suite, a Logic target suite, an XCTest test method): the real ones ran (21 passed), then `no tests ran for OpenClawTests/NoSuchSuiteTests` and exit 1. The same plain `xcodebuild` command exits 0.
- A throwaway failing test printed its full test ID (`OpenClawTests/ZZThrowawayTests/…`) and expectation text, exit 1. A throwaway compile error printed the compiler error line and `xcodebuild exited 65 before running tests`, exit 1.
- `pnpm ios:test OpenClawUITests/ShareExtensionUITests`: passed through the `OpenClawUITests` scheme.
- `pnpm tsgo:scripts` (red with TS2345 before the selector-target fix, green after), `tsconfig.test.root.scripts.json`, oxlint, oxfmt, `check:script-erasability` and the existing `test/scripts/ios-test-results.test.ts` (20 passed) are clean.
- No new Vitest test: `main` is 49 lines over the test-line ceiling, and the ratchet fails any PR with positive test-line growth while that debt stands (allocations do not forgive it). The unmatched-selector behavior is proven by the real `ios:test` runs above and below; `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet` reports net delta 0.
- Rebased onto `main` to pick up #194283 (the first CI run merged with a `main` that failed `tsgo:extensions` in `extensions/deep-research`). Smoke on the rebased head:

<details>
<summary>pnpm ios:test GatewayStatusBuilderTests NoSuchSuiteTests OpenClawLogicTests/WatchChatStatusLocalizationTests</summary>

```text
ios:test: OpenClawTests/GatewayStatusBuilderTests OpenClawTests/NoSuchSuiteTests OpenClawLogicTests/WatchChatStatusLocalizationTests on iPhone 17 (<simulator-udid>)
ios:test: log apps/ios/build/TestResults/2026-11-06T20-29-54-025Z.log
ios:test: Passed: 20 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped
ios:test: results apps/ios/build/TestResults/2026-11-06T20-29-54-025Z.xcresult
ios:test: no tests ran for OpenClawTests/NoSuchSuiteTests; check the target, suite and test names.
[ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code 1.
```

</details>

- Review: hosted ClawSweeper on this PR.

Merge danger: two-way door. Developer tooling only; no app, CI workflow, state or config changes.

perf(control-ui): render cached Subagents without awaiting live activity (#194263)

Follow-up to #193913. That change made the whole native Details composition wait for the live subagent-activity chunk whenever the cached receipt held ordinary children, because independent section roots could otherwise paint before the activity body. The wait cost 60.4 ms natively before the first populated Details frame. It also made it impossible to draw Details in the same frame as the first cached transcript rows, which #194142 needs.

The composition-wide prepared() memo and its Show wrapper are gone, along with the now-unused preloadChatSubagentActivity export. The existing static SubagentActivity presentation becomes the fallback of the activity's existing ChatLazyBoundary. It receives the receipt rows (or the current query rows if the receipt retires first) strictly as noninteractive presentation, at the same geometry as the live row. When the live observer module resolves through its unchanged createIdleImport owner, live rows replace the cached ones in place. A failed chunk still stays inside the boundary's local error view with Reload, and the other sections still render. The receipt, projection, empty/denied retirement and the display-only rule are unchanged.

Proof: 11 interleaved pairs plus A/A on a quiet AWS c7a.4xlarge, native and Team-scale, with active chat and seeded ordinary children. Outputs/Automations movement stays 0 px in 11/11 pairs on both harnesses. First populated Details is earlier natively in 10/11 pairs (paired median -32.3 ms, 1,394 -> 1,329 ms) and at Team scale by -8.8 ms. No hard secondary crosses the standing regression rule. The strengthened e2e holds the real activity chunk request and asserts cached rows in the first Details frame; it fails on main, where Details never appears while the chunk is held. Synthetic before/after stills of that held state are in the PR. Exact-head CI is green, including all selected checks-ui shards, the UI e2e shard and control-ui-performance. The full UI suite could not run because current main fails to build extensions/deep-research/browser (missing client.js, fix in flight as #194283); that gap is identical on main.

Size: UI runtime -11 LOC. CI Chat boot JS -416 B against its base, New and startup unchanged, no caps or baselines touched. Test changes are line-neutral.

Open follow-up: on the default expanded desktop section, a session with four or more ordinary children still caches three rows while live shows all of them.

fix(config): preserve malformed UTF-8 sources before writing (#194181)

fix(config): refuse to rewrite config files that contain invalid UTF-8

When the root config or an include contained malformed UTF-8, `openclaw config set` decoded it with replacement characters (U+FFFD), wrote that back, and rotated the corrupted copy through the backup history, so the original bytes were lost. Writes now check the original file and includes with the existing strict decoder before any backup is staged, and refuse with the existing `<path> must be valid UTF-8.` error. Best-effort reads, Doctor and backup policy are unchanged.

Evidence: built Linux CLI with real root and include files containing invalid UTF-8, twice per ref. Main replaced the bytes and rotated lossy backups; with this change the write is refused with exit 1, and all 48 source and backup comparisons are byte-identical. Valid Unicode and BOM writes rotate normally, and configs written by stable 2026.11.1 still read and update correctly. Details: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194181#issuecomment-6691987416.

Thanks @Alix-007.

perf(control-ui): retain cached child activity in Details (#193913)

On a warm reload, ordinary child activity no longer arrives after the first populated Details frame and pushes Outputs and Automations down. The existing scoped subagents receipt and its projectDetailsSubagents owner now also carry up to three ordinary children with only the facts the preview renders: activity text, progress and start/end time. The parallel receipt, projection and write path from the first attempt are gone. Live empty or unavailable reads retire the receipt, and the receipt stays display-only: cached rows render as noninteractive divs, and live rows get their open and stop actions back from the live query owners.

The activity body's existing createIdleImport owner prepares the lazy chunk only when Details is open and the cache holds ordinary rows. The native desktop composition waits for that preparation, because its independent section roots could otherwise paint before the activity body. A failed chunk import stays inside the activity's existing local error boundary with Retry, and Outputs and Automations still render.

Proof: 11 interleaved pairs plus A/A on a quiet AWS c7a.4xlarge, native and Team-scale fixtures, active chat with seeded ordinary children, archived chat and dashboard. Outputs/Automations movement after the first populated Details frame drops from 112 px to 0 on native and from 61 px to 0 at Team scale, in 11/11 pairs each, with Subagents at final height in that first frame. Active-chat CLS drops from 0.004947 to 0.000855 natively. No hard secondary regresses under the standing rule. Admission is the visible cost: first populated Details is 60.4 ms later natively and 13.8 ms later at Team scale (paired medians); both are reported per pair in the PR. The new native regression ui/src/e2e/chat-details-subagents-reload.e2e.test.ts is red on main and green here, including an actual activity-chunk failure case. 38 focused tests pass, the full UI suite passes 937 files with 4 skipped, and exact-head CI is green.

Known limit: on the default expanded desktop section, a session with four or more ordinary children caches three rows while live shows all of them, so rows past the third still reconcile in. That is three rows less movement than main; a single cached/live presentation policy is a follow-up.

Compatibility: the receipt lives in the disposable Details display cache. All new row and count fields are optional, so receipts written before this change parse unchanged. A downgraded build drops newer receipts as a cache miss and rebuilds them from live data.

Size: UI runtime +77 net LOC. CI Chat boot JS +517 B and New +197 B, both within unchanged caps; startup JS unchanged at 90,250 B. The Team active-chat snapshot grows 937 B.

fix(macos): Dashboard widgets fail to load over Remote over SSH (#193854)

* fix(macos): forward the widget sandbox port over Remote over SSH

The SSH tunnel forwarded only the Gateway port, so Dashboard widgets and
MCP Apps could not reach the remote sandbox listener (Gateway port + 1)
that the Control UI addresses on the tunnel host. Forward it to the same
local port, skipping it when that port is busy or reserved by a Gateway
this Mac hosts.

Refs #145522

* fix(macos): reserve local sandbox ports only while hosting is on

Turning hosting beside the remote primary off keeps the separated
gateway.port, so the port split no longer implies a local Gateway. Read
the hosting preference instead; it stays part of the tunnel configuration,
so toggling it replaces the tunnel and frees or claims the port.

Refs #145522

* fix(macos): retire a stale SSH tunnel before starting the hosted Gateway

A tunnel opened while hosting was off can hold the hosted Gateway's port
or its widget sandbox port. Local startup attached to that listener and
skipped launching, and the later tunnel replacement never reran startup.
Retire a tunnel whose configuration is stale, and wait for its SSH
process to exit, before starting the hosted Gateway.

Refs #145522

* fix(macos): replace an SSH tunnel missing its widget sandbox forward

A tunnel opened while the sandbox port was busy or reserved (a hosted
Gateway still shutting down, a stale tunnel) stayed healthy and reusable
for as long as its control port listened, so widgets stayed unreachable
after the port freed. Record the forward each tunnel actually opened, and
have the manager's reuse check replace a tunnel without it once that port
is available.

Refs #145522

* fix(macos): run the widget sandbox forward in its own SSH process

Both forwards shared one ssh process with ExitOnForwardFailure, so a
sandbox bind failure took the Gateway route down, and the reuse check
retired a healthy Gateway tunnel to add the forward. The probe also bound
loopback with SO_REUSEADDR, which succeeds beside a 0.0.0.0 listener that
ssh then collides with (GatewayPorts=yes) or shadows.

Open the sandbox forward in a separate ssh process owned by the tunnel
manager, retried at most every 30 s and retired with the Gateway route.
Pin it to 127.0.0.1 so ssh_config cannot move the bind, and probe that
address without SO_REUSEADDR so any existing listener counts as busy.

Refs #145522

* fix(macos): log skipped widget sandbox forwards and describe their retry

Log once per route when the sandbox port is in use or reserved, describe
the lookup-driven retry with its 30 s backoff in the docs, and name the
manager fixture test for what it proves.

Refs #145522

* fix(macos): cancel an unfinished widget sandbox forward on retirement

* fix(macos): keep the widget sandbox forward recognizable to shipped PortGuardian

v2026.11.1 shares the version 2 PortGuardian ledger and drops any receipt
whose ssh command it cannot match before it checks the live parent. The
explicit 127.0.0.1 bind address on the sandbox forward was such a command, so
a running stable app could erase the receipt of this build's live forward.
Use the Gateway tunnel's -L shape and pin the loopback bind with a
command-line GatewayPorts=no, and keep the matcher identical to stable.

* fix(macos): keep inherited alias forwards from ending the widget sandbox forward

The sandbox SSH process reads the same ssh alias as the Gateway process. Any
LocalForward, RemoteForward or DynamicForward in that alias is already held
by the Gateway process, so the sandbox copy always failed to bind and
ExitOnForwardFailure=yes ended the sandbox process on every retry, even with
its own port free. ClearAllForwardings would also clear the sandbox -L.

Turn ExitOnForwardFailure off for the sandbox process only. Readiness
already requires this pid to listen on the sandbox port, so a failed own
bind still ends the attempt. The Gateway command is unchanged.

chore(ios): build the app without compiler warnings (#194102)

## What Problem This Solves

The iOS app build emits compiler warnings that hide new ones, including four Swift concurrency "may introduce data races" warnings and unreachable code in Talk.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Developers and agents building the iOS app get a clean build with zero warnings outside vendored ESPProvision, so new warnings stand out.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Concurrency: Cloudflare Access admission checks are already `@MainActor @Sendable`; three web screens now pass them directly instead of wrapping them in a non-Sendable closure. The sidebar's gateway switch action is typed `@MainActor`, which matches its only callers.
- Talk: the simulator check is a runtime constant, so the code after the simulator `throw` is no longer unreachable and the device recognition path stays compiled (and indexed by Periphery) on simulator builds. The fire-and-forget voice-session close follows the `@discardableResult` convention its sibling already uses.
- iOS 26 deprecations: onboarding's security notice joins the same three localized strings instead of `Text +`; the Watch send continuation uses the `nonisolated(nonsending)` overload, with its now-unused `isolation` parameter left unnamed so callers still inherit actor isolation; the share extension sizes itself from its window scene instead of `UIScreen.main`.
- Removed the app delegate's `application(_:open:options:)` handler and its URL queue. With a SwiftUI scene, iOS delivers URLs only to `onOpenURL`, which already routes them to `handleDeepLink`. The two tests that called the delegate method directly covered a path the system never uses. The handler was added in #99572.
- Smaller fixes: an explicit Watch closure capture and an unused `MainActor.run` result in `ChatViewModel`. The native i18n inventory records the onboarding notice's new extraction kind; translation IDs and source strings are unchanged.

Production −14 lines (+42/−56), tests −60.

## Evidence

- Clean `xcodebuild` from an empty DerivedData, Debug, for iPhone 17 simulator and generic iOS device: `BUILD SUCCEEDED`, 0 warnings outside `apps/ios/ThirdParty/ESPProvision` (17 on the base).
- The delegate handler was dead: with lldb breakpoints on both the delegate method and `NodeAppModel.handleDeepLink(url:)`, `xcrun simctl openurl … openclaw-debug://dashboard` hit only `handleDeepLink` via `onOpenURL`, with the app running and with the app not running. After the change, both cases still route from Chat to Overview.
- `xcodebuild test` on iPhone 17 (iOS 27.0): `OpenClawAppDelegateTests`, `OpenClawTypographyTests`, `SessionDashboardScreenTests`, `SettingsHubTests`, `SidebarGatewayPickerTests`, `SwiftUIRenderSmokeTests`, `TalkRealtimeVoiceSessionCleanupTests`, `TerminalHubScreenTests`, `WatchSessionActivationGateTests`: 96 tests passed.
- `ShareExtensionUITests` (scheme `OpenClawUITests`) passed through the real Photos share sheet.
- OpenClawKit `swift test --filter ChatViewModel`: 598 tests passed.
- SwiftFormat and SwiftLint (repo-pinned versions) clean on changed files; `pnpm native:i18n:verify` and `pnpm native:i18n:check` pass.
- iOS Periphery 3.8.0 `--strict` with the CI build-for-testing index: 0 findings. Talk, Watch session and app coverage suites: 94 tests passed.
- No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.
- Review: hosted ClawSweeper on this PR.

Merge danger: two-way door. No state, config, protocol or migration changes; a revert fully undoes it. Blast radius if wrong: iOS deep-link delivery and share-sheet sizing, both checked above.

Snapshot capture waits until the window has settled facts, so it never records an unmeasured range.

Ownership stays with the existing owners. Scope, deletion, incognito invalidation, 30-day pruning and the 512 KiB aggregate cap remain with the sidebar snapshot store. The scroll controller depends on AppSidebarBase plus the one snapshot capture member it calls, not on the owner class. The superseded full-avatar enrichment and cold scroll-restore machinery are deleted. Saved scroll position is not restored: a sidebar saved at 1400 px reloads at 0, as on main.

Proof: 11 interleaved pairs plus independent A/A on a quiet AWS c7a.4xlarge, Team-scale native fixture, chat and dashboard at saved offsets 0 and 1400. Cached rows match settled live in 44/44 reloads versus 17/44 on main, and empty cached frames drop from 27 to 0. Dashboard/0 hello is 79 ms faster (11/11) and final rows are 66 ms faster (10/11). One recorded lead exception: dashboard/0 first painted rows moved from 352 to 368 ms, about one frame, because main's earlier paint was the wrong row set in 10/11 runs. LoAF, CLS and every other secondary hold. Focused units and browser tests 136 passed, native regression 3/3, UI e2e shards and the byte check green on exact-head CI.

Compatibility: the sidebar projection version goes from 4 to 7, so older cached sidebar records, including stable's projection 1, are retired on read while other profiles' sidebar caches and transcript caches survive. The store test covers versions 1 through 6. This is a disposable browser display cache, not server state.

Size: UI runtime +66 LOC. The sidebar snapshot record grows by 1,829 B. The Chat boot JS cap is set to the CI-measured 1,288,049 B plus the owner's 64 B toolchain headroom, 85 B below main's previous cap. New Session, largest-JS and CSS caps are unchanged.

fix(ci): detect imported asynchronous transaction callbacks (#193957)

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193842

## What Problem This Solves

The transaction boundary check incorrectly passes asynchronous callbacks and commit hooks reached through imports, option spreads, and PostgreSQL connection methods.

## User Impact

Internal tooling only; no user-visible runtime change. No SQLite schema/version, DDL, migration, persisted-format, public API, or runtime configuration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing native TypeScript owner to inspect resolved callback results and effective commit hooks, and identify PostgreSQL methods by their declaration owner. This replaces the file-wide async-name heuristic while preserving asynchronous preparation and unrelated async transaction APIs.

Static proof remains conservative for mixed overload sets, erased mutable options, and detached async effects. The guard does not claim exhaustive async safety.

## Evidence

- Actual relocated CLI regression: the baseline exits 0 on ten invalid cases; the repaired CLI reports all ten with exact locations and exits 1.
- All 16 focused tests pass, including valid synchronous overrides, computed keys, lexical shadows, reassigned callbacks, replaced mutable hooks, and unrelated async APIs.
- Targeted tsgo, lint, formatting, and the guard against the complete source checkout pass. Full repository CI remains the broad proof.
- Independent review corrections removed stale options-initializer inference, fixed computed-key precedence, and restored void-erased shorthand-hook rejection (red/green regression verified).

<details>
<summary>Tooling and regression scope</summary>

The guard adds 106 net tooling lines for resolved dependency/owner contracts, while deleting the old name set and literal-only hook scan. The separate allocation grants exactly 189 net test LF for the actual CLI boundary and distinct precision regressions; the shared test ceiling is unchanged.

Release-note context: internal CI guard hardening only; no migration or operator action.

</details>

fix(update): recovery guards copy the whole state database on every check (#193941)

Once an update run has its own recovery record (#188978), each recovery guard check copied the whole shared state database. The guards passed Doctor schema admission, and any read with admission took a private copy, even with allowNativeRead.

These reads now use a fresh native read-only reader on the live file, like the first read in the same guard. Admission and schema policy are unchanged. Reads without allowNativeRead, and reads inside an artifact-preserving scope, still copy.

Native update lanes, base to the same build relabelled, with a live systemd Gateway:
- Guard copies: 12 to 0. Read-only `sync` children: 18 to 6.
- 400 MB database, /tmp on ext4: 96,873 to 90,827 MiB written.
- 2 GB database, /tmp on tmpfs: 51,318 to 51,323 MiB written.

This does not resolve the disk writes in #185656. Whole-database copies from other snapshot callers remain about 94% of the bytes written.

feat(openclaw-id): add Gateway membership authority and publication behind the Labs flag (#192335)

* feat(openclaw-id): add Gateway membership authority and publication behind the Labs flag

* fix(openclaw-id): keep removal enforcement through failures and let stop cancel Discovery

- Keep a tunnel token's binding until its revocation is confirmed; retry unfinished revocations at start.
- Settle each committed mailbox statement's effects before applying the next.
- Cancel Discovery requests when remote access stops, bound each request with a deadline, and run startup publication beside the lifecycle queue.

* fix(openclaw-id): recheck device authority before relaying mail and stop mailbox statements on stop

- Device mail rechecks the caller and its exact active certificate immediately before the request leaves.
- A stopped mailbox reader submits no further statement of the message it is applying.

* fix(openclaw-id): keep tunnel-issued tokens bound across a restart with the Labs switch off

Saved device-token bindings are read from the local claw record once at Gateway
start, whatever the Labs switch says, and every device-token check waits for that
read. A record that cannot be read refuses device tokens until the switch turns
on or the Gateway restarts. No process, socket or remote service is touched.

* fix(openclaw-id): delete spent invites with their reports before each Gateway write

The Gateway's invite sweep, which already expires pending redemptions before
every write, now also deletes invite records the protocol reports as spent
(cap expired, nothing pending) together with their display reports, so stored
invites stay within the protocol's cap. Test fixtures sign revocations with
the claw id and seq, and a mailbox regression covers a captured revocation
replayed after the device was approved again.

* fix(openclaw-id): keep token bindings in their own row so a full claw still saves

At the protocol caps (20 owner devices, 256 members with 10 browsers each,
100 invites) a claw record that also carried a token binding for every
browser would be about 1.3 MiB, past the 1 MiB plugin-state value limit, and
every write would fail. The bindings now live in a second row of the same
namespace; each row stays within the limit (about 790 KiB and 550 KiB with
every text field at its longest). A record written before keeps its bindings
until the next write moves them into the row.

* fix(openclaw-id): retain member profiles and atomically partition claw state

openclaw-013: preserve OCID-keyed display profiles across invite cleanup and retain bounded membership approval times. Reconcile lost write acknowledgements before publishing authority or effects.

* fix(openclaw-id): bound unsigned persisted Discovery metadata

openclaw-013: reject oversized opaque identities and cursors without truncating or changing signed statements. Preserve headroom for membership writes.

* test(openclaw-id): match stored secret fields, not random signature text

The record check matched 'kit' inside random base64 signatures. It now refuses secret-named fields and the OCK1- kit text.

* fix(openclaw-id): keep pending Discovery work bound to the lifetime that admitted it

A check_name, publication, owner notice or mailbox start captured the
service's stop signal only after loading the Gateway key. Turning remote
access off in that window replaced the signal, so the request still went
to Discovery (for check_name, with the link code). Each operation now
captures the signal when admitted and does nothing if that lifetime
stopped while it was being prepared. A mailbox reader started for a
stopped lifetime would also have blocked the next lifetime's reader.

* fix(openclaw-id): address CI guards and review findings

- Capture the owner-notice lifetime before importing the notice sender, so
  turning remote access off during that import also stops the notice.
- Mark the three openclawId.* methods as new in the 2026.11 train.
- Add the OpenClaw ID config schema to the PR wrapper inventory.
- Keep the Gateway database-worker test inventory sorted.
- Document OpenClaw ID remote access on the experimental features page.
- Remove chained type assertions, annotate new assertions, note the claw
  store mock isolation, break the authority/binding-check type cycle,
  classify the OCID profile reader as worker-only, and rename the provider
  constant so it is not counted as an environment variable.

* test(openclaw-id): prove a stop during notice preparation sends nothing

Hold the owner-notice sender's import, turn remote access off, then release
it: no notice is sent. The test fails when the lifetime is captured after
the import. Drop the mocked token-binding round-trip, which real
persistence and reopen coverage already exercises.

* test(openclaw-id): match the test-line allocation to added lines
