commits.message:
fix(gateway): a named session.create or resume matches its snapshot contract

session.create and session.resume return local_session_info as the
snapshot's info, and that info now carries client for a named session.
Only CanonicalSessionInfo declared the field, so the closed
CanonicalSnapshotInfo model refused it: a named create raised
ContractViolation under HERMES_TEST_ISOLATION and logged a wire-contract
error in production. Declare client on the snapshot info too and
regenerate the contracts with scripts/gen_gateway_contracts.py.

The new test drives create and resume through AuthorityConnection.dispatch
and validates each result against its declared model.

Suggested by @BearHuddleston in review (patch applied as written), after
the Greptile finding on canonical.py.

feat(gateway): a client can name itself on session.create

A third-party client can now say who it is: session.create takes an optional
client {name, version?}. It is attribution only. source still picks the
policy, and no toolset, approval, permission, prompt text or telemetry reads
the label.

- Validated beside the editor check (bounded, safe charset); a malformed value
  is invalid_params on field client.
- Kept inside the frozen creation request, so there is no new column, receipt
  key or policy field: an older owner restores the session, and the label is
  part of the exact-retry identity.
- session.info.client echoes it (absent when none was sent); runtime.describe
  lists client in session_create.parameters and capability session-client-v1.
- Plugins read it with hermes_cli.plugin_session.session_client() (published
  in plugin_api.json) and the client / client_version keys of prompt-section
  session info ("" when none). No PluginContext method, no hook kwarg.
- The classic CLI's /new copies the frozen launch request but never the
  creating client's label: the new session belongs to the terminal.
- Contracts regenerated; docs say the label is self-declared and must never
  grant anything.

fix(plugins): a hosted prompt section can read its session info

Under plugins.isolation: host a system prompt section's callable received its
session info as an opaque placeholder: the read-only mapping core hands it did
not cross the host wire as data, so any section that read a key raised and was
skipped. The wire now encodes a read-only mapping like a dict.

fix(groups): an older home restarted mid-turn settles a legacy turn like a live Stop

A legacy turn's older home that restarted leaves its input 'unknown'; its
agent died with the old process, so it reads inactive, the same rule the
live Stop acknowledgement and the moved-home path already use. Before,
Disband waited on that home until its gateway exited.

fix(groups): ask a legacy deferred turn's older homes for its Stop; hold Retry until they answer

A turn deferred before attempt homes were recorded, whose profile then moved from home A to B
while A's gateway stays up, had no exit: Stop resolved to B only, attest refused A's Stop reads,
so Disband was held until A's gateway exited. Retry asked B, saw idle and requeued a new
generation while A could still run the old one.

Now every live recorded home of that member is a candidate attempt home: attest accepts the
Stop reads (_STOP_READS) at those homes while such a turn is stopping or deferred (the turn named
by expected_task_id when the read carries one), each is asked for the room session and sent the
Stop when it holds that exact turn, and the turn settles once each answers it holds nothing or is
absent; unreachable keeps it. Retry refuses session_busy (field=home, naming the home) until then,
and all of local Retry's daemon probes now run before the policy lock.

fix(groups): keep first-home-wins for an attempt record

A resubmit after proven non-admission never reuses a generation:
requeue_not_admitted_task returns the task to queued and start_task bumps
execution_generation before the next submit, so the new home writes its own
attempt key. Letting a later submit REPLACE an existing record only risks
overwriting the home that actually holds a live attempt. Swap the
same-generation test for one that walks the real requeue -> start -> submit
lifecycle after a move and asserts Stop interrupts at the home running it.

fix(groups): keep a moved turn's Stop and Retry on the home that took it

Four gaps after a profile moved. A turn a home proved it never admitted
could run at a second home while its record kept the first, so Stop asked
the wrong one and could cancel it. Removing the mapping made every home the
bot had ever used hold Disband. Retry stayed refused when the old home was
gone, though Stop could settle it. A turn from before these records could
be settled by the new home's "no such session" while the old one still ran.

fix(groups): drop the Discard advice a deferred local turn can't follow

Review (greptile): Discard ends only indeterminate local turns, so the
member_home_unknown refusal's "or Discard the turn" was advice the user
could not act on. The refusal now names only re-adding the profile.

Following that advice now works end to end: a re-added profile reused its
cached member transport, which skipped recording its home, so once it was
unserved again Disband was back to member_home_unknown. Each resolve now
records the home (a read first keeps the common case off the writer), and
a test follows the advice through to a settled turn.

fix(groups): say how to unblock Disband when a member's home is unknown

A turn whose member profile is no longer configured, with no recorded
home, stays deferred: nothing here can reach the daemon that may still be
running it. Disband then refused with the generic "retry deletion after
Stop completes", which no amount of retrying fixes.

It now refuses with reason member_home_unknown, naming the profile and the
way out: add it back to hosted_rooms.profiles so its Stop can be confirmed,
or Discard the turn. MemberHomeUnknownError subclasses RoomStopPendingError,
so callers that catch the pending refusal keep doing so; both the
canonical and standalone surfaces carry the new reason. Desktop does not
map these reasons, so no locale change.

fix(groups): ask a deferred turn's Stop at the home that admitted it

A turn deferred behind an unconfirmed Stop of a local member another
profile's daemon serves was asked about through whatever home
hosted_rooms.profiles named at that moment. After the profile was pointed
at another home whose gateway is up, that gateway had no such session, so
Disband finished while the old home still held the turn (queued).

Each attempt now records the home that admitted it, in the recorded-homes
store, when that home's daemon attests the submit. Once its Stop has begun,
the Stop goes to that home, whose attest still answers for the attempt
(read and stop operations only). It confirms the Stop, or keeps the turn
while alive and silent, and settles it once its daemon is gone, so a moved
profile never holds Disband forever. Records of finished attempts are
pruned on the next submit and dropped with the room at Disband.

Reported-by: dokterdok (review of #149655, failing test b0fa54c35d)

test(groups): show a remapped profile settling a turn its old home holds

This test fails on purpose. A turn is deferred behind an unconfirmed Stop,
then the profile is pointed at another home. That home has no such session,
so Disband finishes while the old home still holds the turn.

fix(groups): a replayed overtaken Continue never strands the newer message, and Desktop hides it

Re-review of 4f84a6dbda3: the router now refuses a Continue for a discussion a newer
message on its thread overtook, but a log written by an older build can already hold
one. Replaying it (and the schema-5 rebuild replays every room) re-pointed the thread
at the old discussion; the newer one's settle no longer matched, so the row leaked and
the room re-planned it forever. _apply_continued now skips a Continue that a newer
message on the thread preceded, the same fence the router applies before writing one.

Desktop's pause rows used the old fence (only messages after the cap notice), so that
case still drew a Continue button the gateway answers with "not paused". The row now
retires on any newer user message in the thread after the discussion's own message.

fix(groups): a capped discussion overtaken by a newer message cannot be continued

Review of 073c24d38a3: when the cap notice for discussion d1 lands after a newer
message d2 on the same thread, paused_discussion still offered Continue, because it
only looked for newer messages after the cap. Continue then re-pointed the thread
row at d1, d2's later settle no longer matched it, and the leaked row kept the room
projecting that thread forever (re-planning d2, starving every other thread).

A newer message on the thread anywhere after the discussion's own message now ends
the pause, the same fence a Stop already had. The transcript schema moves to 5 so
rooms whose newer message the old settle already dropped rebuild from the log and
answer it.

fix(groups): an old discussion settling never drops a newer message on its thread

When a member answers and the room plans the next round, a user message sent on the
same thread in that window reopens the thread under its own discussion. The old
discussion's settle status (room.activity), appended right after, deleted the
thread row by room and thread alone, closing the newer discussion too. The room
showed idle and the newer message got no task, no approval and no reply.

The settle now closes the thread only while it still belongs to the discussion
that settled.

test(plugins): the plugin RPC route test waits with the shared async_wait_until

The test had its own polling helper with asyncio.sleep(0.02), which
tests/AGENTS.md forbids in new tests. It now waits with
tests.waiting.async_wait_until, which gives a timeout message naming what it
waited for. No assertion changes.

docs(plugins): the plugin RPC structured-output example frees the client's request lane

The documented chart.write handler called the model inline. A plugin RPC call
holds its client's request lane until the handler returns, so that client's
next requests on the connection (an interrupt, an approval answer) waited
for the model, which llm.oneshot never did.

The example now needs a session_id, starts the model call in a thread under
contextvars.copy_context() (ctx.llm reads the profile scope from there),
answers {"job"} at once and sends the chart or the error as the session
event chart.written. A semaphore caps it at 4 calls in flight like
llm.oneshot's per-owner cap; a fifth is refused busy, and a slot comes back
when Thread.start fails.

The route's test now runs the page's code block verbatim, in-process and
under plugins.isolation: host: a sessionless call is refused, 4 calls
return jobs while their model calls are held, a 5th is refused busy, the 4
chart.written events carry the jobs and the parsed JSON, and a 6th call is
accepted. In-process it also makes Thread.start fail 4 times and checks
the next call still gets a slot.

Suggested by @BearHuddleston in review.

fix(plugins): the whole-reply fallback never raises, even on a $ref that does not resolve

A structured-output reply whose fenced block does not parse falls back to the
whole reply. That fallback caught ValueError, RecursionError and
jsonschema.SchemaError only, so a plugin schema with a $ref that does not
resolve (jsonschema's _WrappedReferencingError, a referencing Unresolvable)
escaped it and raised where the released parser answered (None, "text").

The fallback now catches any failure, as its docstring already promised, so
it can only turn a released failure into a success and never adds an error
of its own.

Tests pin each catch: a whole reply too deeply nested to parse, an invalid
schema, a dangling $ref, and the schema-mismatch ValueError the docs promise.

Suggested by @BearHuddleston in review.

fix(plugins): a whole-reply fallback that hits the recursion limit keeps the released answer

A recursive schema over a deeply nested reply made schema validation raise
RecursionError inside the new whole-reply fallback, where the released parser
answered text. The fallback now treats that as no match, so the fenced-block
result stands. Found by the Astra review.

fix(plugins): structured output keeps the released answer, and the plugin RPC route runs in the plugin host

ctx.llm.complete_structured parses the first fenced block of a reply,
as released. The previous commit's whole-reply-first order changed the
answer for replies whose JSON strings hold a fence that also parses,
e.g. {"a": "```1```"} parsed to 1 before and to the object after. The
fenced block stays first; the whole reply is tried only when the fenced
block does not parse or fit the schema, and a failed fallback keeps the
released outcome (text, or the fenced block's schema error).

The end-to-end test of the documented route (frontend -> plugin RPC ->
ctx.llm.complete_structured on the plugin's own task, input redacted
with force=True) now also runs under plugins.isolation: host.

fix(gateway): llm.oneshot runs any task key again, as the last release did

#142006 made llm.oneshot refuse a task that is not a built-in or
plugin-registered auxiliary slot. The released gateway ran such a task:
a key with its own auxiliary.<task> block in config.yaml used that
block, and any other key used the default auto route. Clients that
relied on that got an invalid_params error instead of text.

Both llm.oneshot routes (the shared gateway and the TUI gateway) pass
the task through again, agent.oneshot.client_task goes away with the
refusal, and the contract text no longer says unknown keys are refused.
llm.oneshot is now the released shape: no schema/redact/parsed (Sid's
commits) and the released task handling.

docs(plugins): a plugin frontend gets structured output through its own RPC method

The plugin LLM guide shows the route: the frontend calls
plugin.<id>.<name>; the handler, registered with ctx.register_rpc,
masks its input with redact_sensitive_text(..., force=True) and calls
ctx.llm.complete_structured on the task the plugin registered.

The test runs that route end to end on the session authority: a plugin
registers an auxiliary task and an RPC method, auxiliary.<task> points
at a loopback stub model, and a frontend-shaped call gets the parsed
JSON back. The stub saw the request on the task's model with a
json_schema response_format, and never the secret, with redaction
turned off for the profile (force=True). Without force=True it fails.

feat(plugins): redact_sensitive_text is public plugin API

A plugin that sends user text to a model (ctx.llm) needs to mask the
secrets in it first. agent.redact.redact_sensitive_text does that, but
it was a private import, so `hermes plugins validate` warned on it.

List it in hermes_cli/data/plugin_api.json and regenerate the public
API page. A plugin can redact any text with it, which a `redact=` param
on ctx.llm would not give, and it adds no new parameter semantics.
plugin-llm-access.md documents when to pass force=True.

refactor(gateway): llm.oneshot drops schema, redact and parsed again

#142006 widened the core llm.oneshot gateway method with `schema` and
`redact` params and a `parsed` result field. Only one plugin's chart
writer would ever send them; Desktop, the bundled plugins and the TUI
never do. A plugin's frontend already has its own route for this: a
plugin RPC method (ctx.register_rpc, #142005) whose handler calls
ctx.llm.complete_structured on the plugin's own auxiliary task.

So both gateways and the contract go back to the pre-#142006 shape for
these params. Two parts of #142006 stand on their own and stay:

fix(plugins): a task left from an unloaded plugin load cannot publish after a reload

and every plugin install, enable or update) loads a plugin again into the same
host process under the same plugin_key. A task the first load spawned kept
running, and its emit_plugin_session_event was taken for the new load and
published to the session's viewers.

- Hermes numbers each load of a plugin in the host (load), sends it with the
  load request, and forgets it at unload.
- The host binds that load, with the plugin, to each request it serves, so it
  follows the request's code onto the tasks it spawns; session_event carries it.
- The gateway process publishes only when that load is the plugin's current
  one; otherwise it logs and returns False, as the hosted call did before this
  PR forwarded it. A category plugin's fresh instance keeps its key's load.
- ctx.emit_to_session reads the manager's home_path directly: every manager
  sets it, as the other readers of the plugin's own profile assume.
  Suggested by @BearHuddleston in review.

  tests.waiting.wait_until and Events instead of sleep loops.

ctx.emit_to_session from such a task is unchanged (it reached viewers on
main too).

fix(desktop): install get-windows on macOS and Linux again

that declares no platform (pnpm/pnpm#17774), so the filtered install in
scripts/build/node-deps.mjs skipped get-windows on darwin and linux. The

The helper returned False both for the gateway's "not the owner's chat"
verdict and for an agent nobody judged. A /bg task binds no session, so a
delegation backend reads its source as `cli` and only the verdict can refuse
it; with False and unjudged merged, the /bg verdict this PR adds could not
refuse a Daybreak route, and a backend that refused on False would also
refuse the classic CLI and the TUI backend, whose agents are unjudged.

when nothing did. Every `is True` caller is unchanged. Suggestion and test

fix(gateway): a /bg task takes its chat's Daybreak verdicts

The gateway builds a /bg agent outside the turn wiring, so it carried
neither the owner verdict (`daybreak_surface`) nor the Daybreak switch:
a /bg task from the owner's own Desktop chat could not use a Daybreak
delegation route, and never sent Daybreak itself. Set both from the
task's chat source, the same way a turn of that chat does; a /bg task
from a hosted room or messaging chat stays without either.

fix(gateway): Daybreak delegation routes recognize the owner's gateway-hosted chats

A Desktop, Webapp or TUI chat hosted by the gateway runs on the `local`
transport, so a delegation backend that checks the session platform sees
`local` and refuses a Daybreak route even in the owner's own chat. The
gateway already decides ownership from the chat's launch policy for the
main agent's Daybreak switch.

Split that decision out as `_daybreak_surface` and record it on each turn's
agent as `daybreak_surface`, apart from the switch: a Daybreak delegation
route is chosen per task, not by `agent.daybreak`. `turn_daybreak_surface()`
reads it from the turn's bound agent for code with no agent in hand (a
backend's `route_task`), falling back to the platform for other agents.
Hosted rooms, A2A peers, `tool` and `acp` launches and messaging chats stay
refused, and an unreadable policy still fails closed.

subagents (goal text, then task order), so two delegations sharing a
goal string re-adopted each other's workers: a settled card repainted
with a newer call's running child, and the transcript filled with
copies of the same task (#136532).

combined result lacked it. Add it there, and make the card prefer the
exact (delegation id, task index) join. A row that knows its
delegation id no longer falls back to the fuzzy joins — an unmatched

misfile it. Old results without the id keep the previous behavior.

fix(tui): a paste or attach in flight survives a sibling paste landing first

Two image paths pasted back to back both captured the same composer
revision. The first reply's insert went through setInput, which bumped
the revision, so the second reply failed resolveAttachment's freshness
check and returned null; emitPaste's raw-text fallback only runs on a
non-null result, so the image vanished with no chip, text or message
while the gateway had staged it.

The revision now counts only foreign edits (typing, clear, submit,
history, session switch). A result's own landing is recognised by the
value it writes, and every result carries a land() that re-places its
insertion on the composer's live draft, after the results that landed
since it started, so chips read in numbering order. A result records how
many landings its base value already held, so a second mid-draft paste
lands right after the first. TextInput's emitPaste treats other pastes'
commits as non-edits and lands through land(); /image and /paste land
the same way. syncTokens keeps a token whose result has not landed yet,
and a result refused after acceptance drops its token and detaches its
image. A user edit while a paste is in flight still drops the result and
detaches its image.

Built on #149665's draft tracking: attachImagePaths (the backtrack
edit's image restore) captures a DraftMark per step and lands each image
through land(), so a restore in flight and a user image paste both keep
their image; followTyping and the lost-image notice are unchanged.
syncTokens checks the buffered continuation lines plus the edited line
and still exempts unlanded tokens. appendPaste lands a browse paste
through land() too, falling back to raw text as before.

Covers bracketed path paste, empty-paste clipboard probe, Ctrl+V
hotkey, /image, /paste, the input.detect_drop fallback and an edit's
image restore racing a paste.

fix(state): keep a never-answered task run's record; check the repair budget every 250 sessions

fix(state): find legacy refused chats from the index, outside the write lock, and only in real chats

Review of #149982 (6683920665):

- P1 startup cost: the rowid-range heap scan ran inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE and
  read ~87 s on an 18 GB store, one 0.8 s chunk per writable open. Discovery
  is now one index probe per chat session (newest settled assistant row via
  idx_messages_session_id), read with no write lock and a cursor on
  sessions.id; the write lock is taken only around each actual repair, which
  re-reads the transcript inside its own transaction. Real store, read-only:
  1.56 s cold / 0.05 s warm for all sessions; a finished store pays one
  state_meta read.
- P1 subagent/cron runs: sessions nobody continues as a chat (subagent, cron,
  batch, kanban, curator, tool sources; a _delegate_from child; an ephemeral
  child) are never candidates, so a finished run keeps its rows and
  message_count.
- P2 internal rows: a refused turn's head is shown as the user's refused
  message only when user_originated_turn_view (the test #149708's retention
  uses) accepts it; a background-task notice, process notice or hidden row
  leaves the context without being surfaced.
- P3: a repair bumps rewind_count as rewind_in_transaction does; the
  compression-ancestor walk follows only compression continuations (not
  delegate/branch/reset forks); the notice copy no longer contradicts
  "you're not stuck" and names /new, plus Archive for Bot Chat (where /new
  becomes /compact).

fix(state): roll back a legacy-refusal repair whose COMMIT fails

Review (Greptile P1): the transaction helper ran COMMIT outside its
rollback handler. In DELETE journal mode a reader holding a SHARED lock
makes COMMIT fail with "database is locked" while the write transaction
stays open; the open-time wrapper swallowed the error and handed the
writer connection back mid-transaction, so every later write failed at
BEGIN IMMEDIATE ("cannot start a transaction within a transaction").

COMMIT now runs inside the protected block and any still-open transaction
is rolled back. Verified with real sqlite3 (writer + reader on a DELETE
journal file): the previous head leaves in_transaction=True and the next
BEGIN IMMEDIATE fails; this head leaves no transaction and the next BEGIN
succeeds.

fix(state): repair legacy refused chats one transaction at a time, within the open budget

Review (Greptile P2): the pass held one write transaction across the scan
and every candidate repair, and the time budget bounded only the scan, so a
store with many candidates held the write lock past the budget at open.

Candidates are now queued in state_meta by one short scan transaction;
each session is repaired in its own transaction (the repair itself stays
atomic) and the whole pass shares the budget, always making progress on at
least one session. Unprocessed and deferred sessions stay queued for the
next open; the store is marked done only when the scan is complete and the
queue is empty.

fix(state): leave a compacted refused chat alone and tell the user to start fresh

A real /compress on the pre-#149708 tree carries the refused boundary into
the new summary tail and retires the original row with active=0,
compacted=0, so the "summary holds the refusal" check now looks at every
inactive refused boundary in the session, not only archived ones. Such a
chat cannot be unlocked by dropping rows (the summary restates the refused
ask), so it is left as it is, and the refusal notice now adds the way out
for it: if every message is still refused, start a fresh chat.

fix(state): unlock chats a pre-#149708 safety refusal still holds

A provider safety filter judges the whole thread, so a refused turn left in
the model context refuses every later message. #149708 takes a NEW refusal
out of the model context as it happens, but a refusal stored by an older
build is still in the transcript: that chat (Bot Chat included, where /new
becomes /compact) stays locked after the update.

Older builds closed a refused turn with an assistant failed_turn boundary
whose error card reads content_policy_blocked
(conversation_loop._close_durable_failed_turn); current closers never write
that shape, they retain the turn instead. Proven on real rows: the
pre-#149708 tree (ca436069205) run through `hermes chat` against an
Anthropic stop_reason=refusal stream wrote exactly that row, and the next
innocent message was refused again.

A writable SessionDB open now runs a one-time repair (new sibling
hermes_state_legacy_refusal.py, hooked after the schema commit) that applies
#149708's retention to those turns: out of the model context, the ask kept
on screen as a greyed content_refused row. Only a locked chat is touched
(its newest settled turns are all refusals). Left alone: a chat that
answered after its refusal; a chat whose refusal was folded into a
compaction summary (archived refused boundary, or one in a compression
ancestor), since dropping rows cannot unlock it and a summary rewrite is
not safe; boundaries older than the error-card metadata (nothing marks
them as refusals). A chat with a live turn lease or compression lock is
deferred to the next open. Completion is recorded in state_meta, a fresh
store is stamped done at creation, and the scan is rowid-chunked with a
1 s budget per open (the message_uid backfill's shape).

fix(pm): quote exclude entries YAML can't hold as plain scalars

The exclude hint printed `- @scope/name@1.0.0`, and narrowing a quoted
`'@scope/name@1 || 2'` entry dropped its quotes. A plain YAML scalar can't
start with `@` (or `!`, `&`, `*`, `%`, a quote, ...), so pnpm 12.15.0 then
fails to load pnpm-workspace.yaml. Both writers now go through one helper
that keeps a plain scalar only when it reads back unchanged and
single-quotes it otherwise; narrowing keeps the entry's own quote style.

fix(pm): confine plain http to the user's npm mirror and bound it

The first fix let any SHA256-pinned URL use http, so lock.json rows,
archive fallbacks, whisper pins and CI inputs lost the https-only rule.
Only the URL pinned_source rewrote onto an http npm registry may use
it now (Source.http_mirror); everything else stays https.

Plain-http bytes are capped at 256 MiB before the hash check, on the
probe's declared total, the stream's Content-Length and the bytes read,
since lock rows pin no size and an on-path attacker could otherwise
preallocate or stream an arbitrary partial. The largest npm-hosted
artifact is ~25 MB.

An http request may follow redirects on its own host (Nexus,

or an oversized body is MirrorRefused, a transport error that falls
back to the pinned archive instead of failing the install.

fix(tui): chips on an earlier continuation line survive the next keystroke

syncTokens checked only the line being edited, so a chip on a `\`+Enter
line already in the buffer was dropped on the next key. A refused edit
restored while the user was on a continuation line lost its paste bodies and
images that way, and the retry sent bare labels. It now checks the whole
buffered draft.

fix(tui): a cancelled edit is never re-armed, and an unknown rewind outcome is never reported as nothing removed

Round-6 re-review findings:
- A refusal coming back for an edit the user already started over from (Esc Esc,
  /rewind, a queue edit while the send was in flight) re-armed that old edit.
  A cancel generation now gates the re-arm.
- A transport error after the view switched sessions printed "nothing was
  removed", but the owner may have cut already (lost reply). Only a definite
  refusal says so; otherwise the notice says the rewind may have applied.
- Backspacing the draft to empty, or a backslash continuation, ended the draft
  for a browse paste still resolving. Only clearIn (clear, submit, Esc Esc) does.

fix(tui): browse pastes, refused rewinds and sent edit chips keep the user's draft

Three review findings on the backtrack edit, plus a sweep of every async
continuation the feature adds:

- A paste typed in browse that is still resolving (image or file lookup)
  belongs to the draft it was typed into. A session switch, or a draft
  cleared or submitted meanwhile, drops it and the keys queued behind it,
  with a notice, instead of appending raw text to the new draft. Typing on
  in the same draft keeps the raw-text fallback.
- A rewind that cuts nothing (refused: busy, another viewer's turn, stale
  revision, or a transport error before the cut) puts the whole prepared
  draft back: text with chips plus their image and paste tokens, merged
  ahead of any draft typed since, and keeps the edit armed so the retry
  rewinds again. A switch away before the cut says the edit was not sent.
  The post-cut path still queues text + attachments for the session.
- An armed edit stages its paste bodies before the early return, so the sent
  chip opens with Ctrl+P / click like an ordinary submit's.
- Sweep: the browse prefill and the fork prefill no longer overwrite a draft
  typed while their RPC ran; Enter/fork on a browse overlay whose session
  was switched away does nothing; a first-prompt fork prefills only the
  session it created.

New strings: canonical.queue.pasteNotApplied, slashCmd.core.rewind.editNotSent
(all TUI packs + _keys.tui.json).

fix(tui): a cleared edit never revives its images, and a browse paste never drops

The edit image restore followed the draft by text prefix, so after a clear or
send a new draft starting with the same words (or any draft, for an image-only
edit) picked the old images up again. It now follows one draft lifetime that a
clear, send, replace or mid-text edit ends for good.

A paste in browse followed by a key in the same terminal read lost the paste:
the key changed the composer while the paste resolved. Browse paste and typing
now land in arrival order, and a paste that resolves against a changed draft
falls back to its raw text instead of vanishing.

fix(tui): an edited image prompt keeps its images on a remote gateway

Remote edits lose images: restoring an image prompt re-attaches the owner's
stored paths through stageImagePath, which reads them on the TUI machine. With
HERMES_TUI_GATEWAY_URL pointing at a gateway on another machine those paths do
not exist here, so only the caption came back and sending cut the old turn and
sent it without the image. When any named image is unreadable here on a remote
gateway, the composer now keeps the stored text with its image notes (the model
still gets the same path, which the owner can read) and a notice says the
images were not re-attached. Local and readable-remote restores are unchanged.

fix(tui): a queue edit drops an armed backtrack edit

Queue edits can rewind history: with a retained queue item, Esc Esc ↵ armed a
backtrack edit, then ↑ cycled into a queue edit. The composer showed the queued
text but the pending rewind stayed armed, so Enter cut history and sent the
queued text as the replacement while the original queue item stayed behind.
Starting a queue edit now disarms the pending rewind (with the usual "nothing
was removed" notice). The inverse already holds: Esc Esc browse is blocked
during a queue edit and /rewind clears it.

fix(cli): fullwidth spaces wrap by terminal cells in panels

Fullwidth spaces overflow the browser: U+3000 is whitespace but two cells
wide, so a prompt of "a\u3000" rows took the textwrap path (which counts
characters) and spilled past the panel border. Wide whitespace now routes to
the cell-width wrap; narrow whitespace (tabs, newlines) still never does, so
Latin output is unchanged (20,000 random Latin/whitespace inputs identical).

fix(tui): an edited prompt keeps its images while you type, and a paste in browse is a real paste

Typing on after Enter on an edited image prompt cancelled the rest of the image
restore with no message. The restore now follows the draft while it only grows at
the end, and says how many images were not re-attached when the draft is
replaced, cleared or sent first. /image keeps its strict behaviour.

A paste in backtrack browse went in as raw text (CRLF kept, no paste chip, no
image-path detection). It now goes through the composer paste handler, as the
CLI already does.

fix(tui,cli): a paste while browsing is text, never a browse key

TUI: pasting "f" or "q" in backtrack browse forked or closed instead of typing
it, because a single-character paste reached the browse key table. Pasted
input now closes browse and types into the composer.

CLI: a bracketed paste in browse was swallowed (browse stayed open and the text
vanished). It now closes browse and goes to the normal paste handler.

fix(cli): long CJK prompts wrap in one pass, and the pager caches rows

Review finding (P2, cli_render _wrap_cells + backtrack pager): every row
split re-clustered the whole remaining text, so a long CJK prompt cost
quadratic time per repaint (30,000 CJK chars took ~1.7 s on each scroll).

_wrap_cells now walks the text once, reading each character's width once,
and keeps the same output (a 36,000-case random differential against the
previous head, Latin and CJK, keep_ws and indents, is byte-identical).
The pager also caches wrapped rows by (marker, text, width), so scrolling
or stepping never rewraps unchanged history. 30,000 CJK chars: 1.73 s ->
0.005 s for the wrap.

fix(cli): a primed Esc chord works with more keys already buffered

Review finding (P2, cli_backtrack primed_chord): primed_chord included
lone_esc, which requires an empty key queue, so a recognised primed chord
stopped matching when another key was already buffered: Esc + Left + Enter
in one read did nothing, Esc + Enter + X gave "\nX".

The empty-queue condition now gates only lone-Esc eagerness. The primed
chord needs the prime plus an idle, empty composer; the key it replays is
fed at the front of the queue, so the keys behind it run after, in order.

fix(tui): Esc cancels a queue edit even after its text was erased

Review finding (P2, useInputHandlers backtrack prime): an idle, empty
composer entered backtrack without checking queueEditIdx, so a queue edit
whose text was erased no longer cancelled on Esc. A queue edit now keeps its
Esc ahead of the backtrack prime, as on main: one Esc calls clearIn() and
cancels the edit.

fix(tui): an image restore stops when the session or draft changes

Review finding (P2, canonicalRewindPicker prefill): the sequential image
restore had no fence around the whole chain. Switching from session A to B
while the first attach was pending let the chain start the second attach
against B, and its image became a token in B's composer.

The composer now owns the multi-image restore (attachImagePaths): it captures
the destination and composer revision once, stages every image against that
captured destination, and drops the rest of the list as soon as the session
changes or anything other than these attaches edits the composer (clear,
submit, replace, typing).

fix(tui): editing a prompt with several images brings every image back

The rewind prefill attached each image at once; the first attach changed the
composer, so the next one landed stale and was discarded, and the resent prompt
lost every image after the first. Attach them one after another: the composer
attach now returns its promise and the prefill chains them.

fix(tui,cli): editing an image prompt prefills what the user typed

Review finding "Enter on an image prompt prefills the model-side expansion": the stored row holds
the vision description and cache path the model got, and both surfaces put that in the composer.
split_image_notes (agent/image_routing.py, mirrored in ui-tui lib/imageNotes.ts) removes the
leading vision notes and trailing [Image attached at: ...] hints. The TUI attaches each named
image again as a composer image; the CLI prefills the typed text only (an armed CLI edit sends
text, as before).

fix(cli): cell wrap keeps a combining mark with its letter

Review finding "_wrap_cells can emit a row wider than width": the split took
_clip_cells(row, width + 1)[:-1], which drops a trailing combining mark instead of its base
letter, leaving a 9-cell row at width 8 for "中中中中é". The row is now split by cell width
directly over grapheme clusters (a base character plus its zero-width marks).

fix(tui): PgUp/PgDn in the native pager move one screen

Review finding "PgUp/PgDn jump two screens": browseAction returns ±2 for a page and the pager
multiplied that by the row count. A page is now sign × rows, a row stays ±1.

fix(cli): the backtrack pager hard-wraps a long URL or hash

Review finding "a long ASCII token overflows the pager row": _wrap_panel_text keeps long words
whole (break_long_words=False), so a 120-char URL made a 142-cell row in a 40-cell pager. The
pager now asks for break_long_words=True; every other panel keeps the default, byte-identical to
origin/main (240,000 random Latin cases compared against main's function: 0 diffs).

fix(tui): default browse highlights paste-chip and image prompts

Review finding "paste-chip and image prompts are never focused": rewindFocusIndex matched the
transcript row's chip text against the stored, expanded prompt, so default browse found no row
for them. A resumed user row now carries its durable row id (Msg.rowId) and is matched by it; a
row painted at send time (no id yet) is matched with its paste chips expanded and the stored
prompt's image notes removed. The native pager selects by the same rule.

fix(tui): Esc Esc, Ctrl+C or browsing again cancel an emptied armed edit

Review finding "a cancelled edit still rewinds": with the armed edit's text erased, Esc Esc
primed and opened browse while $pendingRewind stayed armed, so the next ordinary message
rewound the session. The second Esc now cancels the armed edit before the browse path, Ctrl+C on
an empty composer cancels it instead of exiting, and opening browse again drops it. A session
switch (/new, /resume) already disarmed it through the sid listener.

test(tui): native browse scroll is pinned by a behaviour case

Review m3. The browse-key cases now include ↑/k scrolling the native
pager back to the oldest prompt with the selection unchanged. Mutation
checked: making the native scroll a no-op turns it red, and dropping the
←/→ selection step turns the two key cases red.

fix(tui,cli): the browse footer sheds whole hints at narrow widths

Review m4. At 80 columns --tui-native cut the footer to "… esc ba…".
Like Codex's prompt-navigation footer, the line now drops hints in order
as the width shrinks: scroll/prompt keys lose their words, then fork,
then the nav keys, then edit, leaving the label. The ladder is built
from the localized line's own segments, so every catalog gets it with

fix(groups): let Retry send a turn again when its saved run is gone

Discard and Disband now recover when a bot's gateway no longer has a
group chat's saved run, but Retry still trusted it. Retry answered as if
it had recovered the turn, nothing ran, and the turn ended up deferred
again.

Retry now checks the saved run first. If that gateway says it's gone,
Retry drops it and sends the same turn again, with the same key and
generation. An unreachable gateway or an untyped 404 keeps it, as before.

fix(groups): an unknown member home keeps a deferred turn of an unserved profile

unserved_member_stopped settled a deferred turn once every home it knew of had no gateway owner. A
turn dispatched before member homes were recorded, whose profile ran from a custom
hosted_rooms.profiles path and whose entry was then removed, left only the conventional profile
directory to probe: absent there, the turn was cancelled locally while the daemon could still run
it at the custom path, and Disband finished.

With neither a roster entry nor a recorded home the real home is unknown, so the turn is kept
(Disband keeps answering room_stop_pending; Discard still applies).

fix(groups): Disband forgets the room's recorded member homes

record_member_home writes a gateway.hosted.member_homes.v1 state_meta row per (room, member) a
profile daemon was reached for; nothing deleted it, so rows piled up per room. disband_room drops
the room's rows in the tombstone's transaction (no turn is left to prove anything for). The
per-room owner key is left as is: the tombstone's replay and ownership reads may still consult it.

fix(groups): an unsigned claim never makes a real grant's owed revoke unneeded

At a member's four owed-revoke slots, _owe_revoke_locked compared the incoming grant's unsigned
expiry with the shortest owed row: a longer claim evicted that row, a shorter one was skipped as
"covered". The home cannot check a member gateway's signature, so bad-signature grants claiming
long lifetimes (handed in through groups.peer.register for an ended room, scope-checked only) could
fill the slots; a real, shorter-lived grant then was neither stored nor revoked, and maintenance
later dropped the forged rows on invalid_room_grant without touching the real grant.

A member at its cap now raises OwedRevokesFullError, the path the gateway-wide ceiling already
takes: the caller (HostedRoomService.owe_grant_revoke) revokes the incoming grant at its member's
gateway at once, and raises if that gateway does not confirm. No owed row is evicted for an
unsigned claim. The PR-added bounds test now asserts the refusals instead of eviction.

fix(groups): Stop decides a deferred turn on the state its cancel commits from

stop_room chose between the deferred confirmed-Stop path and a direct cancel from its earlier
task snapshot. The worker can defer a stopping turn behind its member's unconfirmed Stop after that
snapshot (or while Stop's confirmation calls run); runtime.cancel then re-read it as deferred and
cancelled it directly, without the member's confirmation, and Disband went ahead with the member's
run possibly alive.

runtime.cancel now gates a deferred turn on its own fresh read (confirm_deferred_stop, the
service's _stop_deferred_peer): unconfirmed, the turn stays deferred and is returned as such, and
stop_room counts a deferred result as unconfirmed, so Disband refuses until the member confirms.
The direct cancel stays fenced on the cancel generation that read saw. The preparation-time fence
cancel (no acknowledgement, under the policy lock) never cancels a deferred turn directly either.

fix(groups): Disband settles a deferred turn of an unserved profile once no daemon owns it

A turn deferred behind the unconfirmed Stop of a local member another
profile's daemon serves waits for that daemon's confirmation. Once the
profile is no longer served on this host (its hosted_rooms.profiles entry
removed, or `hermes profile delete`), the transport lookup refuses with
permission_denied and nothing ever confirms: Disband answered
room_stop_pending forever, with no way out (local Discard and Retry refuse
a deferred turn or hit the same lookup).

Choice: settle on proof, not on the lookup error. The deferred-stop check
of the canonical service now also settles such a turn when the profile is
not served here AND no gateway owns any home it was served from (its
conventional home, every home this gateway reached its daemon at, recorded
in state_meta when the producer is built, and the roster's): the
discovery the transport already uses answers `absent` only with no control
socket, no multiplexer serving the home, and no holder of its gateway.lock,
which a daemon keeps until its process exits. A daemon alive but not
answering (socket gone, lock held) keeps the turn and Disband refuses, as
before; a profile still served keeps waiting for its daemon's Stop. No
argv or pid inspection.

fix(groups): Discard re-asks by key when its saved run never existed

When Retry and Discard overlapped, Discard's key lookup on the member
gateway could find the reservation POST /v1/runs had made but not yet
admitted, and save its run id as the receipt. If that admission was then
refused, the member deleted the reservation and the run state. Every
later Discard, Stop and Disband trusted the receipt, got run_not_found,
and the turn stayed deferred and blocked Disband although nothing ran.

A run_not_found answer for the receipt's run now drops that receipt
(only while it still names that run) and asks the member by key again,
which closes the key when nothing ran under it. A later POST under the
key is still refused with idempotency_key_conflict, so this never starts
the turn; a run that did start under the key is found and stopped as
before.

fix(groups): a deferred turn on another profile's daemon needs its Stop

A turn deferred behind another profile's daemon's unconfirmed Stop could
be settled by a later Stop or Disband without asking that daemon: the
deferred-cancel check passed every member on this gateway. With the
daemon's control socket gone while its agent kept running, Disband
deleted the room and left that work going.

A deferred turn of a member another process serves now settles only once
that process confirms it is not running (the interrupt path a live Stop
uses); an unreachable daemon keeps the turn deferred and Disband refuses,
as for a member on another gateway. Members this process serves are
unchanged.

chore(gateway): serve ledger lists the group-chat peer handlers as authority

The peer invite/register/revoke RPCs this PR adds dispatch through the

test(groups): give the serve Disband race a grant scoped to its room

"late.room.grant", so its [before] case saw no owed revoke and went red.

fix(groups): keep the service-wide Stop/approval lock as an override

docs(groups): explain closed keys and grants held during Disband

Document closed-key lifetime and Retry after a lost close reply while keeping the maintainer's non-admitting Discard and older-member refusal. Explain that grants received during Disband must be revoked before the group chat is deleted, and that recovery waits for the held driver lease before its deferral interval.

Requires the no-service guard, route-lock release, retained- and late-grant fixes, closed-key lifetime, lost-reply Retry, and renewed-lease recovery fixes.

fix(groups): let Discard and Disband settle a turn after its member restarted

Discard and Disband could stay refused after the member returned because
Stop did not resolve its lost run. Read fresh status on unknown_execution
and share polling's exact-admission acknowledgement before settling it.
Keep refusing failed or mismatched confirmations, and release later member
turns only through its own resolve-unknown operation.

fix(groups): defer a member's turn when its gateway goes away mid-run

A lost bot could leave its group chat stuck on "running": no Retry or
Discard, and no other bot could run until someone pressed Stop or
restarted the gateway.

Keep watching through read failures, with the lease, Stop and the turn
limit still working. After 30 seconds of unbroken failures, retire that
exact attempt to the existing recovery path, and accept its late reply.

Recovery now holds up too: a probe that times out can't use up the lease
needed to defer the turn, a running turn is stopped at its limit rather
than deferred, a lost route can't block deferral, and Stop still reaches
a member whose history can't be read and doesn't hold the profile lock
while that member stays unreachable. An unconfirmed Stop of a member on
another profile's daemon defers as it does for a member on another
gateway.

fix(groups): settle Retry after a lost Discard reply

A lost close reply left a group chat turn deferred, and Retry reported the reachable member as unavailable. Confirm the conflicting key is closed and cancel that same attempt without starting a run or advancing its generation. A conflict with an admitted run still keeps the turn.

fix(groups): keep discarded keys closed for every live grant

A shorter replacement grant could let a delayed turn start after Discard had confirmed it in the group chat. Keep closed keys for the issuer's maximum status lifetime from closing, so every grant alive then expires first; prune them afterwards.

fix(groups): watch group chat retries after lease expiry

A slow admission replay could start a peer turn but leave its reply unwatched. Revalidate the lease before reopening the same attempt, retaining ownership and cancellation fences.

fix(groups): type the remaining Disband refusals

Overlapping Disbands and members without grant revocation surfaced as
internal errors. Preserve stable reasons and readable next steps. Use the
normalized group chat ID throughout Disband so padded IDs revoke held
grants and return the same deletion result on both surfaces.

Requires type the pending Stop refusal during Disband and the grant
revocation set for shared error handling.

fix(groups): type the pending Stop refusal during Disband

Disband while a member was still stopping reached clients as an internal
error. Return room_stop_pending on both surfaces, preserving a readable
explanation and the group chat for retry after Stop completes.

fix(groups): keep a grant handed in during Disband accounted for

A grant received during Disband could stay live after successful deletion.
Hold it durably and refuse the tombstone atomically while an unexpired
hold remains. Revoke again outside shared locks, for at most three passes;
an unreachable member keeps the group chat and its unrevoked grant.
Forget only grants revoked in that pass. Grants received after deletion
remain ordinary owed revokes through restart.

Take with release route lock during group chat peer revokes and revoke
retained grants before group chat Disband.

Also requires require peer revocation before group chat Disband: the
metadata-only path must refuse peer obligations before its tombstone,
without a separate route-retirement step that could release a late hold.

fix(groups): revoke retained grants before group chat Disband

An expired replacement grant let Disband forget an older live grant. Revoke each retained unexpired grant first, keeping the group chat and routes on failure and allowing acknowledgement-loss retries.

fix(groups): release route lock during group chat peer revokes

A slow Disband blocked registration and grant renewal in other group
chats. Keep its publication fence, release shared locks during peer calls,
and recheck local state before cleanup.

Take this together with these fixes as one set:
- fix(groups): revoke retained grants before group chat Disband
- fix(groups): keep a grant handed in during Disband accounted for

Releasing the lock lets a new grant arrive during revocation. The set
keeps it durably accounted for and revokes it before deletion succeeds.

This set also requires:
- fix(groups): require peer revocation before group chat Disband

The atomic deletion path relies on that guard before metadata-only
Disband can proceed without retiring peer routes.

fix(groups): require peer revocation before group chat Disband

Disband without a service could erase a group chat with live peer access.
Check its normalized ID for stored routes and unexpired owed or held
grants. Keep live chats until a runtime can coordinate revocation;
replay committed deletion without disturbing debt received afterwards.

fix(groups): keep peer calls out of a fenced turn's cancel in preparation

A stopped group chat could deadlock while preparing a turn for another
computer, including during Discard. Persist the cancellation before
releasing the policy lock and let the worker acknowledge it. Repeated
cancels retain the first stop's identity and generation.

fix(groups): keep a slow computer from holding Stop in other group chats

A lent bot can hold its approval or Stop reply open. Order these controls
per group chat so another chat can still stop or answer approvals. All
accepted spellings of a group chat ID share a lock and cached approvals;
idle locks are reclaimed.

fix(groups): Discard never starts a peer turn its member gateway never admitted

Discard of a deferred peer turn whose home lost the run receipt found the run
by replaying the keyed POST /v1/runs. A member gateway that had never admitted
that key started a fresh run with the user's prompt, and Discard then stopped
it and answered session_busy.

The home now asks the member gateway which run the turn's idempotency key
started, without sending the turn: POST /v1/room-members/runs/close (grant's
stop permission, the same room run namespace as /v1/runs/{id}/stop). The member
answers the run id, or closes the unused key in the same write transaction
that reserves keys, so a late copy of the turn is refused with
idempotency_key_conflict and nothing ever runs under it. A closed key settles
the turn at once; a found run is stopped and the turn settles once the member
confirms. An unreachable member, or one too old to have the route (404/405),
keeps the turn (peer_unreachable) and the home never falls back to the
admitting POST. A key whose finished run aged out of the run store is closed
too, which is still "nothing runs under it".

Retry keeps replaying the admission on purpose; Stop/Disband of a deferred
turn already send nothing without a receipt.

docs(groups): Disband waits for every member gateway, as on main

The peer section still described the dropped design (Disband drops the
route and the revoke follows later). Disband now waits for each member
gateway to confirm its turns ended and revokes there first; an
unreachable member keeps the room and route until Disband is run again.

fix(groups): retry an owed revoke until its grant expires

An owed revoke was dropped after 48 backed-off attempts, about two days at the hourly ceiling,
while the grant it names can pass at its member's gateway for up to 30 days. It is now retried,
with the same capped backoff (at most hourly, one per worker cycle), until the grant's capped
expiry, when it is dropped because the member gateway refuses that grant anyway. The table stays
bounded by its per-member and total ceilings.

fix(groups): never drop a live grant at the owed-revoke ceiling

At the 512-row ceiling, recording the revoke owed for a grant raised inside register (gateway
and serve) after the grant had been handed in and probed: no debt was recorded and the grant was
never revoked.

At the ceiling, rows whose grant has expired make room first. A grant that still finds none is
revoked at its member's gateway at once (remote-first, as Disband does); if that gateway does not
confirm it, the error is recorded and raised rather than the grant dropped quietly. A re-seat
whose replaced grant cannot be recorded is refused the same way: the new grant is revoked (its
scope revocation ends the earlier grant too, so the member is invited again).

fix(groups): idle gateways no longer write the room store every worker cycle

With no Bot from another gateway, every worker cycle still ran the owed-revoke maintenance,
which opened BEGIN IMMEDIATE and a DELETE on shared-state.db: ten idle passes, ten write
transactions (main: none).

Due owed revokes are now read with a read-only query; the write transaction is taken only to
drop an expired row, or later to settle one. And a gateway with no peer route and nothing owed
skips the maintenance entirely: anything that can owe a revoke (a published peer route, a grant
handed in) re-arms it, and the first cycle of a process checks once for revokes an earlier process
left. room_link_url is not the gate: a home without it may still seat a member lent by another
gateway, and that route owes its revoke.

fix(groups): Discard of a peer turn waits for its member's confirmed Stop

Discard of a deferred peer turn with no run receipt cancelled it locally, even when the
member's gateway had admitted the run and was reachable; Disband then tombstoned the room
while that run still executed, which the Disband ruling forbids.

Discard now ends such a turn the way Disband does: it replays the admission under the turn's
own key (finding the run, or starting it), stops that run, and settles the turn only once the
member's gateway confirms the run ended. Until then it answers session_busy and the turn holds.
When the member's gateway is unreachable the turn is kept and Discard answers peer_unreachable,
matching Disband: nothing proves what that gateway did with the admission. A turn with a receipt
goes through the same Stop, so Discard is offered for every deferred peer turn.

fix(groups): a capability read no longer creates the RoomLink secret

groups.capabilities on the gateway called gateway_room_grant_secret() to decide room_link,
which mints .room-link-grant-secret on first read. A read-only probe now checks the secret is
present (or can be created) without writing it; the secret is minted when a grant is first
issued.

fix(groups): only an idempotency conflict leaves a peer admission uncertain

The salvaged client treated every 409 on POST /v1/runs as "a run may already exist". The
member gateway answers 409 idempotency_key_conflict for that case only; permission_denied and
admission_conflict are refusals before any run starts, as main classified them. A 409 whose
code cannot be read still counts as uncertain.

fix(groups): let Discard settle a deferred peer turn with no receipt

A deferred peer turn whose admission was never confirmed (no run receipt) could only be
cleared by Disband: Stop counted it unconfirmed, Discard refused every peer turn, and Retry
failed while the member was unreachable. Now that Disband waits for that Stop, nothing could
clear it. Discard (offered as a pending action beside Retry) cancels such a turn: there is no
run handle to stop or follow, so only the user can let it go. With a receipt, Stop or Retry
can reach the exact run, so Discard stays refused there.

fix(groups): watch a retried peer run even when its first status read fails

Retry of a deferred peer turn replayed its admission (the member then runs that generation)
and only then read the run's status; when that read raised, the turn stayed deferred and no
worker ever reconciled the run the replay had just started. The turn is now reopened as soon
as the replay succeeds, before the status read, so a failed read leaves it indeterminate and
watched.

fix(groups): time a retried deferred peer turn from the retry

Retry of a deferred peer turn reopened it with its original started_at, so once 1830 s had
passed since the first start the reconciler stopped it at once as turn_deadline_exceeded:
retrying an old deferred turn always failed. reopen_deferred_task now restarts the attempt's
clock, so the retried attempt gets its own turn time limit.

fix(groups): bound owed RoomLink grant revokes

An owed revoke took its expiry from the grant's unsigned payload (or now+30d), and nothing
capped the rows a caller could create by handing in grants for an ended room, nor the attempts
spent on a member that never answers.

- expiry is capped at now + 30 days (the longest status horizon a member gateway signs),
  whatever the payload claims;
- one row per (room, member, grant), and at most 4 per member: the longest-lived are kept,
  since revoking the scope at the member covers every grant issued before it;
- a table ceiling of 512 rows (registration refuses past it);
- a revoke still unpaid after 48 backed-off attempts (about two days at the hourly ceiling)
  is dropped.

fix(groups): keep Disband waiting for the member's Stop and revoking it first

Maintainer ruling on #148466: Disband keeps today's behaviour. It waits for every member's
acknowledged Stop (a member on another gateway included) and revokes each peer route at its
member gateway before it tombstones the room. A member gateway that cannot be reached keeps
the room and its route, and Disband reports it (peer_unreachable / "still stopping").

- revoke_room_routes is remote-first again, as on main; retire_room_link_records without an
  expiry drops the stored routes and forgets the held owed revokes (the scope revocation just
  sent covers every older grant). The owed-revoke worker remains only for grants the home was
  handed for a room that ended or moved during registration.
- stop_room counts a peer turn still stopping, and a deferred peer turn whose gateway has not
  confirmed its Stop, as pending when Disband requires acknowledgement.
- Disband moves into _disband / _revoke_routes_first (keeps _group's complexity at main's).
  disband_fence / route_publication_lock let duck-typed services without the new fences keep
  working (main's groups tests use them).
- Every test file on main is restored byte for byte. The salvaged tests that asserted the
  background-revoke behaviour now assert the ruling; the salvaged additions to main's test
  files moved to new files (test_hosted_room_two_gateway_peer.py,
  test_hosted_room_peer_http_admission.py, test_groups_methods_peer_routes.py).

fix(groups): keep peer observations bound to their task attempt

fix(pm): name the exclude a too-young pnpm pick needs

`pnpm update --no-save` reports it as STRICT_MIN_RELEASE_AGE_REQUIRES_SAVE,
which names no package. On that error, repeat the update with saving
allowed and no prompt on a scratch copy of the manifests and lock; its
NO_MATURE_MATCHING_VERSION record lists the picks, and the hint prints
each as the `- name@version  # why` line to add.

fix(pm): prune release-age excludes in the update leg, not on installs

pnpm's minimumReleaseAgeExcludePrune runs on every install that
settles the lockfile, so a stale entry made every user build rewrite
the tracked pnpm-workspace.yaml, and CI's install pruned it before the
policy test could see it. Turn it off; `hermes pm update --pnpm` drops
the entries the refreshed lock no longer holds itself, which replaces

first entry's leading comment to the next survivor, and the PM prune

fix(plugins): an unloaded plugin's session env names stay out of shell snapshots

The snapshot exclusions came from the currently registered names. A value injected around a
registration (wrapper built before the plugin registered, env resolved after) could enter a
snapshot, and once the plugin unloaded its name was no longer excluded, so a later command could
restore another session's value. session_env_names() now returns every name declared in this
process, unloaded plugins' included. Found by Copilot on #142008.

fix(plugins): session env names act on the inherited Windows variable

Windows environment names are case-insensitive and os.environ holds them upper-cased, so a
plugin name spelled `pane` neither unset the inherited `PANE` nor replaced it (the child got both).
On Windows the registry now keeps names upper-cased and maps each resolver key the same way, so the
child env, the shell-snapshot exclusions and the resolver results use one spelling. Found by
Copilot on #142008.

fix(plugins): session env values pass the same credential scrub as the child env

A resolver could return a name a terminal backend declares in strip_env_keys;
the scrub removed it and the session-env merge put it back. The merge now runs
the values through _scrub_credentials (Tier 1 incl. backend strip_env_keys,
and Tier 2), so every name the scrub removes stays removed.

feat(plugins): ctx.register_session_env gives each session's commands its own environment values

Tools run in the shared gateway, so a variable of the terminal or pane that
shows a conversation (a pane id, its socket) never reaches the commands the
agent runs for it. A plugin could only rewrite each `terminal` command with
`tool_request` middleware to prefix an `export`, which changes the command
text and does not cover every spawn.

`ctx.register_session_env(names, resolver)` declares the names and a
`resolver(session_id) -> {name: str | None}`. The child-env bridge
(`tools/environments/local.py::_inject_session_context_env`) calls the active
profile's resolvers with the child's own HERMES_SESSION_ID each time it builds
a local child env: terminal foreground and background, `execute_code`'s
`terminal()`, and the other children that already get HERMES_SESSION_*.
`None` unsets a name; an omitted name keeps the gateway's value.

- Names must be valid env names outside HERMES_*, so core session vars stay
  core's. Values pass the same internal-secret and provider-blocklist
  predicates as the scrub, so a plugin cannot put a credential back.
- LocalEnvironment keeps the declared names out of the shared bash snapshot
  (the existing save/restore + dump exclusion for passthrough names). Without
  that, the snapshot sourced before each command replaces the fresh value with
  a stale one when a session's pane changes or goes away.
- A resolver that raises is logged with its traceback and contributes nothing.
- Registrations are scoped to the plugin manager's profile and released on
  unload through the registration ledger.
- Remote backends (Docker, SSH, Modal) are out of scope: they do not receive
  session context vars today either.

The new registrar lives in the hermes_cli/plugins_session_env.py sibling; the
facade method is a delegate, offset by a duplicated docstring paragraph in
_delivery_manager so plugins.py does not grow.
