Omit sensitive process inputs from spawn trace logs (#60034)

## Why

Command arguments and environment variables can contain credentials. Logging them when spawning a child process can expose those credentials in trace output.

## What changed

Replace argument, `arg0`, and environment contents in `spawn_child_async` trace logs with argument and environment counts and a flag indicating whether `arg0` is overridden. Keep the program, working directory, network sandbox policy, and stdio policy in the trace.

## Testing

Add a regression test that captures trace output and verifies that argument, `arg0`, and environment canaries are omitted while the program path remains visible.

GitOrigin-RevId: c317e7dcc6fd8b4eafb6fcfe98dc8634807c813d

Allow extension status content to use multiple footer rows (#60032)

## Why

Extension status content was limited to one row, clipping multiline text and content that wraps at narrow terminal widths.

## What changed

Measure extension status content at the available width and reserve up to four rows in both shared and separate status layouts. Account for mode indicators and warnings, and remeasure when content or available width changes.

Extra status rows yield to the draft and other composer surfaces when vertical space is limited. An unfocused composer keeps a single dim status row.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for resizing, wrapping beside mode indicators and warnings, hyperlink preservation, limited vertical space, cursor placement, footer overrides, focus changes, theme updates, and reasoning effort changes.

GitOrigin-RevId: 6a637b5cf6f34684639a92d920da4795c90abb6f

Unify TUI status line layout for extension content (#60031)

## What changed

- Use the same status renderer for shared footer rows and separate status lines, allocating extension content the width left by the mode indicator.
- Measure extension content with `measure_natural()` instead of rendering it at maximum width.
- Skip reasoning effort status transitions for extension content and clear an active transition when extension content replaces the status line.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for matching shared and separate layouts across terminal resizing, natural width measurement, viewport clipping with hyperlinks, and skipping effort transitions when switching between native and extension content.

GitOrigin-RevId: 4ffc52ec6374f3c2b4995c0472bee25aa15ae7a0

Render UI trees directly into terminal buffers (#60029)

## What changed

Use a shared layout traversal to measure prepared UI trees and paint text directly into terminal buffers. Add natural and viewport-constrained size measurement, and use direct rendering for extension footer content.

Preserve wrapping, styles, and terminal hyperlinks while clipping at grapheme boundaries and leaving overflow ellipses unlinked.

## Testing

Add coverage for size measurement in terminal cells, wide characters at clipping boundaries, and zero-width text around overflow ellipses. Update rendering tests to check painted buffer contents and hyperlinks.

GitOrigin-RevId: 828c45d3400f9e3dfce9a7bd812d1cc0ea51642f

Reuse prepared UI trees for footer rendering (#60028)

## Why

Footer width measurement and rendering each prepared the same UI tree again.

## What changed

- Prepare footer extension content once and share the owned `PreparedUiTree` through `Arc`.
- Resolve colors against the active theme at render time, caching each color resolution within a render pass.
- Share leaf text buffers across prepared chunks instead of copying their slices.

## Testing

Add a test verifying that chunks from a clean text leaf retain slices of the original buffer. Update existing UI tree rendering tests to use the owned prepared representation.

GitOrigin-RevId: daba035c291338f3e0036e9ad4f2fd26f56a3910

Keep configured status lines on the native renderer (#60027)

## Why

Enabling `tui_extensions_status_line` routed configured status lines through a plain-text extension renderer and hid the “Use theme colors” option in the status line picker.

## What changed

Always use the native status line renderer for configured items and their live picker previews, preserving theme colors and pull request links regardless of the extensions flag. Always expose the theme color option in the picker, and clarify that the flag enables experimental MCP status line providers.

## Testing

Update coverage to require native status line content across extensions flag changes and exercise the live picker preview with the flag enabled. Retain checks for pull request hyperlinks and color preference preservation.

GitOrigin-RevId: bce7df5696c2bd3583d3ef99c43e7a2014e17294

Add multiline layout and row wrapping to UI trees (#60026)

## What changed

Render prepared UI trees within a viewport's width and height, preserving authored line breaks and wrapping text while retaining styles and hyperlink ranges.

- Add `wrap: "wrap"` for rows to move children onto additional lines; keep `nowrap` as the default.
- Allocate space to row children while reserving later siblings' minimum widths.
- Mark horizontal clipping and vertical overflow with an unlinked ellipsis, including in single-line rendering.
- Respect word hyphens across style boundaries and nonbreaking spaces when wrapping.

## Testing

Add regression tests for nested row wrapping, sibling width allocation, hyperlink offsets and clipping, and word boundaries. Add a buffer snapshot covering authored line breaks, collapsed whitespace, styles, and links.

GitOrigin-RevId: fdfbdee92808c0a8f55e2fdf11db95d68a76d9a5

Separate UI tree preparation from line rendering (#60022)

## What changed

Add `UiTree::prepare` and `PreparedUiTree` to prepare styled inline text and row structure independently of viewport width. Compute minimum and preferred widths for text and nested rows, including gaps, and retain authored line breaks when filtering zero-width children.

Render the first line from the prepared tree while retaining overflow ellipses and hyperlink clipping.

## Testing

Add a preparation test covering row width measurements across styled text, nested rows, gaps, empty children, combining marks, and non-breaking spaces.

GitOrigin-RevId: 5f63366c0568a01cb55686d9f14c1b3fac90946f

Normalize inline UI tree text across styled leaves (#60021)

## What changed

- Collapse spaces and tabs across inline leaves, trim leading and trailing whitespace, and keep rendering limited to the first line.
- Prepare Unicode line-break opportunities across style boundaries and join graphemes split across leaves. Use the first fragment's style and retain a hyperlink only when all fragments share its destination.
- Preserve row boundaries and explicit gaps, and use row gaps for status-line separators.
- Prevent zero-width fragments from adding row gaps or changing the ellipsis style.

## Testing

Add regression tests for whitespace collapse, split graphemes, hyperlink ownership, zero-width fragments, and line-break consistency between styled runs and contiguous text.

GitOrigin-RevId: 94e58808bc8469e9cd0adddb16c194b9568cfbb6

Strip terminal commands from UI tree strings (#60020)

## Why

The UI tree renderer's CSI-only sanitizer leaves OSC command contents visible in rendered text, including embedded hyperlink URLs.

## What changed

Use `vtparse` to sanitize each string independently, retaining printable text, tabs, and newlines while discarding terminal commands and other control characters. Preserve the existing text limit, first-line rendering, and tab expansion.

## Testing

Add a regression test covering color escapes, carriage returns, OSC hyperlinks, and an incomplete escape sequence before a structured link. Assert the rendered text and the structured link's hyperlink range.

GitOrigin-RevId: 51899f62d10f6a1321f96278616fe7a51bad17d9

Add theme-aware semantic colors to extension UI trees (#60019)

## Why

Extension UI trees previously accepted only named terminal colors and literal RGB values. Semantic colors let extension content follow the active syntax theme and terminal color capabilities.

## What changed

- Accept `primary`, `surface`, `accent`, and `status-*` color roles for text foregrounds and row backgrounds.
- Resolve semantic colors against the active theme when rendering extension footer content. Prefer the `codex.accent` scope for `accent`, falling back to the theme's accent setting.
- Reuse status-line scope mappings and fallback colors, with terminal-default fallbacks for unavailable primary, surface, and accent colors.

## Testing

Add color serialization coverage and rendering snapshots for dark, light, and empty themes in truecolor and ANSI 16-color terminals, including nested foreground and background styles.

GitOrigin-RevId: 156f137859d74178f9ae6aa46a02eecb815e9802

Propagate turn triggers to usage analytics events (#60018)

## What changed

Include `turn_trigger` from turn metadata in tool, artifact, skill, app, plugin usage, and hook analytics events. Omit the field when no trigger is available.

## Testing

Extend app serialization and reducer tests to check trigger propagation, and verify that MCP tool events retain the trigger after turn completion.

GitOrigin-RevId: 975780983d0761eb34fecf5e8b4abe98a432d0c3

Disable bundled skills in the prompt-prefix comparison test (#60017)

GitOrigin-RevId: d2a606620debc2ed043215b79f672d0d85acf2f1

Honor managed runtime authentication modes and expand coverage (#60014)

## What changed

Allow `requirements.toml` to pin `features.runtime_agent_instances.mode` to `dual_header` or `assertion_only`. Apply the required mode when no explicit mode is configured and reject conflicting explicit settings, while preserving legacy boolean requirements.

Document experimental runtime authentication configuration, credential lifecycle, and bootstrap authentication behavior.

## Testing

Add coverage for managed mode defaults and conflicts, runtime reuse and rotation across account requests and restarts, fresh assertions on Realtime and MCP reconnects, and Realtime destination and environment restrictions.

GitOrigin-RevId: bcf9502178f477c1e8232386f1f3e360bf23d667

Adapt multi-agent mode guidance for hosted tools (#60011)

## What changed

- When `multi_agent_v2.disable_native_tools` is enabled, use bundled mode policies instead of model catalog guidance, while preserving explicitly configured mode hints.
- Refer to multi-agent tools and instruct the model to read the full multi-agent skill before calling them. Keep proactive delegation enabled for `Ultra` reasoning and explicit-request-only delegation for other reasoning levels.
- Reset retained nonempty custom mode hints to explicit-request-only guidance when multi-agent support is disabled, including after a cold resume.

## Testing

Extend integration tests and request snapshots to cover hosted-tool guidance, configured hint precedence, proactive mode with `Ultra` reasoning, and the mode reset after a cold resume.

GitOrigin-RevId: 403791ef76f990e385d9c155d9c2edc9acfcd4fe

Add a shared Windows Bazel setup action (#60010)

## What changed

Add `.github/actions/setup-bazel-windows` to prepare MSVC, derive the Bazel Windows path, download the pinned Cygwin snapshot, and run the existing verified Windows dependency bootstrap. Export the Windows system root and host architecture for subsequent steps.

Use the action in the Bazel workflow and argument-comment lint action. Remove an unused `EnvironmentAttachment` import from the session tests.

GitOrigin-RevId: 8dc711dc9301bb44d49be3fdab79bd4ca981b7d0

Add custom gateway selection to TUI sign-in (#60009)

## What changed

- Add the disabled-by-default `gateway_setup_wizard` feature to let users choose a saved custom gateway during eligible local sign-in onboarding.
- Save the selection as `model_provider`, restart the embedded app server with that provider, and complete required primary authentication and gateway OAuth before starting the first chat.
- Show gateway loading and configuration errors, browser sign-in links, and an OAuth retry action. Respect provider policy and launch overrides.

## Testing

Add coverage for onboarding eligibility, saved gateway selection and persistence, and gateway error and OAuth screens. Add a terminal integration test verifying that the selected gateway receives the first chat with authentication.

GitOrigin-RevId: 92bd2da3abd28d6c2274c91b2d7561bf359f0ca0

Refactor TUI clipboard and composer input handling (#60008)

## What changed

- Extract helpers for image paste shortcuts, paste-burst ticks, restricted draft edits, and composer activity detection.
- Thread `ShellPrefixHandling` through text insertion and pending-input flushing.
- Return a configuration rebuild future that does not borrow the app or base configuration.

## Testing

Add a regression test covering image paste while `!` is buffered: Enter preserves the draft during the paste burst, and subsequent submission includes the image and literal `!` without running a shell command.

GitOrigin-RevId: fb9a3c8a70aed524c65022f2c0910ce2ad11d4d2

Start cloud threads with the local GitHub project (#60007)

## What changed

Pass the local project's GitHub origin to cloud prewarming so new cloud threads can provision a repository checkout. Preserve the attached local project when switching backends and resolve its origin for each thread start.

Normalize supported GitHub origins to credential-free HTTPS URLs and select a repository-specific cloud working directory. Unsupported origins retain the blank environment behavior. Keep project metadata outside the app-server wire protocol, and fix HTTP Git URL parsing so query strings and fragments cannot be mistaken for authority text.

## Testing

Add coverage for project routing, origin normalization and rejection, managed environment encoding, local project retention, and Git URL credential stripping.

GitOrigin-RevId: 5859769965faf060461ccc1cbb3fd48f8e2f2155

Reduce SQLite write overhead for thread activity and history (#60006)

## Why

Token-usage observations previously required full metadata writes. Concurrent history writers could also occupy pool connections while waiting for SQLite's single writer.

## What changed

- Update only timestamps and token totals for eligible activity patches, preserving concurrent metadata edits. Retain metadata repair for missing rows, changed sources, missing spawn edges, history promotion, and preview backfill.
- Serialize local history writes before acquiring transaction connections so readers can use the remaining pool connections.
- Use `ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING` for cumulative log-byte limits so SQLite can compute byte and row limits in one pass.

## Testing

Add coverage for token updates preserving concurrent edits, clamping negative totals, and rejecting stale source or missing spawn metadata. Extend metadata repair tests across legacy and paginated history modes to cover token updates, preview backfill, and spawn-edge repair.

GitOrigin-RevId: 4a30fd42a7498c616ed13adb46fc3d7e0226a94d

Expose ChatGPT user IDs in `account/read` responses (#60004)

## What changed

Add a nullable `userId` to `GetAccountResponse`, populated from the same authenticated account snapshot as the rest of the response. ChatGPT and personal access token sessions return the canonical ChatGPT user ID when available; API-only and signed-out sessions return `null`.

Update the cloud client, generated schemas, TypeScript and Python types, and account identity documentation. Default missing IDs to `None` when deserializing responses from older app servers.

## Testing

Extend account response tests to check ChatGPT and personal access token user IDs, null IDs for other providers and signed-out sessions, and ID changes when switching providers with saved ChatGPT credentials.

GitOrigin-RevId: 7ad3da3cfc835c4d08d03c8e91b06cd7e007d874

Apply runtime authentication to realtime connections (#60003)

## Why

Realtime connections bypassed runtime authentication and reused captured authentication headers for sideband handshakes. They need to honor the selected credential source and its transport policy across call creation, retries, and reconnects.

## What changed

- Use runtime authentication for realtime WebSocket connections, WebRTC call creation, and sideband attachment when enabled for supported OpenAI destinations.
- Resolve authentication on every WebSocket handshake, preserving credential ownership and request scope while generating fresh assertions. Reject authentication failures without falling back to bearer authentication.
- Keep call creation and sideband attachment bound to the selected credentials and account network policy, including when inference uses a different provider.
- Avoid runtime initialization for local marketplace and MCP operations, plugin commands that do not use the remote catalog, and model debugging with a configured catalog.

## Testing

Add coverage for fresh handshake credentials on retries and reconnects, credential and account changes, runtime authentication modes, destination validation, and registration failures.

GitOrigin-RevId: 57e53122912fa78a524427b0f51013f76f9f7681

Decouple Guardian retrieval from local message-board handles (#60002)

## Why

Guardian's retrieval, channel selection, and evidence delivery depend on concrete local message-board types. Expose the required operations through shared interfaces so these consumers can use trait-based board handles.

## What changed

- Introduce `BoardReadView` for captured catalogs and post boundaries, with read operations and JSON search configuration but no mutation methods.
- Extend `AgentMessageBoard` with namespace identification, read-view capture, and channel subscription operations, and implement them for the local board.
- Add `message_board_read_tools` to bind the five read-only tools to a captured view.
- Migrate Guardian consumers to `AgentMessageBoard` and `BoardReadView`, retaining Guardian namespace checks and captured read boundaries.

## Testing

Adapt read-view and Guardian retrieval tests to the trait interfaces. Add assertions for the five retrieval tools and rejection of ordinary boards by retrieval binding, subscription capture, and delivery planning.

GitOrigin-RevId: f8c5bc65d8297f6df6e3b02d6c09006bcaea4b1a

Add bounded original-evidence delivery for Guardian reviewers (#60001)

## What changed

Add `DeliveryPlan::deliver` to supply selected originals as `guardian_original_evidence` context in source order. Read whole posts one board page at a time and batch them within the model's tool-output budget, rejecting originals that cannot fit intact.

Record delivered ordinals only after the admission callback succeeds, and advance channel positions when the plan completes. Preserve successful admissions across partial plans so retries and overlapping channel selections do not duplicate evidence.

Add `LocalBoardReadView::read_post_texts` to retrieve posts in the requested order while enforcing the captured board boundary.

## Testing

Add retrieval tests covering ordered delivery into a retained conversation without starting inference, deduplication, failed admission, oversized-original retries, older evidence from newly selected channels, captured-view boundaries, and paged reads.

GitOrigin-RevId: b2f03e039c6677e0b94dceaa7ed75a966edf81eb

Plan Guardian evidence delivery in source order (#60000)

## What changed

Add `DeliveryState` to plan unique evidence originals from selected Guardian board channels in source order. Read request IDs in pages by insertion sequence within a captured board view, and reject evidence beyond the review's source-history cutoff.

Share evidence request-ID encoding between the housekeeper and delivery planner, and expose the source cutoff on `EvidenceSnapshot`.

## Testing

Add retrieval tests covering deduplication across channels, source ordering across storage pages, exclusion of unselected channels and posts appended after capture, and rejection of evidence beyond the source cutoff.

GitOrigin-RevId: fc181a52b46137538bb94a5bba1c1d6bf1bccf32

Add model-driven Guardian channel selection (#59999)

## What changed

Add `ReviewerSubscriptions::prepare` to select evidence channels using the review task, current subscriptions, and captured catalog. Validate unique channel names before atomically replacing the caller's subscriptions within that catalog, preserving subscriptions to channels outside it.

Share typed sampling between selection and housekeeper routing, enforce input byte budgets, and expose `OperationResult` so callers can honor runtime reuse or rollback requirements. Selection observes cancellation and deadlines before saving membership.

## Testing

Add integration coverage for subscription replacement, caller isolation, preservation of later channels, cancellation before sampling, and rejection of selections outside the captured catalog with a rollback disposition.

GitOrigin-RevId: fcab0de88ac862e21cdf3c780c780385e2543604

Add atomic bulk channel subscription updates (#59998)

## What changed

Add `LocalAgentMessageBoard::set_subscriptions` to apply a caller's subscribe and unsubscribe choices for multiple channels in one transaction. Validate all supplied channels before applying changes, and preserve subscriptions for other channels, threads, and agents.

Allow this self-only operation on read-only live connections, reject fixed views, and emit no notifications. Share subscription and opt-out updates with the existing single-subscription API.

## Testing

Add coverage for bulk updates through a read-only connection, atomic failure when a channel is missing, preservation of other channels and agents, and the absence of notifications.

GitOrigin-RevId: 83ed587f9c5deaa3e9de87adb6319f9de0c804b1

Add subscription tools for Guardian reviewers (#59995)

## What changed

Add `ReviewerSubscriptions` to capture a Guardian catalog and expose self-only `subscribe` and `unsubscribe` tools. Restrict requests to channels in that catalog and return captured post IDs so later evidence stays outside the review boundary. Read current membership from storage and filter it through the captured catalog.

Share message-board tool size limits and query the latest channel post directly when updating subscriptions.

## Testing

Add coverage for caller-only subscription changes, rejection of later channels and explicit agent targets, captured post IDs, and unchanged subscriptions for other agents. Extend message-board tests to check unsubscribe post IDs and reject missing channels.

GitOrigin-RevId: 48bf4270d6079f7e436096175c67bb211ccbc248

Add read-only evidence retrieval tools for Guardian reviewers (#59994)

## What changed

- Expose `guardian_board` tools to list channels and threads, search posts, and read evidence through a captured read-only view. Require a Guardian storage namespace and keep reads within the review's fixed cutoff, including searches across unsubscribed channels.
- Support literal, case-insensitive searches over decoded JSON fields and nested function-call arguments so quotes, Windows paths, and Unicode escapes do not hide matching evidence.
- Strip response-envelope harness metadata from captured evidence except for `user_input_order`, preserving message payloads and source ordering.

## Testing

Add retrieval coverage for unsubscribed channels, fixed cutoffs, and escaped JSON searches. Update evidence tests to verify serialized payloads retain source order while excluding other harness metadata.

GitOrigin-RevId: 3128e4a2d59d1f71f2cce0bc6b1fbdf7e2aba287

Add fixed read views for local message boards (#59993)

## Why

Concurrent appends can shift live results between pages. Readers need a fixed catalog and post boundary to browse without including later activity.

## What changed

- Add `LocalAgentMessageBoard::read_view` and export `LocalBoardReadView`, exposing the captured channel catalog and a read-only board handle.
- Freeze channel summaries and apply a post sequence cutoff to searches, thread listings, reply summaries, and individual reads. Later appends are excluded even when backdated.
- Reject all mutations through fixed views, including subscription changes, while preserving live handle behavior.

Views share SQLite storage without holding a transaction open. They do not retain deleted posts.

## Testing

Add integration coverage for frozen catalogs and paginated reads, exclusion of newer and backdated appends, mutation denial, and continued live updates.

GitOrigin-RevId: d32cd4989d07040891fa5d38f6ee91fa1960d0d6

Preserve app invocation context across MCP tool refreshes (#59991)

## What changed

Keep the advertised `_codex_apps.invocation_context` when an app's tool metadata refreshes on the same server connection, while using refreshed values for other metadata. If the invocation context changes on a different connection, skip the call as unavailable.

## Testing

Extend the code-mode compaction test to refresh app tools before resuming a cell and verify that calls retain the original invocation context while picking up the refreshed `resource_uri`.

GitOrigin-RevId: 1b6072faed74623994ea82035a6ed977451984a4

Add inherited styling to TUI display trees (#59988)

## What changed

Support `bold`, `italic`, and `underline` nodes, plus text properties for color, weight, italics, and underlining. Nested text can override inherited styles, including disabling modifiers.

Add row backgrounds that apply to children and gaps. Text colors and row backgrounds accept the eight standard ANSI color names or `#RRGGBB` values, with RGB colors resolved through the terminal palette. Preserve the last visible span's style on overflow ellipses while keeping them unlinked.

## Testing

Add coverage for style serialization and invalid values, nested modifier depth limits, inherited styles and overrides, row backgrounds, styled truncation, and foreground/background palette resolution, including a rendered buffer snapshot.

GitOrigin-RevId: 6b19b6b740cd754890c8adb489fba414a6ee62d3

Resolve startup models using thread creation options (#59987)

## What changed

Replace `ThreadManager::models_manager_for_startup` with `resolve_startup_model`, which accepts `StartThreadOptions` and returns the selected `ModelInfo` before starting or cold-resuming a thread.

Share model resolution and effective session source selection with thread startup so the lookup honors the same catalog, configuration overrides, and provider fallback setting.

## Testing

Update coverage to compare startup model information with the started thread's selected model, including provider catalog defaults and context window overrides. Add coverage for provider fallback being enabled and disabled.

GitOrigin-RevId: 57040c4afeacc47c7596832271898577a3584c89

Render typed prompts as Markdown in the TUI (#59983)

## Why

Typed prompts currently display Markdown syntax literally, including emphasis, lists, and code fences.

## What changed

- Render Markdown in typed prompts while retaining the prompt gutter, background, and hyperlinks.
- Preserve literal rendering for spoken prompts, prompts with inline text elements, and text without visible Markdown formatting.
- Keep the original Markdown when copying a whole prompt, and preserve source text for code block and blockquote copy targets.
- Preserve bold styling when leaving the dim prompt marker and track hyperlink columns incrementally across styled spans.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for prompt rendering at multiple widths, hyperlink positions, terminal bold styling, and copying Markdown source, code blocks, and blockquotes, including original code line endings and fenced tables with table rendering disabled.

GitOrigin-RevId: eda62043ca8a9fe012ea7e0683fe05de6ad1b898

Test rejection of PNGs with readable dimensions but corrupt pixels (#59980)

Add a regression test that corrupts a PNG's compressed pixel data while
preserving readable dimensions. Verify that `load_for_prompt_bytes` returns
`ImageProcessingError::Decode` in `ORIGINAL_DETAIL` mode even when the image
is small enough to pass through without resizing.

GitOrigin-RevId: 92d9239b469d3e3cf4437eb6fecbf7c11d0bcc7a

Test command completion before network denial grace expires (#59974)

## What changed

Extend remote network approval tests to cover executor-owned proxies. Verify that `exec_command` delivers the process result while a network review is pending, without waiting for the denial grace period.

Freeze Tokio time after command startup and use a real-time timeout to detect delayed results. Share the test setup with the existing controller-owned proxy cases, preserving local-binding policy and process-exit cleanup assertions.

GitOrigin-RevId: f07fe273c16d55305ee088223449def68384c104

Enable gRPC and host output truncation by default for Code Mode (#59973)

## What changed

Mark `code_mode_host_grpc` and `code_mode_host_output_truncation` as stable and enable them by default. Code Mode now defaults to gRPC over stdio and truncates output in the host before sending it to Core.

## Testing

Update integration tests to exercise the default configuration and explicit feature opt-outs, covering output budgets, truncation notices, and wait termination. Keep the stdio reconnection test explicitly configured for that transport.

GitOrigin-RevId: 5847a249d698fb9b1ecf4921aca4e6efc501f890

Fix Opus header installation with relative symlink inputs (#59972)

## Why

Opus build inputs can be relative symlinks. CMake can preserve those links during header installation, leaving dangling links in the install prefix.

## What changed

Add and export the `opusic-sys` patch referenced by the Bazel configuration. The patch copies public headers into the CMake build directory and uses those copies for `PUBLIC_HEADER` installation.

GitOrigin-RevId: 03f0e1ab536fdf894dc23a40acc331bf16bcae13

Reduce contention in thread writer lock coordination (#59969)

## Why

Exclusive coordination serialized writer acquisition across unrelated threads and could delay releasing writer ownership while waiting to remove a lock file.

## What changed

Use shared coordination when opening thread writer locks. Attempt the initial stale-lock sweep only when exclusive coordination is immediately available, and keep rollout publication exclusively coordinated.

When dropping a writer guard, remove its lock file only if exclusive coordination can be acquired immediately. Otherwise, release ownership and leave the file available for reuse or later cleanup.

## Testing

Extend the writer-lock test to cover acquisition for different threads under shared coordination, rejection of competing owners for the same thread, and prompt ownership release and reacquisition when cleanup cannot acquire exclusive coordination.

GitOrigin-RevId: 3e187b32dbef3bcfdd8c62e91eca58b615f3879e

Normalize turn context permissions to a required profile (#59963)

## What changed

Make `TurnContextItem.permission_profile` required and remove its legacy `sandbox_policy` and `file_system_sandbox_policy` fields. Normalize older histories into a permission profile during deserialization, preserving the restrictive fallback for malformed filesystem rules.

Keep legacy compatibility fields in rollout serialization so older readers remain usable. Update turn recording, metadata extraction, and permission checks to consume the profile directly.

## Testing

Add coverage for legacy normalization, profile-only serialization, missing permissions, and malformed filesystem rules. Extend rollout round-trip fixtures to cover deny rules and filesystem roots from another platform.

GitOrigin-RevId: 27515fec60cccbac5806b98fb71f54e311a09701

Skip the network denial grace period when remote decisions drain (#59960)

## Why

Completed remote commands wait up to 100 ms for late network denials even when all execution-owned network decision callbacks and requests have finished.

## What changed

Allow deferred network approval cleanup to finish as soon as an executor-owned remote proxy's decisions drain. Retain the grace period when a shared listener could still report an untagged denial, including when that listener starts during the command. Always register the blocked-request observer when starting the session proxy.

## Testing

Extend the paused-time regression test to cover immediate completion after remote callbacks drain and propagation of a late denial from a newly registered shared listener.

GitOrigin-RevId: 41bda6504f6d97d5626beba58cf30fb4a9a2dbdd

Expose model metadata from each thread's catalog and settings (#59958)

## What changed

- Add `ThreadManager::models_manager_for_startup` to obtain the model catalog used when starting or cold-resuming a root thread, including its effective originator.
- Add `CodexThread::selected_model_info` to resolve the model for future turns using the thread's current settings, catalog, and model overrides.
- Share catalog selection logic between startup lookup and thread creation.

## Testing

Add coverage verifying that startup and thread lookups use the thread-specific catalog, preserve the configured context window, and reflect model selection updates.

GitOrigin-RevId: d7976caebb7459e1e9ca55f3c6f6bb2af92cf3de

Bump `ignore` to `0.4.30` (#59955)

GitOrigin-RevId: 43fe84738d323dbeebe0640c0540ed7dcff69ddf

Resolve skill display names in read and installations tools (#59954)

## What changed

Allow `skills.read` and `skills.installations` to resolve visible skills by their full display name or the truncated name returned by `skills.list`. Preserve package locator and alias precedence, merged installation locations, and source filtering.

Reject ambiguous names with guidance to use `skills.list` and pass the intended package locator. Hidden and disabled skills remain unavailable through name lookup.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for name resolution, package and alias precedence, truncated UTF-8 names, merged locations, source filters, and ambiguous names.

GitOrigin-RevId: 5a2526d94f259cadb184563807127cb49955106d

Route broad Codex setup questions through self-knowledge guidance (#59949)

## What changed

Update the `openai-docs` sample skill to read `references/codex-self-knowledge.md` first for broad Codex setup or team customization questions, using its guidance to choose and combine configuration options. Keep other product behavior questions on the existing documentation lookup route.

GitOrigin-RevId: 0d307ab128ee8d3952b1527c20d1e659b79820d3

Narrow openai-docs to product Q&A and first-time API setup (#59944)

## What changed

Refocus `openai-docs` on Codex and ChatGPT Work behavior and first-time API integrations. Skip API questions about existing integrations, action requests, and tasks fully answered by supplied text or data. Retain model migration guidance when users explicitly invoke `$openai-docs`.

Replace the broad routing workflow with guidance to check available tools and settings, consult documentation for the relevant product surface, and verify recent changes through the changelog and linked client changes or tests.

Update the skill's display metadata and affected skill catalog snapshots to match.

GitOrigin-RevId: 0a0e9abbee9975ebd30917b7477f475096f2c86b

Use permission profiles for protected-model startup downgrades (#59933)

## What changed

Check the effective permission profile directly when applying startup restrictions for models that require automatic review, instead of converting it to a legacy sandbox policy.

Preserve the downgrade to `workspace-write` for profiles with full disk write access and enabled network access, excluding external enforcement and writable paths that cannot be converted to local paths. Share writable-path conversion with the legacy sandbox adapter.

## Testing

Add startup regression coverage for profiles that are downgraded, preserved, or rejected, including read-only carveouts and writable paths that cannot be converted locally. Verify restored permissions, automatic review selection, and workspace settings.

GitOrigin-RevId: 256c949f23d84dfba185a45a01b638ff5f1df52e

Improve sidebar chat selection and tab hover highlighting (#59928)

## Why

The sidebar chooser used hard-coded keys and hints instead of configured list bindings, limiting navigation and making custom shortcuts inconsistent.

## What changed

- Use configured list actions for chooser navigation, acceptance, and cancellation, including key chords, page movement, and jumps to the first or last choice. Show the configured shortcuts in footer and retry hints.
- Place “New side chat” first and group existing chats into compact rows with a count and optional thread colors. Keep the selected chat visible in short panes.
- Highlight inactive side-chat tabs on hover while preserving the selected tab's styling. Redraw when the hovered tab changes and suppress hover highlighting during pane resizing.

## Testing

Extend interaction tests and snapshots to cover custom acceptance chords, `j`/`k` navigation, paging, and tab hover styles and redraws with either pane focused, including the fallback when terminal colors are unavailable.

GitOrigin-RevId: bad992b3786215dcb5569acfc72af8841fad949d

Bind Guardian Decisions requests to their credential source (#59914)

## Why

Guardian Decisions retained a copied login key after the saved login changed or was removed. Queued comparisons need to respect credential changes, while runtime-bound threads must remain tied to their startup credential source.

## What changed

- Select login credentials from the thread's `ProviderAuthContext`, falling back to the supplied auth manager when no context exists.
- Resolve saved login keys before sending requests and reject queued comparisons if their credential source has changed. Pin runtime-bound credentials to the source selected at startup.
- Revalidate implicit keys before sending, rejecting missing, padded, or FedRAMP keys. Preserve explicit key overrides and the environment-key fallback.

## Testing

Extend credential lookup and queued-request tests to cover reloaded logins, runtime source pinning, rejection of stale queued comparisons, replacement-key authorization, invalid keys, and logout.

GitOrigin-RevId: 1d975613040e08c3825ba6355a166cf0fa812cad

Resolve Guardian policy from the reviewed thread's catalog (#59913)

## Why

Async classification could use policy from the manager's startup catalog even when the reviewed thread had a different reviewer policy.

## What changed

Share reviewer resolution between synchronous review and async classification, using the thread's catalog and reviewer eligibility rules. Select reviewer metadata from the same catalog snapshot, filter out models unsupported by API authentication, and preserve captured parent metadata when no eligible default reviewer exists.

## Testing

Update the async classification regression test with distinct thread and manager catalog policies, asserting that the thread reviewer's policy appears in classifier instructions.

GitOrigin-RevId: 0b28644d30bda42d2cf1bd8a31de2e8f8d38e1a6

Scope file change approval cancellation to the requesting turn (#59910)

## Why

A delayed file change approval cancellation could interrupt a later turn, even when the original approval was no longer pending.

## What changed

Send `Op::CancelPatchApproval` with the approval ID and requesting turn ID from the app server. Resolve cancellations only for a matching pending approval and interrupt its requesting turn only if it is still active. Route legacy `Op::PatchApproval` abort decisions through the same pending-approval handling.

## Testing

Add a regression test that cancels an approval, then replays that cancellation while a second turn has a pending approval with the same call ID. Verify that the second approval succeeds and its turn remains active.

GitOrigin-RevId: 4c833ccd0f33c2df4e9dfb25e2729ab19b6c879f

Avoid full image decoding for original-detail context estimates (#59908)

Read inline image dimensions with `ImageReader::into_dimensions` instead of
loading the full image into memory. Keep the existing patch-based estimate
and fallback when dimensions cannot be read.

GitOrigin-RevId: fd45eb748ce03134261c867397e1fe46c6023f2d

Validate implicit API keys for Guardian Decisions (#59905)

## Why

Decisions uses a commercial endpoint, so implicitly inherited credentials must exclude FedRAMP API keys.

## What changed

Reject empty, whitespace-padded, and FedRAMP keys selected from cached authentication or `OPENAI_API_KEY`, returning a credentials error without rewriting the key. Explicit `CODEX_GUARDIAN_DECISIONS_API_KEY` overrides retain their existing behavior.

## Testing

Extend the cached-key precedence test to verify that FedRAMP project and service-account keys, including a whitespace-padded key, are rejected even when `OPENAI_API_KEY` provides a fallback.

GitOrigin-RevId: 8904b0e5b30662aaf7eb7535309b01c254bcbb82

Delete incomplete prereleases by release ID (#59903)

## Why

A release can be replaced under the same tag during asset upload. Cleanup by tag could then delete the replacement release.

## What changed

Move GitHub release publication into `.github/scripts/publish-github-release.sh`. Create releases through the API and capture their IDs so an exit trap deletes only the newly created prerelease if asset upload fails. Clear the trap after upload so a metadata update failure preserves the uploaded assets.

Keep existing releases and tags intact, verify tags before creating releases, and continue creating stable releases as drafts until upload completes.

## Testing

Extend the publication test to cover upload failures, retries, metadata update failures, stable drafts, replacement releases, and missing tags. The focused test passes.

GitOrigin-RevId: a310d5b77a66dc6a9cf2d136c280d968f0e7a28f

Keep verified question/answer records whole under elastic budgets (#59902)

## Why

Truncating verified answers can obscure the association between questions and responses. Elastic entry caps must preserve that association.

## What changed

Mark verified answer records in root conversation and trusted user answer sections so elastic preparation keeps them intact when they fit. Replace oversized records with the protected incomplete-answer notice and record zero retained evidence bytes.

## Testing

Add a regression test with two questions and opposite answers, checking that both evidence sections omit oversized records whole and preserve complete records when the entry cap allows them.

GitOrigin-RevId: 0fe9e8c0955cb09845a929274e3d52b816119624

Recompute the approval reviewer when switching models (#59893)

## Why

Switching away from a model that requires automatic review should restore the user's requested approval reviewer instead of retaining the model's enforced reviewer.

## What changed

Recompute the reviewer from the requested preference and model requirements when the model changes without an explicit reviewer update, unless the session uses a trusted guardian reviewer. Preserve an explicit automatic-review preference across subsequent model switches.

## Testing

Extend the app-server settings regression test to cover restoring user review after leaving a protected model and retaining an explicit automatic-review choice across repeated model switches.

GitOrigin-RevId: a5672d1ebe94c2fac201ad460b4789d11df03b1a

Bound REPL provenance costs in elastic context preparation (#59891)

## Why

A reviewer receiving retained REPL responses after compaction can exhaust its context budget on protected response headers alone when the store contains many small results.

## What changed

Select a contiguous suffix of the newest responses before allocating body budgets, bounding elastic selection by the token-derived cost of provenance headers and separators. Preserve retained response bodies and images for subsequent allocation, and include dropped responses in the omission count. Apply this selection to both text-only and multimodal evidence.

## Testing

Extend the elastic REPL regression test with 10,000 responses in both evidence modes, checking budget admission, contiguous newest-response retention, preserved text and images, and combined storage and selection omission counts.

GitOrigin-RevId: 47c10d2f50e863ce4ba186be888788b8be5299dc

Remove incomplete prereleases after asset upload failures (#59887)

## Why

Prereleases are published before their assets are uploaded. A failed upload can leave an incomplete public release and prevent a rerun from recreating its `prereleased` event.

## What changed

Track newly created prereleases and successful asset uploads in the release workflow. Remove a newly created prerelease if its upload fails, preserving the tag so a rerun can recreate the release. Keep existing releases and releases whose assets finished uploading, even if the metadata update fails.

## Testing

Add a regression test that runs the workflow commands with a stubbed `gh`, covering upload failure cleanup, a successful rerun, preservation of existing prereleases, and metadata update failures after upload.

GitOrigin-RevId: 29411d6d1e649f4e8c67e84a41d9de2c9d31558f

Carry targeted moderation decisions on final-answer messages (#59842)

## What changed

Read `final_answer_moderation` metadata and attach `moderation: { moderated: boolean }` to the completed final-answer message only when its item ID matches. Apply this in both normal and plan modes, and reset the pending decision when a new response starts.

Preserve the answer's native item ID and moderation flag through legacy events and history reconstruction. Combine text parts into one legacy event when a moderation decision is present.

Expose nullable moderation data on app-server agent messages and update the JSON schemas, TypeScript types, and Python models.

## Testing

Add an integration test for moderation on completed answers and their legacy events. Extend protocol conversion tests to cover populated moderation data and serialization as `null` when absent.

GitOrigin-RevId: f286b67731a84b3daf5d10b7644f2e31b62f0e53

Add opt-in incremental tools for regular OpenAI Responses (#59832)

## Why

Incremental tool declarations were limited to Responses Lite. Regular OpenAI Responses requests sent the full current tool catalog on each request.

## What changed

- Add the disabled-by-default `incremental_tools_legacy` feature for regular OpenAI Responses, independently of the Responses Lite `incremental_tools` flag.
- Support tool declarations and updates in conversation history, including during compaction, while preserving existing history prefixes.
- Keep hosted `web_search` configuration in top-level `tools` rather than `additional_tools`, including in compaction requests.

## Testing

Extend request-history scenarios and snapshots to cover regular Responses catalog updates, model switches, compaction, and MCP tool removal and restoration. Assert that incremental requests preserve input prefixes and keep web search out of history declarations.

GitOrigin-RevId: fa347409e387aa973ce2e41df8505769b7db1ec2

Add a gated Cloud backend to the TUI (#59828)

## What changed

- Register an additional Cloud connection on supported macOS and Linux launches when `TuiMultiBackend` is enabled, using the selected ChatGPT account and local network policy.
- Preserve backend settings and identify Cloud in connection controls and status.
- Let Cloud supply the model when a thread opens, skip local skills requests and stale results, and allow resume without a local working-directory override.
- Preserve Git metadata in Cloud thread snapshots and continue history hydration past empty filtered pages within the scan budget.
- Report Cloud connection failures and require reopening Codex to reconnect.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for Cloud model bootstrap, skipped skills requests, resume directory handling, history pagination through filtered pages, and Git metadata preservation.

GitOrigin-RevId: 6717f0f5ad7708c5e9b5796d94711dd1eecc49bb

Preserve client metadata through queued submissions (#59826)

## Why

Queued inputs previously stored and dispatched without the submitting client's Responses API metadata, losing attribution such as `client_type` when the queued turn started.

## What changed

- Accept `responsesapiClientMetadata` when adding or updating queued submissions and expose it on returned queue items.
- Persist metadata with the input and forward it when starting a selected item or dispatching an idle queue, including after restoration.
- Preserve existing metadata when an update omits it or supplies an empty map; replace it when a non-empty map is supplied.
- Keep stored inputs readable by older queue workers and update generated protocol artifacts.

## Testing

Extend queue service and app-server tests to cover metadata round trips, preservation and replacement on edits, compatibility with older readers, and forwarding during selected, idle, and restored dispatch.

GitOrigin-RevId: 508043b1d3d0298c9af2be8e05b6999de46596a1

Enable resizing the sidebar chooser (#59824)

## Why

Sidebar resizing previously required an open side chat, leaving the chooser without the same width controls.

## What changed

- Support keyboard resizing, width presets, and divider dragging for the sidebar chooser, with resize hints that fit narrow sidebars.
- Keep keyboard resize mode active across startup thread assignment and replacement of the chooser by a new side chat, so `Enter` finishes resizing without submitting the parent draft.
- Activate resize bindings only when a split is available, and prevent divider drags from starting while the split is animating.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for chooser resizing, width preservation when switching between the chooser and a chat, startup and side-chat creation transitions, draft preservation, and unavailable resize bindings in narrow terminals.

GitOrigin-RevId: 511cd4bb5894e6f33f0cf5d7472bb3013361ffe0

Bind runtime auth to the provider's selected credential source (#59823)

## Why

Runtime authentication must use the credential selected by the model provider. Explicit API keys and command credentials need independent ownership so cached connections and in-flight work cannot cross credential sources.

## What changed

- Register and reuse runtimes per credential source, supporting explicit provider keys and command credentials without falling back to saved login credentials.
- Track `AuthOwner` by credential manager and owner generation across WebSocket state, compaction, and scoring.
- Preserve cached identity and runtime registration state during credential-source outages or failed storage reloads. Require a successful auth reload before logout revokes credentials.
- Reject requests whose production or staging environment differs from runtime registration, including model catalog requests.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for credential selection and runtime reuse, owner isolation, source outages, failed reloads and logout recovery, and environment mismatches.

GitOrigin-RevId: 7bab55e0ea502593393df10046309fd8502edbd0

Add device-code authorization for gateway OAuth (#59822)

## Why

Gateway sign-in needs an alternative for terminals that cannot open a browser.

## What changed

- Add optional `gateway_oauth.device_authorization_url` configuration and a `login_with_device_code` API that presents a verification URL and user code, polls for approval, and persists the resulting credentials.
- Use the configured proxy and network policy, validate verification URLs, and bound OAuth responses. Support cancellation and report denied or expired codes without exposing issuer error details.

## Testing

Add tests for successful authorization and credential persistence, unsafe verification URLs, network-policy denials, denied and expired codes, and cancellation during approval or credential storage.

GitOrigin-RevId: 96398578fb866d34929e85c04eadf468d8cd3255

Allow provider selection for gateway OAuth reads and logins (#59819)

## Why

Gateway OAuth reads and logins previously used only the current provider, preventing clients from authorizing another configured provider without changing the default.

## What changed

- Add optional `modelProvider` params to `account/gatewayOAuth/read` and `account/gatewayOAuth/login`, preserving current-provider behavior for omitted or null params and selectors.
- Validate explicit providers against current managed policy without changing the default or any thread's provider.
- Retain readiness state across providers and send `account/gatewayOAuth/changed` notifications for every configured provider sharing the changed credential.
- Update protocol schemas, TypeScript types, Python models, and documentation.

## Testing

Add coverage for non-default provider login, retained readiness when alternating providers, notifications for shared credentials without starting login, and legacy TypeScript request compatibility.

GitOrigin-RevId: cfd472c322b821fe36b8c133a8de774f4ba48534

Handle TUI message submission receipts and preserve uncertain drafts (#59817)

## Why

The TUI's cached active turn can be stale when a cloud message is submitted. A lost reply also leaves delivery uncertain, so automatically resending the draft risks submitting it twice.

## What changed

- Let the cloud server choose whether an Enter submission starts or steers a turn, and apply its receipt to the matching client message ID.
- Keep Tab-queued input waiting until the admitted turn finishes, including before its start notification arrives.
- Restore rejected submissions to the composer. Hold duplicate or unconfirmed submissions out of automatic delivery until history confirms them.
- Reconcile saved drafts and pending steers by client message ID when resuming sessions, and preserve submissions belonging to other turns during interruption recovery.
- Classify cloud preflight failures as invalid parameters so rejected queued input can be restored safely.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for cloud receipt outcomes, queued-input ordering, rejected drafts, lost replies, interruption recovery, and session resume with identical message text but distinct client IDs.

GitOrigin-RevId: ec4eb581e450488434bc4614ec59273d73ffd0a1

Retry gateway credential exports after unauthorized responses (#59816)

## Why

Cached gateway command credentials need to be refreshed when the gateway rejects them with a `401`.

## What changed

Clear the cached `credential_export` token after an inference HTTP `401` or a WebSocket upgrade rejected with `401`, then rerun the command for one retry. Preserve subsequent primary authentication recovery if the retry is also unauthorized, and document the behavior.

## Testing

Add integration coverage for using a new exported token, reporting an invalid export, recovering primary authentication after the gateway retry, and stopping after a second unauthorized WebSocket upgrade.

GitOrigin-RevId: 3397476dbfd3bec1bd44f90657c4f9e17bb7df67

Pack relative relocations in x86-64 musl release builds (#59805)

## What changed

Add `-z pack-relative-relocs` to the Cargo and Bazel release linker flags for
`x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`, alongside the existing safe identical code folding.

GitOrigin-RevId: 1398ea6775e6b8ec81e624def6c23e8053363544

Support optional thread IDs in hosted file uploads (#59795)

## What changed

Add an optional `thread_id` to `HostedFileUploadContext` and include it as `codex_thread_id` in file creation requests when provided. Keep MCP app uploads without this field while retaining the thread ID in tool-call metadata.

## Testing

Extend upload tests to check inclusion and omission of `codex_thread_id`, and assert that MCP app calls retain `_meta.threadId` without adding it to file uploads.

GitOrigin-RevId: cff15b35e5130e56973f944b3b849807550d298b

repos.name: trycua/cua
repos.description: Scale computer-use 2.0 with open-source drivers, cross-OS sandboxes, and benchmarks for training, evaluation, and data generation.

commits.message:
fix(cua-driver): restore the Windows foreground only after typed input drained (#6779)

* test(cua-driver): model the Windows foreground typing restore rule in TLA+

windows_typing.tla models one foreground input turn: sends, short inserts,
read timeouts, foreground_lost, and the restore decision. With the old rule
(restore on every exit) TLC finds a stalled or short insert whose unread
input is read by the user's window. With restore-only-from-drained every
invariant holds. CUA-3679

* fix(cua-driver): restore the Windows foreground only after typed input drained

with_confirmed_foreground restored the previous foreground on every exit,
including a stalled text unit, a short SendInput and a final drain that
timed out, so input the target had not read could land in the user's
window. It also took the foreground back after foreground_lost.

The body now records a TypingTurn and restores_previous restores only when
nothing inserted may be unread and no other window took the foreground.
Otherwise the target stays in front and the error says focus was not
restored, with foreground_restored:false in the tool result. A final drain
timeout is now an input_delivery_stalled error instead of a silent success.
CUA-3679

* fix(cua-driver): mark undrained input even when the target was already in front

Browser setup fronts the browser before its Enter key, so the keyboard
helper saw previous == target and returned a stalled drain unmarked; the
caller then restored its own prior window. Mark every undrained exit.
The model gains the zero-insert SendInput exit. CUA-3679

* fix(cua-driver): do not resend the setup tab close chord while it may be unread

If Ctrl+W was inserted but not confirmed read, abort's cleanup would send
a second Ctrl+W that could close another tab once both are read. CUA-3679

* fix(cua-driver): send no setup cleanup input while a setup key may be unread

Browser setup aborts after a failed Enter or Ctrl+W. When that key was
inserted but not confirmed read, cleanup would still send Ctrl+W. Track it
on the handle, skip input-based cleanup, and report it in the refusal
detail; opened_setup_page stays true. CUA-3679

* fix(cua-driver): record an unread cleanup Ctrl+W in the setup refusal detail

abort() copied input_may_be_unread before its own cleanup Ctrl+W, and
close() dropped that send's error. Cleanup now records it and abort reads
the flag afterwards. CUA-3679

fix(cua-driver): keep a session's last use on its lifecycle record (#6773)

* fix(cua-driver): keep a session's last use on its lifecycle record

Move last_activity into LifecycleRecord and delete SESSION_ACTIVITY and
touch_session. The idle sweep re-checks in_flight and last use under the
records lock in the same critical section that removes the record, so a
call that lands after the sweep picked a session keeps it live. Revoke
walks the lifecycle records, so a declared session with no dispatch yet
is revoked too.

fix(cua-driver): keep a macOS sheet's own id for focus and snapshot scope (#6758)

* fix(cua-driver): send keys and clicks to a macOS window's open sheet

With Finder's Go to Folder sheet open, `cua set` filled the field but
Return was refused as window_not_key ("the app's focused window is
15304") and a click on 15304 was refused off_space_or_ax_unresolved.
TextEdit's Save As panel, a remote sheet, failed the same way. Sheet
elements already resolve to the window they are attached to, but the
focused-window read behind the key gate, bring_to_front and pid-only
keys used the sheet's own CGWindowID, and a request naming the sheet's
id found nothing in AXWindows, which lists only the parent.

A focused sheet now counts as the window it is attached to, through the
existing sheet-to-parent resolution, in focused_window_id_of_pid and the
focused element's window. A request that names a sheet's own id is
judged as that window: background-input facts (AX membership,
minimized, element ancestry, competing windows) use it while the event
still goes to the sheet's window and coordinates; get_window_state
walks the parent window, sheet included; bring_to_front brings the
parent and accepts the sheet in front of it. Sheets are read from each
AX window's AXSheet children, only when the id is not a listed window.
A window that is neither the target nor one of its sheets is still
refused, and the document-edit check keeps the raw focused window.

The remote Save panel's own window belongs to the panel service, so
naming it with the app's pid is still refused as another process's
window; address the panel through the document window, where its
elements and now its keys land. Windows and Linux have no sheets of
this kind.

fix(cua-driver): keep idle-end launch ownership only until a terminal end (#6738)

* fix(cua-driver): kill an app this session launched after its idle end

kill_app refused, with foreign_process_termination_denied, a process
launch_app had started for the same session label minutes earlier. The
launch is recorded under the session's key, and the registry's session
end hook deleted those records on every end, including the idle sweep
that ends a session after five minutes without calls. A client that
then starts the same label again (cua_cli does) holds a fresh session
with no proof that it launched anything.

An idle end now keeps the session's launch records; the session is only
paused and its label can be started again by its own transport. The end
hook reads the new session::session_end_reason and drops the records for
every other end (explicit, transport, process exit). An explicit
end_session drops them too when the session had already idled out,
since that end runs no hooks: the dispatch removes them when the caller
owns the session. Each kill still reproves the process fingerprint, so
a reused pid never inherits ownership, and a different session label
is still refused. Core only, so macOS, Windows and Linux behave alike.

Reported downstream as HoloWork HW-97.

The browser engine shares that store and drops a session's records from
its own end hook too; it now keeps them on an idle end as well. Found
live: with only the registry hook changed, a kill after the idle sweep
was still refused.

(cherry picked from commit 9d9fa7fb704cf04f8838aa35d6fda1b48ce69cdb)

* fix(cua-driver): end idle-kept launch records on every terminal end

An idle end keeps a session's launch records so its label can kill what
it launched after a restart. Three paths broke that promise:

- Transport teardown and revocation listed only live sessions, so an
  idled session's records outlived both. Idle ends of named sessions
  are now tracked as dormant, and a later explicit, transport or revoke
  end makes them terminal and reruns the end hooks with its reason.
  end_session no longer drops the records itself after dispatch.
- The browser engine reaps its browsers on every end but kept their
  pids in the shared store across an idle end, and classified browser
  ownership by pid alone. It now drops exactly the pids it reaps and
  re-attests the process fingerprint before treating a pid as its own.
- A revival could land between an end and its cleanup, which then
  erased the new episode's launches. Revival is refused under the
  tombstone lock while cleanup is pending.

* fix(cua-driver): finish an idle run's cleanup with the terminal end that replaced it

A terminal end arriving while idle hooks still ran handed out cleanup
progress the idle run then abandoned, so revival could be admitted
before the terminal hooks ran. The running idle pass now runs the
terminal hooks itself before it releases the progress.

* fix(cua-driver): clear capture scope inside the tracked session cleanup

An end that paused on a cursor reader cleared the capture policy after
a revival had already finished its hooks and bound a new one. Clearing
it in retry_session_cleanup puts it behind the same revival barrier.

* fix(cua-driver): let a terminal end replace an idle end deferred behind a dispatch

A pending idle end kept its reason when an explicit, transport or revoke
end arrived before the in-flight dispatch finished, so the session ran
only idle cleanup and kept its launch records.

* fix(cua-driver): bind a managed browser to its launch fingerprint

The engine matched its browsers by pid and re-attested against the
shared store, so a later launch_app that reused the pid passed as the
browser, and reaping the browser removed that launch's record. Each
managed browser now keeps its own fingerprint for both.

A control can be disabled only because its app is in the background.
When the target app is not frontmost, the element_disabled refusal now
recommends foreground delivery, which run_steps' foreground_fallback
reads, and a foreground call into such an app skips the early AXEnabled
read so activation can enable the control first.

The SDK workflow only ran when the CD run concluded success, so a failed
installer-bump job skipped the Python and npm publish for 0.39.0. Also wait
for PR checks to register before watching them, which made the bump fail
immediately with 'no checks reported'.

fix(cua-driver): refuse clicks fast while a detached session's dialog blocks the tab (#6646)

* test(cua-driver): a dialog Chromium dropped without a close event must not lock the tab

* fix(cua-driver): clear a dialog record that Chromium no longer shows

browser_dialog now drops the record when Page.handleJavaScriptDialog
answers 'No dialog is showing', and the CDP reader drops a session's

fix(cua-driver): press a shortcut's key where the keyboard layout types it on macOS (#6659)

* fix(cua-driver): press a shortcut's key where the keyboard layout types it on macOS

On an AZERTY Mac, `hotkey cmd+a` sent to Slack quit it. Every macOS
chord path (press_key, hotkey, their no-auth and global HID variants)
mapped letters, digits and symbols to fixed US key positions, so cmd+a
pressed the key that types q there, cmd+w pressed z, and cmd+= zoomed
out.

A single printable character is now pressed by the key that types it
with the chord's modifiers held, read with UCKeyTranslate over the main
typing keys: the Command layer when Command is held (QWERTY on Russian
and on Dvorak - QWERTY Command), the Control layer when Control is held
(the key that types ^C for ctrl+c; Return and Tab are left out), the
plain layer otherwise. Of several keys, the US one is kept, then the one
that types the character with no modifier. A character the layer has no
key for, named keys, and every key when the layout has no Unicode data
keep the US position, as macOS does for a shortcut whose character is
not on the layout.

Checked against the 249 layouts installed with macOS 26: for letters,
digits and punctuation with Command or Control, every chord presses a
key that types its character, or the US key when none does.

Windows already sends layout virtual keys and X11 resolves keysyms on
the current keymap, so both press the right key for a letter.

Reported downstream as HoloWork HW-106.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(cua-driver): keep US key positions for Screen Sharing chords

Screen Sharing forwards virtual key positions to the guest, which applies
its own layout. Reading the host layout there pressed the AZERTY A key
(US Q) for cmd+a on a US guest. Chords aimed at Screen Sharing now keep
the US positions its physical text path already assumes.

* fix(cua-driver): keep US positions for desktop chords into Screen Sharing

press_key_global reaches the frontmost app, which may be Screen Sharing. It now resolves its key through target_key_code like every other chord path, and layout_key_code is gone so no path can bypass the Screen Sharing rule.

fix(cua-driver): find a macOS app by any name it ships, without guessing (#6657)

* fix(cua-driver): find a macOS app by any name it ships

launch_app by name could not find an installed app unless the name was
an exact `<name>.app` directly inside one of six folders, although its
schema takes the app's display name. Adobe InDesign 2026 (installed one
folder down), "Échecs" (Chess on a French Mac, a name only its
InfoPlist.loctable has) and an app whose display name differs from its
file name all answered APP_NOT_INSTALLED. locate_by_name listed the
localized-name scan as skipped until a non-English name turned up.

When the existing fast paths miss, locate_by_name now scans the same
roots and one folder down, and matches every name a bundle ships: its
file name, CFBundleDisplayName and CFBundleName, and their localized
values from InfoPlist.loctable and each .lproj InfoPlist.strings
(legacy folder names like German.lproj included). The ranking lives in
a new core module, app_names: names compare without case (Turkish's
dotted and dotless i included) and canonically decomposed, but
otherwise as shipped; forgiving a user's spelling (accents, spaces) is
the client's job. An exact name beats a name the query starts, and a
name in one of the user's languages beats the same rank in another. A
tie at the top is refused as APP_NAME_AMBIGUOUS with the candidates,
and a name found only inside another stays APP_NOT_INSTALLED with
closest names as suggestions, never a guess. launch_app launches the
bundle the name resolved to instead of resolving it a second time.

Checked on the 83 apps installed on a macOS 26 Mac: each of the 2,783
names they ship in any language, given as shipped, in lower and upper
case, and decomposed, finds its own app (7,934 queries, none missed or
wrong).

Windows and Linux name lookup are unchanged.

Reported downstream as HoloWork HW-103, HW-104 and HW-7.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(cua-driver): keep each copy of an app and read Base names

Copies of one bundle id stay separate bundles, so a name only a later copy
ships launches that copy; at a top tie the first copy still wins over a
refusal. Base localizations count as unlocalized names, and a root that is
itself a bundle is scanned as that bundle.

* fix(cua-driver): rank every app name before guessing a bundle id

locate_by_name no longer returns an exact <name>.app before ranking, so a
file name another app also shows is refused as ambiguous. A bundle id is
tried only when no app ships the name. Finder is scanned as a root. The
launch helpers take the resolved locator, so a bundle-id locator is not
looked up again as a name.

* fix(cua-driver): try a known bundle id first and scan each bundle once

A bundle id LaunchServices knows no longer loses to an app name it starts,
and a bundle under two overlapping roots is one candidate, not a tie with
itself.

docs(remote-access): propose client-owned P2P transport (#23636)

### What this PR does

Before this PR: the client-owned P2P design was recorded outside the
desktop repository that maintains the shared remote-access packages.

After this PR: a bilingual proposed Agent Note defines the shared
package boundary, endpoint adapters, authenticated signaling, connection
selection, bounded binary transport, and implementation acceptance
criteria.

Fixes: N/A — no linked issue.

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

Keep the P2P implementation with the desktop-maintained shared packages
while leaving the existing Relay runtime and account service boundaries
intact. The proposal uses `node-datachannel` on desktop and
`react-native-webrtc` on mobile behind an independent
`@cherrystudio/remote-transport/p2p` entry point.

The following tradeoffs were made: attempt P2P before handing a new
connection to business traffic; authenticate the candidate with fresh
Noise and grants; retain Relay fallback and bounded
negotiation/buffering. STUN is configurable and optional to self-host.

The following alternatives were considered: server-owned P2P signaling,
a `relay-client/p2p` export, additional signaling/TURN services,
migration of active business sessions, and a separate custom UDP
transport.

Links to places where the discussion took place: N/A — agreed in the
development conversation. Related Relay integration work: desktop #23505
and [mobile
#1600](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio-app/pull/1600).

### Agent Note / Spec

Agent Note:
[English](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/blob/docs/remote-p2p-plan-20261105/.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-11-05-remote-p2p.md)
/
[中文](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/blob/docs/remote-p2p-plan-20261105/.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-11-05-remote-p2p.zh.md).

Spec PR: This PR.

Acceptance criteria: the following are defined for subsequent
implementation and remain pending:

- AC1: shared package ownership, portable exports, and isolated native
dependencies.
- AC2: new/old endpoint compatibility, pairing, direct access, and P2P
opt-out.
- AC3: identity, generation, grants, and single-use candidate binding
without authorization bypass.
- AC4: one business connection, bounded negotiation, and deterministic
handoff/failure handling.
- AC5: real binary transfers, slow-reader backpressure, bounded queues,
and cleanup.
- AC6: cross-network/mobile lifecycle validation, existing Relay
fallback, and measured performance.

### Verification

- Documentation: `pnpm docs:check` passed (links, structure,
frontmatter, Agent Notes, bilingual pairing, terminology, and generated
index).
- Documentation: focused `pnpm docs:check-pairing` passed; scoped Oxfmt
check passed for the translation sidecar. Markdown is excluded by the
repository formatter configuration.
- Scope: `pnpm change:scope --base origin/main` confirmed only the two

signature, and DCO sign-off passed.

documentation-only PR does not claim those criteria are satisfied.

None. Documentation only.

Review the ownership, authentication, handoff, and deployment boundaries
before implementation. The note remains `proposed`. This PR contains no
package, application, Relay runtime, or deployment code changes; the

docs(spec): propose illustrations within assistant replies (#23551)

### What this PR does

Before this PR:

There is no upstream-approved contract for generating illustrations at
specific positions in ordinary assistant replies.

After this PR:

The proposal specifies opt-in inline illustration intents, immediate
placeholders, asynchronous generation, saved-message ownership,
cancellation and explicit retry. It now defines independent Automatic
maximum and Forced target settings, a one-time upgrade from the
exploratory exact-count switch, and per-illustration selection of
user-image references surviving actual request context shaping.

This PR changes only the proposed English/Chinese Agent Note and its
consistency record. It ships no application behavior.

Fixes: N/A — no linked upstream issue.

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

An external MCP cannot own placement or saved-answer lifecycle within
ordinary Cherry Studio replies. Main-process parsing and job/file
ownership give live views and persisted messages a consistent ordered
contract.

```text
reply → ordered text/placeholders
complete prompt + optional user originals → background generation → saved illustration
```

The following tradeoffs were made:

- Forced mode asks for an exact target through the system prompt; the
parser enforces that same maximum. Missing or truncated intents do not
trigger an extra language-model call. Automatic and Forced quantities
default to 1, range from 1–10, and persist independently.
- Only materialized user images in the current topic/branch and actual
model request are candidates. Invalid, unsupported, excessive or
unreadable selections explicitly fail that illustration rather than
silently dropping inputs.
- Reuse the default painting model and managed storage. Two concurrent
requests, a five-minute active timeout, restart abandonment and explicit
provider-billed retry bound ownership.
- Initial scope is ordinary single-model chat, with generation Off by
default. Agent sessions and multi-model reply groups are excluded.

The following alternatives were considered:

- A standalone MCP or proxy still needs application changes for
placement and persistence.
- Renderer-only parsing leaves saved messages and duplicate-submission
control inconsistent.
- Separate image configuration duplicates existing capabilities; an
exact-count switch alongside Forced mode duplicates quantity controls.

Links to places where the discussion took place: [implementation draft
#23556](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/pull/23556). The draft
is local-exploration evidence, not upstream approval.

### Agent Note / Spec

Agent Note: [English
proposal](https://github.com/leezehuan/cherry-studio/blob/de3d228cb65dcb5b823dbcc16216efa3c8c8db84/.agents/notes/proposed/feature/2026-11-03-reply-illustrations.md),
[Chinese
proposal](https://github.com/leezehuan/cherry-studio/blob/de3d228cb65dcb5b823dbcc16216efa3c8c8db84/.agents/notes/proposed/feature/2026-11-03-reply-illustrations.zh.md),
with their sibling consistency record.

Spec PR: This PR.

Acceptance criteria:

- AC1 — Persist Automatic, Forced and Off modes across restarts.
- AC2 — Reserve the original position and start image work on a complete
intent while later text continues.
- AC3 — Replace placeholders in order and retain illustrations in saved
replies.
- AC4 — Prevent duplicate submissions on repeated updates or remounts.
- AC5 — Preserve ordinary text and code examples across marker/chunk
boundaries.
- AC6 — Preserve the written answer and show an explicit image failure
state.
- AC7 — Operate without a separate image MCP or its loopback server.
- AC8 — Expose independent mode-specific quantities and enforce the same
active limit in prompts and parsing.
- AC9 — Expand the complete prompt as plain text beside its
illustration.
- AC10 — Convert old exact-count settings once while preserving
subsequent user choices.
- AC11 — Let the model select only application-issued user-image
candidates present in the actual request.
- AC12 — Send clean prompts and deduplicated ordered originals through a
supported image-input mode; omitted references stay text-only.
- AC13 — Fail invalid, unsupported, excessive or unreadable selections
explicitly without losing the answer.
- AC14 — Show original names/previews and retain file ownership after
deletion of the upload message.
- AC15 — Keep the saved prompt/selection on explicit retry, use the
current painting model, and recheck inputs and limits.

Leezehuan, the implementation author, owns verification. Each AC assigns
its test/scenario owner in the note. This Spec establishes target
behavior and does not claim implementation completion.

### Verification

- Updated English and Chinese proposals were compared for quantity
rules, candidate exclusions, provider input modes, failure behavior,
ownership, retries and AC1–AC15. Their existing sidecar matches both
blobs.
- All seven documentation gates were run on this Spec checkout through
the installed `tsx` CLI: links, structure, frontmatter, Agent Note
format, pairing, terminology and generated index. All passed.
- `change:scope --base upstream/main`, the final three-file diff and

- The update commit is SSH-signed and DCO-signed-off. GitHub reports
