fix(relay): regenerate missing image thumbnails on request (#9174)

## Summary

Clients ask for an image's small `.thumb.webp` thumbnail first and fall
back to `.thumb.jpg` on a 404. Images uploaded before
[#9003](https://github.com/block/buzz/pull/9003) only have the JPEG, so
every client pays an extra 404 for them and transparent avatars keep
showing on a black background. The same thing happens when a thumbnail
write failed at upload time.

When a thumbnail variant is missing but its image original exists, the
relay now regenerates the thumbnails on that request and serves them
with 200. It uses the same generator and storage writes as upload, which
are now one shared `store_image_thumbnails`. Later requests are ordinary
hits.

- GET (full and range) and HEAD both regenerate, so a HEAD-then-GET
client sees the same result.
- Regeneration runs only after the existing tenant, auth and sidecar
checks for that thumbnail.
- It is bounded. At most two regenerations run per relay process
(`try_acquire`, no waiting), and originals larger than `max_image_bytes`
are skipped. In both cases, and for non-images, missing originals or any
decode or storage error, the response is the 404 it is today. Errors are
logged at warn.

### Related issue

Follow-up to [#9003](https://github.com/block/buzz/pull/9003) and
[#9105](https://github.com/block/buzz/pull/9105), which made relays
write WebP thumbnails and clients prefer them.

### Testing

Two router-level tests against Postgres and MinIO upload a PNG through
the real route, then delete its thumbnails:

- `missing_thumbnail_is_regenerated_from_image_original`: GET and HEAD
of `.thumb.webp` and `.thumb.jpg` return 200 with the right content
type, and both objects are stored afterward. With regeneration disabled
it fails with `GET webp: 404, expected 200`.
- `missing_thumbnail_is_not_regenerated_when_unsafe`: a non-image blob,
a missing original, an oversize original and a busy relay (no free
permit) each return 404 and store nothing. Once the permits are free,
the same request returns 200. Removing the size cap or the permit guard
fails it.

feat(loadgen): model agent turns and sustained holds (#9182)

## Why

The loadgen agent polled HTTP `/query` every few seconds. A real agent
harness (`buzz-acp`) never polls when idle. It works in bursts around
each prompt, and those bursts are the load a fleet of active agents puts
on the relay. To answer "how well does the relay handle N active users
plus their agents over a sustained period", the loadgen needs to model
those bursts and hold them for an hour or more.

## What

- **`[agent.turn]`**: an idle agent starts a turn on a Poisson schedule
and runs one turn at a time. A turn lasts 0.5–1.5 × `mean_secs`. The
steps follow `buzz-acp`:
- **Start**: a `limit:1` `/query` finds the message to answer
(`http_query`), which stands in for the harness's subscription. Then the
harness's own reads (`turn_context` op): for a threaded message, its
thread context in one `/query` (root by id, newest 13 replies, the
agent's own newest reply) plus a `/count` when the window is full. Then
kind:39000 metadata, project home (kind:30621, kind:30617) and the
author's profile. Then two kind:7 reactions on the message.
- **Work**: typing every `typing_secs` and observer frames of
`frame_bytes` every `frame_secs` over the socket, plus `reads` tool
reads (`/query`, limit 50).
- **End**: a threaded reply, under the root that NIP-10 `resolve()`
gives. Then reaction removal: query own reactions, then a kind:5
deletion for each.
- One HTTP action at a time runs next to the socket. Socket publishes
(presence, typing, frames) don't wait for their OK: each OK is matched
as it arrives, one missing after 30 s is an error, and at most 128 wait
at once. So the socket and HTTP sides stay on schedule while either is
slow, as in the harness. A 2xx response that doesn't decode counts as an
error. No agent request starts after the stop.
- The request mix approximates sustained turns: every turn reads like a
first prompt. A harness already holding a thread reads 25 replies (not
13), batches profile lookups and caches project-home lookups for 30 s,
so this reads profiles and project homes more often than a busy harness.
- `agent.channel_subscriptions`: one live mentions REQ per channel, like
the harness. `agent.presence_interval_secs`: presence heartbeats.
- `agent.query_interval_secs = 0` turns polling off.
- **Sustained holds**: ramp steps may now repeat a level. A 60-minute
hold can be six 600 s steps, each one reported and judged, so drift
shows up as a trend.
- New op `turn_context`. New scenario
`perf/scenarios/local-agent-turns.toml`. `perf/LOADGEN.md` documents the
model.

All new fields are off by default (`turn.per_hour = 0`, presence 0, no
channel subscriptions), so existing scenarios run unchanged.

## What got simpler

- The agent loop's per-action branches now go through one `sent` result.
The observer frame build, the HTTP submit and the `/query` body read are
shared helpers. The old inline frame code is gone.
- "Hold for an hour, judge every 10 minutes" is now a ramp of repeated
levels. No new abort-window concept was needed.
- Identified debt, not touched here: abort is still judged only at step
end, so a collapsed relay is not detected until the step closes.
Repeated short steps reduce that gap.

## Testing

- On a Blox workstation at 6bb151d1: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy
-p buzz-test-client --all-targets -D warnings`, and `cargo test -p
buzz-test-client --lib` (103 passed). The five turn tests passed 10/10
repeated runs. Three mutants (awaiting the OK again, dropping the stop
guard in `submit`, dropping it in `query`) each fail a test.
- `local-agent-turns` against a local relay at 6bb151d1: both steps 0
errors, 0 clients cancelled.
- `agent_turns_read_react_stream_reply_and_remove_their_reactions` runs
an agent against a fake socket and a fake HTTP relay. It asserts the
exact thread-context filters and count, the metadata, project and
profile reads, the reactions, typing, frames and presence, and that
typing or frames arrive while a tool read is held. It also asserts the
threaded reply under the right root and the deletion of exactly the
reactions the agent added.
- `agent_turns_keep_moving_while_socket_oks_lag`: the same journey with
every socket OK 1.5 s late, past the 1 s heartbeat.
- `a_turn_stopped_while_adding_a_reaction_sends_nothing_more` and
`a_turn_stopped_while_reading_its_reactions_deletes_none`: the stop
lands while a reaction POST or removal query is held, and no request
follows it.
- `agent_turn_reads_that_do_not_decode_are_errors`: 200 responses that
are not events count as errors, and no turn reacts.
- `a_timed_out_route_is_recovered_again_after_a_renewal` (desktop) fails
2 times in 10 on unmodified main as well. That flake is pre-existing and
unrelated to this change.
- Live: a single-relay run with 10k humans and 20k turn-taking agents
(held at 1x for 60 min, then 1.5x and 2x). Results will be added here.

Fixes five defects in the `buzz` CLI.

no longer publishes. It now reads the viewer's DM group metadata (kind
39000, `t=dm`, `p=viewer`) and drops every DM listed in the viewer's
newest relay-signed visibility snapshot (kind 30622), the same hidden
set the desktop uses. It keeps paging until it has the requested number
of visible DMs or the history runs out, so hidden DMs never crowd out
visible ones. Hidden DMs stay hidden; reopening one brings it back.
- **Uploads accepted only images and MP4.** The CLI now leaves type
acceptance to the relay, as the desktop does: unsniffable files go up as
`application/octet-stream`, and the relay's own allow and deny rules
apply. Local size caps match the relay's defaults (50 MB images, 500 MB
MP4, 100 MB other files). `messages send --file` adds an imeta
`filename` (the basename, with control characters and both path
separators replaced by spaces) and writes non-media files as a plain
link (`[name](<url>)`) instead of `![image](…)`; inline media still
embeds.
- **`messages get --kinds` silently ignored bad values.** Any
non-numeric or out-of-range (above 65535) kind now fails with a
bad-input error, exit 1.

bad input (exit 1), and `messages send --file` returns the upload's own
error instead of wrapping every failure as `Other` (exit 4). The "auth
tag may be stale" hint on every 403 is gone: the relay answers 403 for
ordinary permission denials, such as a non-moderator reading moderation
data, so the hint misled.

`--relay` and no `BUZZ_RELAY_URL`, the CLI uses the relay an agent's
inherited `BUZZ_CREDENTIAL_PROVIDER` token acts on, from its `describe`
answer. If that lists several relays, it fails with exit 1 and asks for
`--relay`. An explicit flag or env var still wins and is still checked
against the credential. Paired tokens never choose a relay, `auth
desktop unpair` never asks the desktop, and otherwise the default stays
`http://localhost:3000`. Help text says so.

Cache channel memberships once per user (#9060)

## Summary

A cold client in 280 channels can issue 280 separate membership reads,
each checking out a database connection. Cache the user's complete
active-membership set per community so those channel checks share one
read.

Keep the existing membership rules and 10-second freshness bound,
measured from connection checkout. Moka now accounts for snapshot size
with a 64 MiB weighted budget per relay. Each snapshot holds at most
16,384 UUIDs. The database pool controls query concurrency; there is no
separate 16-load limiter. Channel discovery keeps its separate filtering
rules. No schema change or migration.

### Request flow

1. Look up the community/user entry in Moka. A fresh complete snapshot
answers channel checks by binary search.
2. A fresh `PointChecks` marker sends each check to the database; it
stores no permission decision.
3. On a miss, create a lightweight, weighted loading entry. Requests for
that user share its lock.
4. Recheck after acquiring the lock. If waiting for that user’s lock
times out, use a point check.
5. Fetch at most 16,385 membership IDs. Above 16,384, retain a
`PointChecks` marker instead of a partial list.
6. Otherwise, sort the complete list into a compact immutable UUID
array.
7. Replace the loading entry through Moka. Its weigher now includes the
completed payload plus estimated bookkeeping.
8. Let Moka manage admission, eviction, and 10-second expiry. Membership
changes remove the relevant user or community entries.

Publication and invalidation share a short synchronous lock. A loader
publishes only while its original loading lock still identifies the
current entry. An old load can finish its original request, but cannot
repopulate an invalidated entry. Database failures propagate;
cancellation releases the user lock. Both database-query futures
allocate only when used, which keeps nested handler futures small. Cache
hits allocate neither query.

The budget covers estimated retained cache weight. Moka enforces it on a
best-effort basis; query buffers and snapshots held by active requests
can add memory. This is not a strict process-memory ceiling. Empty
entries and fallback markers have nonzero weight. There is no separate
memory-reservation or eviction implementation.

### Operational notes

- A newly granted membership can be absent from another relay's cached
snapshot until the Redis invalidation arrives, or until the 10-second
freshness bound expires if it is lost. Cached write checks can briefly
deny access; explicit channel subscriptions already confirm missing
membership against the database.
- `buzz_membership_cache_hits_total` counts channel checks served from a
fresh snapshot. `buzz_membership_cache_misses_total` counts bounded
full-set load attempts. Timeouts now use point checks, recorded by
`buzz_membership_cache_fallbacks_total{reason="wait_timeout"}`. The
other fallback reason is `oversize`; the `load_limit` path has been
removed. Before/after hit ratios are not directly comparable.
- Keep `channel_id` in membership invalidation messages for
compatibility with older relay instances during rolling deployments,
even though the new local cache invalidates by user.

### Related issue

Follow-up to #9012.

### Testing

**Current head: `a79a40cc5a6e4c7c611ed1b6bcbdd8b8c0490ef2`, including
main `f82944e3180e28502f5ea599ac9973aa6398ddb3`.** Commit `393b32583`
fixes the large-membership test fixture by refreshing planner statistics
after bulk seeding. Before that fix, the boundary test failed locally
and was the sole PostgreSQL test failure in GitHub CI (1,409/1,410
passed); the repaired test passes in 3.54 seconds including setup and
all checks. An isolated copy of the production schema/query at 16,384
memberships selected a quadratic join without statistics and a hash join
after `ANALYZE`; the latter executed in 10.86 ms. The cap and freshness
rules are unchanged.

At this exact head, the full regular buzz-db/buzz-relay suite passed
1,963/1,963 and the full PostgreSQL suite passed 1,310/1,310. This
includes both previously failing Git-auth cases and the repaired
membership boundary test (2.302 seconds including setup and checks).
Rebuilt signed live checks also passed. Full local `just ci` passed
(exit 0). GitHub CI is green: 79 successful checks and 31 skipped, with
none pending or failed at verification. The [verified matched A/B at
this
head](https://github.com/block/buzz/pull/9060#issuecomment-6673813172)
against main `f82944e31` is complete: four 6,600-client arms in both
orders show 90.98–91.24% fewer membership-cache queries and 73.76–74.23%
fewer authorization checkouts. Auth error rates improved in both orders;
auth p99 and overall operation errors were mixed. Average relay RSS
increased 1.6–4.3%, with flat to slightly lower sampled peaks;
PostgreSQL average PSS decreased 1.7–5.2%, with mixed peaks. The
16,384-row production query executed in 24.953 ms after fixture ANALYZE.
Signed pool-4 and 4,097/16,384/16,385-membership probes passed. See the

[completed A/B at the earlier `6f0358875`
head](https://github.com/block/buzz/pull/9060#issuecomment-6672419096)
is reported separately; it does not establish current-head performance.

Users above 16,384 memberships still use uncached authoritative point
checks. The higher cap reduces how many users hit that fallback; it does
not eliminate the cost. Each maximum-size list contains 256 KiB of UUIDs
plus overhead within the unchanged 64 MiB estimated cache budget.
Temporary allocations and retained readers can add memory outside that
budget.

`a79a40cc5a6e4c7c611ed1b6bcbdd8b8c0490ef2`, using the rebuilt relay and
an isolated database: non-members cannot post; grants allow both private
channels; removal blocks writes and delivery from A while B continues;
re-add and resubscription restore A. Delivery checks completed in 1.776
s after removal and 0.466 s after re-add. A user grown above 5,000
memberships used snapshots with no oversize fallback. After growing
beyond 16,384, authoritative point checks still enforced removal and
re-add; four oversize fallbacks were recorded. The relay stopped and all
three test ports closed. Binary SHA-256:

start an isolated local relay as described in

before membership, grant both, remove one, then re-add. Subscribe to
both channels during the test. At the current head, verify a user with
5,000 memberships still uses snapshots, then give the second account
more than 16,384 memberships and repeat the permission checks through
the fallback path. This was agent verification; human confirmation is
still pending.

#### Historical load test, before the memory-bound refactor

These measurements apply to `519509451`, before weighted eviction, the
per-user cap, and bounded loads. The refactored version was subsequently
measured at `6f0358875`; see the linked report above. The current-head
comparison is complete and reported separately
[above](https://github.com/block/buzz/pull/9060#issuecomment-6673813172).

Compared base `f9ef721e688847ed0c1512081160b6e42cdf92fd` with head
`519509451c10d94074f597124d19f2254f0b96d1` on a dedicated Linux
workstation. Ran base → fix, then fix → base. Each arm used 6,600
clients, 100 connects/second, six generator shards, and a 300-second
hold. Both versions used pool size 50, the same notices index, CPU
allocation, restored fixture, and load generator
(`4813b8cd15411355f05599e263ab15dd04e7afcc`). All four arms and 24 shard
reports completed; recorded binary hashes, fixture manifests, index DDL,
and shard configurations were verified.

| Metric | First pair: base | First pair: fix | Reverse pair: base |
Reverse pair: fix |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Per-channel membership query calls | 1,319,382 | 7,205 | 1,367,525 |

| All membership-related query calls | 1,419,429 | 216,639 | 1,457,453 |

Linux page cache was not dropped. The first baseline arm performed

fix(relay): close legacy sockets after community FI upgrades (#8991)

## Summary

When a community starts requiring NIP-FI, the periodic community
revalidator now closes its existing legacy root and audio WebSockets
with Close 1008. It reads current policy from the writer by immutable
community ID, with a 500 ms budget per read. Failed reads retry on later
sweeps; late registrations are caught by the next pass.

Enforced FI admissions survive. Optional-shadow admissions remain
legacy. Off and repair mode retain their existing behavior. No client
request or Redis notification is needed.

The default sweep interval is 30 seconds, not a deadline during database
failure, overload or paused processes. Already-running requests and
descendant work may finish. Receipts prove policy acceptance and remain
`pending`. The `pending_reasons` value changes from
`registry_baseline_unverified` to `connection_closure_unverified`;
clients must tolerate unknown reasons. This change does not certify
fleet-wide completion.

### Related issue

[BUZZ-512](https://linear.app/squareup/issue/BUZZ-512), under the
revised eventual-closure scope. Builds on merged #8985 and #8988. The
replacement starts from main and adds no activation schema or migration.

### Rollout and limits

There is no new flag. Count already-required communities before
deployment: each relay closes their legacy sockets on its first
successful sweep. Closures within a community can cause simultaneous
reconnects. Keep new upgrades disabled until every serving relay runs
this version.

Observe `buzz_community_auth_policy_checks_total{outcome}` and
`buzz_community_auth_policy_disconnects_total` per relay, and verify
real idle root/audio Close 1008 probes plus FI reconnects. Counters
record checks and cancellation requests, not fleet completion. A binary
rollback requires no migration and restores the old pending reason, but
loses eventual closure; it does not undo durable policy. See the
[operator
contract](https://github.com/block/buzz/blob/1c74532516f697c2f06498646326f8c479574b14/docs/community-auth-upgrades.md).

### Testing

The real-socket journey runs a local relay against isolated PostgreSQL
and Redis. It covers idle root/audio closure after a durable change
without pubsub, actual read timeouts and recovery, late registration on
both routes, FI reconnects, unrelated sockets, and Off/repair/Enforce
controls.

With local PostgreSQL and Redis configured per the repository's test
guide, run:

```sh
CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target/fi-closure-review scripts/postgres-test-run.sh -p buzz-relay --lib -E 'test(sweep_closes_idle_root_audio_and_late_registrations_after_read_recovery)'
```

Expected: one passing journey, covering both late-registration routes
and all socket controls.

The journey passed at `1c74532516f697c2f06498646326f8c479574b14` in a
branch-specific build target (5.56 seconds). Independent source review
has no remaining P1/P2 findings. Earlier shared-target results are
unreliable and are not acceptance evidence. All mandatory push hooks
passed in the same isolated target, including Rust unit tests, both
Tauri Clippy modes, Tauri tests and file-size checks. Hosted CI passed
at this head. The full local `just ci` chain was not completed. Human
runtime acceptance remains open. No merge or deployment is included.

Studio: preserve S3 dataset files with colliding names (#16830)

## What was broken

S3 audio datasets can silently pair transcripts with the wrong
recording. Distinct object keys can map to one local filename, so the
later download replaces the earlier recording while both manifest rows
remain. Manifest shards can also overwrite each other, and structured
downloads overwrite existing files in an explicitly supplied
destination.

## Repro

1. On main at `0ab3f0773`, prepare an S3 audio dataset containing
distinct `datasets/audio/clip.wav` and `datasets/audio//clip.wav`
objects. Reference each by its full S3 URI in a JSONL manifest.
2. Load it through `prepare_s3_dataset_download`.
3. Both rewritten audio paths point to the second recording. Case-only
and NFC/NFD filename differences cause the same loss on case-insensitive
or normalization-insensitive filesystems.

## Fix

Reserve distinct local paths before downloading, using the existing
suffix allocator with case-insensitive, Unicode-normalized reservations.
Keep the original S3 key-to-path mapping for JSON, JSONL and CSV
reference rewriting. Existing local files are preserved.

Parquet references cannot be rewritten here. If an audio filename must
change, fail before downloading with guidance instead of returning a
dataset bound to the wrong file. Non-colliding Parquet audio paths stay
unchanged, and colliding Parquet manifest shards can still be renamed
safely.

## Test

Thirteen initial regression cases fail on main. Expanded coverage checks
recordings and transcripts across JSON, JSONL and CSV, manifest shards,
generated suffix collisions, existing files, and Parquet refusal and
compatibility paths. Tests use the existing fake S3 client with real
local files; no AWS credentials or GPU are needed.

From `studio/backend`:

```text
$ python -m pytest -q --tb=short --timeout=330 tests/test_s3_audio_dataset.py tests/test_s3_dataset.py
97 passed in 1.95s
```

```text
$ python -m pytest -q --tb=short -n 4 --dist loadgroup --timeout=330 tests/test_s3_audio_dataset.py tests/test_s3_dataset.py tests/test_s3_runtime.py tests/test_s3_optional.py
120 passed in 11.16s
```

All seven repository checks, the pinned formatter and strict i18n parity
pass locally. No schema or dependency changes.

Studio: stop WebKit restyling the whole page when dialogs, menus and the browser pane open or close (#16961)

## Problem

On long chats in WebKit (the macOS app, and the Linux app's WebKitGTK),
closing any dialog or menu took 5 to 7 seconds, and on Linux WebKit the
browser pane took over 20 seconds to open. Chromium (Windows) was not
affected.

WebKit restyles every element on the page when certain document-level
listeners or stylesheets change:

| Side effect (Playwright WebKit, 1 -> 100 turns) | WebKit | Chromium |
|---|---|---|
| Add / remove a non-passive `wheel` or `touch*` listener on document |
27-38 ms -> 2.6-2.8 s | 0 |
| Add / remove a `pointermove` / `pointerleave` listener on document |
25-35 ms -> 2.6-2.7 s | 0.1 ms |
| Remove an injected `<style>` | 60 ms -> 2.95 s | 11 ms |
| Body `data-scroll-locked`, `pointer-events`, `aria-hidden`, focus
restore | under 100 ms | under 4 ms |

Three things hit those paths:

- Radix's scroll lock (`react-remove-scroll`) adds non-passive wheel and
touch listeners on the document when a dialog or modal menu opens and
removes them on close, and `react-remove-scroll-bar` removes its
injected stylesheet on close.
- Closing a dialog while focus is still inside it during the exit
animation (Settings, command palette, search, rename, shortcuts) costs
one more full pass.
- `react-resizable-panels` removes and re-adds its document pointer
listeners each time the chat's panel group re-registers, which is what
the browser pane triggers (3 passes on open, 2 on close, with or without
any CSS).

## Fix

- `src/lib/remove-scroll.tsx`, aliased for `react-remove-scroll` in
`vite.config.ts`: the same component and the same `data-scroll-locked`
counter on `<body>`, but no document listeners; the styles the library
injected live permanently in `index.css`. Under a modal layer nothing
outside it can be wheel-scrolled anyway (body is `pointer-events: none`
and the thread sits under the #16902 cover), and lists inside dialogs
scroll on their own.
- `src/lib/pointer-listener-pin.ts`: one passive no-op document listener
per pointer event type registered at startup, so the panel library's add
and remove no longer change the set of listener types WebKit tracks.
- `index.css`: the transparent cover #16902 puts over the thread while a
modal is open now also covers the side pane (browser, research). The
pane sets its own `pointer-events: auto` once shown, so without the
library's document listeners its file view would scroll under a modal
menu; the cover blocks it without a per-open listener.
- `index.css`: elements that restore their own pointer events stay inert
under a modal layer, so a wheel over them cannot scroll what sits behind
it. Two class-keyed rules, CSS only:
- inside a dialog or menu Radix has turned into a lower layer (for
example the Skills list under its actions menu);
- in the page while the lock is up (toolbars, the Downloads card,
sidebar row actions), except the thread (its cover handles it), the top
dialog, popper popups, and window chrome, toasts and overlays meant to
work over a modal (marked `modal-pe-live`).
- The side-pane cover keys on a static class, so toggling the lock only
restyles those elements: about 13 ms at 200 turns in the long-chat gate
(budget 30 ms).
- `vite.config.ts`: `react-remove-scroll/UI` is pre-bundled for the dev
server. It is only imported by the stand-in, so a cold dev server found
it late and reloaded the page, which native Safari did not recover from.
- `src/lib/closing-dialog-focus.ts`: when a dialog starts its exit
animation with focus inside it, the focused element is blurred; Radix
still returns focus to the trigger afterwards.

## Results

Real macOS (GitHub `macos-15`, real WebKit, 150 turns, 2 reps, all arms
on one runner), time to close:

| Surface | Before | Scroll-lock replacement only | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Settings | 4,982 ms | 4,130 ms | 970 ms |
| Command palette | 6,948 ms | 734 ms | 677 ms |
| Search chats | 6,044 ms | 726 ms | 674 ms |
| Rename chat | 4,906 ms | 430 ms | 428 ms |
| Composer menu | 5,124 ms | 655 ms | 628 ms |
| Tools menu | 5,124 ms | 598 ms | 650 ms |
| Chat options | 4,746 ms | 640 ms | 648 ms |

Opening was already fast on real macOS and stays so. On Linux WebKit
(Colab, 100 turns, 3 reps) the browser pane opens in 1.9 s instead of
22.4 s and closes in 0.9 s instead of 11.1 s; Settings open/close goes
from 6.6 / 7.1 s to 1.2 / 1.1 s. Chromium is unchanged or 10 to 40 ms
faster.

Behaviour is the same in both engines: wheel over the browser pane under
the Tools menu moves it 0 px (it scrolls normally with no menu open);
the lock attribute is set and the body has `overflow: hidden` and
`pointer-events: none` while a dialog or menu is open; wheel over the
thread under Settings or the tools menu moves it 0 px while the Settings
pane itself still scrolls; focus lands on the same element after close.
Screenshots of 10 surfaces, open and after close, show no visible change
(pixel differences at 100 turns match a base-vs-base run).

## Tests

- New `studio/frontend/tests/webkit-modal-page-restyle.test.ts`: the
alias, the static lock styles, the pointer listener pin and the
closing-dialog blur.
- Long-chat gate (#16931): PASS.
- Full frontend suite: 15,088 pass; the one failure is the KaTeX
stylesheet test that also fails on main in a local setup with a
symlinked `node_modules`. `node scripts/typecheck.mjs --tests` is clean.

One deliberate change: clicking the side pane, or a page control that
restores its own pointer events (Downloads button, banners), while a
modal menu is open now only closes the menu, as clicking the thread
already did. Wheel over the Skills list, the Library toolbar, the
Downloads card or the sidebar under a modal menu moves them 0 px (they
scroll normally otherwise). Recipe Studio comboboxes inside its dialogs
stay usable.

Not covered: touch devices such as iPad Safari (the lock's touch
cancelling is dropped), and users with reduced motion, for whom the
closing-dialog blur does not run.

Studio: stop menus, sidebar and browser pane from restyling the whole chat (#16938)

## Problem

On a long chat, toggling the sidebar, opening run settings, the model
picker, chat options or the browser pane each restyled the whole thread,
about 9,200 to 18,400 elements at 150 turns, on every engine (Chromium /
Edge for Windows, WebKit for macOS and Linux). Typing in WebKit paid a
similar cost on every keystroke.

The cause is CSS rules where the styled element comes after a `:has()`,
for example `X:has(...) Y` or `X:has(...) > Y` (139 such rules in the
built CSS: wallpaper and glass rules, Tailwind `group-has-*` variants,
hub README badge rows, menu rows). When anything under `X` changes, the
browser re-checks every element that could match `Y`, and their
right-hand parts (`a`, `img`, `[data-slot]`, `[data-state]`,
`:focus-visible`) match every source chip, favicon, tool card and
reasoning row in the thread. Deleting just these rules took a sidebar
toggle from 9,216 to 141 elements restyled; no single rule was
responsible (14 each caused it alone).

## Fix

82 of the 139 rules are rewritten so `:has()` is in the subject or
replaced by a flag; the look is unchanged.

- Wallpaper and glass rules (about 60, `index.css`): read flags on the
host element (`data-wallpaper-ready`, `-outline-off`, `-flat`,
`-frame-flat`, `-image`, `-preview-outline-off`).
`chat-background/host-flags.ts` mirrors them from the wallpaper layer
before paint, using exactly the old `:has()` argument for each flag, and
only writes on a change. Flags are repeated in the selectors so
specificity is unchanged.
- Windows page blur radius: reads `data-sidebar-frame`, set in
`__root.tsx` from the sidebar's own condition.
- Hub README badge rows: `hub/lib/badge-rows.ts` marks them with
`data-badge-row`.
- RAG embedding menu row: the item checks its own later siblings for the
pin, so it is the subject.
- Sidebar row actions (12 `group-has-*`):
`[&:has(~.sidebar-row-action...)]`, since the actions are always the
row's last siblings.
- Info hint: marks itself `data-near-focus` when its row has keyboard
focus.
- Queue editor hint, library card time, RAG pin, project chat date: the
group sets a custom property in its own `has-[...]` class and the child
reads it.
- Four selector strings in `has-anchor-order.test.ts` were being picked
up by Tailwind and shipped as real rules; they are now spelled so the
scan skips them.

The remaining 57 rules (shadcn primitives, chat model notice, files
panel, sidebar nav hover, composer pills, toasts, sidebar footer fade)
are left as they are and listed in an allowlist; keep-only bisects show
none of them costs anything on a sidebar toggle or on WebKit typing.

## Results

150 turns, base vs this PR side by side, 3 reps (restyle counts
identical across reps):

| Chromium | Elements restyled | Style time |
|---|---|---|
| Sidebar toggle open / close | 9,216 -> 135 / 9,270 -> 188 | 111 -> 3.6
ms / 114 -> 4.5 ms |
| Run settings open / close | 9,363 -> 258 / 18,397 -> 256 | 112 -> 10
ms / 202 -> 6.8 ms |
| Model picker open / close | 10,493 -> 1,464 / 9,423 -> 390 | 123 -> 18
ms / 110 -> 6.6 ms |
| Chat options close | 9,498 -> 463 | 132 -> 25 ms |
| Browser pane open / close | 9,581 -> 583 / 18,242 -> 146 | 130 -> 24
ms / 221 -> 11 ms |
| Settings open (dialog mount) | 2,115 -> 2,111 | 48 -> 45 ms |

WebKit typing at 150 turns: p50 61 -> 25 ms per key, p95 66 -> 33 ms
(`:focus-visible` and `[data-state]` inside these rules were re-checked
across the document on every keystroke). Chromium typing is unchanged.

Look: every element's computed style (including `::before` / `::after`)
and a pixel diff, base vs this PR, on a solid thread (tool cards,
reasoning rows, source chips, favicons), sidebar row hover, an open row
menu, keyboard focus on a row's pin, and solid and Liquid Glass 3D over
a wallpaper (thread, welcome page, Appearance). Computed styles are
identical apart from the per-session wallpaper blob URL and the random
welcome greeting; pixel diffs are 0 outside the greeting.

## Guard

- `tests/has-subject-after.test.ts` (about 1 s) compiles `index.css`
with the build's Tailwind plus every `has` class in the scanned sources
and fails on any new rule of this shape outside the allowlist, on stale
allowlist entries, and on `@custom-variant` definitions that contain
`:has(`.
- `tests/has-host-flags.test.ts` checks the new flags and markers are
wired up.

## Tests

Full frontend suite passes except the KaTeX stylesheet test that also
fails on main in a local setup with a symlinked `node_modules`; `node
scripts/typecheck.mjs --tests` is clean. Existing tests that matched the
old selector text are updated.

Studio: keep Glass cheap on the Linux app by dropping its live blur except the sidebar's (#16957)

## Problem

On the Linux desktop app (WebKitGTK, which paints on the CPU), every
live `backdrop-filter` is re-run on every frame, so a caret blink or a
scrolled line re-blurs every glass surface on screen. With Glass on,
typing, scrolling Settings and the Glass controls all pay for it. After
#16921 (child layers), the remaining WebKit Glass cost is the live blur
itself.

## Fix

Linux desktop app only. `WindowMaterialMount` sets `data-glass-cpu` on
`<html>` when `isWebKitGTK(navigator.platform, navigator.userAgent)`
holds, with the same conditions as the other Glass flags (not Solid, not
Transparent, route in scope). All new rules key on it:

- Live blur is turned off everywhere except the sidebar (and the framed
titlebar sidebar), which keeps its real blur and looks exactly as

Studio CI: long-chat gate measures every interactive area under every appearance mode (#16931)

Extends the long-chat CI gate from #16801 / #16902 so it also catches
lag in every interactive area, and a new feature or appearance setting
that is itself slow (the way Glass shipped).

## What it measures

After the existing long-chat checks (unchanged), on the Linux Frontend
CI lane in Chromium, the gate opens the real `/chat` page from the same
production build with every `/api` call answered in-process, seeded with
40 and 200 turns of a fixed agent turn (reasoning, web search, tool
calls, code, long reply).

- 30 areas: typing and scrolling the chat; Settings, every Settings tab
(read from the page), a Settings dropdown and scrolling inside Settings;
command palette, search chats, model picker; composer, tools,
permission, chat options, account, organize and chat row menus; sidebar
sections and toggle; browser pane; run settings; API monitor; rename;
shortcuts dialog; message action menu, copy, click, reasoning and tool
expand/collapse, code copy and source card.
- Appearance modes are read from the app's own material and lens lists,
so a new material is measured with no gate edit: default, Transparent,
frosted, blurred, liquid, liquid-3d, macOS, both lens modes, Glass menus
off, dark and dark Glass.
- One Chromium trace per page, split per area: elements restyled and
layout objects (exact counts), style, layout and paint time, longest
task, and CPU time on every browser thread.

## When it fails

- An area's restyle or layout count grows more than 2x from 40 to 200
turns (counted above 3000 elements).
- A mode makes an area cost more than 4x its baseline in CPU or elements
restyled (baseline = default look; lens, menus-off and dark Glass are
compared with plain Glass), with at least 150 ms extra CPU.
- An area stops running.
- Coverage: every visible menu or popup trigger on the chat page must
belong to an area or be listed with a reason, and a unit test requires
every keyboard shortcut to map to an area or a stated reason.

CPU and "did not run" failures are measured again on fresh pages before

responsible. All thresholds can be overridden with `LONG_THREAD_AREAS_*`

Runs first (about 1 s): reads every rule in the built CSS and flags

disappear are reported so the list can be pruned
(`LONG_THREAD_HAS_LINT_WRITE=1` regenerates it).

The nine known whole-chat areas also get a fixed ceiling on elements
restyled at 200 turns, about 1.2x today's count, so they cannot get
worse; deleting an area's entry restores the normal 2x growth check once
it is fixed.

Studio: blur the glass Settings dialog on its own layer so scrolling it stays cheap (#16942)

## Problem

With Glass on, scrolling inside the Settings dialog is expensive in
Chromium (the engine behind the Windows app's WebView2): the dialog's
own `backdrop-filter` is re-run for every frame its content scrolls. The
long-chat gate measured Glass Settings scrolling at 10 to 22x the CPU of
the solid window.

## Fix

The glass Settings dialog no longer carries the `backdrop-filter`
itself. A `::before` layer underneath it (`position: absolute; inset: 0;
z-index: -1`, inside `isolation: isolate` on the dialog) carries the
same blur. While the panes above it scroll, the layer's backdrop is left
alone. This is the pattern glass dialogs with sticky content already use
(`:has(.sticky, [data-glass-float])::before`).

It applies only to Settings (`[data-settings-dialog]`), whose shell is
`overflow-hidden` and never scrolls. Dialogs that scroll their own box
(the shared `DialogContent` default is `overflow-y-auto`, for example
Connections) keep the direct blur: an absolute layer there would scroll
away with the content and leave the lower part unblurred. It also does
not apply on WebKit (`data-glass-layers`, macOS and Linux apps), where
the layer costs about 9% more scroll CPU; WebKit keeps the direct blur
exactly as on main. The layer has no `will-change`, which added nothing
measurable. Solid, Transparent and Glass menus off are untouched.

## Results

Browser CPU for 40 wheel steps scrolling Settings, Glass Liquid 3D, same
build base, 3 reps each:

| Chromium, Glass Liquid 3D (3 reps, medians) | main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Settings scroll CPU (40 wheel steps) | 5,290 ms | 3,240 ms |
| Settings scroll frames p50 / p90 | 17 / 50 ms | 17 / 50 to 67 ms |
| Style dropdown inside Settings, open | 80 ms | 110 ms |
| Typing / Tools menu | 16 / 68 ms | 16 / 71 to 87 ms |

About 39% less CPU while scrolling Settings in Chromium, close to having
no blur on the page at all (2,990 ms). The trade-off: opening the Style
dropdown inside Settings is about 30 ms slower with the layer, with or
without `will-change`, and the p90 scroll frame rose to 67 ms in one of
two runs (headless software compositing). Scrolling Settings is the
frequent, sustained cost; the dropdown open is a single short one.
WebKit is unchanged (the rule does not apply there; in WebKit the layer
would cost 5 to 6% more scroll CPU). Glass off is unchanged in both
engines.

## Tests

- New `studio/frontend/tests/glass-dialog-blur-layer.test.ts`: other
dialogs keep the direct blur; Settings drops it and isolates; its
`::before` layer sits at `z-index: -1`, covers the dialog, ignores
pointers and carries the blur; the Settings shell stays
`overflow-hidden`.
- 113 dialog and backdrop related tests pass; `node
scripts/typecheck.mjs --tests` is clean.

Studio: classify MLX repos by name or model-card tag everywhere (#16883)

## Problem

Unsloth Studio decided whether a Hub repo is MLX in two different ways,
and each screen used only one of them:

| Rule | Used by |
|---|---|
| Repo name only (`mlx-community/` owner, or an `mlx` segment in the
repo name) | Model picker format filter and MLX/Safetensors row labels,
`/api/models/list` defaults |
| Model card only (`library_name: mlx` or an `mlx` tag) | Hub page
search format filter, On Device inventory, Hub inspector
precision-folder card, picker precision-folder expansion, backend MLX
precision-folder listing |

The Hub marks a repo as MLX only from its README front-matter and never
inspects the weights, so many real MLX uploads are untagged, and many
tagged ones have no MLX in the name. The same repo therefore landed in
different formats depending on the screen:

- `unsloth/gemma-4-E2B-it-UD-MLX-4bit` (no `mlx` tag or library): MLX in
the model picker, Safetensors on the Hub page and On Device, and no
precision-folder expansion.
- `FluidVoice-Labs/Qwen3.5-9B-4bit` (tagged `mlx`, no MLX in the name):
MLX on the Hub page, Safetensors in the model picker.

## Change

- `hub/lib/format-filters.ts` owns both halves: `hasMlxCardTag({ tags,
libraryName })` and `isMlxId(id, hintedIsMlx?)`, which mirrors
`isGgufId(id, hintedIsGguf)`. `recommended-fit.ts` re-exports them, so
existing imports keep working.
- Every surface that has both an id and model-card data now uses name OR
tag: picker Hub search rows (filter, label, precision-folder click),
picker search and recommended id filters (via the tags of the rows
already fetched), cached rows, Hub search format, On Device inventory
(cached repo id or local path/title), and the inspector precision-folder
card.
- `matchesFormatFilter` gains an optional `hintedIsMlx` and keeps GGUF
precedence: a GGUF repo's `mlx` tag never moves it into the MLX filter,
matching `detectResultFormat`. Name-based behaviour for GGUF ids is
unchanged.
- Backend: the name rule moves from `routes/models.py` to
`hub/utils/mlx_variants.py` as `looks_like_mlx_repo`, so the MLX
precision-folder listing in `hub/services` can accept name-matched repos
too, without importing a route module.

All classification uses data the search listing already returns. No
per-repo requests are added for classification.

## Tradeoffs and scope

- Clicking a picker row that matches only by name now makes the same
single variants request that tagged rows already made, to look for
precision folders.
- Surfaces that only have an id (curated catalog seeds,
`hfModelFitsDevice`, `/api/models/list` defaults, picker local rows)
keep the name rule because they have no tag data.
- Weight-based signals were considered and left out. A U32 dtype or
`quantization_config.bits` without `quant_method` also matches non-MLX
formats such as modelopt NVFP4, EXL3, CoreML, OpenVINO and ONNX exports.

Studio: keep emoji and rare CJK characters intact when an .xls record boundary splits them (#16713)

## What was broken

Binary XLS cell text can lose supplementary Unicode characters during
RAG parsing. Emoji and CJK names become replacement characters when a
UTF-16 surrogate pair crosses a BIFF CONTINUE record. The damaged text
is then stored and indexed, so searches for the original name can miss
it.

## Repro

1. On main at `91be10960`, use xlwt 1.3.0 to write `'A' * 4105 +
'\U0001f600tail'` into the first cell of an `.xls` workbook.
2. Read it with `office_formats.xls`, or upload it for RAG indexing.
3. The emoji becomes two replacement characters. Prefix lengths 4104 and
4106 round-trip correctly; 4105 splits its surrogate pair across
records.

## Fix

Keep single-fragment strings on the direct decode path. For continued
strings, normalize compressed fragments to UTF-16LE bytes and decode the
joined stream once. This preserves pairs across record boundaries while
retaining width changes, metadata skipping, replacement of malformed
Unicode, and the returned record position.

This fixes both shared strings and cached formula results. It does not
change XLSX parsing.

## Test

Ten regression cases fail before the fix; all 18 selected cases pass
afterward. Coverage includes shared and formula strings, emoji and CJK
characters, compressed/wide transitions, full 8KB record boundaries,
formatting metadata, malformed surrogates, and separate-string
boundaries. Upload-to-FTS tests verify that a split CJK surname remains
searchable, with stub embeddings and real ingestion/SQLite.

From `studio/backend`:

```text
$ python -m pytest -q --tb=short --timeout=330 tests/test_rag_office_formats.py
158 passed in 4.54s
```

```text
$ python -m pytest -q --tb=short -n 4 --dist loadgroup --timeout=330 tests/test_rag_office_formats.py tests/test_rag_parsing.py tests/test_rag_ingestion.py tests/test_rag_retrieval.py
330 passed, 1 skipped in 6.79s
```

The skip is the opt-in real-embedder test. Separately verified
xlwt-produced workbooks at all three prefix lengths. The broken case now
round-trips exactly, and the controls are unchanged. Local ASCII/BMP
single-fragment microbenchmarks show no regression.

All seven repository checks and the pinned pre-commit formatter pass. No
schema or dependency changes.

Studio: refuse MLX prompts longer than the served context (#16821)

## Problem

An MLX load in Unsloth Studio did not refuse a prompt longer than its
context window. On a load pinned to ~41k tokens, a 152k-token prompt
came back as an empty 200 when not streamed. Streamed, the same request
spent about 20 minutes in prefill while the cache dropped the earliest
part of the conversation. llama.cpp loads refuse the same request up
front with a context-size error (HTTP 400).

## Root cause

`MLXInferenceBackend._check_context_budget` runs only when
`_kv_context_budget` is set, and `_resolve_kv_policy` sets that only for
loads with a quantized KV cache. Every other load admitted any prompt:

- where the cache can be bounded, `max_kv_size` gives a rotating cache,
which silently evicts the start of the prompt during prefill;
- where it cannot (hybrid models with layers that never rotate), the
cache grows past the context the load was asked to serve.

With no free room, `generation_budget_for_window` fell back to the
default budget, so generation still went ahead.

## Change

A new `_prompt_within_window` counts the prompt and raises
`ContextBudgetExceeded` when it leaves no room in the served context
(prompt + 1 > window), using the same threshold and error as the
existing budget check. It runs whether or not `max_tokens` is set, on:

- single requests, through `_generation_limit` (text, raw completion,
vision, audio), and
- resident batch rows, through `_plan_text_row`.

The refusal reuses the existing `ContextBudgetExceeded` plumbing (worker
payload → orchestrator → route), so clients get the same typed context
error a quantized-KV MLX load or a llama.cpp load already returns.

`_kv_context_budget` is intentionally not reused for this: setting it
also disables batching and makes every vision request prepare its media
to count tokens.

## Tradeoffs

- On loads without a KV budget, a prompt with media is still counted at
placeholder level, as before. That can under-count images but never
refuses a prompt that fits. Counting images exactly would mean preparing
media on every request.
- An explicit `max_tokens` that runs past the window during decode is
unchanged; this PR only covers the prompt.

## Validation

New tests in `studio/backend/tests/test_mlx_inference_backend.py`, each
parametrized over an unset and an explicit `max_tokens`: one covers the
text and vision single-request paths, including a cached-prefix prompt
that must be counted in full; the other covers batch-row planning. Each
production edit was mutated on its own and the matching test failed
(6/6).

```bash
python -m pytest studio/backend/tests/test_mlx_inference_backend.py studio/backend/tests/test_mlx_load_warm_and_narrow.py -q
# 584 passed
```

Real models, loaded with a 512-token context and sent a ~2000-token
prompt:

| Model | Cache bound | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mlx-community/Qwen3-4B-4bit` | rotating, enforced | admitted (single,
explicit `max_tokens`, batch) | refused in under 0.05 s on all three |
| `mlx-community/Qwen3.5-0.8B-4bit` (mlx-vlm) | not enforceable |
admitted on all three | refused on all three |

A short prompt still generates normally on both.

Studio: decode escaped spreadsheet text during RAG indexing (#16712)

## What was broken

Spreadsheet previews decode Excel's `_xHHHH_` text escapes after #16592,
but RAG ingestion uses a separate reader and still indexes the encoded
strings. Stored text differs from the preview, and lexical searches can
miss the decoded cell contents.

This is the backend follow-up noted in the merge comment on #16592.

## Repro

1. On main at `91be10960`, put `Zebra_x006D_arker` in an XLSX shared
string, inline string or cached formula result.
2. Upload it for RAG indexing. Ingestion completes, but the stored text
still contains the escape.
3. Search for `zebramarker`. There are no lexical matches.

## Fix

Decode each text run before joining it, preserving quoted underscores
and literal uppercase `_X` sequences. Combine UTF-16 surrogate pairs
after joining runs, and replace unmatched surrogate units so the result
remains valid UTF-8 for indexing. Cached formula strings use the same
decoder. Number and error cells are unchanged.

## Test

Nineteen regression cases fail before the fix; all 21 selected cases
pass afterward. Coverage includes shared, inline and cached strings,
rich-run boundaries, phonetic hints, quoted escapes, supplementary
Unicode, and Strict OOXML. Upload-to-FTS tests cover `.xlsx`, `.xlsm`,
`.xltx` and `.xltm`, using stub embeddings with the real ingestion and
SQLite paths.

Studio: load long chat history faster on Linux by mounting parked history in larger steps (#16924)

Follow-up to #16854. On the Linux desktop app (WebKitGTK), loading a
long chat's history became about 60 to 80% slower after #16854, because
history was mounted 2 messages per frame for the whole thread (about 142
commits instead of about 9 for a 150-turn chat). The first messages
appeared at the same time; the extra time was the background history
load, with about 150 frames over 50 ms instead of about 30.

## Fix

WebKitGTK only. Each widening step measures how far the first mounted
row is above the viewport top (read after the existing anchor capture,
so no extra layout pass):

- Within the window controller's reach (2000 px), rows stay unparked and
can move what the reader sees, so they still mount 2 per step, as in
#16854.
- Past it, rows are parked as they land, so the step ramps 2, 8, 16 and
holds at 16 (`FAR_MOUNT_CHUNK`). The first step of every load stays at 2
so the tail paints as early as before.
- Coming back within reach drops straight to 2. Pausing during scroll,
typing and pointer drags, `flushSync`, and the anchor correction are
unchanged.

Chromium (Windows) and macOS never call the new path; their step stays
`CHUNK_MESSAGES`.

The cap is 16 rather than 32 on purpose: 32 brought the load time back
to within 2 to 6% of before #16854 with Glass off, but made single
frames up to about 1.4 s on CPU-painted WebKit. 16 keeps the worst frame
at the level of the 2-per-step loader.

## Results

GitHub ubuntu-latest, Playwright WebKit, 150-turn heavy chat, time until
all 300 messages are mounted, per-runner medians of 3 loads (two runners
of different speed):

| | Before #16854 | main | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Glass off, runner a | 13.6 s | 21.3 s | 15.1 s |
| Glass off, runner b | 8.1 s | 13.2 s | 9.2 s |
| Glass on, runner a | 14.4 s | 24.5 s | 17.0 s |
| Glass on, runner b | 8.5 s | 15.6 s | 10.2 s |

- First messages appear on the same frame as main (the first step is 2
rows on both).
- No reader shake: the message at the middle of the viewport did not
move by 1 px or more in any load, the same as main.
- Chromium loads identically to main (all 300 messages at 5.6 s, 32 per
step in both).

## Tests

- `progressive-mount-controller.test.ts`: the step stays small near the
reader and for unknown geometry, ramps 2, 8, 16 past the reach and
holds, drops back when the reader returns, never changes the step on
other engines, and covers a 300-message thread in about 20 commits
instead of about 142.
- Glue tests pin that only WebKitGTK takes the adaptive step.
- 72 related tests pass; `tsc -p tsconfig.app.json` and `node
scripts/typecheck.mjs --tests` are clean.

Studio: release a streamed encoder's safetensors mapping once its weights are pinned (#16914)

## Summary

**Real host RAM (`MemAvailable`) does not change with this PR.** The
memory released is a clean, file-backed page-cache mapping that the
kernel could already reclaim. What drops is the process's own RSS / PSS:
the memory Studio appears to use in `top`, task managers and PSS-based
tooling. The open mapping of the model file is also released.

Under a VRAM budget, Studio streams the int8 text encoder from a pinned
host copy. The encoder's original safetensors file then stayed mapped
and fully resident for the life of the model, on top of the pinned copy.
On Qwen-Image-2.1 that is the whole 8.7 GiB int8 encoder file, so the
process showed about 28.6 GiB PSS at 8 and 12 GiB budgets when about
19.9 GiB is actually needed.

This PR makes the plain pre-quant loader return tensors that do not hold
that mapping. Once the weights are pinned, the file is unmapped. Outputs
are bit-identical and per-step speed is unchanged.

## What / why

- **What (1):** `load_plain_prequant_safetensors` now returns each
tensor as a base-less alias of the same storage
(`torch.empty(0).set_(storage, offset, size, stride)`, no copy).
`_mapped_tensors` in the same file already builds its tensors this way.
- **What (2):** `build_text_encoder` in `diffusion_comfy_components.py`
(single-file int8 ConvRot text encoders) had the same leak:
`codes.to(torch.int8)` returns the view itself. It now loads base-less
aliases too. The MiniMax-H3 conditioner is not affected:
`pin_module_in_place` already replaces `_parameters` / `_buffers`
entries instead of using `.data`, for this reason.
- **Why the mapping leaked:**
- `safe_open(...).get_tensor()` returns views of one storage that maps
the whole file.
- `Int8ConvRotLinear` registers `weight` and `weight_scale` as buffers.
`load_state_dict(assign=True)` installs those views as they are.
- Streaming re-points each host weight at its pinned copy with
`tensor.data = pinned` (`_GroupPinner`, the pin arena). That swaps the
storage but keeps the view's `_base`, so every int8 weight and scale
kept the old file storage alive.
- Parameters were not affected, because `nn.Parameter(view)` already
drops the base. That is why the DiT never leaked and only the
buffer-based encoder did.
- A gc scan at load end on the budget run found 504 CPU tensors (6.5
GiB) still pointing into the file mapping, none of them reachable from
Python. These were the view bases.
- **Effect:**
- The mapping is clean page cache, so `MemAvailable` did not move: the
kernel could reclaim those pages.
- What changes is what Studio reports as its own memory. RSS / PSS /
task-manager memory now matches what the process really holds.
- Each streamed model no longer keeps an 8.7 GiB mapping open. On
Windows, an open mapping also keeps the file from being deleted.

Studio: keep Glass fast on WebKit by giving glass surface contents their own layers (#16921)

## Problem

With Glass on, WebKit (macOS app, and the Linux app's WebKitGTK)
repaints a glass surface's blurred shadows and backdrop whenever
anything inside it changes. Measured on Colab CPU (software paint),
Glass Liquid 3D, medians of 3 runs:

| WebKit | Glass off | Glass on (main) |
|---|---|---|
| Scrolling inside Settings, per frame | n/a | 164 ms (p90 244 ms) |
| Typing in the composer, per key | 26 ms | 56 ms |
| Composer menu open | 315 ms | 516 ms |

Chromium (Windows WebView2 engine family) is mostly unaffected.

## Fix

On WebKit only, while a frosted Glass material is applied on the current
route, `WindowMaterialMount` sets `data-glass-layers` on `<html>`, and
the direct children of the dialog, sidebar, composer and files panel get
`will-change: opacity`. A repaint inside one of them then stays in its
own layer instead of re-blurring the whole surface.

- `opacity`, not `transform`, so absolute and fixed descendants keep
their containing block.
- Solid, Transparent and out-of-scope routes never carry the flag, so
turning Glass off restores the exact previous tree. The attribute toggle
is idempotent.
- Chromium, Edge and Android user agents never get the flag.

## Results

Same harness and build base, WebKit, Glass Liquid 3D, medians of 3 runs:

| WebKit | main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Scrolling inside Settings, per frame | 164 ms (p90 244) | 73 ms (p90
82) |
| Typing in the composer, per key | 56 ms | 44 ms |
| Composer menu open | 516 ms | 480 ms |

Chromium and Glass off are unchanged.

Look: screenshots of the composer and the Settings dialog, Glass on and
off, Chromium and WebKit, pixel-diffed against main. WebKit Settings
with Glass on is pixel-identical (0 changed pixels). The only
differences are on the welcome screen, where the "How can I help?"
greeting fades in, and they are the same size in the Glass-off pair
where this change does nothing.

## Tests

- `studio/frontend/tests/glass-webkit-layers.test.ts`: the flag is
WebKit only and never set for solid, Transparent or out-of-scope routes;
the rule uses `opacity`, not `transform`, and no `:has()`.
- 270 Glass and material related frontend tests pass; `tsc -p
tsconfig.app.json` is clean.

Studio diffusion: reuse the early quant probe's result instead of spawning a second child (#16910)

## Summary

Follow-up to #16882, which starts the quant scheme probe child early on
a cold image load. Three cases spawned a second child that the serial
probe never needed:

1. **The early child ends with no table** (hit the 180 s
`_CHILD_PROBE_TIMEOUT`, or exited without a result). `_scheme_supported`
saw no early table and spawned a fresh child, so a wedged probe stalled
the first load twice as long (about 360 s instead of 180 s) before the
in-process fallback. The early thread now records that its child ran
without a table, and the load goes straight to the in-process probe, as
it does after a failed serial child.
2. **The startup warm races the early child.** If a load arrives before
the startup warm (`prewarm_probe_table`) takes the probe lock, the warm
blocks on the lock while the early child runs, then finds `_SMOKE_CACHE`
empty and runs its own child. The early thread now writes its definite
verdicts into `_SMOKE_CACHE`, as `prewarm_probe_table` does, so the warm
sees them.
3. **A plan that never reaches the probe** (the bf16 seed path that
returns before `_planned_quant_scheme`) discarded the early table. Where
the verdicts cannot be persisted (`UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_PROBE_CACHE=0`, no
card UUID, no storage root, or no passing scheme), every such plan
spawned another child. Those verdicts are now kept in `_SMOKE_CACHE`,
the same verdicts the serial probe caches.

The out-of-memory case is unchanged: a `None` verdict is still not
cached, and the load still takes it from the early table without a
second child. `UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_PROBE_OVERLAP=0` still restores the
serial probe exactly.

## Evidence

CPU only, the probe child replaced by a fake (sleep plus table), same
harness on all three trees: base = `f85c190501` (before #16882), merged
= `9c084751ab` (#16882), this branch.

| case | base | merged #16882 | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| child ends with no table: children / wall (child = 1.0 s) | 1 / 1.20 s
| 2 / 2.05 s | 1 / 1.05 s |
| startup warm blocked behind the early child: children | 1 | 2 | 1 |
| 3 plans on the bf16 seed path, verdicts not persistable: children | 0
| 3 | 1 |
| 3 plans on the bf16 seed path, persistence on: children | 0 | 1 | 1 |

- 96 enumerated planner cells (auto / explicit x keeps-bf16 x eager x
prior verdict state x child outcome): with
`UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_PROBE_OVERLAP=0` all 96 traces match base exactly on
both trees; with overlap on, free VRAM is never read, and the planner
never returns, while a probe child or the overlap thread is alive.
- Remaining extra child versus base: a plan that never reaches the probe
still pays one early child per process (disclosed in #16882), now once
instead of per plan.

## Tests

- `studio/backend/tests/test_diffusion_probe_overlap.py`: 3 new tests
(no-table child spawned once, startup warm reuses the early table,
verdicts kept on a plan that never reaches the probe). All 3 fail on
`origin/main` and pass here; the 6 existing tests pass on both. The
fixture now stubs the in-process probe body (`_run_smoke_probe`) instead
of `_smoke_probe`, so a cached verdict is answered the way the real code
answers it.
- 18 related backend test files (probe, quant, cold start, early probe):
2305 passed, 13 skipped; the one failure
(`test_diffusion_comfy_community_files.py::test_moss_pipeline_takes_a_supplied_vae`)
fails the same way on `origin/main`.

## Not proven

- No GPU run: the timings above use a fake child. The fix only changes
which cached table the load reads, not the probe itself.

When an image model compiles inside its first render (the default speed
tier on a card where the denoiser fits, for example FLUX.2-klein-4B on
an A100), every Studio start threw away a whole Dynamo attempt per block
type before compiling:

dropout `p`, the attention dispatch default.
- Those ops guard the float to a constant, the tensorify pass raises

with the floats specialised (`compile_attempt_0` and `compile_attempt_1`
for both FLUX.2 block types).

misses the AOTAutograd cache, since its graph still has the float
inputs. It cost 5.7 s of the 8.3 s compile on FLUX.2-klein-4B.

## Summary

A load that compiles at its first render (the default speed tier when it
is not deferred) paid three one-time, model-free costs inside that
render: starting inductor's compile workers, Triton's `triton_key()` (a
hash of the Triton install) and inductor's `torch_key()` (a hash of
torch's sources). The deferred tier already warms the first two on a
side thread from the 2nd image (`start_deferred_prewarm`), and the first
render of an inline load gets none of that.

This PR:

- starts the same side warm-up from `load_pipeline` as soon as the
compile-cache context begins on a CUDA target, so it runs while the rest
of the load (speed layer, CUDA graph setup, placement) finishes;
- adds inductor's `torch_key()` to the warm-up (`warm_inductor_key`). It
is cached per process, so the first compile reads it instead of hashing
torch's sources;
- reuses the existing thread, once per process, joined by the deferred
engagement as before. Kill switch: the existing
`UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_DEFERRED_PREWARM=0` (warms the pool inline only).

Nothing about the compile itself changes: same knobs, same graphs, same
cache keys.

Studio: restore WebKitGTK offscreen code fences in batches and on any pointer release (#16919)

Follow-up to #16854. Two review findings on the WebKitGTK (Linux
desktop) code fence paths; Chromium (Windows) and macOS never enable
these paths, so nothing changes there.

## Problems

1. Scrolling back to a dense code fence below the 240-line window cap
remounted every highlighted token in one commit. When the fence goes
offscreen it is parked as plain text and `FenceLines` unmounts, but
`useFenceHighlightLimit` stays mounted with finished progress, so coming
back skipped the 512-token batches. A 120-line fence with 64 tokens per
line came back as 7,680 spans in a single render.
2. A fence that came into view while a finger was down stayed
unhighlighted after the finger lifted. The restore is deferred while a
pointer is held and retried on release, but `releasePointer()` returned
early unless a mouse press had been recorded. Touch never records one,
and neither does a mouse press that began before the listeners attached.

## Fix

- `useFenceHighlightLimit` takes the parked state. Parking restarts the
batched progress and pauses the queue, so returning remounts one batch
at a time. The reset only runs when the parked state changes, so it is
idempotent.
- `releasePointer()` always clears the held pointer and schedules the
retry when a restore was deferred. Repeated calls coalesce into one
frame.

## Tests

- New `studio/frontend/tests/code-fence-offscreen-restore.test.ts` runs
the real hook and listener code extracted from `code-fence-defer.tsx`:
- a dense fence that is parked and restored returns at most one
512-token batch per commit, and does no highlight work while parked;
- touch release, normal mouse release, and a mouse press that began
before the listeners attached all restore the fence.
- Each test fails without its fix (3 of 4 fail on main; the normal mouse
case already worked).
- `desktop-webkit-paths.test.ts` updated for the new `releasePointer`
body.
- 108 of 108 tests in the 13 files that read `code-fence-defer.tsx`
pass; `tsc -p tsconfig.app.json` is clean.

Studio: merge LoRA and LoKR adapters into ComfyUI-quantized weights (#16874)

A ComfyUI-quantized single file (fp8 or int8 ConvRot) loaded with
adapters bakes them before the compile, and they then run as layers on
every step. A LoRA adds two small GEMMs per adapted Linear. A full-rank
LoKR adds about a quarter of the Linear's own GEMM in bf16, which costs
more than the fp8 GEMM it sits next to. ComfyUI patches the adapters
into the weights instead (dequantize, add the delta, requantize), so
they cost nothing per step there.

Seconds per step, RTX 6000 Ada, 1024², community adapters from #16711's
set, lower is better:

| | Before (main) | After (this PR) | ComfyUI v0.44.0 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Krea 2 Turbo fp8 + LoKR | 1.27 | 0.74 | 1.07 |
| Krea 2 fine-tune fp8 + LoRA | 0.83 | 0.76 | 0.81 |
| MOSS-Image SFT int8 ConvRot + LoKR (fused `qkv`) | 1.19 | 0.54 | 0.44
|

The remaining MOSS-Image gap is the base model's own int8 step (0.54
against 0.44 without adapters too).

## Change

New `diffusion_lora_quant_merge.py`, called where a resident quantized
load bakes its adapters:

- Every adapted Linear is dequantized in float32 (ConvRot rotation
undone), the deltas are added (`scale * B @ A` for a LoRA, `kron(w1,
w2)` with its row slice for a LoKR), and the result is quantized back
into the layer's own `Float8Tensor` / `Int8Tensor` (or plain float)
tensors: a per-row scale recomputed for the merged weight, and seeded
stochastic rounding, as ComfyUI rounds a patched weight.
Round-to-nearest dropped every delta below half a step: the MOSS-Image
LoKR's effect fell from 19.6 to 16.5 per pixel.
- The PEFT and LoKR layers are then removed, so the compile sees the
base model alone (MOSS-Image's fused int8 path included).
- The original quantized data of every touched layer is kept in host
memory. A weight change copies it back into the same tensors and merges
again; weight 0 is the original weights. Compiled code and captured
graphs read those tensors, so they stay valid.

Kept on the current adapter-layer path: offloaded loads (the host copy,
not the card's, is the source there), adapters that also touch a text
encoder, DoRA / LoRA-bias layers, anything but a plain or ConvRot Linear
with a registered weight, other weight formats, and a host without room
for the backups in its usable RAM (cgroup limits included).
`UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_LORA_QUANT_MERGE=0` turns it off.

At `max` speed, diffusers' QKV fusion is skipped on a merged load: its
fused `to_qkv` is a copy that a weight change would not reach. Studio's
own fused paths (Z-Image, MOSS-Image, int8) are views of the projections
and follow it.

A weight change that fails (an out-of-memory during the re-merge) leaves
the base weights and records the adapters at weight 0, so the next
request merges again. A load that ended up offloaded refuses weight
changes with a reload message, as a streamed graph already does.

## Verification

- The table above, against ComfyUI on the same files.
- Weight 1, weight 0, weight 1 again through `/images/generate` with no
reload, for the Krea 2 LoKR, the Krea 2 LoRA, the MOSS-Image LoKR and

Studio: reduce long-chat panel and scrolling lag on Linux (#16854)

Opening panels and scrolling long chats can stall WebKitGTK because
offscreen message content still participates in style and layout work.
For Linux threads with 100+ messages, park completed offscreen bodies
behind measured placeholders while retaining their React state. Restore
rich content for scrolling, focus, find, selection, and print. Also
reduce offscreen code highlighting and keep browser-panel constraints
stable during opening and closing.

Prevent blank chat frames while history loads or the native scrollbar
jumps. A transparent fixed-background sentinel synchronizes WebKitGTK
overflow scrolling with main-thread painting. Commit small history
batches and their anchor corrections in the same rendering frame, pause
loading during scrolling, typing, composition, and pointer interaction,
and hold message heights during thumb drags. Reuse the existing
measurement-free collapsible for tool panels to avoid repeated forced
layouts from closed disclosures.

Keep text stationary as history loads: preserve the compensated anchor
between batches so intervening reflows are included, and absorb
fractional inserted heights in a leading spacer under one pixel. WebKit
can then apply whole-pixel scroll corrections without repeatedly moving
the text between fractional positions.

progressive-mount, autoscroll, and message-window tests pass on the
updated branch.

Studio: stop dialogs and menus from restyling the whole chat on open and close (#16902)

## Problem

On a long chat, opening or closing any dialog or modal menu (Settings,
command palette, search chats, model picker, chat options, composer
menu, selects) freezes the app. Measured in the real app on a 100-turn
thread (Colab CPU, no GPU):

| Surface | Chromium, 1 turn -> 100 turns | WebKit, 1 turn -> 100 turns
|
|---|---|---|
| Settings | 160 -> 553 ms | 787 -> 7,403 ms |
| Command palette | 67 -> 486 ms | 467 -> 6,637 ms |
| Search chats | 72 -> 420 ms | 468 -> 6,725 ms |
| Composer menu | 47 -> 382 ms | 436 -> 6,680 ms |

On real macOS WebKit (GitHub `macos-15` runner, 150 turns) Settings
takes 3.8 s, the composer menu 3.0 s, the tools menu 4.6 s. Windows Edge
(WebView2 engine) takes about 1 s for Settings at 150 turns.

A Chromium trace shows almost all of it is style recalc: opening
Settings restyles 15,882 elements at 100 turns against 3,222 at 1 turn
(426 ms against 90 ms), with layout under 12 ms.

## Cause

Radix modal layers write `pointer-events: none` on `<body>` while they
are open. `pointer-events` is inherited, so every open and every close
restyles each element of the chat. Applying each modal side effect alone
on the 100-turn production fixture:

| Side effect | Elements restyled | Style recalc |
|---|---|---|
| body `pointer-events: none` | 40,214 | 460 ms |
| body scroll-lock attribute and style | 3 | under 16 ms |
| `aria-hidden` on the app root | 2 | 0.2 ms |
| portal append | 2 | 0.3 ms |

## Fix

CSS only, no component changes:

- `:where(.aui-thread-viewport) { pointer-events: auto; }` gives the
thread scroller an explicit value at zero specificity, so the inherited
change stops there.
- While the lock is up (`body[style*="pointer-events: none"]`), a
transparent `::after` cover over `.aui-thread-root` keeps the thread
unclickable and unhovered exactly as before. It sits at z-index 49,
under the z-50 layers Radix portals to `<body>`.

Behaviour under a modal layer is unchanged in Chromium and WebKit:
clicks never reach the thread, no message is hovered, wheel scrolling
behaves the same, outside-click dismissal, scroll lock, focus trap and
tooltip blocking are unchanged.

## Results

Production fixture, same main commit, base vs this change, one lock open
or close:

| | Base | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Chromium, 100 turns | about 460 ms | 2 to 7 ms |
| Chromium, elements restyled over 6 toggles | 241,284 | 93 |
| WebKit, 100 turns | about 2,400 ms | 14 to 25 ms |
| Long-chat gate check at 200 turns | 840 ms | 5.7 ms |

Typing cost is unchanged. Real-app numbers (menu bench, base vs this PR,
Chromium and WebKit, with Glass on and off) will be added below once the
run finishes.

## Tests

- `studio/frontend/tests/modal-lock-thread-cover.test.ts`: pins the
explicit value on the scroller and the cover under the lock.
- `tests/studio/playwright_long_thread_gate.py`: the long-chat gate now
also measures one lock open or close at 200 turns and fails over 30 ms
(`LONG_THREAD_MAX_LOCK_MS`), with a hint pointing at inherited
properties written on `<body>`.
- Frontend suite: 15,027 of 15,029 pass locally; the one failure is a
KaTeX stylesheet test that also fails on main in that local setup.

Studio: wait for a pending embedding model download instead of failing every linked-folder file (#16722)

Fixes #16714

## What was wrong

When a linked folder synced while the embedding model's Settings
transfer was still pending, every file went to the embedder and each one
failed the same `EmbeddingModelDownloadRequiredError` check in `_load`.
All of them were then saved to the folder's `failed_files` list, which
keeps unchanged failed files out of periodic syncs for 6 hours (#13095).
The folder stayed at "N files that couldn't be indexed" after the
download finished, until a manual Rebuild.

## What this changes

- `embeddings.download_required(model)`: True while the model's
pending-download marker is set and the cache-only loader still can't
load it. It costs nothing when no transfer is pending. Otherwise it asks
the loader, which retires the marker once the cache is complete, so a
finished download reads False.
- `folder_sync._reconcile_folder`: before ingesting, if there is work
and the download is still pending, the job fails with one job-level
message ("The embedding model '...' is not downloaded yet. Indexing
starts on its own once its Settings download finishes."; a folder with
auto sync off is told to sync again instead). No file is marked failed
and the existing index is left as it is. The periodic sync then indexes
the folder by itself once the transfer lands, with no Rebuild needed.
- A download-required error that still happens mid-sync (the transfer
going pending after the check) is not written to `failed_files`, so the
next sync retries those files. Entries written that way before this
change are no longer held back either, so folders already stuck like the
one in the report recover on the next periodic sync.
- The three raise sites now build the message with one shared helper, so
the stored error text can be recognized reliably.

## Testing

On Windows 11, Ryzen 5600H, RTX 3050 4 GB, Python 3.12:

- New `tests/test_rag_folder_sync_download_pending.py` (8 tests): the
check skips the loader when nothing is pending, follows a pending
transfer to completion, and leaves other load failures to the documents.
The sync waits without marking files, then a periodic sync indexes all
of them once the download lands. A Rebuild while pending keeps the
existing index. Mid-sync download errors aren't held back, but a
genuinely bad file still is. Pre-existing stuck entries retry.
- Real Studio end to end (`run.py --api-only`, sentence-transformers on
CPU, empty HF cache, `RAG_FOLDER_SYNC_INTERVAL_S=5`): saved
`unsloth/bge-small-en-v1.5` in Settings (stored with `download_pending:
true`), linked a 40-file folder, then started Studio's own download
through `POST /api/hub/download` and waited, triggering only periodic
syncs.
- main: `40 file(s) could not be indexed`, each failing with "is not
downloaded yet". After the download completed, the folder still showed
40 failures and 0 documents.
- this branch: "The embedding model 'unsloth/bge-small-en-v1.5' is not
downloaded yet..." with 0 failed files. After the download completed,
the folder went idle with 40 documents and 0 failures.
- Related suites on this branch and on a clean copy of main gave
identical results: test_rag_linked_folders,
test_rag_folder_sync_retirement, test_rag_folder_scan_filters,
test_rag_linked_folder_grant_retry, test_folder_sync_account_rotation,
test_embedding_model_settings/resolve/security_gate,
test_offline_embedding_minimal, test_openai_embeddings_studio_fallback,
test_rag_embed_llama_server, test_rag_embeddings,
test_rag_embedding_identity, test_rag_reembed, test_rag_ingestion,
test_rag_source_files_indexing, test_conversation_archive,
test_rag_reconcile_orphaned. The failures that do occur (symlinks and
case-sensitive paths in test_offline_embedding_minimal,
test_openai_embeddings_studio_fallback and test_rag_embed_llama_server)
happen on clean main too on this Windows machine.
- `ruff check` is clean on the changed files.

Not covered: the llama-server embedding backend end to end (no
llama-server binary on this machine). Its raise site only switched to
the shared message helper.

## Follow-up (maintainer)

- Merged current main (conflict with #16607's per-thread connection
reuse in `finish_pending`, resolved keeping both).
- The job-level message no longer says "still downloading": the pending
marker is also set when the Settings download was never started, so it
now says the model is not downloaded yet.
- The new test module clears the process-wide embedding resolution memo
around each test; without it, 7 tests in
`test_rag_embed_llama_server.py` failed when run after it in one
session.
- Real loader repro (no mocks, CPU, tiny sentence-transformers model,
empty HF cache, pending marker set, 40-file folder, then the snapshot
lands and the next periodic sync runs): main fails all 40 files and
still holds back all 40 after the download; this branch fails 0, then
indexes all 40 on the next periodic sync and retires the marker.
