Studio: validate each dataset snapshot once per provenance attestation (#16790)

Before a Studio training run starts, `attest_loaded_dataset` checks that
every data file of the loaded dataset comes from an exact Hugging Face
cache snapshot. For each data file it re-validated the whole snapshot,
and that check walks every file in it (resolve, `is_file`, `open`). The
answer depends only on the snapshot (repo + commit, or the snapshot
folder), so a dataset with K data files paid about K^2 file checks
before the first step, twice when an eval split was attested from the
same files.

Single-file datasets were unaffected. Datasets sharded into many parquet
/ json files (common for larger Hub datasets) waited seconds to minutes
on "starting".

## Change

`attest_loaded_dataset` wraps the two whole-snapshot validators
(`exact_dataset_snapshot_for_commit` for `hf://` / URL sources,
`exact_dataset_snapshot_path` for local-path sources) in
`functools.lru_cache` objects created inside the call, so each snapshot
is validated once per call. Nothing is cached across calls, so no
attestation outlives the call that made it. Every data file still gets
its own resolve and its own `st_size == num_bytes` check, and the
returned snapshot path and reason strings are unchanged.

## Results

File checks (`resolved_dataset_snapshot_file` calls) per attestation:

| Data files (K) | Hub sources, main | Hub sources, this branch | Local
paths, main | Local paths, this branch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 50 | 2,550 | 100 | 2,600 | 150 |
| 200 | 40,200 | 400 | 40,400 | 600 |

Attestation time on Linux (fake HF cache, median of 3 runs per arm, each
arm run twice):

| Data files (K) | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 50 | 0.65 / 0.78 s | 0.03 / 0.02 s |
| 200 | 12.1 / 14.3 s | 0.09 / 0.12 s |
| 500 | 59.1 / 70.7 s | 0.22 / 0.22 s |

Studio MiniMax-H3: opt-in FlashInfer SM120 fused block kernels for FP8 and NVFP4 (#16875)

## What

Opt-in (`UNSLOTH_H3_FLASHINFER=1`) use of FlashInfer 0.7.3's MiniMax-H3
SM120 fused block kernels for a resident FP8 or NVFP4 H3 denoiser:
`diffusion_ops.minimax_h3_*_pre_attention`, `*_out_proj` and
`minimax_h3_mlp_*_sm120` (FlashInfer PRs #6169 / #6196), in a new
`video_minimax_h3_flashinfer.py` with one guarded hook in `video.py`
before compile.

- Engages only on sm_120 with flashinfer >= 0.7.3 and a resident fp8 /
nvfp4 denoiser; per-op kill switches `UNSLOTH_H3_FI_PRE`,
`UNSLOTH_H3_FI_OUT`, `UNSLOTH_H3_FI_MLP`.
- Weights are repacked into FlashInfer's layout at install, one block at
a time, and the stock weights are released, so peak VRAM matches stock.
The repack is exact (codes and scales equal FlashInfer's own quantizer
byte for byte).
- An install-time self-check runs each op against the stock block;
anything missing or failing (no flashinfer, no JIT toolchain, a
mismatch) keeps the stock path with the reason logged.
- A missing JIT toolchain (no nvcc, a runtime-only CUDA install, no
ninja) is logged as one line with the build's own diagnosis (for example
`nvcc: not found`) and the toolchain it needs. A streamed or int8 / bf16
denoiser is refused before flashinfer is imported.
- One compiled graph is shared by all 50 blocks: 0 graph breaks, the
same graph count as stock (10 NVFP4, 3 FP8).
- The NVFP4 pre-attention kernel needs one scale shared by q/k/v;
without it, only the out-projection and MLP ops engage.
- The FlashInfer attention kernels (varlen fp8 / nvfp4, dense FP4) were
evaluated and are not used: on the default INT8 path they double or
triple LPIPS against bf16.

## Numbers (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, sm_120, H3 t2v 960x544x124, 20
steps, 2 prompts, LPIPS against Studio's bf16 render)

Per op (real inputs, M = 19,315 tokens, medians of 6): NVFP4
pre-attention 1.64x, out-projection 1.65x, MLP 1.53x faster than
Studio's ops (whole block 1.13x); FP8 1.14x / 1.30x / 1.13x (block
1.05x). Error against the reference is the same as Studio's ops (ratio
1.00).

| arm | s/clip | s/step | peak VRAM GiB | LPIPS h00 / h01 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FP8 stock (hosted file) | 55.86 | 2.701 | 55.3 | 0.262 / 0.411 |
| FP8 + FlashInfer | **52.46** | 2.530 | 55.0 | 0.260 / 0.399 |
| NVFP4 stock | 47.47 | 2.308 | 47.6 | 0.483 / 0.635 |
| NVFP4 + FlashInfer | **43.27** | 2.099 | 47.8 | 0.490 / 0.661 |

Repeat runs are bit-identical and agree within 0.15 s/clip. The NVFP4
LPIPS change (+0.007 / +0.026) is inside the 0.04-0.05 spread between
two equally valid NVFP4 quantizations of the same weights. 1,951 calls
per op per render, 0 fallbacks.

The NVFP4 rows used a locally built H3 NVFP4 checkpoint; Studio main has
no hosted H3 NVFP4 file, so on main today this lever engages on the FP8
path only.

## Tests

`tests/test_video_minimax_h3_flashinfer.py` (gating by arch / version /
residency, kill switches, repack round trip, fallback when flashinfer or
the toolchain is missing, self-check failure keeps stock, one-line
reason for a failed JIT build, invalid y margin).

With the switch off, the H3 load path is unchanged: the new module is
imported lazily at H3 load, `install_h3_flashinfer` returns before
touching the denoiser, flashinfer is never imported, and importing
`video.py` costs the same (median 0.229 s on both sides, 10 runs each).

## Not covered

RTX 5090 (32 GB cards stream H3 at this size, and the lever disables
itself when streamed), other resolutions and step counts, torch versions
other than 2.13. These kernels are not in FlashInfer's prebuilt cache:
first use JIT-compiles for about 4 minutes and needs nvcc >= 12.8 and
ninja.

Studio: probe STT Transformers availability off the event loop (#16783)

`GET /api/inference/audio/stt/status` (the speech-to-text status route)
calls `stt_sidecar.is_available()` twice inside the async handler. The
first call in a backend process runs `ensure_stt_available()`, which
imports PyAV, torch and Transformers. That import ran on the event loop,
so every other request waited on it, including chat token streams that
were already running.

The route is hit from Voice settings, dictation, the Audio page, chat
audio upload, and the loaded-models indicator (which polls every 5 s
when enabled), so the first visit after a launch could freeze an ongoing
chat stream for one to several seconds.

The probe now runs once per request through `asyncio.to_thread`, the
same way the route already runs its other blocking probes
(`downloaded_model_ids`, `_audio_cpp_runtime_status`). The result fills
both `available` fields. `/v1/models` already makes this exact call from
a worker thread, so the threaded path is an existing production path on
every OS.

The JSON response is identical, it is returned at the same time, and
errors are handled the same way.

Studio: draw nothing for the glass lens when it is Off (glass 1.4 to 2.1x faster without GPU rendering) (#16852)

With the glass lens set to Off, which is the default, the composer still
drew a full copy of the background image inside itself, only to paint a
faint tinted line along its edge. This PR stops drawing that copy
whenever the lens is Off, on every platform.

- **Speed:** without GPU rendering (the Linux desktop app on some NVIDIA
setups), the copy was re-blurred on every frame. Removing it makes glass
interactions 1.4 to 2.1x faster there (table below), which is part of
the lag in a [Reddit
report](https://www.reddit.com/r/unsloth/comments/1xokuk4/why_does_unsloth_lag_so_much/).
With GPU rendering the copy was cheap, so speed is the same.
- **Looks:** the faint tinted line is gone and the composer shows its
glass style's normal edge (screenshots below).
- **Unchanged:** the Magnify and Shrink lenses, which still draw their
copies because the lens effect needs them.

## Details

`Lens` always rendered its rim, a full-size clone of the wallpaper with
a CSS filter, kept in place by a 300 ms poll; only the fill was skipped
for Off. Now `lensDrawn(material, lens)` in `model.ts` returns false for
Off and `ComposerGlassLenses` mounts nothing.

The edge changes because `.unsloth-composer-surface:has(> .glass-lens)`
cleared `--composer-shadow`. With no lens, each glass style's own edge
shows again (inset highlights and a soft glow for the Liquid styles, a
1px outline for the others) instead of the wallpaper-tinted rim line.

Glass without GPU rendering is still slower than the solid theme. The
rest of that cost is the backdrop-filter panes and glass menus, which
this PR does not touch.

## Performance

Without GPU rendering, lens Off. Median ms from the action to the next
painted frame (33 ms is the 60 Hz floor for the slider and menu;
scrolling is per frame, 17 ms is 60 fps):

| | main | this PR | glass off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Glass strength slider step | 325 | 154 | 83 |
| Scrolling Settings, per frame | 60 | 35 | 9 |
| Opening a menu in Settings | 301 | 210 | 162 |

Measured on the real Studio UI against main `7b7ebff5d3` in system
WebKitGTK 2.52.6 (the desktop app's engine) at 1920x1080 on an RTX 3090,
with Liquid Glass 3D, a background image and glass menus on. Magnify
measures the same on both builds, and with GPU rendering
(`WEBKIT_DMABUF_RENDERER_FORCE_SHM=1 WEBKIT_FORCE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1`)
lens Off was already fast and is unchanged (74 ms per slider step on
both).

its commits, and the gate fails on current `main` by design (that is the
regression it catches).

## Why

#16603 came back because nothing in CI measured per-keystroke cost
against chat length. Bisecting the Studio frontend from `v0.1.913` to
`main`:

| Build (200-turn agent chat, about 427K tokens) | Style work per
keystroke |
| --- | --- |
| before #16333 | 15.6 ms |
| #16333 (wallpaper fade `:has()`) | 619 ms |
| `v0.1.914-beta` | 144 ms |
| `main` | 136.5 ms |
| `main` + #16656 | 4.6 ms |

#16333 added a descendant `:has()` on elements that hold the whole
thread (`[data-wallpaper-workspace]`, `[data-chat-content-root]`), so
Chromium (Desktop, Chrome, Edge) walks every message on each keystroke.
Firefox is not affected, which matches the "browser is fine" reports.
#16751 (Reduce Motion default off) then made scroll pay that walk more
often (61 ms to 188 ms per wheel step), which is why turning Reduce
Motion back on did not help typing. #16300 (`d56738f40`) already removed
two other #16333 rules that restyled the whole page on every key
(real-app bisect: 563.8 to 91.2 ms per key), which is why 0.1.914 was
slow but not as slow as #16333. The fade rule stayed. #16656 removes
every such rule and adds a static guard test; this PR adds the runtime
gate so a new rule of that shape, or anything else that scales with chat
length, cannot ship again.

## What the gate does

`tests/studio/playwright_long_thread_gate.py` runs **first** in every
frontend lane, right after `npm ci`: Frontend CI (Linux, Windows),
Composer compatibility (Ubuntu, macOS, Windows, Safari) and Inline
images (Ubuntu, macOS, Windows).

1. Builds `smoke-thread-weight.html` for production
(`vite.long-thread.config.ts`) and seeds an agent-style history inside
the real app ancestors (`?shell=1`: sidebar workspace, wallpaper, chat
content root) with open reasoning, tool cards, web sources, compaction
markers, code, KaTeX and tables. The fixture shape is checked, so a
fixture that stops rendering something fails.
2. Measures the 200-turn chat first. Two untraced keys decide how much
to trace: a healthy page traces 10 keys, a slow one 2, and a page
hundreds of times slower than healthy fails on the untraced number
alone.
3. Fails if `:has()` matching costs more than 5 ms per key at 200 turns,
or if total selector matching per key grows more than 2x from 40 to 200
turns. A second repeat runs only when the ratio is near the limit. Both
checks are ratios or tiny budgets on selector matching, so a slow runner
cannot fail them.

## What a failure says

A failure prints ms per key at each size, how far over budget it is and
the top selectors with their match attempts. Selectors tried on most of
the DOM are marked as likely victims of a whole-page restyle. It then
pins down the trigger: it removes `:has()` rules from the stylesheet
text before fresh page loads (rules switched off in a page that already
rendered leave Chromium's `:has()` state behind and blame the wrong
rule) and bisects for the rule whose removal makes typing cheap, trying
rules that search an element holding the thread first. Each rule found
is mapped to its likely source with a text match, worded as a
possibility. On current `main`:

```
FAIL: :has() matching costs 63.6 ms per keystroke at 200 turns, budget 5.0 ms (12.7x over); total selector matching 358.9 ms/key
  pin-down at 60 turns, untraced style recalc per keystroke: 48.5 ms with all 262 :has() rules, 1.1 ms with none of them
  Measured: removing only this rule takes the keystroke from 48.5 to 1.8 ms (no :has() rules: 1.1 ms); this rule on its own costs 4.9 ms:
    :is([data-wallpaper-workspace], [data-chat-content-root]):has(> .chat-wallpaper[data-ready] .chat-wallpaper-image[data-fade="false"]) .thread-bottom-fade
    It is possible this section caused the issue, but we cannot be sure (a text match):
      studio/frontend/src/index.css:6210 (exact text match)
    Pattern: `:has(> .chat-wallpaper[data-ready] .chat-wallpaper-image[data-fade="false"])` on `:is([data-wallpaper-workspace], [data-chat-content-root])` searches all descendants (no leading `>`, or a space inside), so Chromium re-walks everything under that element after each DOM change, whether or not anything matches.
      `[data-wallpaper-workspace]` (first found in studio/frontend/src/app/routes/__root.tsx:720) holds the whole thread, so every keystroke walks every message.
```

`tests/studio/test_css_culprit.py` covers the source mapping and the
`:has()` shape check.

## Replay against past stylesheets

The gate on this branch, with only `index.css` swapped in from each
commit (CPU runner):

without it |

## Other changes

and the `?shell=1` app shell.
- The gate's Chromium step installs missing Linux libraries only when
Chromium cannot launch, through `retry-with-apt-lock.sh` with

browser steps.

Context parallel: accept Unsloth's fast Qwen3 attention and compiled FastModel attention (#16870)

## Problem

Context parallel (Ulysses) refuses Qwen3 under both loaders. Both paths
stop at the same check in `context_parallel.py`
(`_supports_context_parallel`), for two reasons:

- **FastLanguageModel:** `_uses_fast_llama_attention` matches only
`LlamaAttention_fast_forward` by identity. `Qwen3Attention_fast_forward`
also attends through `run_attention`, which already performs the Ulysses
exchange, but is refused.
- **FastModel:** the compiled attention fails the Hugging Face registry
check in `ulysses_hybrid`. Unsloth Zoo's compiler moves the attention
body into a module-level `Qwen3Attention_forward`, and the class
`forward` only calls it, so the class forward itself never references
`ALL_ATTENTION_FUNCTIONS`.

Behind the first refusal was also a latent bug.
`Qwen3Attention_fast_forward` sized its RoPE table by the local shard
length, while positions under context parallel are global. Llama already
scales it by the CP size.

## Fix

- `attention_dispatch.context_parallel_attention`: a declaration on an
Unsloth attention forward. It says the forward attends only through
`run_attention` and sizes RoPE by the global length while a CP manager
is active. `context_parallel` accepts any declared forward instead of
matching the Llama forward by identity. `llama.running_forward` resolves
the forward pre_patch's gate actually runs.
- Declared forwards:
  - Llama keeps DPO / GRPO (`rl = True`).
- Qwen3 is declared for SFT only, so DPO / GRPO on the fast Qwen3
attention still raise the existing Llama-only message until they get
their own parity run.
- Mistral, Cohere and Granite stay undeclared: their RoPE / window still
use the local length.
- `Qwen3Attention_fast_forward` sizes RoPE by `kv_seq_len * cp_size`
under context parallel, as Llama does. It is unchanged without a CP
manager.
- `ulysses_hybrid`: a class forward that only calls one module-level
function counts as registry attention when that function reads the
registry. Zoo's compiled attention qualifies. A forward calling several
functions, like the fast forwards, does not, so no registry wrapper is
installed where nothing would call it.

The delegation follow is not Qwen3-specific: every zoo-compiled text
attention that delegates to one registry-reading function now passes the
check under FastModel. Families with 2-rank CPU gloo parity against one
process (SDPA rows, SDPA packed, eager; every parameter grad within rtol
1e-4): qwen3, llama, mistral, qwen2, qwen3_moe, gemma, gemma2, granite,
cohere, cohere2, olmo2, mixtral, qwen2_moe, phi3, glm4, smollm3,
exaone4, apertus, ernie4_5, hunyuan_v1_dense, granitemoe, seed_oss,
olmo3. Compiled Qwen3-Next / Qwen3.5 with eager attention also work now
(before: `found no eager_attention_forward`). MoE and multimodal queries
still go through the capability gate.

Sliding window, softcap and sinks stay refused on the fast forwards.
Ring stays sm80+ only and Ulysses-only on the compiled path.

## Testing

New `tests/test_cp_unsloth_attention_gloo.py` (CPU gloo, 2 ranks against
one process): before, 10 failed and 1 passed (the "undeclared forward
stays refused" control); after, 11 passed.

| case | what is checked |
|---|---|
| fast Qwen3 attention, GQA split / kv replication / packed documents |
output, input grads and every parameter grad within 1e-4; one Ulysses
exchange per call; RoPE covers the global length |
| zoo-compiled Qwen3 attention, generated by
`unsloth_compile_transformers("qwen3")` | class forward delegates to
`Qwen3Attention_forward`; 2-rank parity for SDPA rows, SDPA packed and
eager |
| DPO / GRPO | still refused on the fast Qwen3 attention, still allowed
on Llama |

Existing suites on the branch:
- CP / Ulysses / context parallel RL / wrapper registry / refusal tests:
233 passed, 2 skipped;
- `test_parallel_cp_compose_gloo.py`: 60 passed;
- `test_cpu_route_context_parallel.py`: 10 passed;
- `test_parallel_capabilities_*`: 74 passed.

Kaggle 2 x T4, fp16, NCCL, torch 2.11 / transformers 5.20.2 / TRL 1.15.
Base is the merge base, head the branch, on the same VM:
- Base refuses FastLanguageModel and FastModel Qwen3 under CP2 Ulysses

- Head matches one process on the same rows within the A/A band in every

negative controls fail.
- Every rank logged Ulysses exchanges on the path under test.

Pipeline parallel: refuse the MoE router aux loss over several micro-batches at Trainer init (#16822)

## Problem

With `UNSLOTH_PP_SIZE` set, a MoE model whose router load-balancing loss
is on, with the Trainer batch split into more than one micro-batch, is
refused. The pipeline adds that loss per micro-batch, which is not the
loss one GPU forms over the whole batch. The refusal only fired inside
`trainer.train()` at the first step (`_pp_training_step`), after the
model had already been split into stages and the trainer built. Every
other pipeline refusal fires in the Trainer init, before anything is
split.

Repro on CPU gloo, PP2, tiny qwen3_moe, `output_router_logits = True`,
batch 2 (2 micro-batches):

```
NotImplementedError: Unsloth: UNSLOTH_PP_SIZE=2 (pipeline parallel) splits each Trainer batch into 2 micro-batches, ...
phase = train, split = True
```

## Fix

The same refusal now also runs in `pp_trainer_refusals`, before the
split:

- `_plan_microbatches` is the micro-batch arithmetic from
`resolve_microbatches`, pulled out so it only needs plain inputs: the
requested count, `UNSLOTH_PP_MICROBATCHES`, stage count, schedule and
batch size. `resolve_microbatches` calls it, so the step and the init
check agree on the count. Behaviour and notices are unchanged.
- `_router_aux_coef_at_init` reads the coefficient the last stage will
apply, from the inputs the trainer will act on:
- plain Trainer: the config's `output_router_logits` and the CausalLM's
coefficient;
- TRL trainers: `router_aux_loss_coef` from the config arguments (None =
the architecture's value; 0.0 = off). TRL rewrites
`output_router_logits` inside its own init, after this check runs.
- Only families whose aux loss the pipeline carries are checked; other
MoE models are already refused by the split.
- `_refuse_split_router_aux_at_init` predicts the micro-batch count for
`per_device_train_batch_size`, and for `per_device_eval_batch_size` when
the Trainer evaluates, but only when every rank surely gets a full batch
(the dataset has at least batch x dp rows). It raises the same message
when that count is above 1. A missing dataset (an evaluation-only
Trainer never trains), a smaller dataset (Accelerate's batch sharding
and padding set the size), a dataset with no `len()` and SFT packing
(TRL rebuilds the rows inside its own init) are left to the per-step
check.
- The per-step check stays, for cases only known at the step, such as a
smaller last batch.
- The message also names `router_aux_loss_coef = 0.0` as a way to turn
the loss off.

## Testing

CPU gloo, torch 2.13, transformers 5.17.0, TRL 1.15.0.

| test | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| refused at init (config flag / TRL coefficient x gpipe / 1f1b): phase
is init, model not split, every parameter unchanged | 4 failed | 4
passed |
| allowed layouts still train (aux off; TRL coefficient 0.0;
`UNSLOTH_PP_MICROBATCHES=1`; batch 1) | 4 passed | 4 passed |
| unit: 1F1B padding, eval batch, TRL coefficient None / 0.0 / 0.1,
plain Trainer coefficient 0, non-dividing micro-batch count, non-carried
model | failed | passed |
| unit: evaluation-only Trainer (no `train_dataset`) with a splitting
train batch is allowed, a splitting eval batch is refused;
`train_dataset` read from kwargs and positional args | failed | passed |
| unit: datasets smaller than one batch per dp rank (1 row, 2 rows, 8
rows at batch 5 x dp 2, a dict eval set) are left to the step; a full
batch per rank is refused; iterable dataset and packing left to the step
| failed | passed |

Existing pipeline / parallel env / MoE aux suites
(`test_parallel_env.py`, `test_pp_env_gloo.py`,
`test_pp_moe_aux_gloo.py`, `test_parallel_cp_compose_gloo.py -k "pp or
parallel_env or moe"`): 196 passed.

Studio: stop read aloud from waiting on a model catalog rescan (#16831)

With the "Unsloth model" read-aloud engine, Read aloud in chat can take
seconds longer than Generate on the Audio page for the same text and the
same loaded speech model. A user on Discord reported 10 to 20 s in chat
against about half a second on the Audio page.

## Cause

Before every utterance, `generateStudioTtsAudio` looks up the loaded
speech model with `GET /v1/models` (`resolveReadAloudModel`, added in
#14191) so it can name it in `/audio/generate`. `/v1/models` lists every
downloaded model, and the scan behind it is cached for only 30 s
(`_CATALOG_TTL_S`). A click more than 30 s after the last listing, which
is the usual case for reading a finished reply, waits for a full rescan
of the downloaded models. The Audio page never lists the catalog, so it
does not pay this cost. Auto read-aloud and the Settings › Voice preview
use the same function and wait the same way.

## Fix

Read aloud now lists models from `GET /api/inference/loaded-models`,
which #10728 added so agent startup would not wait on the same scan. Its
rows are the same `_openai_model_objects` entries that `/v1/models`
marks `loaded: true`, including `task` and `audio_workflows` for a
speech model kept beside the chat model, so the chosen model id does not
change.

There are no backend changes. The "Custom endpoint" engine and system
voices do not use this lookup and are unchanged. If the reporter was
using "Custom endpoint", this PR does not address their delay.

Not addressed: the same report says auto read-aloud does not speak a
scheduled task's reply when the chat is opened. `AutoReadAloud` only
speaks a reply that finishes while the chat is open, which is how it
treats every chat opened from history. Speaking unread scheduled results
on open would need a separate product decision.

## Verification

Live on `origin/main` (`16060aba73`) with a CPU-only Studio,
`gemma-4-E2B-it` Q4_K_M as the chat model and Kokoro-82M loaded beside
it. I sent the request sequence the adapter sends (the listing, then
`/audio/generate` naming the speech model it found), waiting 35 s before
each one. Listing time:

| Round | `/v1/models` (main) | `/api/inference/loaded-models` (this PR)
|
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 3.25 s | 0.02 s |
| 2 | 13.16 s | 0.01 s |
| 3 | 3.78 s | 0.01 s |

Generation took about 9 s on both (Kokoro on the CPU). Both listings
returned the same loaded rows, and every response came from Kokoro.

- `read-aloud-studio-voice.test.ts` now serves the loaded-models
listing, and a new test checks that read aloud never requests
`/v1/models`. It fails on main.
`tts-custom-connections-disabled.test.ts` mocks the new path.
- 380 tests in the read-aloud, TTS and model-catalog files pass. Full
frontend suite: 14943 pass and 18 fail. 17 of those also fail with
main's versions of these files. The remaining one is a find-in-page
timing test that passes 3 out of 3 times when run alone.
- Typecheck passes. Biome and ESLint report the same findings on these
files as on main.
- I did not click Read aloud in a browser.

Context parallel: give decoder layers no mask inside a CP step so block compile keeps one graph on packed rows (#16862)

## Problem

Under context parallel (Ulysses) with packed or padding-free rows,
Unsloth's block compile recompiles the decoder layer more often than one
process does on the same rows. On 2 CPU gloo ranks with GA 2 that was 6
recompiles and 5 graphs per rank, against 1 recompile and 3 graphs for
one process.

Hugging Face builds each layer's `attention_mask` from the shard-local
`position_ids`. When a rank's shard of a packed row holds no document
start (for example row lengths `[8, 2, 6]` give rank 0 positions
`0..7`), the packed-sequence detection finds nothing and the layer gets
`attention_mask = None`. Other rows give the same rank a tensor. The
compiled decoder layer guards on the argument's type and recompiles on
every switch. The mask was only dropped by the `self_attn` pre-hook,
inside the layer, after the compiled call had already guarded on it.

## Fix

- `context_parallel.py`: a decoder-layer pre-hook sets `attention_mask`
to `None` while a CP manager is active.
- It is registered once per layer, first in hook order, next to the
existing `self_attn` hook, so the compiled layer always sees the same
argument.
- CP attention never read this mask: it uses `packed_seq_lengths` and
the validated right padding, and the `self_attn` hook already dropped
it.
- Layers that also hold a `linear_attn` are skipped, since that scan
reads the padding mask.
- Outside a CP step, or without CP, the layer receives the original mask
object.
- `parallel_capabilities.py`:
- `cp.ulysses` / `cp.ring` declare the decoder-layer hook. It is not
exclusive, so it composes with block compile.
- The "packed rows x cp Ulysses (DDP), Unsloth block compile" cell opens
for what was measured: qwen3 / llama, LoRA, SDPA, no sliding window,
torch >= 2.13.
- Everything else in that combination stays unverified through a
separate, unmeasured cell.

## Testing

`test_block_compile_packed_rows_under_cp_match_one_process`, 2 CPU ranks
against one process on the same rows with the real block compile:
- qwen3 / llama x packed / padding-free x GA 1 / 2;
- loss, grads and parameters checked;
- Ulysses engaged and packed lengths used;
- compile counters checked against one process.

Studio diffusion: measured activations for Lumina-Image-2.0 (int8 stays resident on 16-24 GB cards, ~3% per render) (#16808)

Lumina-Image-2.0 had no row in `_MEASURED_IMAGE_ACTIVATION_MIB`, so the
planner priced its activations with the flat 8 GiB guess. That guess
cost it residency in two places:

- **L4 (22.5 GB):** the flat plan missed all-resident by 43 MiB (20,364
MiB needed vs a 20,321 MiB budget). It streamed the Gemma-2-2B text
encoder on every new prompt. This hits the default load, because AUTO
picks int8 there.
- **16 GB cards, int8:** the transformer was streamed every denoise
step.

This PR adds a measured row for `lumina-2`. One narrow planner rule
comes with it: a plain bf16 Lumina-2 keeps the whole-module offload the
flat plan already took on 16 GB cards (see "bf16 on 16 GB cards" below),
so no load gets slower than on main.

### Measurement

The protocol is the same as the existing rows. Each run does one load,
then records `max_memory_allocated` per phase (encode, denoise, VAE
decode) above the resident weights. Settings: bf16, CFG 4, 1024^2 and
2048^2, eager / default / max tiers plus int8, on a Colab A100 (all
resident) and an L4.

| Text encoder | 1,130 | 80 when resident; 1,130 is the streamed reading
|
| Denoise | 486 | eager; 250 compiled, 285 int8 |
| Decode, untiled 1024^2 | 4,497 | 2,439 eager. The first decode on the
default / max tiers peaks at 4,497 on A100 (3,471 on L4) for the cudnn
benchmark workspace; later decodes take 1,413 |
| Decode, tiled 1024^2 | 4,497 | Tiling is a no-op at 1024^2, so this is
capped at the untiled figure |
| 2048^2 worst | 4,497 | Eager denoise 1,914, tiled decode 2,466 |

Both tiers use the worst figure in each column, and the usual 1.2x
margin is applied on top.

### Results

Colab L4, Studio in process. Base is the merge base `9ebc608923`. Each
phase ran fresh processes in the order base, head, base, head, base, so
the three base arms give the A/A spread. Settings: 20 steps, CFG 4, 3
prompts after 1 warmup render. The 16 and 22 GiB caps are simulated on

- **int8 (what AUTO loads on 16-24 GB cards):** about 3% less wall time
per render (0.7-0.9 s) on every card. The saving comes from renders with
a new prompt, which no longer upload the encoder. Steps run at the same
speed, or 1% faster at 16 GiB, where the transformer no longer streams.
- **Explicit bf16 at 16 GiB:** same placement as main (whole-module
offload), and every head arm sits inside the base A/A range on both
tiers. The two bf16 rows ran on the final head, in a later L4 session
than the int8 rows.
- **Peak VRAM:** every head arm stayed within its card. The peak
reserved shown is the larger of the two head arms.
- (*) This row ran an earlier head whose decode figure was 3,471. On a
16 GiB card it gives the same plan as the final row.

### bf16 on 16 GB cards

With the measured row alone, an explicit bf16 load at 16 GiB moved from
whole-module offload to "transformer resident, encoder streamed". On the
L4 that was about 1% slower per render on the eager tier (0.8571 vs
0.8458 s/step, 18.90 vs 18.70 s), and the same within noise on the
default tier. Streaming the 4.8 GB Gemma-2 encoder block by block on
each new prompt costs about what uploading the 4.9 GB transformer once
per call saves.

So `prefer_whole_module_offload` now also prices a Lumina-2 plan that
the measured row moved off a streamed-transformer pick, exactly as it
priced that streamed pick on main: plain bf16 where whole-module offload
is cheaper goes back to whole-module offload (with main's VAE tiling and
generation guard), and everything else keeps the measured plan. int8 /
fp8 loads are not plain bf16, so their gains above are untouched. The
rule is opt-in per family (`_CALIBRATED_KEEPS_WHOLE_MODULE =
{"lumina-2"}`); no other family's plan changes.

### Outputs

- **bf16, eager tier:** all 5 arms (3 base, 2 head) wrote byte-identical
images for all 3 prompts, before and after the bf16 rule.
- **int8 and the compiled default tier:** these are not bit-reproducible
from one process to the next, so even two base arms differ. Each process
picks one of a few kernel variants, and the image hashes cluster by
variant, not by placement. For example, the same 3-image set came out of
a resident head arm and a streamed base arm in different runs. LPIPS
between any two arms is at most 0.0041.

### Tests

There are four planner cases in
`tests/test_diffusion_calibrated_activation.py`, built from the planner
inputs a real L4 load logged:

- int8 on a 16 GB card keeps the transformer resident.
- int8 on an L4 goes all resident, while bf16 keeps streaming the
encoder.
- More VRAM never picks a slower tier. On main, 12 to 14 GB went from
whole-module offload to streaming the transformer every step.
- bf16 at 16 GB keeps the whole-module plan main took (same offload,
tiling and slicing, no calibrated guard), while int8, another family, or
a card where streaming prices cheaper keeps the measured plan. Emptying
the family set makes it fail.

All four fail on main and pass here. The calibrated activation, auto

`test_every_image_family_vae_is_covered_or_kept_stock_on_purpose`, is an
import error between this host's diffusers and huggingface_hub installs,
not the changed code.

### Not covered

- RTX 3090 / 4090 class 24 GB cards and Windows were not run.
- The bf16 rule was not timed on a 16 GB card whose fast host link makes
streaming price cheaper than whole-module offload; there the measured
resident-transformer plan stands, which never streams the transformer
per step.

Studio LTX-2.5: keep a streamed denoiser partly resident per request (#16845)

## What

LTX-2.5 was outside the per-request DiT residency fit
(`video_stream_residency`) that Wan, HunyuanVideo-1.5 and LTX-2 (#16787)
use on the `group` / `streaming` tiers. On cards that stream the LTX-2.5
DiT (L4, 16-24 GiB budgets) every forward copied all 48 blocks from the
host while part of the card stayed idle: 11.55 GiB of H2D per forward
for GGUF Q4_K_M and 23.6 GiB for the INT8 DiT on an L4.

1. `ltx-2.5` joins `RESIDENT_FAMILIES` (exact name), so the leading
blocks stay resident per request, sized from the measured request peak
with the existing margin, and only the rest stream through the existing
prefetch.
2. LTX-2.5's Gemma 4 encoder runs in a worker process on the same card.
Before an encode that is not a cache hit,
`video_ltx25.lend_resident_dit_for_encode` streams resident blocks again
when that makes the encoder fit: the whole encoder if lending gets it
there, else the worker's own layer-streamed need (`stream_need_mib`,
reported in its ready message; #16750's streamed encode), and pins them
back right after the encode. The room check is the worker's
`_encode_room_mib`, so both processes compute it the same way.
3. A cancelled encode that borrowed blocks stops the worker before they
are pinned back (it may still be computing on the lent memory); the next
encode restarts it.

Placement only: the same weights and kernels run. Kill switch: the
existing `UNSLOTH_VIDEO_DIT_RESIDENT=0` (also disables the lending).

Studio LTX-2.5: release the server's cached GPU blocks before an encode, so later prompts stop encoding on the CPU (#16804)

## What

Since #16750, the LTX-2.5 Gemma 4 encoder worker streams its layers
through the GPU when the whole encoder does not fit. Its room check is
the load budget minus what the server process holds
(`torch.cuda.memory_reserved`). After the first render, the server still
holds that render's cached allocator blocks, so the room drops below the
streamed-encode need and every new prompt after the first one encodes on
the CPU (165-231 s per prompt on Colab L4 / A100 hosts).

This PR empties the server's CUDA (or XPU) cache right before a
non-resident encode request, so the worker's room check counts only
memory the server is using. Cache hits and resident encoders are
untouched. Placement only: the worker's own routing (whole, streamed,
CPU) is main's.

The first version of this PR also added its own per-module streaming in
the worker; #16750 landed an equivalent layer-streamed encode first, so
the worker now matches main and only the server-side release remains.

Pipeline parallel on CPU: run the chunked cross entropy on the last stage (#16846)

## Problem

On the CPU backend, Unsloth Zoo's chunked cross entropy is armed only
inside its `SFTTrainer.compute_loss` wrapper. Under `UNSLOTH_PP_SIZE`
the pipeline training step drives the stages itself and never calls
`compute_loss`. So the last stage silently falls back to full `[rows,
vocab]` logits. The loss stays correct; only memory and time regress,
and nothing reports it.

Measured on CPU gloo, PP2, tiny Qwen3 (vocab 151936), LoRA, 3 steps:

| | chunked CE calls (last stage) | lm_head forwards | logit rows per
tensor |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | 0 | 6 to 12 | full rows (36 to 40) |
| after | used every micro-batch | 0 | at most one chunk |

## Fix

`_pp_training_step` now finds the model the zoo wrapper would arm
(`_cpu_chunked_ce_model`). It only does so when the trainer's
`compute_loss` is that wrapper and the loss type is `nll`. The step arms
the chunked loss around `stage.step` and disarms it in a `finally`, the
same window `compute_loss` gives it on one process. GPU training and any
trainer without the zoo CPU wrapper are unchanged.

## Testing

after 4 passed. The two failing tests check that the step arms and
disarms the flag; the other two check that it stays off for another
`compute_loss` or loss type. `tests/test_pp_env_gloo.py`: 15 passed.

LoRA + trainable lm_head | chunked CE never ran (8 cells void) | 11 pass
|
| PP2 negative control (each rank divides by its local token count) |
could not fail (path never ran) | fails as expected |

already matched one process before this change and are unchanged.

Installer mirror test: bound the probe speed by the batch time, not a fixed 1 KiB/s (#16871)

## Summary

The Windows `GGUF inference smoke (API, tools, vision)` job runs
`tests/studio/test_mirror_fallback.ps1` first, and one of its checks
fails now and then on unrelated PRs. In the last day it hit the staging
runs for #16825 (int8 diffusion on RDNA3) and #16804 (LTX-2.5 encode),
and a rerun of the #16825 job passed:

```
  PASS  probe: gives up at its deadline, cancelling what has not answered
  FAIL  probe: a ranged 1 KiB answer is 206 with its speed
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

The check wanted the `/ok` probe's speed above 1024 bytes/s.
`Wait-MirrorProbe` measures speed as bytes read over the probe's own
clock, so for a 1 KiB answer that floor really means "answered in under
a second". The probe gives that batch of 6 URLs 1.5 s, and on a busy
Windows runner the local server can take longer than a second to answer.
The probe is then working correctly and the check still fails.

Reproduced locally with `pwsh`: delaying the test server's `/ok` answer
by 1.1 s, still inside the 1.5 s deadline, fails this check on main.

## Change

`tests/studio/test_mirror_fallback.ps1`, this one check. It now asks
for:

- status 206, as before;
- the whole 1 KiB in the probe's buffer (`Position -eq 1024`), which the
old check did not look at;
- a speed of at least 1024 bytes over the batch's total time from the
test's own stopwatch. The probe's clock starts after that stopwatch, so
a correct speed can never be below this bound. A zero, missing or
miscomputed speed still fails.

No installer code changes.

## Testing

`pwsh -File tests/studio/test_mirror_fallback.ps1`, Linux pwsh 7:

| case | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| as is | pass | pass, 0 FAIL lines in the whole file |
| `/ok` answers after 1.1 s (slow runner) | FAIL | pass |
| `/ok` answers 200 instead of 206 | FAIL | FAIL |
| `/ok` sends 512 of the 1024 bytes | pass (not caught) | FAIL |

Studio diffusion: protect the first and last NVFP4 steps by default on sm_100-class cards (W4A16 auto) (#16759)

## Summary

NVFP4 diffusion runs on sm_100-class cards (B200, GB200, B300: compute
capability 10.x) now use the W4A16 step-protect schedule `auto` by
default. On a protected step each FlashInfer NVFP4 linear dequantises
its own 4-bit weight to a transient bf16 copy and runs a dense GEMM, so
the activations are not quantised to 4 bits on that step. Same
checkpoint, same resident bytes. Every other card, including consumer
Blackwell (sm_120), keeps protection off by default, exactly as on main.

`auto` = the first `ceil(0.08 * steps)` steps plus the last one. That is
`{0, last}` on schedules up to 12 steps and `{0, 1, 2, 3, 49}` at 50
steps.

- The default is read from the card the model's NVFP4 layers sit on (the
current CUDA device when they are not on one yet). An unreadable card
keeps the old default, off.
- Only a model that owns FlashInfer NVFP4 layers gets the default
(`attach_own_controller`). Every other model keeps the unarmed global
controller, so its CUDA graph keys, graph caps and logs are unchanged.
This is tested.
- `UNSLOTH_NVFP4_PROTECT_STEPS` still overrides on any card: `off` (or
`none` / `false` / `no`) turns it off, `auto`, `all` or an explicit list
(`0,-1`) turns it on, including on sm_120.
- The compile cache keys the schedule against the card's own default:
unset shares a bundle with `auto` on sm_100 and with `off` elsewhere.
Any other value keys apart. A bare `0` (protect step 0) used to key the
same as off; it now keys apart too.
- NVFP4 itself stays opt-in (`NVFP4_DIFFUSION_DEFAULT = False` is
unchanged). This only changes what an NVFP4 run does once it is on.

## Why sm_100 only

B200 (sm_100, torch 2.12.1, torchao 0.17.0, flashinfer 0.6.6) on the two
shipped image NVFP4 policies. Held-out suite: 24 prompts x 2 seeds = 48
pairs per arm, LPIPS against a bf16 reference. Speed: 3 warm-ups, then 6
cycles x 8 timed renders per arm with the arm order rotated. Two arms
that resolve to the same schedule (`auto` and `0,-1`) agree to 0.25%, so
that is the noise floor.

Z-Image-Turbo (9 steps, 1024x1024, `auto` = steps 0 and 8):

| arm | p50 s / image | vs off | LPIPS vs bf16 (mean) | paired delta vs
off [95% CI] | peak alloc GB |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| protect off (main) | 0.5279 | - | 0.2222 | - | 16.293 |
| protect `auto` (this PR on sm_100) | 0.5367 | +1.7% | 0.2060 | -0.0162
[-0.0295, -0.0028], 32/48 better | 16.328 |
| protect `all` | 0.5523 | +4.6% | 0.2040 | -0.0181 [-0.0320, -0.0043] |
16.293 |

FLUX.1-schnell (4 steps, 1024x1024, `auto` = steps 0 and 3):

| arm | p50 s / image | vs off | LPIPS vs bf16 (mean) | paired delta vs
off [95% CI] | peak alloc GB |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| protect off (main) | 0.3798 | - | 0.2001 | - | 23.524 |
| protect `auto` (this PR on sm_100) | 0.3824 | +0.7% | 0.1931 | -0.0070
[-0.0111, -0.0030], 33/48 better | 23.563 |
| protect `all` | 0.3844 | +1.2% | 0.1919 | -0.0082 [-0.0123, -0.0041] |
23.524 |

Wan2.2-TI2V-5B video (50 steps, every linear NVFP4, B200): protecting
steps 0-3 and 49, which is exactly what `auto` resolves to at 50 steps,
moved held-out LPIPS from 0.362 to 0.321 for +2.5% render time.

On sm_100 `auto` is accuracy-positive on all three measured models with
every confidence interval clear of zero, for 0.7-2.6% of render time and
+35-39 MB peak (one extra captured CUDA graph for the second branch).
The 4- and 9-step schedules are among the measured wins, so the default
is not limited by step count.

Consumer Blackwell (sm_120, RTX PRO 6000 class), 24 prompts, paired
LPIPS deltas vs `off` with bootstrapped 95% intervals:

| model | `auto` time vs off | `auto` LPIPS delta [95% CI] | `all` time
vs off | `all` LPIPS delta [95% CI] |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen-Image-2.1 | +2.5% | -0.005 [-0.017, +0.008] | +20% | -0.004
[-0.016, +0.009] |
| Z-Image-Turbo | +5.1% | -0.017 [-0.045, +0.009] | +20% | -0.021
[-0.049, +0.008] |
| FLUX.1-schnell | +17% | -0.004 [-0.012, +0.007] | +34% | -0.004
[-0.012, +0.007] |

On sm_120 no interval clears zero, the dense bf16 GEMM on a protected
step is much slower relative to NVFP4, and the second CUDA graph capture
adds 15 s (Qwen-Image-2.1) to 47 s (FLUX.1-schnell) to the first image.
So sm_120 and every other non-sm_100 card stay off by default.

## Tests

- `test_a_model_with_nvfp4_layers_defaults_to_auto_on_sm100_only`:
unset, empty, `off`, `0` and `all` on capabilities 10.0, 10.3, 12.0, 9.0
and no CUDA. Unset / empty resolve to `auto` on 10.x only and to off
everywhere else; explicit values are used as given on every card. The
sm_100 unset cases fail on main and pass here; the sm_120 / sm_90 /
no-CUDA cases pass on both, since those cards keep main's default.
- `test_the_default_leaves_models_without_nvfp4_layers_unarmed`: the
global controller, graph key and pipeline controllers stay off for a
plain model.
- `test_protect_steps_key_apart_only_off_the_cards_default` (sm_100
default and off default) and the generic graph-switch test cover the
compile cache key.
- On a real RTX PRO 6000 (sm_120), the unset default resolves to off and
the controller stays unarmed; `UNSLOTH_NVFP4_PROTECT_STEPS=auto` still
arms it.
- Base vs head on the NVFP4, CUDA graph, block graph, compile cache,
multi-GPU and video NVFP4 suites (15 files): head 832 passed, 1 failed,
78 skipped. The one failure,
`test_execution_device_reports_the_primary_of_a_split_pipeline`, also
fails on main and is not touched here.

## Not covered here

- No new B200 run for this narrowing: the sm_100 numbers above are the
existing measurements, and the sm_100 behaviour is the same `auto` they
measured.
- B300 / GB200 (also capability 10.x) were not timed; they get the
sm_100 default.
- Families beyond Z-Image-Turbo, FLUX.1-schnell and Wan2.2-TI2V-5B
(Qwen-Image-2512, HunyuanVideo-1.5) have no sm_100 protect measurement.
- The torchao NVFP4 backend has no W4A16 branch, so it is unaffected (no
controller is attached there).

Studio chat UI test: drag the monitor grip again when a native resize stops early (#16861)

## Summary

`Chat UI Tests (chat)` on Linux has started failing on unrelated PRs
with the same assertion in the floating monitor geometry check:

```
tests/studio/playwright_chat_ui.py:956, in exercise_floating_monitor_geometry
AssertionError: [ui] FAIL: resize width: expected 296, got 260
```

It failed 3 of the last 17 completed `Unsloth UI CI` runs (#16858, which
only touches the bookmarks test, plus `inprocess-native-tool-formats`
and `download-speed-limit`, the #16828 branch, which only touches
backend hub code). #16828 also hit it once more with `got 256`, and a
rerun passed. Playwright and Chromium are the same version (1.64.1) in
passing and failing runs, and nothing under `studio/frontend` merged in
the window where it started.

The numbers point at the pointer drag, not the resize logic. The check
drags the native grip with `mouse.move(..., steps = 10)` from 8 px
inside the corner to 40 px past it. 260 is 256 plus the first 4 px step,
and 256 is no step at all. So the native resize took at most the first
pointer step and dropped the rest. The same step passes in the other 14
runs on the same code.

## Change

`tests/studio/playwright_chat_ui.py`, the "resize width / height" step
only. The drag target is an absolute point, so if the box is not at the
wanted size after the drag, the test drags the grip again from wherever
the corner is now, up to three drags, and logs a line when it retries.
The width, height, left edge and top edge assertions after it are
unchanged, so a resize that really stops following the grip still fails
after the third drag.

## Testing

- `python -m py_compile tests/studio/playwright_chat_ui.py`.
- This PR's own `Unsloth UI CI` run exercises the step on Linux.
- I could not reproduce the dropped steps locally. The change only adds
the retry, so it cannot make a passing run fail.

Studio MiniMax-H3: price the slab compaction against the host reserve so a 16 GiB L4 render is not OOM-killed (#16849)

## What

MiniMax-H3 at a 16 GiB budget on a 24 GB L4 with a 53 GiB host: the
renderer was killed by the kernel OOM killer 6 s into its first request,
in 2 of 2 runs (dmesg `anon-rss:14129712kB, shmem-rss:37705728kB`; in
the A/B run below both main arms died 6 s after `video.loaded` with
py-spy samples inside `compact_host_slabs` / `_pin_host_tensor`).

Cause: at load 0 of 50 denoiser blocks are resident. The first 960x544
request's re-fit has room for 11, and #16639 releases 4.28 GB of their
host copies. `compact_host_slabs` then frees 5.37 GB of mostly-dead
pinned slabs by re-pinning every weight with a leaf in those slabs. For
int8 weights only the scales live there, but the whole weight was
re-pinned (13.2 GB), all before any old slab is freed, next to a
conditioner share sized at load to leave only the 7.98 GB reserve. At 12
GiB the re-fit keeps no block resident, so nothing is compacted, which
is why that budget survived.

`video_minimax_h3_residency.py`:
- only the inner tensors stored in a slab being freed are re-pinned, not
the whole weight;
- the move is priced against the load's reserve before pinning: the
conditioner's resident share yields first, and a slab that still does
not fit waits for the next re-fit;
- the conditioner share is topped up again after the compaction.

Placement only. Kill switch `UNSLOTH_H3_COMPACT_PRICED=0` (main's
behaviour).

## Numbers (Colab L4, H3 t2v 960x544x124, 20 steps, default INT8, one
VM, S F F S C C R at 16 GiB then S F F S C C at 12 GiB; R = main with
`UNSLOTH_H3_TE_RESIDENT=0`, C = the reference graph on the other stack)

| | main | this branch | main, conditioner share off |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16 GiB s/clip | killed in 2 of 2 runs | **376.13** (377.24 / 375.02) |
429.15 |
| 16 GiB encode per new prompt | - | 50.3-54.8 s | 104.9-105.6 s |
| 16 GiB s/step | - | 16.59 / 16.60 | 16.59 |
| 16 GiB host peak / MemAvailable floor | - | 48.5-48.6 / 5.06-5.22 GiB
| 45.7 / 18.1 GiB |
| 12 GiB s/clip | 389.60 | 392.11 (no compaction at this budget:
unchanged path) | |

Fix-tree load log at 16 GiB: share 11988 MiB at load, 517 MiB yielded,
`compacted 5.37 GB (moved 358.3 MB)`, then `5244 MiB ... copied` after
the pins, so about 15-16 GiB of the 25.9 GiB conditioner stays in RAM.

Frames: at 16 GiB the two branch runs and the share-off run are
bit-identical (16 of 16 sampled frames per prompt); at 12 GiB main and
branch are bit-identical. RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell no-regression: whole
card 54.53 vs 54.72 s/clip (the controller does not run there), 16 GiB
55.44 vs 55.42 s/clip with the compaction moving 328.6 MB instead of
9422.9 MB; frames bit-identical in all 4 prompt pairs.

## Tests

`studio/backend/tests/test_h3_compact_priced.py`, 6 CPU tests (only the
inner tensor stored in the slab moves, the compaction never takes the
host under the load reserve, the conditioner share yields before the
pins, a slab that does not fit waits for a later re-fit, the share is
resized after a compaction, the kill switch moves whole weights
unpriced); all fail on main. H3 CPU test files: main 638 passed, branch
644 passed, 77 skipped both.


## L4 at full card (no budget cap)

Same L4 type, S F F S on one VM (S = merge base, F = this branch),
960x544x124, 20 steps, default INT8. This is where the first request's
re-fit keeps the most blocks resident (29 of 50, 11.28 GB of host copies
released), so the compaction moves the most.

| | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| s/clip | 338.19 / 339.62 | 340.11 / 340.01 |
| s/step | 16.33 / 16.34 | 16.34 / 16.34 |
| compaction at load, then at the re-fit | 4.29 GB freed (moved 9811.9
MB), 4.29 GB freed (moved 6934.6 MB) | 4.29 GB freed (moved 332.2 MB),
3.22 GB freed (moved 75.3 MB) |
| conditioner resident | all 25.9 GB | about 24.5 GB (share sized to the
7982 MiB reserve) |
| host MemAvailable floor | 5.04 / 5.08 GiB | 4.40 / 4.40 GiB |

Frames bit-identical in every pair (S vs F and both A/A pairs, 16 of
16). Main's whole conditioner fits here with 750 MiB above the reserve.
On the branch the re-fit compacts 3.22 GB of slabs instead of 4.29 GB
(the int8 data was never moved out of its original slabs, so fewer of
them drop under a quarter live), and the conditioner share stops at the
reserve instead. Same render time, about 0.6 GiB lower MemAvailable
floor, still well clear of the kill.

## Cell sweep (CPU)

`compact_host_slabs` base vs branch over 1152 cells (1 / 4 / 8 weights
per dying slab, plain / int8-wrapper / mixed weights, tail live fraction
1-50%, MemAvailable from 2 GB under to 20 GB over the reserve,
conditioner share absent / empty / small / ample): weights hold their
exact values in every cell; the branch never pins more than main (17.7
GB vs 72.9 GB in total) and never takes MemAvailable lower than main;
678 cells free the same slabs, 186 leave some for a later re-fit because
the copies do not fit the reserve, 288 have nothing to compact on either
side; with `UNSLOTH_H3_COMPACT_PRICED=0` the branch frees and pins
exactly what main does in every cell. Tests also pass on torch 2.6.0 and
2.14.1.

Studio video memory plan: count the forward's headroom before keeping whole-module offload (#16805)

## What

`refine_memory_plan_for_components` keeps whole-module offload whenever
the largest loaded component fits the device budget. A whole-module
onload holds the DiT and the denoise phase's activations at the same
time, so a DiT that fits only bare OOMs in its first forward. The video
load now prices the DiT at its denoise phase:
`refine_memory_plan_for_components(pipe, plan, headroom_mib=...)` with
`headroom_mib = min(runtime_headroom_mib, 4096) +
DEFAULT_BASE_OVERHEAD_MIB`, the same denoise-phase pricing
`_video_prefer_whole_module` already uses to pick whole-module offload.
When the DiT plus that headroom does not fit, the DiT streams, as it
already does for an oversized component. A text encoder runs in its own
phase and keeps the bare size check; the decoded-clip share belongs to
the VAE phase and is not added. The image path passes no headroom and
keeps the bare check (byte-identical decision).

## Numbers (Colab RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell held to a budget with a VRAM
ballast, same VM per table, every arm a fresh process)

LTX-2.5 two-stage distilled 1280x704x121, GGUF Q4_K_M, 16 GiB:

| | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| render | OOM in the first forward, both arms | 20.31 / 19.95 s per
clip (A/A 1.8%, arms bit-identical) |
| plan | whole-module offload | streaming (`loaded transformer is 11642
MiB (+6144 MiB runtime headroom), above the 13396 MiB device budget`) |
| peak VRAM | - | 15.5 GiB |

This table was measured on an earlier revision of the branch (flat
runtime headroom); the current pricing makes the same decision on this
cell (replayed on CPU: 11642 + 6144 MiB > 13396 MiB, streaming).

Wan2.2-TI2V-5B, bf16 DiT (`transformer_quant=none`), 1280x704x121, 10
steps, S F F S at 14 GiB plus an S F control at 16 GiB:

| budget | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| 14 GiB | `offload=model`; CUDA OOM on the first render, both arms |
`offload=streaming` (`loaded transformer is 9559 MiB (+6144 MiB runtime
headroom), above the 11348 MiB device budget`); 39.11 / 39.56 s per
clip, 3.15 s/step, peak alloc 9.8 GiB |
| 16 GiB (control) | `offload=group`, 38.74 s per clip |
`offload=group`, 38.80 s per clip; frames bit-identical to main (16 of
16) |

MiniMax-H3 is not reachable: its modular load returns before the refine
call. Wan2.2-TI2V-5B at 8 GiB (a streamed plan, which the refine leaves
alone) and H3 at 12 GiB kept their plans and bit-identical frames on
that earlier revision.

## Which cells move

A CPU sweep of every conventional video family (Wan 2.1 / 2.2,
HunyuanVideo-1.5, LTX-2 / 2.5, Cosmos 3) x 14 budgets (6-96 GiB) x 2
clip sizes x 4 memory modes x bf16 / GGUF Q8 / Q4 DiT x
loaded-vs-estimated size drift, through each tree's own planner and
refine: 10080 cells; 5877 whose plan is resident or group offload are
untouched by construction; of 4203 whole-module plans, 3928 keep their
policy and 275 move from whole-module offload to streaming, every one of
them a cell where the DiT plus the denoise headroom exceeds the budget.
No cell moves the other way, and no resident plan starts offloading.
torchao-quantized DiTs (the default int8 / fp8 path) skip the refine, so
only bf16 and GGUF loads are affected.

## Tests


`test_refine_with_headroom_streams_a_component_that_fits_only_without_activations`,
`test_refine_headroom_applies_to_the_denoiser_not_a_larger_text_encoder`,
`test_refine_prices_the_denoise_phase_not_the_decoded_clip`; they fail
on main. The refine tests also pass on torch 2.6.0 and 2.14.1.

Studio: let the floating browser go anywhere, and float per chat (#16859)

Follow-ups to #16775 (the floating browser window), from using it.

### Floating window

- **Drag it anywhere in the chat.** It no longer steps around the
composer: it can sit over the composer or up over the chat header, and a
resize can take it to the chat's full height. It still opens just below
the header's controls.
- **Always in front.** The window now stacks above everything in the
chat, the chat header (z-40) included, so nothing paints over it
wherever it is dropped.
- **Floating belongs to the chat it was chosen in.** Before, choosing
the floating window made every later browser open float, in any chat.
Now each chat remembers its own layout: the chat you floated it in
floats again after a close or a chat switch, and other chats keep
opening the browser docked. A float the app chose by itself (closing the
browser while the model is still using it) is not remembered as the
chat's choice.
- **The chat header keeps its browser button while the window floats**,
since the window no longer occupies the side pane. The full view
shortcut stays with the floating window's own bar while it is up.

### Docked browser size

- The docked browser opens at about 540px, between 30% and 50% of the
chat, instead of half of it.
- It can still be dragged much wider: up to 70% of the row (72% with the
chat on the right; research keeps its 58%).

### Verification

- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run i18n:check:strict`, `npm run build`,
`npm test` (14996 tests, 0 failures).
- Tests: `tests/browser-floating-preview.test.ts` now drags the window
over the composer, up over the header and resizes it to the full chat
height; `tests/browser-floating-layout.test.ts` checks that a second
chat opens its browser docked and the first floats again on return.
- Exercised in a local Studio (web): dragged the window onto the
composer and up to the top of the chat, with `elementFromPoint`
confirming the window is on top in both spots; the header's new tab
button present while floating; a new chat opening its browser docked.

### Not tested here

- Desktop (Tauri) native web views were not run on this host.

libghostty-vt: some final C ABI cleanups (#15125)

Changes to the C API:

- `ghostty_terminal_select_output` takes `const GhosttyGridRef*` rather
than a struct by value.
- `GHOSTTY_TERMINAL_DATA_CURSOR_STYLE` is now
`GHOSTTY_TERMINAL_DATA_CURSOR_SGR_STYLE` with the same value, since
`GhosttyCursorStyle` means the cursor shape.
- The allocator vtable functions have named typedefs so the parity test
can compare their signatures. The ABI is the same, but the Zig side
moves to `anyopaque` to match the header's `void*`.
- Render state keys that have no value to report return
`GHOSTTY_NO_VALUE` rather than `GHOSTTY_INVALID_VALUE`.
- NULL handles and output pointers no longer crash. Functions that
return a `GhosttyResult` return `GHOSTTY_INVALID_VALUE`. Functions that
can't report an error do nothing, or return false, 0, or NULL. The
headers and the conventions page now document this.
- `GHOSTTY_TERMINAL_OPT_GLYPH_PROTOCOL` is disabled by default, and a
NULL value disables it again. Embedders opt in.
- `ghostty_color_x11_names` returned a garbage pointer without the color
feature. It now returns an empty table.
- The Windows DLL exported the two CRT section markers, 211 exports
against the 209 in `symbols.txt`. They now have hidden visibility.

**AI usage:** Some of these found by a Fable reviewer that I ran in
parallel to me hand-reviewing every single header and signature. I wrote
all the docs and this PR message.

rename the GHOSTTY_MODE_* macros in `ghostty/vt/modes.h` so that each
one matches the name of the mode in Zig, and drop the aliases. The docs
and header comments that referred to the old names are updated to

The C ABI tests translated `ghostty/vt.h` themselves in
`GhosttyZig.initVtCTest`, so the C API test binary ended up with two
translations of the same header. Have `c_deps` provide the one import,
`ghostty-vt-h`, to both the mode test and the ABI tests.

  `<sys/types.h>`; `ghostty/vt.h` needs only compiler-provided headers
  and now translates for every target, linking libc only if the module

corresponding definition in `ghostty/vt.h`.

  GHOSTTY_MODE_* macro
- move the translate-c setup out of build.zig into src/build/c_deps.zig,

- generalize checkGhosttyHEnum into checkEnum, used by both it and the

  quota std uses

terminal: RefCountedSet reuses dead IDs instead of rehashing (#15121)

Once every ID in a `RefCountedSet` has been handed out, `add` now reuses
the ID of a dead item in place.

Previously it returned `NeedsRehash`, and every caller responded by
cloning the entire page at the same capacity, copying every row, cell,
style, grapheme and string just to free up IDs. This caused quite a lot
of allocation and throughput churn.

This has a huge impact on alt-screen apps (TUIs) in particular, because
they don't generally ever allocate new pages and have a fixed size and
usage pattern (usually) and constantly overwrite styles, links, etc. You
can see below how this plays out with benchmarks.

`ghostty-bench +terminal-stream` at 120x80, 8 MiB inputs:

| Input | Scrollback | main (ms) | set-reuse (ms) | Speedup |
| --------------- | ---------- | ----------- | -------------- | -------
|
| links.vt | 0 | 90.2 ± 0.7 | 67.3 ± 0.6 | 1.34x |
| styled-heavy.vt | 0 | 50.7 ± 0.4 | 44.5 ± 0.3 | 1.14x |
| styled-mixed.vt | 0 | 90.4 ± 1.2 | 83.6 ± 0.3 | 1.08x |
| ascii.vt | 0 | 10.2 ± 0.1 | 10.2 ± 0.2 | 1.00x |
| styled-plain.vt | 0 | 13.2 ± 0.3 | 12.9 ± 0.1 | 1.02x |
| osc.vt | 0 | 161.6 ± 2.0 | 163.3 ± 4.6 | 0.99x |
| links.vt | 10KB | 39.8 ± 1.1 | 39.5 ± 0.4 | 1.01x |
| styled-heavy.vt | 10KB | 30.9 ± 0.7 | 30.5 ± 0.2 | 1.01x |
| styled-mixed.vt | 10KB | 66.5 ± 0.5 | 66.3 ± 0.5 | 1.00x |

I also wanted to know whether real programs hit this, so I recorded
about 25 seconds of them:

| Workload | Rehashes (main) | Page copies | Instructions |
| ------------------------------ | --------------- | ----------- |
------------ |
| `rg --hyperlink-format` + less | 6 | 12 -> 6 | -14.2% |
| chafa playing an animated GIF | 148 | 150 -> 2 | -8.4% |
| `eza --hyperlink -R` + less | 2 | 8 -> 6 | -3.1% |

And then there are a bunch I tested that didn't move much (but all moved
towards faster): nvim, helix, btop, htop, tmux.

`NeedsRehash` can now only happen if the living count is wrong. Safe
builds assert there, and release builds still fall back to the clone. In
a future PR we can probably remove this entirely.

terminal: RefCountedSet reclaims the dead ID insert passed over

When `add` reclaims a dead ID, `insert` may still reuse a smaller dead
ID that it reaps on its probe path. The reclaimed ID then stays dead
and out of the table, but `free_cursor` had already moved past it, so
the next reclaims scanned the rest of the set first and only found it
again after wrapping around.

Point `free_cursor` back at it in that case so it is the next ID
reclaimed. Harmless before, since it was found eventually, but it is
the cheapest dead ID to reuse.
terminal: RefCountedSet.releaseMultiple asserts n > 0
terminal: RefCountedSet checks table membership, not a sentinel bucket

terminal: RefCountedSet only reaps dead items it may displace

Only reap a dead item whose PSL is at most the held item's. The bucket
then never ends up with a shorter PSL than it had, so every probe
sequence through it stays intact. Otherwise the dead item is probed
past like any other.

terminal: find style runs with one scan in RowBuilder.scan (#15111)

`RowBuilder.scan` previously handled each kind of special cell
separately, each with its own run scan. Rows with frequent style changes
paid for failed group comparisons of plain cells and styled runs every
one or two cells.

This finds each run with a new `Mask.eqlEnd`, which returns the index
where the run ends and checks the next cell on its own before checking
groups. Rows with graphemes get a separate scan specialization, while
the common version is inlined.

Background color cells no longer produce style runs: their color is
stored in the cell, and `RenderState.Cell.style` is already undefined
for them. This also removes the only use of `Mask.eqlExact`.

`Mask.eql` now ORs the differences and checks the masked bits once,
which avoids emulated 64-bit lane comparisons on baseline x86-64.

Dragging a triple-click selection over a blank row currently clears the

terminal/kitty: evict the oldest image by transmission (#15103)

The [Kitty graphics
protocol](https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/graphics-protocol/) has a
[storage
quota](https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/graphics-protocol/#image-persistence-and-storage-quotas):
older images are evicted to make space for newer images.

Image eviction treated an
[animation](https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/graphics-protocol/#animation)
as new again each time it showed another frame, so a playing animation
outlived images transmitted after it.

#15094 fixed the same problem for image numbers - this PR fixes it for
eviction.

To reproduce, start with `ghostty --image-storage-limit=12` and run the
below script:

```sh
# Start a green animation:
printf '\e_Ga=T,q=2,i=1,f=24,s=1,v=1,c=8,r=4;/wAA\e\\'
printf '\e_Ga=f,q=2,i=1,f=24,s=1,v=1,z=100;AP8A\e\\'
printf '\e_Ga=a,q=2,i=1,s=3\e\\'
# Show a blue image:
printf '\e_Ga=T,q=2,i=2,f=24,s=1,v=1,c=8,r=4;AAD/\e\\'
# Let the animation advance:
sleep 1
# Show a yellow image, going over the quota:
printf '\e_Ga=T,q=2,i=3,f=24,s=1,v=1,c=8,r=4;//8A\e\\'
```

- Before this PR: the newer blue image disappears, leaving the older
green animation.
- After this PR: the older green animation disappears, as in Kitty
(checked using larger images to hit kitty fixed quota).

commits.message: fix(ci): pin clang-format 18.1.8 in the firmware formatting check (#24806) _Requested by **David**_ ## What changed and why Fixes the Repo Checks / Formatting failure on PRs that touch firmware C files with compound literals, for example #24393 (run 42305654687, job 128194880599, `tests/test_power_off_queue.c`). GitHub's `ubuntu-latest` moved to ubuntu-26.04. Its clang-format adds a space before compound-literal braces, while the firmware pre-commit hook pins clang-format 18, which removes it. The hosted check therefore rejects files the local hook accepts. The Formatting job now installs `clang-format==18.1.8` into a dedicated venv under `$RUNNER_TEMP` and runs that binary. That matches the local pre-commit pin and holds when runners change again. No runner image is pinned. ## Product invariants affected None. The change is limited to the CI formatting step. ## How it was verified - The workflow file parses as YAML. - The local firmware formatter check is still clang-format 18, per scripts/pre-commit. - Not run here: the hosted Formatting job. The first real run on this PR is the check. ## Tests None added. The hosted Formatting job is the test. ## UI evidence Not applicable. ## Failure class (fixes) Failure-Class: new New class definition: `.github/failure-classes/FC-clang-format-runner-image-drift.json`. This PR is its evidence. ## New guards (only when adding a check or ratchet) The Formatting job now pins the formatter version itself. The local pre-commit guard already refuses other versions.

fix(ci): pin clang-format 18.1.8 in the firmware formatting check

ubuntu-latest moved to ubuntu-26.04, whose clang-format adds a space before
compound-literal braces that clang-format 18 removes. The hosted check then
rejects firmware files that the pre-commit hook accepts.

Install clang-format==18.1.8 into a dedicated venv and run that binary, so the
check matches pre-commit and does not depend on the runner image.

Episode-join variant F behind a runtime flag (#24730)

<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"Git-on-my-level"} -->
_Requested by **David** · [project
thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01DkCywHd8HiN61t59mu7kXF?thread=cmsg_01DkCywHd8HiN61t59mu7kXFJgw6sqNwiEHdyUMJyStka4)_

## What changed and why

Production path for episode-join **variant F** (David, 2026-11-05: ship
under the $0.5/user/mo cap, est. ~1.5¢; ramp 5→25→100% as soon as each
step is safe). Today, with recorded-time episodes on, every join to a
live owner inside 30 minutes is decided by time alone and Jev never runs
(the boundary counters read 0).

- **Mark (attach):** in `_attach_once`'s recorded-time owner branch, an
admitted user's join to a *live* owner 2 to 30 minutes after its last
speech still joins by time (Home hides it under the live row), and is
marked `pending_boundary[cid] = {variant: 'f', ...}`. Shorter gaps,
overlaps, late audio and closed owners keep today's rules.
- **Settle (first moment):** `_settle_boundary` asks Jev with the F
state only: the previous member's transcript (last 12,000 chars) and the
new speech (first 8,000 chars), rendered as in the offline F run; no
summary, time features or voice flag. `p < 0.2` (`MOVED_ON_THRESHOLD`)
splits the conversation into a new episode (`moved_on`, or
`source_change`). **No answer, error, timeout or out-of-range answer
keeps today's join.** F calls use their own Jev lane,
`episode_boundary_f` (same gateway model `omi:auto:jev-decisions` →
pinned `typesafe/jev-1.13` as the offline run). Client timeout 3.0 s,
one attempt; the gateway's 2.5 s provider deadline is authoritative.
- **Flag:** Omi flag store rule `episode_f_join` is the ramp and the
instant kill (`scripts/omi_flags.py set episode_f_join --rollout 5 |
--inactive`, propagates in 15–60 s, no deploy). With no rule or an
unconfigured store, `EPISODE_F_JOIN_PERCENT` (default **0**) buckets
uids. `EPISODE_F_JOIN_ENABLED=off` overrides both. Admission is checked
at attach *and* again at settle, so a kill also stops already-marked
joins from calling Jev. **Merging ships F dark.**
- **Known difference from the scored offline run:** offline F saw the
candidate's *whole* transcript. In production the join settles at the
conversation's first moment, so Jev sees the speech so far (the first
moment, up to 8,000 chars). This is not a timeout limit. A full
transcript exists only after the conversation finalizes, and by then its
moments have been folded into the joined episode's live notes. Settling
later would mean splitting after notes were written, which this PR does
not do. The ramp's share-closed and size guardrails measure the effect.
Settling at finalize would be a follow-up.
- **Guardrail metrics:**
`omi_jev_decision_total{lane="episode_boundary_f",outcome}` + latency
histogram (error and timeout rate);
`omi_episode_boundary_total{outcome=f_pending|f_continue|f_close|f_no_answer|f_disabled|f_pending_conflict|f_pending_error|f_later_member}`
(share Jev closes; `f_later_member` counts joins kept without a question
because another member recorded later); new
`omi_episode_closed_members{arm}` and
`omi_episode_closed_span_seconds{arm}` (episode size; histogram count ÷
arm percent compares episodes per user, arm = `f|control`).
- **Bug fix found on the way:** `database.episodes._close` computed a
closed episode's recorded window from its *pre-detach* membership, so
after any split-off the successor failed the `recorded_window_overlap`
check and the moment was dropped as `skipped_closed`. Only an admitted F
split now opts into the post-detach membership (`merged`). Ordinary
closes, including flag-off legacy pending detaches, retain main's

feat(pusher): byte-budgeted storage admission (default off) (#24799)

## What changed and why

Add process-wide non-waiting admission for custody PCM queued/running on
the existing storage executor. PR-A #24788 supplied the gauges and
pressure alerts. This PR adds admission, bounded refusal/error counters,
an agent-tier refusal alert, hermetic saturation tests and the runbook.
**The flag remains 0 everywhere.**

A full budget returns before submission, without a receipt, commit
callback or opcode-203 ACK. It never raises into receive supervision or
selects a close code. Original PCM, exact checkpoints, owner and start
remain charged to the socket's existing 20 MiB budget. **The first live
refusal immediately pauses intake** in that same cancellable receive
task; it probes every 50 ms until the window commits, before reading
another frame. Refusals cannot accumulate windows toward socket byte
exhaustion. There is no extra retry task or global waiter list. Enabled
windows cap at 4096 checkpoints.

Live admission uses 75% of the total; shutdown tails may use the full
limit and bypass the intake pause. A full tail returns without an ACK
and retains its producer fence. Outer-handler cancellation interrupts a
paused receive task but skips the cancellation-time tail commit
entirely. Connected or disconnected, this path submits no storage,
produces no receipt and sends no ACK; the held producer fence and client
WAL replay own recovery. Cleanup cannot wait for a new PCM storage
operation or its retries. Already-submitted storage still holds its
reservation until actual settlement and cannot send a late ACK. The
existing external-cancellation close classification is preserved. Record
begin/fail/seal/abandon/markers and projection operations remain
ungated; executor pools are unchanged. Known-deleted retained owners use
the existing gone-owner disposition. Every unresolved owner stays fenced
in finalization: A's receipt cannot certify B's uncommitted tail.

Acquire faults roll back partial mutation and fail open using flag-0
storage dispatch. Release faults retire exactly their own reservation
and are swallowed. Acquire fail-open also calls the shared fallback
helper for every fault; the caller owns the rate-limited warning. Both
acquire/release errors use `omi_pusher_storage_pcm_errors_total{reason}`
through the enum helper and logs limited to one per reason per minute.
Late post-cancellation storage failures are counted/logged through the
same bounded path. Enabled capacity remains held until actual storage
settlement, including caller cancellation.

Flag 0 preserves successful PCM/checkpoint/receipt/opcode-203 bytes,
storage dispatch/cancellation and observational gauge semantics. It does
**not** promise identical failure finalization: the new finalizer can
still hold unresolved fences and defer inline finish after genuine
failures at flag 0. Genuine storage-error handling remains in effect.

## Flag, ramp and rollback

`PUSHER_STORAGE_PCM_BUDGET_MB=0` is off / kill switch in code, manifests
and dev/prod charts. Enabled deployment values must be >=27 MiB: ceil(20
MiB x 4/3), so an idle live lane admits any legal socket window.
Smaller/malformed unvalidated startup values select off. Proposed canary
size: 512 MiB (384 MiB live / 128 MiB reserved).

Separate approved enablement train, owner uicleanup (omi-lifecycle): dev
chart -> one canary pod for 15 minutes with socket kills <=15/15min and
memory p99 <75% of 3.5 GiB; inspect refusals, accounting/GCS errors and
capacity/abandon outcomes -> fleet within one day of a clean canary, or
report the failed gate. Rollback: chart value 0 through ordinary
rollout, without rebuilding or changing custody objects/tokens. No
enablement, GCP access, PR merge or deploy in this task.

feat(observability): error-class sentinel sweep with new/surge alerting (#23947)

* feat(observability): error-class sentinel sweep with new/surge alerting

Detect new or surging prod error classes before a ramp trips on them. A
15-minute backend-sync sweep (Cloud Scheduler, jobs.yaml) fingerprints
ERROR+ Cloud Logging entries for the transcription fleet as exception type +
raising site + logger (id-normalized), keeps a 7-day hourly baseline in
Redis, and raises omi_error_class_alert_firing for classes that are new
(>=20/h) or surging (>=50/h and >=5x baseline). Grafana rules
omi-error-class-firing (page) and omi-error-class-sweep-silent (dead-man,
also catches permission_denied) deliver it; both ship unpaused. Kill switch:
state PAUSED on the scheduler job.

A log-based metric keyed by fingerprint is infeasible (label extractors are
single-entry regexes; the fingerprint needs traceback stitching and id
normalization), Loki log alerting is retired, and Monitoring-policy
provisioning is .github-owned, so the detector ships as the scheduled job
(cited in backend/docs/runbooks/error-class-alerts.md). backend-runtime
needs a one-time logging.read grant from the lead; until then the sweep
fails loud as outcome=permission_denied and the dead-man fires.

Failure-Class: none -- new detector, no failure-class contract touched

* fix(observability): error-class sentinel review round 1

New-class detection keys on absent baseline rather than record age; the
dead-man rule uses boolean modifiers so a stopped sentinel still pages; the
baseline mean divides by the hour span since first appearance; buckets prune
by age; the 6h dedupe is one per-class key; the paging signal is the
monotonic omi_error_class_alert_fired_total counter (immune to stale
cross-instance gauges); WARNING-level exceptions keep doubled thresholds and
unknown-level entries use standard thresholds. Prod stays ENABLED (rebutted
in the PR: PAUSED silences nothing the dead-man would not).

Failure-Class: none

* fix(observability): error-class sentinel review round 2

The paging rule keys on omi_error_class_last_fired_timestamp_seconds
(time() - max(...) < 900): increase() over a series born at its alert value
stays zero, so the first firing would never page, while a timestamp ages out
of the window and stale series drop from the query. The baseline divisor is
elapsed hours since the first bucket, not buckets+1. The two read passes are
merged and re-sorted before stitching, and stitching absorbs the immediately
preceding level-header line, so warning-logged tracebacks keep their doubled
thresholds across the pass split.

Failure-Class: none

* fix(observability): strip identifier-shaped tokens before fingerprinting

Lead privacy rule 2026-10-29: fingerprints and labels become Redis keys,
GMP label values and log lines, so they must never carry a user- or
document-identifiable token. Firebase-UID-shaped 28-char alnum tokens and
20+-char base62 ids escaped every existing rule (HEX needs hex-only chars,
SLUG a 4+ digit run), and site=/payload-site/frame-path values entered
fingerprints unscrubbed.

  base62 20+, ip, hex>=12) applied before template normalization
- extract_site(): every return path (frames, site=, payload fields,
  inline file:line) scrubbed, so paths embedding ids fold to
  users/<fuid>/...

  diff itself contains zero identifier-shaped tokens) prove no shape
  survives into fingerprint or label; placeholder stability keeps one

scrubbing must be shape-based, not statistical. The rule is now any 20+

exception slot keeps its name: EXC_RE admits only a controlled grammar

## What changed and why

Mobile could restore a confirmed deletion from cached conversation
history after reopening. It also restored failed deletes without telling
the user why the conversation returned. Clear only the confirmed row
from the current and legacy caches, and show a failure when the delete
is refused. Queue the failure message behind any active Undo prompt.

Confirmed deletions also remove the row and its processing cards from
other open lists and fence stale writes from separate providers. Persist
the confirmed ID for its account before rewriting either cache. A
restart during eviction or after a failed write leaves the marker in
place. Successful eviction clears the marker after both snapshots have
been saved.
