combined run. Main then landed the equivalent pin in 5503c2dcd8. This
branch takes the workflow from main, with no workflow changes in the
final diff. The workflow passed actionlint and the four local mobile CI
infrastructure tests. The final revision passed 194 focused Flutter
tests, including the latest Home row and linked-task filters and a
regression for late live updates during Undo and an in-flight delete. A
refused request still reports failure after navigation. Late merge
completion retires the sources without publishing a deleted target. A
stale full page excludes confirmed deletions from its storage cursor,
and an in-flight next-page request retries at the corrected offset. A
simulated interruption before the cache rewrite completes verifies that
the durable marker hides only the deleted row after restart. A completed
request from an earlier sign-in session cannot alter the replacement
session cache, even when the UID matches.

fix(memory): stop stale-vector cleanup from claiming the account gate

The stale canonical vector cleanup runs on memory read paths (search
hydration). It claimed the exclusive per-account destructive-operation
gate for each delete, so concurrent user deletes of conversations and
memories lost the race and returned 409 account_gate_busy. A skipped
delete also left the stale rows to be re-hydrated (a Firestore read per
hit) on every later search.

Fence the Pinecone delete with external_write_fence instead, the
non-claiming mechanism that provider upserts already use. The fence
still refuses while a deletion, legal hold, or running destructive
operation owns the account, and provider failures still propagate to the
search-side handler, which keeps them off the result.

## Problem and measurement

The provided Phase 1a evidence record
(`/Users/dazheng/workspace/omi/data/run-2026-11-05-omi-pipeline/firestore-phase1-1a-0450Z.md`,
measured 2026-11-06 ~04:50Z, 1h GMP rates) attributes ~409 billed
reads/s to `database.batch_pipeline_store:oldest` and ~63/s to
`oldest_retry`. Each refresh queries three priorities: pending oldest
(bounded 501-row policy-hold prefix), ready oldest, and retry oldest.
This PR makes no production access or new live measurement. Expected
saving is approximately **300–400 reads/s**, an estimate to verify after
rollout; caller-level evidence cannot attribute those reads precisely by
plane.

## Callers and planes (base origin/main)

- Serving: `backend/utils/batch_pipeline/serving.py:211` calls
`QueueMetrics.refresh` on every full `Serving.reconcile`. Supervisor:
`serving.py:438`, default 20s ticks, shared `min_refresh_seconds=30`
(`serving.py:384`, `config/batch_pipeline.py:478`), so default effective
cadence is 40s per instance before this PR. Explicit `/reconcile`
(`routers/batch_pipeline.py:274`) also reaches this path. Owner-only
recovery returns before metrics; global repair/recovery calls share this
service path.
- Scrapes: `backend/routers/batch_pipeline.py:282` directly refreshes on
projection-pump/read-only-metrics instances; other scrapes call
`reconcile_async(periodic=True)` at line 285. They share the same 30s
process reservation. The projection-pump background loop updates its
local tick gauge only; it does not refresh the store queue on its own.
- GPU: `backend/utils/batch_pipeline/pump.py:914` refreshes through
`Pump.sample_metrics`; `diarizer/batch_pipeline_runtime.py:191`
supervises it independently every 15s, `min_refresh_seconds=0`. There
are two worker processes per pod, but **only process index 0** samples
(`batch_pipeline_runtime.py:266` on the base). `Pump.run_once` has an
inline sampler (`pump.py:324`), disabled by deployed runtime
construction (`inline_metrics=False`). The GPU health `/metrics` handler
only exports its registry; it does not query the store. No direct
standalone sweeper/repair-job QueueMetrics refresh caller was found.

## Fix and cadence

- Default-on `FIRESTORE_READ_LEVERS.batch_metrics_oldest_leader=100`; no
new env flag/budget entry. Existing levers retain their defaults.
- Serving elects one queue sampler per store namespace using the
existing `LeaderLease` implementation and a separate `queue_metrics`
role, TTL 20s. Followers issue **zero** oldest/oldest_retry/capacity
queries and leave those gauges absent. Maintenance ownership and its 60s
TTL are unchanged. The advisory lease retains existing fail-open
behavior on lease-store errors or when its existing global lease switch
is disabled.
- GPU uses the permitted **60s** queue-query fallback: its adapter
requires a per-pod fresh signal, so electing only one pod would exclude
healthy pod activity. Busy-time now uses an independent sampler
heartbeat at the existing 15s-plus-IO tick cadence, with the old queue
clock accepted for mixed fleets/rollback.
Local/timeliness/projection/lifecycle samplers retain their previous
schedules. Capacity retains its independent observation clock.
- Effective oldest-age dashboard cadence: **40s by default on serving**,
meeting the <=60s target. GPU queue queries have a **60s minimum
interval**, with up to one 15s sampler tick plus IO jitter before the
next sample; after 60s the queue sample becomes absent until refreshed,
while per-pod busy-time stays fresh on its independent heartbeat.
Default lease handover is within **60s**, excluding IO/runtime delays.
Scrapes can refresh serving sooner. Existing nondefault longer serving
tick/reservation settings can exceed this; keep the effective cadence
<=60s. The over-SLA **timeliness sampler is unchanged**.
- Queue gauges stop exporting at **60s** without successful observation,
including a stopped refresh task. Never-observed and failed samples
cannot become fresh zeroes. Adapter `<60s` freshness filters remain; a
delayed GPU query may briefly make queue demand unavailable, retaining
capacity; busy-time remains fresh on its independent per-pod heartbeat.

## Problem

The recorded 2026-11-06 ~04:50Z Phase 1a measurement found ~2,073
NOT_FOUND reads/s out of 3,834 privacy reads/s: conversation tombstones
829/s, account deletion markers 695/s, missing conversations 549/s.
Source: `firestore-phase1-1a-0450Z.md` in the prescribed
`omi-workspace/data/run-2026-11-05-omi-pipeline/` run record. These are
dated recorded measurements, not a fresh production measurement or a
forecast of savings. The prescribed scout report records the 2026-11-04
Redis-bypass seeding regression (54k to 530k reads/10 min), which ruled
out reviving that path.

## Change and invariant

A cached NOT_FOUND must never hide a tombstone, account deletion, legal
hold, or newly existing conversation. The process-local 50,000-entry LRU
stores only real NOT_FOUND reads, keyed by client/plane, uid and exact
document path, with the owner's WQ26 memo token and server revision
including nanoseconds. Each reuse requires that same decision to have
re-read the token inside the same transaction and compared it
identically. The owner token remains in Firestore's conflict set; TTL is
a second 60-second bound, measured before the live absence read. No
Redis, speculative seeding, positive rows or authorization decisions
enter this cache. Missing/malformed tokens, full-row exports and
nontransactional calls stay live.

The existing Commit fence already rotates tokens atomically for all
writer families, including metadata-only conversation CREATE and
merge-upsert. Added regression coverage for those create shapes and
extended the actual-writer emulator matrix to run with negative lookup
caching as well as generation memoization. Legal holds retain their
existing external-fence policy; their writes invalidate the lookup
hints.

**Net-zero flags (lead2 ruling 258db3 (03)):** the sole new lever is
`privacy_negative_lookup_cache` (0 off, positive percent selects the
candidate cohort). Existing `privacy_checks_shadow` selects shadow mode
within that cohort; shadow takes precedence and always reads live,
bypassing generation-memo hits to gather evidence. With the new lever 0,
existing decision-shadow behavior stays unchanged. No
`privacy_negative_lookup_shadow` lever remains.

The retired `batch_privacy_memoize` slot pays for the new lever: remove
`BatchPrivacyMemo`, its store/projection caller plumbing, snapshot-only
replay instrumentation/assertions, and all runtime/worker chart literals
(including the worker's former 100% value). The live authority walk and
the WQ26 generation memo remain. Tests retain retired-key/off-path,
ordering, retry and denial-parity guards. The flag registry records the
replacement; the shared `FIRESTORE_READ_LEVERS` env budget slot has no
separate per-sublever budget entries. Known lever inventory: exactly one
added and one retired.

Identifier-free hit/miss/mismatch counters are on both Cloud Run GMP
keep-lists and survive isolated sync-worker exits/SIGKILL. The GPU
worker registers the counter on its private registry, and a real
pod-parent endpoint test verifies each child's series is retained once.
No negative-cache cohort is enabled; runtime config changes only remove
the retired lever.

Privacy-critical read suppression depends on complete WQ26 writer
coverage. Standalone/external writers bypassing the fence remain a
rollout blocker. Shadow moves the token read ahead of the lookup
families and intentionally gives up generation-memo savings for sampled

hf mf supercard - UID write on super card generation 2

The gen2 branch refused `-u` with "Not supported on this card". These
cards do take a UID write: a five command knock, the new UID one byte
per command (always seven commands, zero padded), then a HLTA which
commits it. The card answers the halt instead of staying silent, and
without it everything before is discarded when the field drops - which
is why the sequence is absent from the vendor app, whose HLTA is emitted
by the Android NFC stack on teardown.

The new UID must match the card's current UID length, the parts are
physically 4b or 7b. Outcome is decided by re-selecting and comparing
the UID, not by the status byte.

Verified on a 4 byte card. The 7 byte path is inferred from the sequence
always carrying seven UID bytes and is untested.

A refused -r / -u now returns an error instead of PM3_SUCCESS.

Merge pull request #7448 from emincan2000/fdcan-bit-timing-range

stm32/fdcan: keep bit timing within the register fields

stm32/fdcan: reject bit timings the registers cannot hold

Hand-built NominalBitTiming and DataBitTiming values were still masked
to the field width, so a prescaler past 512 or 32 programmed a different
bitrate. Assert the documented ranges in debug builds, and cover the
FDCAN prescaler limits with a unit test.

Merge pull request #7400 from Eleocraft/embassy_crypto_consts

Embassy crypto consts

Merge pull request #7449 from emincan2000/sdmmc-v1-clkdiv-range

stm32/sdmmc v1: do not accept a divisor of 258

Merge pull request #7446 from emincan2000/i2c-v2-timing-clamp

stm32/i2c v2: clamp SDADEL and SCLDEL to their 4-bit range

crypto: test the size constants, end docs with a period

The tests tie each constant to the array type its constructor takes, so a mismatch no longer compiles. embassy-boot checks its key and signature sizes.

boot: use SEC1_SIZE as the P-curve verifying key size

KEY_SIZE was switched to FIELD_SIZE, which is 32/48 instead of the 65/97 bytes from_sec1 takes.

Merge pull request #7447 from leftger/usb-uvc-camera

usb: add a UVC camera device class

stm32/sdmmc v1: do not accept a divisor of 258

clk_div maps a rounded-up divisor x to CLKDIV = x - 2 and accepted x up
to 258. CLKDIV is 8 bits, so x = 258 gave 256, which the u8 cast turned
into 0, and the card clock ran at half the kernel clock (24 MHz instead
of about 186 kHz with a 48 MHz kernel clock). Accept x up to 257 and
return BadClock above it, and add a test for both ends.

Merge pull request #7444 from emincan2000/fmac-iir-y-headroom

stm32/fmac: leave one free slot in the Y buffer

stm32/fdcan: keep bit timing within the register fields

calc_can_timings accepts prescalers up to 1024, which is the bxCAN BRP
range. FDCAN used the same function for set_bitrate and
set_fd_data_bitrate, but NBRP holds 1 to 512 and DBRP 1 to 32, and the
config code masks the value before writing it. A larger prescaler was
therefore cut to its low bits: with a 100 MHz kernel clock,
set_bitrate(10_000) wrote prescaler 113 instead of 625 (55.3 kbit/s)
and set_fd_data_bitrate(125_000) wrote 18 instead of 50 (347 kbit/s).
Pass the FDCAN limits to the calculation so these bitrates fail like
any other unreachable one.

The register accessors also masked before subtracting 1, so the
largest valid values (prescaler 512, data prescaler 32, seg2 128, ...)
became 0 and the subtraction overflowed. Subtract first and let the
accessors return the register values.

usb: add a UVC camera device class

Video class 1.1 camera over an isochronous IN endpoint: MJPEG, YUY2 or NV12, with probe/commit negotiation of format, frame size and interval. Adds a WBA65 example that streams generated color bars.

stm32/i2c v2: clamp SDADEL and SCLDEL to their 4-bit range

Timings::new computes SDADEL and SCLDEL from the kernel clock and only
bounds them from below. Both are 4-bit fields in TIMINGR, and the
computed values are often larger (99 for SCLDEL at 100 kHz with a
100 MHz kernel clock), so the PAC setter keeps only the low 4 bits and
the setup time becomes whatever those bits happen to give: 80 ns at
100 kHz and 20 ns at 400 kHz with a 100 MHz clock, below the 250 ns and
100 ns the I2C specification requires.

Clamp both to 15. That gives the longest delay the field can hold,
which is what the larger computed values asked for, and keeps the setup
time above the specification minimum for kernel clocks up to 300 MHz.

stm32/fmac: turn the clock off on drop

Fmac had no Drop, so its clock stayed on after it was dropped. The next
Fmac::new then skipped the RCC reset (enable_and_reset only resets a
peripheral whose clock is off), the old filter kept running with START
set, and the new instance's LoadX2/LoadY writes went to the running
filter as input samples.

Disable the clock in Drop, as Cordic does. FromAdc borrowed the Fmac as
&'d mut Fmac<'d, _>, which no longer compiles once Fmac has a Drop, so
it takes the Fmac lifetime as a separate parameter.

Merge pull request #7442 from henrik-nil-acc/synopsys-otg-reset-control

synopsys-otg: abort control transfers on a bus reset
Merge branch 'main' into fmac-iir-y-headroom

Merge pull request #7443 from emincan2000/cordic-q15-result-length

stm32/cordic: fix the q1.15 result length check

stm32/fmac: leave one free slot in the Y buffer

The FMAC needs the Y buffer to hold the M previous outputs an IIR filter
reads back plus at least one more slot (the "d" headroom in the reference
manual; ST's IIR examples document it as minimum 1). Fmac::new sized the
buffer to exactly the requested capacity, so controller_2p2z,
controller_3p3z and iir with Data::Prefilled of M values all ran with no
headroom, and the outputs were wrong from the second sample on.

Add the free slot when configuring the Y buffer.

stm32/cordic: size the q1.15 result slice from the result buffer

The q1.15 blocking_calc and async_calc built the result slice with the
length of the argument buffer. The check against the result length could
then never fail, and a result buffer shorter than the arguments was
written past its end.

Merge pull request #7421 from jseketa/stm32-h7-crs-sync-port

stm32/usb: on H7, sync the CRS to the OTG port in use

Merge pull request #7352 from kumbung01/fix-nrf-timer-frequency

stm32/usb: sync the CRS on H7RS too

`Syncsrc::Usb` (0b10) is OTG_FS SOF on H7R/H7S but OTG_HS SOF on H7 (RM0477 §9.4.2 vs RM0433 table 98), so the #7420 fix only reached H7. Pick the source per family instead of assuming OTG_HS is 0b10.

The guard also has to use the right clock gate: RCC_APB1HENR on H7, RCC_APB1ENR2 on H7RS.

Checked: stm32h743zi, stm32h745zi-cm7, stm32h723zg, stm32h7s7l8, stm32h7r3z8, stm32f407vg, stm32g0b1re.

Merge pull request #7441 from leftger/stm32-usb-vbus-detection

stm32/usb: add optional VBUS detection

Merge pull request #7439 from tobymurray/stm32-usb-u5-phy-tune

stm32/usb: apply the OTG_HS PHY tuning on U5

stm32/usb: fold the OTG_HS PHY clock gate into the PHY bring-up

The device path re-set USB_OTG_HSEN right after common_init, which already sets it through rcc::enable_and_reset; only the separate USB_OTG_HS_PHYEN gate was needed. Move that gate into otghs_phy_enable and reduce both call sites, device and host, to a single call.

stm32/usb: share the OTG_HS PHY bring-up between device and host

`new_hs_host` never ran the PHY tuning on WBA, and U5 host mode had no tuning at all. Move the tune-then-enable sequence into `otghs_phy_enable` and call it from both device and host init, for U5 and WBA.

The disconnect and squelch thresholds are raw 3-bit values in the PAC because ST's SVD does not enumerate them, so name the codes that RM0456 and RM0515 define. The reset values are named too: they document what the PHY would otherwise run with.

examples/stm32g0: add USB VBUS detection example

Show Driver::new_with_vbus on the NUCLEO-G0B1RE: wire DP/DM to CN10
pins 12/14 and feed VBUS through a divider to PA9 (D8).

synopsys-otg: abort control transfers on bus reset

Same hang as #7347 fixed for stm32/usb: a bus reset during a control
transfer left the device unresponsive until power was removed. Here
data_in waited for EP0's EPENA, which survives the reset, and data_out
for a packet that never came.

- data_out, data_in and accept end on a bus reset (USBRST) or a new
  SETUP.
- The interrupt wakes EP0's OUT waker on any bus event, instead of the
  stages registering the bus waker.
- A bus event masks USBRST until Bus::poll runs, so a waiting stage
  unmasks it. Otherwise a reset after a suspend raises no interrupt.

stm32/usb: add optional VBUS detection

The full-speed USB peripheral has no VBUS input and its suspend event only
means the host stopped traffic for 3 ms, so a self-powered device cannot
tell a suspended bus from an unplugged cable. Endpoint transfers then block
until a timeout instead of failing.

Add Driver::new_with_vbus, which takes an ExtiInput and reports
PowerRemoved/PowerDetected from Bus::poll. When VBUS drops, disable all
endpoints so pending transfers return EndpointError::Disabled, and clear
DPPU to signal disconnect to the host. PowerDetected restores DPPU and the
host reset re-enumerates.

The constructor is gated on the exti feature; Driver::new is unchanged.

Fixes #3740

stm32/usb: abort control transfers on a bus reset

stm32/usb: apply the OTG_HS PHY tuning on U5

RM0456 15.2.3 step 3 asks for COMPDISTUNE = 0b010 and SQRXTUNE = 0b000 in
SYSCFG_OTGHSPHYTUNER2 before the PHY is enabled; both are the reference
manual's recommended values. On U59x/5Ax both reset to 0% offsets; on
U5Fx/5Gx COMPDISTUNE already resets to 0b010. The WBA path already writes
them; the U5 path enabled the PHY without them.

p2: a reloaded page's leftover layer no longer blocks the drawer swipe

After a live reload the page loads new code, and the browser restores the route it had: with a sheet open
(the activity sheet, a notice's details), the restored layer may name something the new code no longer shows
(a run's row keyed differently). Nothing renders it, yet it stays in the route: the drawer's swipe waits for
open layers to close and never starts, and Back first closes the invisible layer. A refresh after closing
everything cleared it, so it looked like the gestures broke until a refresh.

- Sheets and viewers count themselves while on screen (`useShownModal`); the drawer's swipe waits only for a
  layer that shows (`modalShown`).
- A top sheet or viewer layer that nothing shows for 1.5 s leaves the route (`useUnshownLayers`, in the app's
  layout), so Back and the gestures act on what is on screen.
- The activity sheet finds its run by the call it shows when the run's row key changed.

fix(coding-agent): match grep globs relative to path (#11895)

The grep tool's `glob` was matched from the folder pi was started in,
not from `path`. A glob with a folder in it found nothing when `path`
was a different folder.

Example: pi runs in `/tmp/g`, and `/tmp/g/repo/migrations/main/a.js`
contains `hello`.

| Call | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `path: "repo", glob: "migrations/main/*.js"` | `No matches found` |
`migrations/main/a.js:1: hello` |
| `path: "repo", glob: "**/migrations/main/*.js"` |
`migrations/main/a.js:1: hello` | same |
| `path: "repo", glob: "*.js"` | works | same |

The empty result looks like a real negative, so the model concludes the
file does not exist. Grep prints results relative to `path`
(`migrations/main/a.js`), which is the form the failing glob used.

**Cause:** ripgrep always matches `--glob` from its own working
directory and has no option to change that. `grep.ts` started rg without
`cwd`, so it inherited pi's.

**Fix:** for directory searches, start rg with `cwd: searchPath` and
search `.`, then resolve rg's `./…` output paths against `searchPath` in
`formatPath`. The output format is unchanged. The glob is now anchored
at `path`: a lookalike at `repo/nested/migrations/main/b.js` does not
match `migrations/main/*.js`, and `**/migrations/main/*.js` still
matches both.

Searching `.` instead of the absolute path is needed for symlinks. rg
takes its working directory from the OS, which returns the real path
(`/tmp/real/repo`), but it builds found paths from the search argument
as given (`/tmp/link/repo/...`). Those don't share a prefix, so the glob
would miss again (macOS `/tmp` is a symlink). With `.`, the found paths
are already relative.

Single-file searches are unchanged: rg cannot start inside a file, and
it ignores `--glob` for files named directly.

A leading `./` in the glob (`./src/*.ts`, `!./dist/**`) is now dropped,
because rg never matches it.

The `glob` description now says the glob is relative to `path`, and that
a pattern without `/` matches file names at any depth.

Alternatives considered:
- Prefix `**/` to globs that contain `/`, as `find` does: a one-line
change, but it also matches nested lookalike folders (#10418).
- Rewrite the glob to an absolute one: rg reads a leading `/` as
anchored at its working directory, not at the filesystem root. It would
also need glob escaping of folder names, special handling for basename
globs, and Windows drive handling.

**Behavior change:** a glob written relative to pi's cwd while `path`
points elsewhere no longer matches. That only worked by accident and
contradicted the output format.

**Testing**
- New regression test in `test/tools.test.ts` with a plain and a
symlinked `path`: an anchored folder glob, the nested lookalike, `**/`,
`./` and `!./`. It fails on main with `No matches found`.
- `test/tools.test.ts` passes (111 tests), and `npm run check` passes.
- Windows: ran the built tool with Windows Node and `rg.exe` on `C:`,
covering relative, absolute and junction `path`, `**/`, `./`, `!./`, no
glob, and a single file. All gave the expected output with `/`
separators.

fix(coding-agent): edit keeps line endings of untouched lines, diffs only around changes (#11751)

The edit tool rewrote the line endings of lines it did not touch. It
could also fail after the file was already written, for example by
running out of memory while diffing a large file. Encoding handling
(non-UTF-8, UTF-16) was split out into a separate PR.

## Line endings (#8544)

**Problem.** The edit tool looked for the first line ending in the file,
normalized the whole file to LF for matching, and wrote the whole file
back with that one ending:

```
a\nb\r\nX = 1\r\n   edit X = 1 -> X = 2   =>  a\nb\nX = 2\n    (both CRLF became LF)
a\r\nb\nc           edit c -> C           =>  a\r\nb\r\nC     (the LF became CRLF)
a\rb\nX = 1\n       edit X = 1 -> X = 2   =>  a\nb\nX = 2\n    (untouched lone CR became LF)
```

**Solution.** Matching still runs on the LF-normalized text, so matching
itself is unchanged: exact and fuzzy matching, multiple edits,
duplicates, overlaps and error messages. `applyEditsToNormalizedContent`
now also returns the replacements it applied.
`applyReplacementsToOriginal` maps each replacement back to the original
text and splices it in there. Normalizing only shortens CRLF to LF, so
the original offset is the normalized offset plus the number of CRLFs
before it. A range that covers a normalized LF therefore covers the
whole CRLF. Text outside the replaced ranges keeps its bytes.

Line breaks in the new text use the line ending of the line where the
replaced range starts. For an unterminated last line, they use the
ending of the line before. A lone CR is used only in files with no LF at
all (classic Mac files). Elsewhere a lone CR is more likely a control
character inside a line.

Fuzzy matches still rewrite the whole lines they touch, as before. They
now return those lines as one replacement instead of rebuilding the
file, so lines outside the replacement keep their endings.

A kept CR and an LF can meet at a splice seam and would then merge into
one CRLF line break. For example, in `a\rb\nc` the edit `b -> \nB` would
write `a\r\nB\nc` (normalized `a\nB\nc`) while the diff shows
`a\n\nB\nc`. Deleting `b` would write `a\r\nc` while the diff shows
`a\n\nc`. Whenever a piece ending in CR is followed by a piece starting
with LF, an LF is added at the seam. This turns the CR into a CRLF of
its own, so the written file normalizes to exactly the content the diff
and patch describe. No kept byte is changed or removed; the one added
byte sits where the replaced text was. For a pure deletion between a
lone CR and an LF there is no other way to keep both line breaks.
Writing the merged bytes and diffing them instead would silently join
two lines the model meant to keep apart.

Pure LF and pure CRLF files produce the same output as before. For files
without any CR, the normalized result is written directly, as before.

## Diff before writing, only around the changes

**Problem.** `execute` wrote the file and then ran `generateDiffString`
and `generateUnifiedPatch`. Each diffs the whole file with jsdiff, which
takes roughly 10 to 15 times the file size in memory, however small the
change. A two-line edit of a 50 MB file crashed with
`--max-old-space-size=256` after the new content was already on disk,
and took about 4 s with the default heap. The TUI preview
(`computeEditsDiff`) diffed the whole file again.

**Solution.**
- The diff and patch are computed before the file is written, so a
failure there leaves the file unchanged.
- The edit tool and the preview use a new internal `generateEditDiff`.
The replacement positions are known, so it diffs only a window around
each replacement: the replaced lines plus 32 unchanged lines on each
side, with overlapping windows merged. jsdiff still does the diffing;
the window results are renumbered to file line numbers. The display diff
uses the same formatter as `generateDiffString` (extracted into
`formatDisplayDiff`), and the patch is jsdiff's `structuredPatch` hunks
shifted and written with `formatPatch`, as `createTwoFilesPatch` does.
- `details.diff`, `details.patch` and `firstChangedLine` have the same
format and content as before for every file size. The one possible
difference: in runs of repeated lines, jsdiff may align a change
differently within a window than over the whole file. The patch still
applies and describes the same edit.
- The exported `generateDiffString` and `generateUnifiedPatch` are
unchanged.
- The model-visible result is unchanged.

## Behavior differences

- Files with mixed line endings or lone CRs keep their bytes outside the
edited text. Files that use only CR line endings now get CR in inserted
lines; before, the whole file was converted to LF.
- Not changed: matching still builds a few file-sized strings (the
normalized text and the fuzzy normalization used to count duplicates),
so a very large file can still run out of memory during matching, before
anything is written.
- Removed unused internal helpers: `detectLineEnding`,
`restoreLineEndings` and `applyReplacementsPreservingUnchangedLines`,
which became the private `widenReplacementsToLines`. None of them were
exported from the package. `packages/durable` has its own copy and is
not changed.

## Testing

- `npm run check`: clean.
- `test/tools.test.ts`, the edit test files,
`test/edit-diff-window.test.ts`, `test/file-mutation-queue.test.ts`, the
BOM regression and `test/tool-execution-component.test.ts`: 174 passed.
- New tests, all with `Buffer.equals` on the written bytes:
  - mixed endings with LF first and with CRLF first (#8544)
  - lone CR
  - pure CRLF and pure LF with inserted lines (unchanged behavior)
- multiple edits in a mixed file, each new line getting its line's
ending
  - fuzzy match widening in a mixed file
- diff before write: `generateEditDiff` is mocked to throw, and
`writeFile` is never called
- `test/edit-diff-window.test.ts`: 2000 random edits on files with
distinct lines give exactly the whole-file `generateDiffString` and
`generateUnifiedPatch` output; 2000 random edits on files of repeated
lines give a patch that applies to the old content and yields the new
content; a small change in a 20 MB file is diffed in a child process
with a 96 MB heap, where the whole-file diff runs out of memory; a
replacement of 150,000 lines (no call-stack overflow)
- seams: insertion after a lone CR, deletion between a lone CR and an LF
(written bytes checked, and the patch applied to the old content gives
the intended content), and an inserted CR ending before a kept LF
- random property test: 3000 random mixed `\n`/`\r\n`/`\r` files with
random edits, checking that the written content normalized to LF equals
the content that was diffed. It fails without the seam rule.
- On `origin/main`, all new tests fail except pure CRLF and pure LF,
which pass there because that behavior is unchanged. Without the seam

fix(ai): omit empty tools array for tool history on openai-completions (#11891)

## Problem

`openai-completions` sends `"tools": []` whenever a request has no tools
but the transcript contains tool calls or tool results. vLLM 0.20+
rejects this
([vllm#39780](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39780)),
directly or behind LiteLLM:

```
400: `tools` must not be an empty array. Either provide at least one tool or omit the field entirely.
```

Trace: session uses tools -> all tools disabled (or SDK call without
tools) -> next request has `tools: []` -> 400 on every request. There
was no way to opt out.

The empty array came from #150 (2024), a workaround for LiteLLM raising
`Anthropic doesn't support tool calling without tools= param specified`.
Current LiteLLM adds a dummy tool itself for Anthropic in that case
(`litellm/llms/anthropic/chat/transformation.py`).

The OpenAI spec defines `tools` as an optional array, so omitting it is
valid. vLLM issue #39741 reports that OpenAI also rejects `tools: []`
with `empty_array`; not verified here.

## Change

- Omit `tools` by default when there are no tools.
- New `compat.requiresToolsWithToolHistory` (default `false`) restores
`"tools": []` for proxies that need it, such as older LiteLLM versions
in front of Anthropic.
- Regenerated `models.schema.json` and `models-configuration.md`.
- Tests: default omits the field (#11843), the compat flag sends `[]`.

## Risk

Setups that relied on the implicit `[]`: older LiteLLM with Anthropic,
and possibly OpenRouter Claude models (the only built-in Claude models
on `openai-completions`). Not verified against OpenRouter; those users
can set the flag.

fix(tui): draw fullscreen Kitty images after the rows they cover on every terminal (#11890)

Closes #11835

## Problem

In Orca, fullscreen inline images show only their first row; regular
mode shows them in full.

Orca renders Kitty graphics with xterm.js's image addon, which stores an
image as tiles in the cells it covers. WezTerm does the same. For a
5-row image, `TuiAltScreen` wrote:

```
row 1: move, clear line, image sequence   -> image covers rows 1-5
row 2: move, clear line, ""               -> erases image row 2
...
row 5: move, clear line, ""               -> erases image row 5
```

Regular mode clears the covered rows first and draws the image last, so
it was unaffected. Fullscreen already had that ordering, plus a redraw
when a covered row changes, but only for WezTerm (#10319).

## Fix

Use the draw-images-last path and the covered-row redraw for every Kitty
terminal instead of only WezTerm. Cost is bounded by the viewport (the
visible rows and the images in view, re-placed from the uploaded copy
without retransmitting), not by scrollback.

## Testing

- Headless repro with Orca's exact `@xterm/xterm@6.1.0-beta.336` +
`@xterm/addon-image@0.10.0-beta.331` and Orca's patches applied,
counting image tiles per row: before, fullscreen kept tiles only in the
first image row; after, all rows.

covered row, scrolling, and a cropped image:

| Terminal | Old interleaved output | Draw images last |
|---|---|---|
| Ghostty 1.3.1 | correct | correct |
| Kitty (latest) | correct | correct |
| herdr 0.9.5 in Ghostty | correct | correct |
| WezTerm nightly 20260117 | first row only | correct |

- Regression tests in `packages/tui/test/tui-alt-screen.test.ts` no
longer depend on terminal env vars. `tui-alt-screen.test.ts` passes, and

- src/web/elanor.css loads Elanor's fonts, the pi brand's tokens and the components'
  styles before style.css; p2's element resets move into a layer below Elanor's.
  data-color-scheme follows the theme for the tokens' dark colours. The web bundle
  emits .woff2 fonts.
- @base-ui/react needs @babel/runtime >= 7.29.7: the shared copy moves to 7.29.10, and
  the coding agent's install lock with it.

feat(p2): sandboxes run natively only; programs found on the PATH and in ~/.local/bin

Drop the Docker fallback (Dockerfile, container, image, the home-only folder rule). A host needs Linux, a usable
/dev/kvm, Node >= 22 and QEMU >= 7.2; the launcher looks for them on the PATH of SSH commands and in ~/.local/bin, where
user installations live (e.g. a QEMU built with --prefix=$HOME/.local on a distribution whose QEMU is too old), and
Gondolin starts QEMU through the same PATH. The host test names what is missing. The Envs contract keeps "docker" in
SandboxSupport's runtime (no longer reported) so open pages keep binding.

fix(p2): a tap beside Send no longer closes the keyboard without sending

The focus-keeping pointerdown covered only Send and Stop; a thumb landing in the
composer's padding or the button row's gaps blurred the textarea, so a phone's
keyboard closed and nothing was sent. The whole composer keeps the textarea focused
(text fields and portalled sheets excepted), and the last round button reaches the
composer's right edge. The composer sends only for its own form's submit (chat mode's
name sheet submitted the composer too).

fix(p2,chord): archived sessions' files answer at once; migrated files keep their times

/artifact, /download, POST /upload and DownloadStore check the catalog before reaching the session's worker: an
archived or unknown session answers 404 (an upload to an archived one 409) at once instead of after a refused
worker start (60 s each). Files writes take an optional created for imports; the summary keeps its newest in created
order. The migration carries each artifact version's, upload's and download's time from the old file's mtime and
verifies it.

fix(env): Stop and timeouts end remote calls at once while the host is down

An abort while the connection reconnects rejects at once instead of after the start;
an aborted request whose cancel the daemon does not answer within 1 s settles as
aborted; exec enforces its timeout locally from the call; file operations stop
waiting for the connection when aborted; ssh uses ConnectTimeout=15 so a host that is
down fails in 15 s. Reported on p2's bash tool while slayer rebooted.

fix(p2): Envs contract version 2, still serving version 1 to open pages

0fc460120 changed the Envs contract (EnvSummary.users, delete's force) under the same version, so pages loaded
before that deploy waited unbound on p2.envs. Envs is now version 2, evolved from 2a32a605a's declaration (version
1), and its provider still serves 1 through `accepts`: rows without users, a delete that is never forced.

feat(p2): list what blocks deleting an environment, and delete anyway after confirming

The Envs sheet lists the sessions using an environment (archived ones and subagent locations included), each
opening its session, and offers "Delete anyway" with a confirmation: the sessions keep their history and their tools
refuse to run until they move (never falling back to this device). Deleting a sandbox now also removes its run
directory on the host (launcher command `forget`).

fix(scripts): biome-check skips files Biome does not support, as the CLI does

The WASM workspace throws "The file does not exist in the workspace" for a file it has no language for (a
Dockerfile, a shell script) instead of skipping it, so npm run check crashed on platforms without the native Biome
(Android). Ask the workspace's file features first and skip unsupported files.

feat(p2,chord): per-host stores and Files v2; session files move into the session's store

Chord app kit: Files v2 replaces the kit's Files (one per host): spaces, paths and folders,
immutable blobs with versions (numbers never reused per path), copies sharing a blob,
idempotency keys, indexed metadata (source, ref, key) plus free meta, chunked writes,
ranged reads, paged and live folder listings, a summary per space, cancel, copyFiles,
filesFacet and the @earendil-works/chord/app/files subpath.

p2: the server and every session get a Chord store and a files directory
(server/store.sqlite, sessions/<id>/store.sqlite and files/); Durable runs on the
session store (StoreStorage); outboxes are off until p2 syncs. Artifacts, uploads and
download snapshots live in the session's Files and are served through the session worker;
clone copies the session directory, fork copies its files. The server refuses the old
layout; npm run migrate-data converts it (verified per session, resumable, --dry-run).

Merge pull request #11771 from adafruit/dhalbert-samd-claimed-pins

atmel-samd: track claimed pins in a table instead of by hardware state

Merge pull request #11773 from MakerClassCZ/native-sim-test-fixes

Fix native_sim stack overflow crash, negative os.urandom() size and msgpack test

atmel-samd: remove speaker_enable_in_use, now redundant with claimed_pins

claim_pin() and reset_pin_number() kept speaker_enable_in_use in step
with the claimed_pins[] bit for SPEAKER_ENABLE_PIN. The flag was needed
when claims came from pin registers, because the speaker enable pin is
driven low as an output when released.

The only behavior change: with a debugger attached, SPEAKER_ENABLE_PIN
(PA30, also SWCLK) is now in use like the other SWD pin.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

tests: fix extmod/msgpack_pack.py and add its expected output

The first pack() wrote to an undefined name. The test only runs where
msgpack exists, which is not the unix port, so this went unnoticed.
CPython has no msgpack, so the test needs its own .exp.

os: raise ValueError for a negative urandom() size

os.urandom(-1) tried to allocate 4294967295 bytes and raised MemoryError.
Raise ValueError, as CPython does. tests/extmod/os_urandom.py checks it.

zephyr-cp: leave room for Perfetto when raising a stack overflow on native_sim

Raising the RuntimeError for a C stack overflow allocates the exception,
and gc_alloc() then emits a Perfetto counter. The encoder needs about
2.5kiB of stack, more than the 1kiB left by CIRCUITPY_EXCEPTION_STACK_SIZE,
so the simulator crashed instead of raising. extmod/re_stack_overflow.py
shows it.

atmel-samd: don't reset the pin numbered like the Max3421E EIC channel

common_hal_max3421e_max3421e_deinit_irq() passed pin->extint_channel to
reset_pin_number(), so it reset whichever pin had the same number as the
IRQ pin's EIC channel. The IRQ pin itself is a DigitalInOut, released by
common_hal_max3421e_max3421e_deinit().

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

atmel-samd: track claimed pins in a table

pin_number_is_free() decided whether a pin was in use by reading its
PINCFG, PMUX and DIR registers, so any pin left configured looked
claimed. For example, the UF2 bootloader leaves the D13 LED pin as an
output. Today the boot-time reset_all_pins() hides that, but it goes
away when atmel-samd switches to finalizer cleanup. Every other port
already tracks claims in software.

Keep a claimed_pins[] table instead:
- claim_pin() and the new claim_pin_number() set a bit.
- reset_pin_number() clears it.
- reset_all_pins() keeps claims only on never-reset pins.
- SWD pins are still in use while a debugger is attached.

Claim pins where they are configured without a DigitalInOut: PWMOut,
FrequencyIn, CAN, sdioio, the ParallelBus data pins,
ParallelImageCapture, QSPI flash and the USB pins.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

zephyr-cp: share the host X11 display with the native_sim container

If DISPLAY is set when the container is created, mount the X11 socket
directory (read-only, since it is a locked read-only mount under WSLg)
and pass DISPLAY, so make run-sim can open the simulator window.

The host's X cookie names the host, so it does not match inside the
container. Copy it as a wildcard entry into a mounted directory each
time the script runs, so a cookie renewed by a new desktop session
reaches an existing container too. ZCP_NO_DISPLAY=1 turns this off.

Document how to reach the REPL over the simulator's pty from a second
shell.

zephyr-cp: take qstr values from py/qstrdefs.h

The qstr header was generated from the MP_QSTR_ names alone, so a value
had to be recovered by unescaping the name. That is ambiguous when two
escapes meet: MP_QSTR__brace_open__colon__hash_b_brace_close_ became
"{_colon_#b}" instead of "{:#b}", and bin() crashed the native_sim build
(mp_obj_str_format looked the field name up in a NULL kwargs map).

Preprocess py/qstrdefs.h and pass it to makeqstrdata.py first, as
py/py.mk does, so its Q() lines give the values.

ci: pin ubuntu-24.04 for browser-dependent jobs broken by Ubuntu 26

ubuntu-latest now resolves to Ubuntu 26, which breaks two CI jobs in
dependency setup before any test code runs:

- Enterprise Workflows entry: Playwright has no chromium build for
  ubuntu26.04-x64, so 'playwright install --with-deps chromium' fails.
- Linux E2E Tests (advisory): the webkit2gtk-driver package was renamed
  upstream to webkitgtk-webdriver with no compatibility shims, so apt
  cannot satisfy the install list.

when Playwright ships Ubuntu 26.04 support and the package list learns
the new spelling.

Merge pull request #7895 from screenpipe/fix/enterprise-unpinned-upload-fail-closed

fix(enterprise): fail closed when no upload destination pin is deployed

fix(enterprise): fail closed when no upload destination pin is deployed

Direct upload tickets previously accepted any destination host when
SCREENPIPE_ENTERPRISE_UPLOAD_PINNED_HOSTS was unset (logged but not
refused). Plaintext customer batches could be redirected anywhere by a
compromised control plane or a manipulated ticket.

Now direct upload modes refuse to resolve until a destination pin is
deployed. SCREENPIPE_ENTERPRISE_UPLOAD_ALLOW_UNPINNED=1 is the explicit

commits.message:
test: turmoil: heal link latency before the liveness checks

# Summary

`heal_network()` now sets every link's latency to zero, as it already
did for message loss, instead of restoring the seeded latency band. The
liveness phase therefore checks the healed cluster over timely links.

# Details

Seeded links delay each message by up to 50 ms, while the replication
RPC deadline is the soft TTL of `heartbeat_interval`, as little as
37.5 ms. A healed cluster could time out its AppendEntries RPCs and
fail the liveness phase with nothing wrong in it. When chaos restores
link quality without healing, `restore_link_quality()` still restores
the seeded band.

The new `healing_removes_latency_that_exceeds_the_rpc_deadline` test
sets the link latency to `heartbeat_interval` and checks that a
request-response exchange finishes within the soft TTL after healing.
It lives in the fuzz binary, so `make test-turmoil-default` and
`make test-turmoil-threshold`, which the CI turmoil jobs run, now also
run the binary's tests.

change: examples: carry conflict hints over HTTP, gRPC and turmoil

# Summary

network-v2-http, the gRPC example, tests-turmoil's simulated network
and the minimal benchmark now carry `AppendResult` with its conflict
hint, instead of converting through `AppendEntriesResponse`.

# Details

- network-v2-http's `/append` route replies with `AppendReply`, a new
  serde wire type for `AppendResult` that keeps the acknowledged log id
  and the hint. raft-kv-memstore and raft-kv-log-wal-sm-mem get hints
  through the shared server and client. raft-kv-rocksdb's own `/append`
  route, which the jepsen test app also builds, replies with
  `AppendReply` too. The crate's first test checks that every
  `AppendResult` survives the JSON round trip, including an empty
  conflict hint; the CI `examples` job and `make test-examples` now run
  the crate's tests. The getting-started guide's server sketch replies
  with a wire type and links to `AppendReply`.
- The gRPC example's unary `AppendEntries` reply uses the StreamAppend
  encoding, so a conflict reply carries the conflict log id and the
  hint. A client built before this change still reads the new replies
  correctly: it reads a success reply's `last_log_id` as a partial
  success up to that log id, which gives the same result, and ignores
  the new fields of a conflict reply.
- tests-turmoil sends a bincode `AppendReply`, so the fuzzer and the
  scenarios exercise hint-guided probes under partitions, crashes and
  storage loss. The new probes change each seed's schedule: the CI
  replay of seed 812 still passes, but runs 12,800 simulation steps
  instead of 13,200, so it may no longer hit the log ID reuse
  interleaving of #2167. The scripted
  `restored_leader_preserves_entry_identity` scenario still covers that
  bug.
- The minimal benchmark's in-process network implements `RaftNetworkV2`
  instead of the v1 `RaftNetwork` behind the legacy `Adapter`, and
  passes the target's `AppendResult` unchanged. `full_snapshot` hands
  the snapshot to the target's `install_full_snapshot()`, so the v1
  snapshot receiver and the `openraft-legacy` dependency are removed.
  Throughput is unchanged within noise.

Upgrade tip:

The network-v2-http `/append` JSON reply changed, so a node built from
this version and one built from the previous version cannot replicate to
each other. Upgrade every node of a cluster that uses network-v2-http at
the same time.

change: raft: guide probes with conflict hints in AppendResult

# Summary

A follower that rejects AppendEntries because of a conflicting
`prev_log_id` now reports a `ConflictHint`, and the leader uses it to
choose its next probe instead of relying on binary search alone. The
AppendEntries APIs return `AppendResult`, whose `AppendError::Conflict`
carries the hint: `Raft::append_entries()`, `Raft::stream_append()`,
`RaftNetworkV2::append_entries()`, `RaftNetworkV2::stream_append()`,
`NetAppend::append_entries()`, `NetStreamAppend::stream_append()` and
multiraft's `GroupRouter::append_entries()`.

# Details

`AppendResult`, `AppendError` and `ConflictHint` are new public types in
`openraft::raft`. `Ok(log_id)` is the last log id the follower accepted;
it replaces both `Success` and `PartialSuccess`. A hint is one ordered
vector of the follower's log ids after it truncated the conflicting
entries: the local committed position when known, selected later leader
boundaries, and always the retained tail. It describes the in-memory log
and makes no durability claim.

The leader compares every sample with its own log, including the first,
which may be uncommitted. A shared committed leader id identifies a
common prefix even when the two logs end that leader's run at different
indices, and a purged position gives no negative evidence. The hint
narrows the search range and places the next probe right after the
greatest shared log id; an empty hint means an empty follower log. It
never advances `matching` or counts toward a quorum: if a crash erases
the suggested prefix, the next conflict resumes ordinary search without
retracting quorum progress. The leader ignores the hint of a conflict
that answers no inflight request, such as a heartbeat's.

The default `stream_append()` sends each request through
`append_entries()`, so it carries the hints the unary transport
delivers. It continues only after an acknowledgement of the whole
request, and a debug assertion checks that each acknowledgement lies in
the range of the request that was sent.

`AppendError` and `ConflictHint` do not implement serde, so a later
change to either cannot silently change the bytes on the wire. Each
transport defines its own wire type and decides whether it carries the
hint; without it, the leader uses binary search. `AppendEntriesResponse`
and `StreamAppendResult` stay as serializable formats without the hint.
`AppendEntriesRequest::last_log_id()` is now public, and the new
`AppendEntriesResponse::into_append_result()` rebuilds a result from the
request that was sent. The legacy v1 `RaftNetwork` keeps returning
`AppendEntriesResponse`, and its adapter converts. The gRPC example's
StreamAppend reply gains an optional `hint` field, which older peers
ignore; its unary reply, the other examples, tests-turmoil and the
benchmark keep their wire formats.

Upgrade tip:

A follower server that sends the result of `Raft::append_entries()`
keeps its wire format with:

    let reply = raft.append_entries(req).await.map(AppendEntriesResponse::from);

A `RaftNetworkV2::append_entries()` that receives that format rebuilds
the result from the request it sent:

    let prev_log_id = rpc.prev_log_id.clone();
    let last_log_id = rpc.last_log_id();
    let response: AppendEntriesResponse<C> = send(rpc).await?;
    Ok(response.into_append_result(prev_log_id, last_log_id))

A transport that implements `stream_append()` or serves
`Raft::stream_append()` keeps its format by converting to and from
`StreamAppendResult`:

    // Follower: send the old format.
    let wire: StreamAppendResult<C> = result.map_err(Into::into);
    // Leader: decode it.
    let result: AppendResult<C> = wire.map_err(Into::into);

Either way, the leader gets no hints from that transport. Code that
inspected the result replaces `is_success()` with `is_ok()`, and
`is_conflict()` with `matches!(r, Err(AppendError::Conflict { .. }))`.

feat: replication: probe the inherited tail first

# Summary

Start matching-point discovery at the new leader's first entry so
caught-up followers can acknowledge its no-op in one round trip.

# Details

Keep binary search as the fallback after the optimistic probe fails.
Every send consumes the pending probe, including a snapshot send. A
probe whose start has left `[matching.next_index(), searching_end]`
since it was chosen is skipped, so it neither resends entries the
follower already holds nor probes a position known to conflict.

The zero-entry partial-success tests now lose the optimistic first
request, so their remaining probes still exercise binary search.

This changes only internal replication state and preserves existing
transport APIs and wire formats.

refactor: examples: add raft-kv-memstore-weighted-membership

# Summary

Add a variant of `raft-kv-memstore` whose type config selects
`WeightedMembership` and `WeightedChange` from `openraft-membership`,
and point the membership docs at it. Its `/init` and
`/change-membership` routes take the weight of each voter and a write
weight; storage, network and the other routes are those of
`raft-kv-memstore`.

# Details

- `app_http::Server::add_openraft_routes()` needs
  `MembershipEdit: From<ChangeMembers>`, because its
  `/change-membership` takes only a set of voter IDs. A voter set
  states no weights, so `WeightedChange` has no such conversion. The
  example registers the routes one by one: `/init` and
  `/change-membership` from `src/membership_api.rs`, and the other
  routes of `app-http` unchanged.
- The integration test runs each node as a process of the example's
  binary, so it can stop nodes. It initializes node 1 alone, adds
  three learners, sets the weights `{1:2, 2:1, 3:1, 4:1}` with write
  weight 3, and checks that the change went through a joint config.
  After it kills voters 3 and 4, a write still commits, because voters
  1 and 2 weigh 3. CI and `make test-examples` run the test.
- The example has no `test-cluster.sh`: the integration test already
  shows each call that sets up a cluster.
- The membership chooser in `membership/src/docs.md` now starts with
  OpenRaft's default `Membership`, and names for each membership the
  edit type that `Raft::change_membership()` takes. The README and a
  new `Membership` / `MembershipEdit` entry in the getting-started
  guide link the chooser. The link points into the repository,
  because `openraft-membership` is not on docs.rs yet.
- The membership guide and README, the provided-memberships FAQ, the
  feature guide and `examples/README.md` link the example.
- The FAQ states when a change needs no joint config: every old read
  quorum intersects every new write quorum, and every old write quorum
  intersects every new read quorum. The previous wording did not say
  which kinds of quorums must intersect.
- The four `rust,ignore` snippets of the membership guides are now
  `no_run` doctests, so `make docs-check` type-checks the documented
  calls. Their hidden lines set
  `AsyncRuntime = openraft_rt_tokio::TokioRuntime`, because the crate
  depends on `openraft` without `tokio-rt`. The crate README and the
  FAQ keep `rust,ignore`: hidden lines would show on GitHub and
  crates.io, and `openraft` cannot depend on `openraft-membership`.

chore: ci: check wasm builds and run rt-tokio tests

# Summary

CI now builds the library crates for `wasm32-wasip1` and runs
`openraft-rt-tokio`'s tests on native and on wasm. A change that turns
tokio's `rt-multi-thread` back on for wasm, or makes
`TokioRuntime::new()` build the wrong runtime flavor, now fails CI.

# Details

- `make wasm-check` builds `openraft` (default features, no default
  features, `serde,single-threaded`), `openraft-legacy` and
  `openraft-membership` for `wasm32-wasip1`. It builds one crate at a
  time and only `--lib`: crates built together can hide a feature that
  one of them forgot to request, and test targets pull in
  dev-dependencies such as the workspace tokio, whose `rt-multi-thread`
  does not compile for wasm.
- `make test-wasm` runs `openraft-rt-tokio`'s tests on `wasm32-wasip1`
  under `wasmtime`, with and without `single-threaded`.
- `test_new_runtime_flavor` asserts that `TokioRuntime::new()` builds a
  multi-thread runtime on native and a current-thread runtime on wasm.
- The `wasm` job runs both targets. The `rt-tokio` job runs
  `openraft-rt-tokio`'s tests on native; no CI job ran them before, and
  `make test-runtime` runs them only as part of `make verify-full`.
- Neither new target is part of `make verify-full`, so contributors do
  not need the wasm target or `wasmtime` installed.

feat: rt: build openraft-rt-tokio and openraft-legacy for wasm

# Summary

`openraft` with default features and `openraft-legacy` no longer
enable tokio's `rt-multi-thread` on wasm targets, so both compile for
`wasm32-wasip1`. Native builds get the same tokio features as before.

# Details

tokio emits a `compile_error!` on wasm when `rt-multi-thread` is on.
Two crates turned it on for every target:

- `openraft-rt-tokio` uses it only in `TokioRuntime::new()`, which
  Openraft itself never calls. The feature now comes from a
  `cfg(not(target_family = "wasm"))` dependency table, the same
  condition tokio checks. On wasm, `new()` builds a current-thread
  runtime and ignores `threads`.
- `openraft-legacy` inherited the workspace tokio entry, which enables
  `rt-multi-thread` among other features, although the crate only uses
  the `tokio::io` traits. It now depends on tokio with `io-util` alone.
  A crate that relied on `openraft-legacy` for another tokio feature,
  such as `macros`, must enable it itself; no crate in this repository
  did.

A wasm build needs Cargo's feature resolver 2, the default since
edition 2021: resolver 1 enables the features of target-specific
dependencies on every target.

The same problem in 0.9 is discussed in #2269.

test: jepsen: widen the bridge-partition write deadline to 4 s

# Summary

The bridge-partition liveness check now requires the first write within
4 seconds of installing the partition, instead of 1.5 seconds.

# Details

A storage stall on a newly elected leader can push the first write past
1.5 seconds without any regression of #2080. In the failing CI run, the
new leader stalled for about 300 ms while saving its Vote, longer than
its 300 ms lease. A leader without a quorum acknowledgement times its
quorum-loss quiet periods from its Vote change, so it then sent nothing
until its first 700 ms quiet period ended. Meanwhile the old leader
raised its term every 300 ms through the bridge, and the new leader
needed three more election rounds to win. The first write completed at
2487 ms; nine earlier CI runs completed it in 782-893 ms.

One more round, plus the wait for the next write attempt, would land
near 3 seconds, so the bound is 4 seconds. A #2080 regression still
fails the check: the old leader then blocks every election, so no write
completes in the 10-second window.

The quiet-period timing stays unchanged in openraft. It only delays
recovery when the stalled leader is needed for every quorum, as in this
topology.

Failing run: https://github.com/databendlabs/openraft/actions/runs/42051798385/job/127329529795

fix(updater): reuse a verified installer, keep it on feed failure

The in-app update downloaded the installer again even when an identical one was already in the update download folder. Before requesting a download, the main process now streams the SHA-256 of the file the download would write and, when it equals the newsfeed hash, records it as a finished download so the update overlay offers the install. A file with a different hash is removed and downloaded as before.

The installer and its download record are also no longer deleted when the newsfeed could not be fetched or verified; they are cleared only when a fetched and verified newsfeed has no update for the platform.

Merge pull request #3457 from input-output-hk/fix/update-installer-job

fix(watchdog): keep the update installer running after the watchdog exits
docs(changelog): record the update installer fix

fix(watchdog): keep the update installer running after the watchdog exits

On Windows the installer needs elevation, so the watchdog starts it through ShellExecuteEx. Windows places the elevated process in the watchdog's job object, and that job kills its processes when it closes, so the installer was killed as the watchdog exited. Once ShellExecuteEx has started the installer, the watchdog now clears the kill-on-close limit on its job, keeping breakaway allowed.

commits.message:
fix: refcount toolsets on Runner so close() waits for last holder

Track active Runners holding each BaseToolset in a weak-reference
registry so Runner.close() only closes a toolset when no other active
Runner still holds it. This prevents parallel Runners sharing an agent
or parallel AgentTool invocations from closing a stateful toolset
while sibling runs are still in flight.

Thanks to @claxman for originally proposing this fix in PR #7045.

Closes #4045

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1015953186

fix: run OAuth2 auth response token exchange off the event loop

Loading a stored OAuth2 authorization response in CredentialManager called the synchronous get_auth_response helper directly on the event loop, so redeeming an authorization code stalled concurrent requests on the server for up to the 10-second token request timeout. CredentialManager now awaits a new private AuthHandler helper that exchanges the code through the async exchanger, which offloads only the token request to a worker thread, so the loop keeps serving other requests and a redemption no longer also holds a worker thread running a nested event loop.

Co-authored-by: George Weale <gweale@google.com>
PiperOrigin-RevId: 1015946422

fix: type the API server eval managers as optional

ApiServer annotated its eval set managers with names it never imported, so type checkers could not check them, and a server built with None for them crashed with AttributeError on the dev server's eval endpoints. The managers are now imported for type checking and typed as optional, and the endpoints that need a missing manager answer with a 500 that names it.

Co-authored-by: George Weale <gweale@google.com>
PiperOrigin-RevId: 1015916711

fix: pass raw argument values to a callable require_confirmation

Since 82fe029 ("fix: convert Enum tool arguments to the declared member")
and 58332a2 ("fix: convert list[Enum] tool arguments to the declared
members"), FunctionTool converts Enum, Optional[Enum] and list[Enum]
arguments to members in _preprocess_args. check_require_confirmation runs
the same preprocessing, so a callable require_confirmation got the members
too, and a predicate written against the value the model sends silently
stopped matching for a plain Enum parameter:

    FunctionTool(manage_file,
                 require_confirmation=lambda path, action: action == "delete")

With `action: Action` (a plain Enum), the predicate got Action.DELETE,
`Action.DELETE == "delete"` is False, and the delete ran without asking
for confirmation. On 2.13.0 the predicate got "delete" and the call paused.

A callable require_confirmation now gets Enum arguments as the values the
model sent, as before_tool_callback does, while the tool function still
gets the members. Everything else the predicate sees is as on 2.13.0:
Pydantic model and int coercion still apply, subclass _preprocess_args
overrides still run, and with FUNCTION_TOOL_ARG_VALIDATION on the
predicate still gets the validated members.

check_require_confirmation runs the usual preprocessing and then, with
FUNCTION_TOOL_ARG_VALIDATION off, passes each Enum member in the args,
alone or in a list, to the predicate as its value. Doing it after
preprocessing keeps subclass _preprocess_args overrides applied.

Co-authored-by: Haran Rajkumar <haranrk@google.com>
PiperOrigin-RevId: 1015855826

fix: refcount toolsets on Runner so close() waits for last holder

Track active Runners holding each BaseToolset in a weak-reference
registry so Runner.close() only closes a toolset when no other active
Runner still holds it. This prevents parallel Runners sharing an agent
or parallel AgentTool invocations from closing a stateful toolset
while sibling runs are still in flight.

Thanks to @claxman for originally proposing this fix in PR #7045.

Closes #4045

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1015852016

fix: stop rerunning a waiting wait_for_output node on resume

Merge https://github.com/google/adk-python/pull/7991

On resume, a `wait_for_output` node whose earlier run ended waiting (no output,
route or interrupt) is no longer run again with the input it already handled;
it stays waiting until its next trigger. Agents in task or chat mode and nodes
with `rerun_on_resume=True` still rerun. A custom node that waits on the user

fix(workflow): key a resumed sub-agent's run by the path its events carry

When a chat turn resumes in a sub-agent (the runner picks the agent that
replied last, or the one whose function call the user answered), the scheduler
runs it with no parent context. Its Context takes its path from the static
agent tree, so its events carry `root_agent@1/sub_agent@1`, but the scheduler
registered the run as `sub_agent@1`. Rehydration looked for that key, never
found the run, and started the sub-agent fresh. That is harmless for an
LlmAgent that reads the function response from history, but a node that relies
on its recovered state does the wrong thing: a sub-agent with
`rerun_on_resume=False` whose interrupt was answered runs again and asks again
instead of completing with the answer.

A step with no parent context is now keyed and numbered under the static
parent path its Context derives, so the run key equals the event path and
rehydration finds the sub-agent's earlier run in the invocation.
`reserve_run_ids` still reserves every ancestor on that path. Numbering under
the static parent is what keeps the earlier attempt at this from regressing
`test_llm_agent_as_node.py::test_three_layer_llm_agent_transfer_round_trip`:
when an invocation is continued in a grandchild and it transfers to its parent,
the parent's run is `root_agent@1/child_agent@2`, after the reserved
`child_agent@1`, instead of landing on the earlier run at
`root_agent@1/child_agent@1` and being fast-forwarded.

No turn boundary is needed inside an invocation: a message sent with an
existing invocation id is treated as a retry of that invocation and is not
appended to the session, so the invocation's earlier runs are the traversal
being replayed.

Visible effects on persisted `node_info.path`, only for turns that resume in a
sub-agent:
- A parent reached by transfer from a resumed grandchild is now
  `root_agent@1/mid_agent@2` (it was recorded as `root_agent@1/mid_agent@1`,
  the same path as the grandchild's ancestor). The root agent is still
  `root_agent@2`, as before.
- A continued invocation that resumes a sub-agent replays its earlier runs in
  that invocation, so the sub-agent answers in the run where it replied last
  (for example `root_agent@2/sub_agent_1@1`) rather than in a second run under
  its first run's path.
PiperOrigin-RevId: 1015300365

fix: accept AgentTool input_schema args that use aliases

Merge https://github.com/google/adk-python/pull/7764

AgentTool validates the call's args against the wrapped agent's
input_schema, then sends the validated model as JSON to that agent, whose
node runtime validates it again. That JSON is keyed by field name, so the
second validation rejected it for any field read through an alias. Node
input and output validation now also accepts field names, so the JSON
validates again for validation_alias, alias_generator, AliasPath and
nested schemas. That JSON is also keyed by field name when the schema
sets serialize_by_alias.

Data a node validates against a schema is now accepted by field name
even when the schema reads that field only through an alias or sets
validate_by_name=False. The JSON AgentTool sends still leaves out every
field whose value is None, as before.

ci(workflows): forward one secret to the component upload, pin the Wokwi CLI install and stop persisting checkout tokens (#13073)

* ci(release): forward only the component registry token to the upload workflow

The release workflow called upload-idf-component.yml with
secrets: inherit, so the job that pushes the component to the registry
could also read the tools upload PAT, the Discord webhook and every
other repository secret. The called workflow now declares the one
secret it reads, IDF_COMPONENT_API_TOKEN, under workflow_call, and the
release workflow forwards exactly that. The secret is declared
optional so a direct workflow_dispatch run keeps taking it from the
repository as before.

* ci(wokwi): install a pinned wokwi-cli release and verify its checksum

The Wokwi tests installed the CLI with curl piped into sh from
wokwi.com, which fetches whatever the latest release is at that
moment: a changed script or a bad release would run unverified on the
runner that holds the Wokwi token. The step now downloads the
v0.29.1 Linux binary from the wokwi-cli release itself, checks its
sha256 before making it executable and puts $HOME/bin on the PATH,
which is where the installer linked it. Bumping the version means
updating the two values together.

* ci(workflows): stop persisting the checkout token in the jobs that never push

actions/checkout keeps the job token, or the PAT a step passes it, in
the clone's git config by default, where every later step of the job
can read it. Forty checkouts now set persist-credentials: false: those
jobs build, test, publish sizes, deploy docs over SSH or talk to
GitHub through the token they are given explicitly, and the release
steps that write gh-pages clone it again with the token on the URL.

Six checkouts keep their credentials because the job pushes from that
clone: the external libraries report and the baseline JSON files to
gh-pages, the runtime test badge, the rebuilt Python tool binaries,
the version bump and tag of a release, and the tag deletion of a
rollback.

fix(serial): avoid retaining unused HardwareSerial from startup (#13010)

* fix(serial): Avoid linking unused UART0 from framework startup

Use a weak startup reference supplied by the HardwareSerial
implementation. Preserve the original default-pin operation and
ordering whenever an application actually links HardwareSerial.

Move USB CDC event dispatch next to HWCDCSerial and USBSerial so
HWCDCSerialEvent() and USBSerialEvent() keep running from loopTask
when no HardwareSerial code is linked.

Coordinated with FastLED/FastLED#4892.

* fix(serial): Register default UART0 pads without HardwareSerial

loopTask now calls uartSetPins() from the UART HAL instead of a weak
HardwareSerial hook. Serial-free images keep the default pads
registered with Peripheral Manager, so a later RMT/LEDC attach still
runs the UART detach, while HardwareSerial stays out of the link.

* fix(uart): Register UART0 console pads at startup without a driver

Serial-free images never install the UART0 driver, so the startup
setPins() only stored the pins and Peripheral Manager kept the default
pads as INIT. Another peripheral taking SOC_RX0/SOC_TX0 then left the
ROM UART route in place beside it.

uartRegisterConsolePins() records the ROM-routed pads as UART0 RX/TX.
Taking either pad runs the UART detach; the last pad also releases its
route when no driver exists. The next begin() still attaches the pads
fully. HardwareSerial is not linked for this.

* fix(uart): Release boot console pads moved before begin()

If setPins() moves UART0 away from the boot-registered pads before a
driver exists, release the old pads so Peripheral Manager does not keep
a stale UART0 owner whose detach would act on the new pin.

`MISE_ENABLE_TOOLS` / `MISE_DISABLE_TOOLS` (`enable_tools` /

feat(task): support zip:: includes for config and tasks (#15439)

Config and task includes accepted local paths, `git::` and `oci::`, but
not a zip archive, even though plugin installs do. A team that publishes
shared tasks or a base config as a `.zip` on a release page or file
server can now include it directly.

```toml
include = ["zip::https://example.com/platform-config.zip"]  # mise.toml at the archive root

[task_config]
includes = ["zip::https://example.com/shared-tasks-1.0.0.zip"]
```

mise downloads the archive, unpacks it into a directory and loads it
exactly like an `oci::` artifact: executable file tasks and `.toml` task
files for `task_config.includes`, and the root `mise.toml` for
`include`. Non-TOML files that start with a shebang are made executable,
since zip entries here are not trusted to carry modes.

- Only http(s) URLs are accepted; anything else fails with a clear
message.
- Task includes stay experimental, like the other remote sources.
- A URL names no content, so a config zip is refreshed like a branch
(`fetch_remote_versions_cache`) and paranoid mode rejects it.

Closes #15431

## Test plan

- unit tests for the provider (prefix match, URL validation, download
and unpack against a mock server)
- new e2e `test_task_zip_include`: task include, config include,
paranoid rejection, non-http rejection

fix(completion): forward a shim's completion request to its tool (#15429)

Tab completion for a tool run through a mise shim (`aube`, `pitchfork`,
...) offered mise's own commands instead of the tool's ([usage
discussion 1623](https://github.com/jdx/usage/discussions/1623)).

A shim is the mise binary under another name. mise answered the hidden
`__complete_word__` request before shim handling ran, so the shim
answered for mise:

```
$ ~/.local/share/mise/shims/aube __complete_word__ --shell fish --line "aube ins"
install        Install the tools in your config, or specific tool versions
install-into   Install a tool version into a directory outside mise
installs       [experimental] Inspect and choose identity-layout installations
```

The real `aube` binary answers `install` and `install-clean` for the
same line. With this change mise answers the completion request only
when invoked as mise itself. Under any other name the request continues
into shim handling, which already forwards it to the tool behind the
shim, so the shim now returns the tool's candidates. `mise
__complete_word__ ...` is unchanged.

Checked with a debug build: as `mise`, `ins` still completes to
`install`, `install-into` and `install-dev`; as a differently named
symlink, the request now reaches shim handling instead of returning
mise's list. I did not run it against a real installed aube or pitchfork
shim, and the new e2e test asserts only that a non-mise name no longer
returns mise's commands.

fix(backend): kill a hung asdf list-all at fetch_remote_versions_timeout (#15424)

`fetch_remote_versions_timeout` did not stop an asdf plugin's
`bin/list-all` that hangs. mise logged nothing and waited until the
script exited on its own, holding the tool-version lock the whole time
(a CI `mise install` waited behind one for hours).

```sh
mkdir -p /tmp/sleepy/bin
printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\nsleep 600\necho 1.0.0\n' > /tmp/sleepy/bin/list-all
chmod +x /tmp/sleepy/bin/list-all
mise plugins link sleepy /tmp/sleepy
MISE_FETCH_REMOTE_VERSIONS_TIMEOUT=5s mise ls-remote sleepy
```

Before, this printed nothing until the script finished. Now it fails
after about 5s with `timed out after 5s` and a hint to change
`fetch_remote_versions_timeout`, and the script's process group is
killed.

The cause was `run_with_timeout`: it ran the work in `thread::scope`,
which joins the thread before returning, so the timeout error only
surfaced after the script exited, and the child was never killed.
`list-all` and `ruby-install --update` now run through
`CmdLineRunner::with_timeout`, which kills the process group at the
deadline.

Behavior change: `bin/list-all` now runs with stdin closed, including
under `--raw`, where it used to inherit stdin. mise runs `list-all` in
many non-interactive places (background version fetches, `ls-remote`,
completions, CI), where a prompt could never be answered, so a plugin
that relies on prompting here is unlikely to work today. A script that
does read stdin now gets EOF.

Not changed: the python-build `git.update` call still uses
`run_with_timeout`. Git runs several subcommands there, so it needs its
own change.

Fixes #15421

fix(npm): reinstall aube trees whose dependency links were restored as file symlinks on Windows (#15425)

## Problem

On Windows CI, an npm tool installed by mise's embedded aube can still
fail at run time after a cache restore, even with the junction check
from #14418:

```
mise install --locked   ->  cspell@10.4.0 · already installed
cspell lint ...         ->  Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package 'picomatch'
```

This is the reopened report on #14417 (mise 2026.11.1).

## Cause

Reproduced on a Windows machine: install `cspell@10.4.0`, archive the
mise data dir with Git for Windows' `tar.exe` (what `mise-action` does),
delete it, and restore it.

- With `tar`'s default symlink mode the links are dropped, and #14418's
check catches that.
- With native symlinks (`MSYS=winsymlinks:native`, where the restore
succeeds as it did on the reporter's runner), aube's directory junction
comes back as a **file** symlink that points at the right directory.
Win32 opens through it, so `picomatch/package.json` looks present and
the health check passes, but node does not follow a file symlink as a
directory, so the package cannot be resolved. `mise install` says
"already installed" and never repairs it.

## Fix

On Windows, a dependency that is a file symlink now counts as missing,
so the tree is treated as not installed and `mise install` reinstalls it
from the lockfile (a package directory is never a file symlink, so
healthy trees are unaffected). Unix is unchanged.

## Validation

- Reproduced the failure above on Windows; confirmed the restored link
reports `is_symlink_file` and that the previous check returned healthy
for it.
- The existing
`virtual_store_entry_without_dependency_links_is_detected` test and
clippy pass on Linux. A new Windows-only test covers the file-symlink
case (it skips itself when the runner cannot create symlinks); it has
not been run on Windows, nor has the patched binary been run there.

Fixes #14417

fix(lock): keep tool_config.locked pins out of the lockfile after an install (#15428)

Fixes #15417.

With `tool_config.locked = true` and the default `lockfile_mode =
"generate"`, installing or running one tool could write a different
tool's unrecorded pin into `mise.lock`. The next run then accepted that
pin, so the lockfile stopped being the reviewed contract.

```toml
[tool_config]
locked = true

[tools]
"http:fixture-a" = { version = "1.0.0", ... }
"http:fixture-b" = { version = "2.0.0", ... } # only 1.0.0 is in mise.lock
```

Before: `mise exec -- fixture-b` failed with "not in the lockfile", but
it first installed `fixture-a`, and that install regenerated the
lockfile and added `fixture-b` 2.0.0. Running the same command again
succeeded.

After: the lockfile stays byte-identical and both attempts fail. Only an
explicit `mise lock` records the new version.

After an install, lockfile generation now withholds tools whose config
sets `tool_config.locked` and whose resolved version the lockfile does
not record yet, and keeps the entries it already has for them (they are
not pruned as unselected). Entries that are already recorded are still
refreshed. `mise lock` itself is unchanged.

The e2e test fails without the change and passes with it.

The `github:` backend could install a Python wheel instead of the native

fix(upgrade): stop --bump doubling prefix: on two-part prefix requests (#15426)

`mise upgrade --bump` no longer rewrites a two-part `prefix` request to
a version that cannot resolve.

With this config and 1.26.2 released:

```toml
[tools]
cargo-binstall = { prefix = "1.23" }
```

`mise upgrade --bump` proposed `prefix:prefix:1.1` and failed with `no
versions found for cargo-binstall`. It now bumps to `prefix:1.26`.
One-part prefixes such as `{ prefix = "27" }` already worked and behave
the same.

The bump split the `prefix:`-marked display form (`prefix:1.23`) at its
first dot, which produced a bogus vendor prefix of `prefix:1.`. It now
splits the version the user wrote. Requests that are not `prefix`
requests are unchanged.

Fixes #15419. Thanks to @kjanat for the report and the root-cause trace.

Adds `e2e/cli/test_upgrade_bump_prefix_request`.
