fix(node): upgrade transformers.js to 4.3.2 to pick up patched sharp (#4885)

## Summary

`@lancedb/lancedb` pins the optional dependency
`@huggingface/transformers` at 3.0.2, which requires `sharp ^0.33.5`.
Every npm install of LanceDB therefore pulled in a sharp version with
critical advisories (GHSA-wq5f-xc86-pv6w, GHSA-rgj7-g3m4-5g8c). No 3.x
release of transformers allows a patched sharp, so this upgrades to
4.3.2, which requires `sharp ^0.35.4`. A fresh install resolves that
range to 0.35.5, the first release that fixes both advisories.

- `nodejs/package.json`: `@huggingface/transformers` 3.0.2 → 4.3.2.
- `nodejs/pnpm-workspace.yaml`: remove the `sharp: ^0.35.4` override. It
only covered our own install, not consumers, and transformers now
requires that range itself.
- `nodejs/examples`: transformers 3.0.2 → 4.3.2, sharp 0.33.5 → 0.35.5.
- Both lockfiles resolve sharp to 0.35.5; `pnpm audit` reports no sharp
advisories in either.

`TransformersEmbeddingFunction` needed no code changes. The transformers
types are only used in private fields, so the published typings don't
change.

`docs/web-tests/ts` and `docs/web-tests/blob-v2/ts` are left alone: they
resolve transformers through a published `@lancedb/lancedb`, so they
pick this up after a release.

## Evidence

Embeddings from the built-in `huggingface` embedding function (default
`Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2`) on 4.3.2, compared with the same mean pooling
on 3.0.2, for three sentences:

```
transformers 4.3.2: 3 x 384
text 0: max|diff|=6.62e-07  cosine=1.00000000
text 1: max|diff|=6.26e-07  cosine=1.00000000
text 2: max|diff|=7.33e-07  cosine=1.00000000
```

End to end through a table, `search("a feline sat down")` returns `["The
cat sat on the mat.", "A dog barked at the mailman."]`.

## Merge Risk

**Door:** Two-way. A revert restores the 3.0.2 pin.
**Blast Radius:** Node `huggingface` embedding function, and install
footprint of the optional dependency (onnxruntime-node 1.19.2 → 1.30.0,
which still downloads the CUDA provider on Linux x64 by default, as
1.19.2 did).

feat: expose the remaining refresh options on the SDKs (#4890)

The server's backfill request takes a row filter, failure limits,
per-call timeouts and worker sizing, and SQL exposes all of them through

only batch_size, GPU placement and the retry and error policies. Anyone

`row_timeout_seconds`, `init_timeout_seconds`, `num_workers` and

through unchanged. `RefreshColumnOptions` now serializes straight into
the request body, so the three SDKs share one producer. Node gets a
`RefreshColumnOptions` object, which also carries the options it lacked
before. A LanceDB Embedded refresh rejects every option other than
batch_size and GPU placement, naming the option.

requested `k`. With the Rust dependency and Python/Node execution tests
already on main via #4881, document the tiers across Rust, Python, Node
and the search guide, extend the remote request matrix to cover `0.1`
and `0.25`, and align the Python test package with beta.11.

`0.1` and `0.25` target empirical mean partition-routing recall of 80%
and 90% for L2, cosine and dot through `k=100000`. These are not
per-query or final Recall@k guarantees. Default Auto is unchanged;
Hamming and larger `k` remain uncalibrated, and remote queries require
corresponding server support. This PR makes no additional performance
claim. See [Lance

measurements and limitations.

commits.message:
fix: match ExifTool directories case-insensitively on Windows (#2837)

ExifTool auto discovery accepts the path from shutil.which only when its
directory equals one of the trusted directories. shutil.which keeps the
spelling of the PATH entry, and the default Windows PATH spells System32
as C:\WINDOWS\system32, so the exact comparison against
C:\Windows\System32 fails and image and audio metadata are silently
dropped.

Compare os.path.normcase of both sides. normcase is the identity on
POSIX, so Linux and macOS matching is unchanged; the candidate already
goes through abspath, which normalizes separators.

(LocalSettings.dictationOpensTask, on by default). Off, a task started

happy-android analytics: consent read at every check, no turning on over an undeleted id, failed rows told by the client

Consent at the boundaries: live() and isLive() also read consent as it is,
beside the generation, so a consent read as off records and sends nothing
even before its collector runs; the transport's last check is isLive.

The deletion hold across a restart: while the last install id can't be
deleted, Analytics.allow() refuses turning analytics back on, and neither
switch is then written down as on (the device switch writes on only once
allowed; the Account screen writes the opt-out off only once allowed). The
stored setting stays off, so a restart can't bring the old id back. Both
screens say so with a new string, "Analytics couldn't be turned on. Try
again later.", in every language: the "not saved" one says analytics will
be on again at the next start, which a refusal isn't.

Failed rows: MessageSender holds no analytics state. A failed outbox row
carries why it failed (SendFailure, from its stored error) on its ChatRow,
and when the row is seen the client's errorSeen tells it once per row and
generation (SeenErrors, the last 500 in memory, cleared with the rest on an
opt-out). Being keyed on the row as seen, it can't race the failure.

happy-android analytics: opting out ends analytics at once, outside the flows

A revocation bumps a consent generation synchronously (the device switch
as it is set, the Account screen's opt-out as it is tapped, and consent read
as false), cancels the PostHog requests on their way, and deletes the queue,
throttle, cards seen, crash mark, flags and install id on the lane,
non-cancellably and without waiting for those requests. Every record, error,
exposure, incident, open, flag answer and send checks the generation it was
made in. A revocation holds analytics off until consent is read as off or
the person turns it back on, and no generation starts while the old install

go. Deliberate actions send feature_used when they succeed; opening or
viewing anything sends nothing. app_opened carries the configuration
snapshot (accounts is relay_accounts, voice_enabled is gone). An empty
restore is nothing_to_restore. Pairing gains sign_in_required; sign-in
gains wrong_server. docs/analytics-catalog.json is the v2 master.

happy-ios: error_shown for browser, artifact and file loads

A browser failure is read by its BrowserProblem kind; its words never.

happy-ios: daily_summary counts and the rest of its state

Each count sits where the person does the thing once: an opened screen,
a pick, an answer, a stop, a photo, a made task or bot, a todo change,
a search, a push tap, an account switch. provider_kinds,
provider_accounts and experiments_on join the day's state.

happy-ios: error_shown, sign_in_result, voice_session_ended, purchase_result

Each is read from the error's type or a closed result, never a message.
Mappings live in AnalyticsMappings with tests.

happy-ios: chat_failure_shown/action and message_sent

A failure card reads its typed failure for analytics (kind, untyped
without one, the provider's type, whether the turn ran on a pool, when it
happened) and never its ids, labels or message. The agent chat hands each
card to chat_failure_shown once it shows in the conversation on top while
the app is active; the engine's five-minute rule and bounded dedupe keep
an old or already-seen card from counting. Retry and switch-and-continue
log chat_failure_action.

message_sent goes once a send is accepted: from the agent chat with its
target (Chief of Staff, a bot, else a session), model, provider type and
effort, and from the relay outbox for Happy CLI sessions with its source.
Attachments, steering and new conversations count toward daily_summary.
The store's snapshot names the bots' agents for the target.

happy-ios: analytics starts at launch; connection_issue, app_crash, device switch

The composition root starts Analytics.shared for a build that may send,
and always wires its consent. The scene's foreground starts app_opened and
the 30 s flush; its background flushes under a background task.

connection_issue: each link reports to ConnectionWatch as it changes (an
agent's status with its last failure's code, a Happy account's socket and
the network path); AnalyticsBridge says which one the app shows, so an
incident is the shown link down for 10 s or more in the foreground, ended
by its recovery, a move to another, or the background.

app_crash: a MetricKit subscriber maps crash and hang diagnostics to the
catalog's reason by exception type and signal only.

AnalyticsBridge also follows the open Happy account's analyticsOptOut and
gives daily_summary its state. Settings has this phone's own Analytics
switch for every kind of account; off deletes the queue.

happy-ios: pairing reports pairing_result; PairingAnalytics goes

A pairing's end is one pairing_result (side phone, relay or direct, how it
started, ok/failed/cancelled and a closed error code) through
Analytics.shared. "They don't match" is a failure with emoji_mismatch,
not a cancel. A team server's malformed code is a failed sign_in_result.
PairingAnalytics, whose sink nothing set, and its test are deleted.

happy-ios: analytics client from the shared catalog

HappyCore/Analytics sends the catalog's iOS events to PostHog's /batch/
without the SDK: a typed Swift catalog (AnalyticsEvent), an allowlist at
the send boundary built from the same enums (AnalyticsSchema), a random
install id, and an on-disk queue (500 events, 7 days) flushed every 30 s
and on background, retried with the same $insert_id. The engine also keeps
error_shown's throttle, the chat failure dedupe set and the daily counts.
Nothing is sent from debug builds (except to HAPPY_ANALYTICS_CAPTURE),
tests, UI automation or a build without HappyPostHogKey; any account's
analyticsOptOut or the device switch stops it and deletes the queue.

docs/analytics-catalog.json is the shared catalog, byte-identical with
happy-desktop; AnalyticsCatalogContractTests holds the Swift catalog to it.
docs/product-analytics.md replaces the Expo-era list with a pointer to it.

commits.message:
Read leak roots that leaks prints by address alone

Summary:
`idb profile leaks --json` (and `idb profile memgraph --json`) could report a nonzero `leakCount` with an empty `groups` list. The companion builds the groups from the roots of the tree `leaks` prints, and it only recognised roots that `leaks` had typed:

```
4 (10.1K) ROOT CYCLE: <Node 0x101864120> [48]
```

`leaks` prints an allocation it cannot type, such as a plain `malloc` block, by address and size alone:

```
7 (224 bytes) ROOT LEAK: 0x101204460 [32]
   6 (192 bytes) 0x101204620 [32]
```

The totals line still counted those leaks, so a process whose leaks were all untyped got a count with no groups. This is what the iOS 27 simulator runtime's `leaks` reports for `ReplHost`, so the end-to-end test that checks the two agree failed with every client.

The parser now reads both root forms. Roots `leaks` could not type are grouped together with no type name: `LeakGroup.typeName` is optional, and on the wire it is the empty string, as `ProfileFrame.binary` already is for an unknown binary. Their node and byte counts come from the tree as before. If `leaks` counts leaks but prints no root the parser can read, parsing now fails with "leaks output has no leak roots" instead of returning a report whose groups contradict its count.

No `idb.proto` change and no client change: both the Python and Rust clients show the untyped group with an empty `typeName`. A client talking to an older companion still sees the old report.

The new parser fixture is real `leaks` output from `ReplHost` on an iOS 27.0 simulator; the existing iOS 26.5 fixture parses identically.

Differential Revision: D130308061

fbshipit-source-id: 517898148662305e94376e94b1593b3975dafdae

Fix two profile output bugs in the Python client

Summary:
Two bugs made `idb profile` fail in the Python client:

- **Every successful profile exited 1 in builds that bundle an older protobuf.** The report is turned into JSON by reading each field's `FieldDescriptor.is_repeated`. Older protobufs, whose C++ implementation some builds still bundle, have no `is_repeated`, so the conversion raised `AttributeError: 'google.protobuf.pyext._message.FieldDescriptor' object has no attribute 'is_repeated'` once the companion's result arrived. The conversion now uses `is_repeated` when the descriptor has it and otherwise compares `label` with `LABEL_REPEATED`'s number, which still never reads `label` on protobuf 6 (which deprecates it) or 7 (which removes it).
- **`profile trace` without `--json` always failed.** It printed the trace's tables by reading `tables` from the whole report, but the report holds them under `trace`, so it raised `KeyError: 'tables'`. It now reads them from `trace`, and prints the tool's own output, as `--json`-less profiles do, when there is no trace report.

Neither changes what is sent to the companion or what `--json` prints.

Differential Revision: D130019238

fbshipit-source-id: 6a1ae7d2fa673c29bff3c21ec29c1b30f16b21d8

Stop waiting on a stream's stop event once the stream has ended

Summary:
`stop_wrapper` races each read against the caller's stop event in a task it creates once. When the companion ends the stream itself -- `idb camera inject` once a camera has shown the whole video, `idb log` when the log ends -- the generator returned and left that task waiting on an event nobody would set. The CLI waits for every pending task before it exits, so such a command took an extra two seconds to exit and then printed:

```
[ERROR] - asyncio - _GatheringFuture exception was never retrieved
future: <_GatheringFuture finished exception=CancelledError()>
```

`stop_wrapper` now cancels the task and waits for it whenever it returns. The two client tests that set the stop event themselves to dodge the leak no longer do, so they fail on a leaked task if it comes back.

___

Differential Revision: D130186852

fbshipit-source-id: 9380177ad5013814f93fc030e14db38b38fd186e

Add a client opt-in for simulator notification service extensions

Summary:
Expose `--service-extension` on `notification send` and its compatibility alias. Python and Rust clients verify the companion capability before sending an NSE request, so an older companion cannot silently post an unprocessed banner.

Clients that cannot add a CLI flag can opt in with the reserved top-level `idb-service-extension` boolean in the payload. The client consumes it before delivery. Payloads without the marker preserve their original bytes, and ordinary notifications retain their existing behaviour.

Regenerate the command manifest, Rust grammar and compatibility fixtures for the additive option.

Reviewed By: mark-cmd-alt

Differential Revision: D129940808

fbshipit-source-id: bf140c2b526af10556f6c2668212c84763eb7742

Expose opt-in notification service extension delivery over gRPC

Summary:
Add an additive `process_service_extension` flag to `SendNotificationRequest` and advertise `supports_notification_service_extension` in the companion handshake. An absent flag preserves ordinary notification delivery.

The companion invokes the simulator's NSE-aware delivery path only when requested, and runs the operation under RPC cancellation. Existing clients retain the old behaviour; newer clients must check the capability before requesting extension processing. Default values are supplied in Rust protobuf consumers so the additive wire change leaves them buildable.

Differential Revision: D129940807

fbshipit-source-id: 448062ea6488bcfa7bc32f625b727ff863a1ed20

Route simulator notifications through service extensions on request

Summary:
Expose an opt-in service-extension path on `simulator.notification.sendPush`. An ordinary send remains unchanged; a requested NSE send invokes the separate SimulatorFrameworkBridge guest operation and requires a delivered or suppressed outcome.

Reject unsupported simulator types and invalid bundle identifiers. Preserve guest errors rather than silently posting the unprocessed payload. No wire/RPC changes or SpringBoard shim are included here; the companion and client capability is stacked above this library API.

Differential Revision: D129940804

fbshipit-source-id: c409355405b34da8ca42d440f6c689497628ef61

Add local NSE processing to SimulatorFrameworkBridge

Summary:
Add a simulator guest operation that runs the installed notification service extension through Apple's extension host and delivers its returned content. No APNs token, injected shim or SpringBoard restart is required.

The guest validates the payload, reports delivery or suppression, and does not fall back to posting the original payload when extension processing fails. Timeout and insertion initiation have one atomic order; an in-flight insertion timeout reports an unknown outcome. Cleanup completes before returning, and cleanup errors cannot overwrite the observed insertion result.

The shared bridge protocol moves to version 7, with host transport and command-name plumbing in the same layer so it builds independently. Older hosts keep their existing guest/version sockets; mismatched guests fail explicitly. The simulator notification API and companion RPC are separate child diffs.

commits.message:
fix(optix): LLVM 23 vs OptiX fixes (#2202)

* fix(optix): use the NVPTX target DataLayout for all modules

LLVM 23 rejects PTX generation when the shader group module has OSL's
hard-coded DataLayout instead of the NVPTX target machine's layout.
OSL also replaced the bitcode inputs' layout before linking.

Set the destination triple before obtaining the target layout, and
apply that layout to the shader group, shadeops, and renderer modules
before linking. Use it for empty modules and all supported LLVM
versions so the linked modules agree with the code generation target.

Representative shader groups produced byte-identical PTX with the old
and new layouts on LLVM 15, 20, and 22.

* fix(optix): preserve shadeop call arguments with LLVM 23

LLVM 23's dead argument elimination can replace shadeop call
arguments with poison when linked renderer bitcode makes them appear
unused. OSL later discards non-inlined shadeop bodies and links against
separately compiled PTX that still expects those arguments.

Give defined library functions available_externally linkage on LLVM 23.
This permits inlining while preventing LLVM from treating their bitcode
bodies as final definitions when optimizing surviving calls. Keep
function declarations and earlier LLVM behavior unchanged.

Assisted-by: OpenAI Codex / GPT-6

Signed-off-by: Tim Grant <tgrant@nvidia.com>

fix(daemon): keep double quotes in Windows shell-node scripts (#4074)

A `path: shell` node on Windows ran its `args` as `cmd /C <script>` with
the script as an ordinary argument. `std` escapes every `"` in an argument
as `\"`, which `cmd.exe` does not understand, so `echo "a b"` printed
`\"a b\"` and `python -c "print('hi')"` failed with a syntax error.

Spawn it as `cmd /S /C "<script>"` with the script appended through
`CommandExt::raw_arg`. `/S` makes `cmd` strip exactly the outer quotes, so a
script that itself starts with a quote (a quoted program path) also works.
Unix still runs `sh -c <script>` unchanged.

`clonable_command::Command` only describes a command, so the raw argument is
applied where it becomes a `std::process::Command` (`to_std_command`, used by
`PreparedNode` on every spawn, restarts included). The command is recognized
by its `cmd /S /C <script>` form, which `shell_command` is the only producer
of; a test pins the two together.

Fixes #4073

Co-authored-by: Philipp Oppermann <dev@phil-opp.com>

A daemon disconnecting mid-spawn after a survivor reported ready left the

fix(coordinator): finalize a dataflow left Recovering by a resent finish report (#3635)

* fix(coordinator): finalize a dataflow left Recovering by a resent finish report

that died. When the coordinator has already processed the disconnect, the
orphan reclaim has taken the dataflow out of `running_dataflows` and left
the store record `Recovering`, so the resend lands in the `Entry::Vacant`
arm of `handle_dataflow_event` and is dropped. The recovery sweep then
rewrites the record as a terminal `Failed` and the per-node results are
lost.

Settle the record from the resent report instead. The report only covers
the daemon that sent it, so the record is finalized only once the reported
node results cover every node the record assigns via `node_to_daemon`: a
dataflow another daemon is still running stays `Recovering` for that
daemon's status report to re-establish, rather than being finalized and
having its nodes stopped as orphans. A duplicate report cannot settle it
twice, because the first one moves the record out of `Recovering`.

Both finalize paths now share the status derivation in
`dataflow_store_status`.

Fixes #3631

* fix(coordinator): cover dynamic nodes and keep partial resent reports parked

The coverage check used the record's `node_to_daemon`, which after an
earlier recovery holds only the reconnecting daemon's nodes, and which
lists `path: dynamic` nodes that a daemon never reports a result for.
Derive the expected nodes from the persisted descriptor instead, the same
resolution `reestablish_running_dataflow` does, skipping dynamic nodes.

Park a report that does not cover the whole record in a separate map
rather than in `dataflow_results`: readers there treat any entry as a
finished dataflow, so a partial one made `dora list` show Finished,
`stop` reply success without stopping anything, and `clean` delete a
record that was still `Recovering`. Move the parked reports into
`dataflow_results` once they cover the record, or when another daemon
re-establishes the dataflow as running, and drop them when the recovery
timeout fails the dataflow terminally.

Archive the settled dataflow like the normal finish path, so its name
survives and name-based `logs` / `stop` still resolve it.

* fix(coordinator): only skip a dynamic node once its daemon has reported

The coverage check skipped every `path: dynamic` node, so a resent finish
report settled a dataflow while a daemon hosting only dynamic nodes was
still running it. Such a daemon never finishes on its own: `should_finish`
is only evaluated when a node stops, and its dynamic node is still running.
The settled record then made the daemon's next status report look like an
orphan, and it was stopped.

A dynamic node counts as covered only once the daemon it belongs to has
reported. The record's `node_to_daemon` holds the id from before the
reclaim and a reconnecting daemon registers under a fresh `DaemonId`, so
the two are matched by machine id, which survives the reconnect.

* test(coordinator): build coordinator_with_store on test_coordinator; add changelog entry

main's #3799 added a required Coordinator field the hand-written literal
lacked, so the test target no longer built after merging main.

fix(daemon): keep a given-up backpressure receiver marked until it has drained (#3634)

fix(daemon): keep a given-up receiver marked until it has drained

`note_drained` cleared the receiver's `gave_up` mark as soon as its channel
had `CONTROL_EVENT_HEADROOM` (50) slots free. Data never takes those last 50
slots: `offer_event`, `send_with_timestamp` and `deliver_when_room` all
require them. So a receiver that ran into the stall limit was given up on
with 49 free, and the first take already brought it to 50. The mark went away
on that one take, and the producer's next backpressure send was deferred and
held for another full `BACKPRESSURE_STALL_LIMIT`. #3610 gave up once per
receiver; this made it once per message again.

Require the channel to be more empty than full (`GAVE_UP_RECOVERY_ROOM`)
before holding producers for the receiver again. Make the test start from the
state real traffic leaves the channel in rather than a full one, and check
both that the mark survives a single take and that a recovered receiver takes
deliveries again. `docs/yaml-spec.md` described recovery as "until the
receiver takes an event again", the same too-eager rule, so it says half empty
now.

Fixes #3630

* fix(tensor-pool): copy peer GPU writes into receiver-owned pools

* test(tensor-pool): verify receiver allocation and compare full consumption

* docs(tensor-pool): keep placement docs and archive review benchmark

* test(tensor-pool): run its interpreter tests in contract-tests only

dora-tensor-pool-python is excluded from every bulk cargo test --all job:
its tests start an embedded interpreter (Python::initialize) and spawn a
python3 -m unittest subprocess, which hard-fail on a runner without an
interpreter (windows-latest is most at risk, where python3 may not be on
PATH). Add it to the exclusion lists in ci.yml and nightly.yml, and to the
single interpreter-equipped runner, make qa-test-python in contract-tests,
keeping the three lists in sync as the repo policy asks.

Also harden the embedded-source regex in test_cuda_helpers.py to tolerate
any raw-string delimiter arity and fail loudly if the source is restructured.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(tensor-pool): centralize device-index parsing and harden device restore

Registration, transit and copy paths parsed the CUDA device index with
inconsistent one- and two-stage strip_prefix chains. Centralize them in
parse_cuda_device_index (strict cuda:N requirement, fallback 0 matching the
legacy registration behaviour) and pin the contract with a unit test.

_query_cuda_device returns -1 rather than raising when the runtime is
uninitialized, so the old unwrap_or(0) never caught it and a -1 flowed into
_set_cuda_device(-1), a no-op that silently left the caller on the receiver's
device. Add query_cuda_device_or_default to clamp (-1 but also any negative)
to 0 - CUDA's default selection - and use it in both the GPU- and CPU-source
branches. Rewrite the stale comment that claimed the same-device branch still
saved/restored the caller explicitly.

Also document the one-time receiver-GPU CUDA context cost the writer pays,
which the review called out as inherent to the receiver-owned-pool design.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(tensor-pool): reject receiver devices the writer cannot select

The receiver's `device="cuda:N"` is parsed and applied by the writer
process, so it names a physical GPU only when every node exposes the same
GPUs in the same order. `_set_cuda_device` ignores cudaSetDevice's return
code, so an index outside the writer's CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES silently left
the pool on whichever device was current while registration succeeded.

Verify the selection by reading the device back after setting it, and fail
registration with the cause instead of dropping the error behind `.ok()`.
Document the shared-numbering requirement in the README placement
contract; the same GPUs in a different order cannot be detected from an
ordinal, so comparing physical identity is recorded as a follow-up.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(tensor-pool): validate the receiver device before classifying the path

An unselectable receiver ordinal never reaches `allocate_receiver_gpu_pool`:
the peer probe fails on an invalid ordinal, so a GPU source classifies as
HostStagingTransit and the CPU-source branch runs its own DMA path. Both
set the device through `_set_cuda_device`, which ignores cudaSetDevice's
error, allocate on the sender's device and publish the requested (wrong)
index.

Validate the ordinal once, before `classify_transport`, with a set/read-back
helper, so same-device, P2P, transit and CPU-source registration all fail
before any allocation. The per-function check added in 32c35cf could not be
reached for the case it was written for, so it is removed rather than
duplicated; its test now covers the read-back helper and relies on the
call site being upstream of classification.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(tensor-pool): correct what receiver placement actually changes

The placement section claimed the writer gains a CUDA context on the
receiver GPU and framed the device-ordinal rule as new. Both were already
true on the existing paths: `_ensure_p2p_pair` selects both GPUs of the
pair and host-staging/CPU-source registration allocate on the receiver, and
those paths already resolve the receiver's ordinal in the writer's
`CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`.

What is new besides placement: an unselectable receiver ordinal now fails
registration on every local CUDA-receiver path, where host-staging and
CPU-source used to ignore it and leave the pool on the writer's current
device. Say so in the README and the PR description.

docs: correct stale daemon/node transport documentation (#4048)

* docs: correct stale daemon/node transport documentation

The architecture docs still described a shared-memory control channel
between daemon and node (ShmemChannel, raw_sync, 4 KiB regions, drop
tokens, Unix sockets, LocalCommunicationConfig). None of that exists in
the source: DaemonCommunication has only Tcp and Interactive, and
DataMessage has a single Vec variant. Zero-copy transfer is Zenoh shared
memory between nodes, with a TCP daemon path as the fallback.

- Daemon to node: TCP only, one loopback listener per node, plus the
  dynamic-node NodeConfig listener; complete request, reply and event
  lists taken from DaemonRequest, DaemonReply and NodeEvent.
- Node to node: describe the direct Zenoh path, the startup handshake,
  and when an output stays on the daemon path.
- Remove the ShmemChannel, synchronization-protocol, DropToken and
  region-size sections; describe the real Zenoh SHM lifecycle.
- Daemon-to-daemon topic is .../control/..., not .../output/....
- Apply the same fixes to the published guide copies, the cli.md
  internals section, AGENTS.md and the adora-project skill.

* docs: apply review feedback on the transport documentation

- Routing conditions: a consumer under another daemon that declares
  `input_timeout` also pins the output to the daemon path
  (`watches_liveness` in output_routing.rs). The handshake-timeout and
  no-session cases are decided by the node, not by the daemon's routing,
  so they are listed separately.
- MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES: the direct path has no 64 MiB cap of its own, but a
  payload that does not get an SHM buffer (for example one larger than the
  node's pool) takes the daemon path, where the limit applies.
- cli.md: small payloads on the direct path also go node to node over
  Zenoh, as a heap-buffered put.

Applied to both the docs/ and guide/ copies.

test(cli): hold the refused port with a connected socket so macOS refuses (#4070)

The 2026-11-05 nightly (#4026) still failed
`refused_connection_points_at_dora_up` on macOS after #4056, now with
`Operation timed out (os error 60)` after ~75 s. macOS drops a SYN to a

Merge pull request #4443 from metebalci/audio-out-zlp-rearm

audio: re-arm the OUT endpoint after a zero-length packet

audio: re-arm the OUT endpoint after a zero-length packet

Without a dedicated hardware FIFO (CFG_TUD_EDPT_DEDICATED_HWFIFO == 0,
for example DWC2 in DMA mode), audiod_rx_xfer_isr() copies each received
packet from the linear buffer into the OUT FIFO, and returns through
TU_VERIFY when tu_fifo_write_n() writes nothing. It writes nothing for a
zero-length packet, so the function returns before usbd_edpt_xfer()
re-arms the endpoint and before tud_audio_rx_done_isr() runs. The
endpoint then receives nothing until the host selects an alternate
setting again.

A zero-length packet is a Transfer Delimiter (USB Audio Data Formats
2.0, 2.1), which a host may send in place of any packet. Write to the
FIFO only when the packet has data, so that the re-arm and the callback
run for a zero-length packet too.

Add a unit test that sends a packet, a zero-length packet and another
packet to an isochronous OUT endpoint.

Preserve pending bulk UVC payloads across COMMIT (#4415)

- Keep a queued bulk payload and its endpoint claim across a re-COMMIT; release the frame after it drains.
- Add tud_video_frame_xfer_abort_cb() for frames ended by COMMIT, endpoint halt or a failed or refused transfer; its weak default forwards to tud_video_frame_xfer_complete_cb().
- Serialize frame ownership with a class mutex; a refused first payload returns false and leaves the buffer with the caller.
- Examples implement the abort callback and never refill a buffer the driver still owns.
- Unit tests for COMMIT, halt, refusal and callback paths.

Fix hardware-free tooling, CI and BSP follow-ups (#4406)

Update benchmarks for ty 0.0.99 (#4957)

## Summary

Rerun the benchmarks with [ty 0.0.99](https://github.com/astral-sh/ty/releases/tag/0.0.99): CLI wall time and peak RSS for all 18 projects, plus diagnostic fetching and incremental edits for all 17 LSP fixtures. The project revisions, dependencies, configuration, file scope, and concurrency settings are unchanged.

Against ty 0.0.96, the geometric-mean CLI runtime decreased by 1.8%. Home Assistant took 2.11 seconds, compared with 2.09 previously. LSP diagnostic fetching decreased by 1.7%; incremental edits increased by 3.1%. RSS was essentially unchanged overall. These aggregate changes may include run-to-run variation. Individual incremental results include pandas increasing from 43.8 to 52.7 ms and HTTPX from 7.5 to 8.9 ms.

The other checkers retain their November 4 CLI and November 3 LSP measurements. The existing NumPy/Zuban CLI timeout and three Zuban incremental-edit crashes are retained. This isolates the ty release update using the same [recorded harness](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/tree/504457130a2183e9f0c6f4e92ce1c43e970b70ca/scripts/ty_benchmark).

[Raw CLI and LSP measurements](https://github.com/astral-sh/ty/tree/0c120ac4a867fbdff8955ea9f6887d0d13775210/benchmark-results/2026-11-06-ty-0.0.99), including the prior ty measurements and input metadata, are preserved in the commit history. The final diff contains only the report and charts.

## Test Plan

- Verified the official release archive checksum and executable version/hash.
- Passed the frozen runner's 43 focused tests and strict type check with ty 0.0.99.
- Passed all 18 CLI root-scope checks and 34 LSP benchmark tests; verified that temporary edits were restored and input/dependency fingerprints were unchanged.
- Independently recomputed raw sample statistics and checked retained results, report values, and both rendered chart themes.
- Passed repository hooks on the changed files.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

[SortedCollections] Add differential fuzz tests for SortedDictionary and SortedSet

Run random sequences of operations on SortedDictionary and SortedSet and
compare them against a standard Dictionary/Set model after each step:
count, contents in sorted order (forward and backward), offset-based
indexing, lookups for every key in the domain, and value semantics of
earlier copies.

SortedDictionary operations include subscript assignment, the
`_modify` accessor (`take()`, optional chaining, inout), updateValue,
removeValue, modifyValue(forKey:default:), the default subscript,
remove(at:), removeFirst/removeLast(_:), popFirst/popLast, filter,
mapValues, and rebuilding from a sequence.

SortedSet operations include insert/update/remove with members that are
equal but distinguishable (checking that insert keeps and update
replaces the stored member), remove(at:), removeFirst/removeLast(_:),
the form* set algebra operations, and the element range subscripts.

In debug builds, nodes hold at most 4-5 keys, so even small key domains
produce multi-level trees. Building with COLLECTIONS_INTERNAL_CHECKS
also validates the B-tree after every mutation; with that, these tests
catch the bugs fixed in 93745231 (remove(at:) not rebalancing) and
3a80514a (empty root after removal through `_modify`).

[BasicContainers] Don't resolve the hole before shrinking in UniqueDictionary

Resolves the FIXME added in #836: when removing an entry through
`updateValue(forKey:with:)` triggers shrinking, there is no need to
restore the hash table's invariants first, since resizing rehashes every
item anyway.

Factor the part of `RigidDictionary._punchHole(at:)` that doesn't touch
the value slot into `_punchHole(withMovedValueAt:)`, and use it on the
shrink path of `UniqueDictionary._removeEntry(withMovedValueAt:)`, which
now mirrors `_removeValue(at:)`.

[BasicContainers] Add differential fuzz tests for the hashed containers

Run random sequences of operations on RigidSet, UniqueSet,
RigidDictionary and UniqueDictionary, and after each step compare them
against a standard Set/Dictionary model: count, contents (via index
iteration), positive and negative lookups, and `_checkInvariants()`.

The operations cover insert/update/remove, the closure form of
`updateValue(forKey:with:)`, `memoizedValue(forKey:_:)`, `reallocate`/
`reserveCapacity`, `removeAll` (with and without keeping capacity),
Rigid <-> Unique conversions via `init(consuming:)`, and `_consumeAll`.
Keys use a configurable number of distinct hash values, from no
collisions down to a single collision chain, and all elements are
lifetime-tracked to catch leaks and double destroys.

These tests found the bugs fixed in #835 and #836.

feat(cli): create-app --framework react (+ vue alias, fix JS config filename) (#1815)

Scaffolds a Vite + React app (TS or JS) with @formkit/react, FormKitProvider +
defaultConfig(formkitConfig()), the Regenesis Tailwind theme, an example form,
and optional Pro. `vue` is now an alias for `vite`. Vue JS projects now get

perf(react): lazy aggregate value clones (−16% mount, −33% @1500) (#1814)

bench: add react-flat/react-validated/react-rows scenarios and build the bench
in production mode (it was bundling Vue/React dev builds).

* test(react): cover group _value during a delayed commit

perf(vue,react): lazy state.empty for groups/lists (O(n²) → O(n)) (#1813)

* perf(vue,react): compute group/list state.empty lazily instead of on every commit

empty() walks every key of an object (for...in), and a group commits once per
child commit, so mounting n inputs did O(n²) key walks. state.empty is now
computed on read for aggregates (Vue computed; React cached getter invalidated
on commit). Inputs are unchanged. Refs #1792.

* perf(react): read state.empty from the committed context.value snapshot

commits.message:
Add back comment reflowing (revert #1327). (#1328)

* Prepare comment handling for comment reflowing

- Return Substring views from whitespace trimming helpers in Comment.swift to avoid intermediate allocations.
- Track 0-space leading indentation for comments at the start of a file and avoid merging end-of-line comments with subsequent standalone line comments.
- Account for pending indentation when emitting PrettyPrinter findings at the start of a line.

* Add comment reflowing for line and block comments

- Add ReflowCommentsConfiguration with regularComments and docComments behaviors (.never, .onlyLinesOverLength, .always).
- Reflow standalone line and block comments by parsing their body as Markdown and wrapping paragraphs while preserving inline spans, code blocks, and banner lines.

* Support Markdown lists, task lists, and blockquotes when reflowing comments

- Reflow ordered, unordered, and task lists while preserving bullet spelling, post-marker spacing, loose-list blank lines, and continuation alignment.
- Reflow blockquote blocks while preserving leading '>' prefixes across lines and blank separator lines.

* Support commentPragmas and built-in ignore directives when reflowing comments

- Always exclude swift-format-ignore and swift-format-ignore-file directives from comment reflowing.
- Add commentPragmas regex patterns to ReflowCommentsConfiguration to exclude matching single- or multi-line directives from reflowing.

* Ensure reflowing works as expected when comments are in or overlap with selected line ranges.

* Use binary search when matching commentPragmas line ranges

* Fix star-tab block comments and inline closing delimiter overflow

* Exclude trailing blank lines from indented code blocks when reflowing

* Fix container prefix stripping on verbatim blocks in lists and blockquotes

* Preserve Markdown link and attribute reference definitions when reflowing

* Preserve shortcut and collapsed reference links and fallback link titles

* Fix inline source slicing on indented and lazy continuation lines

* Preserve inline formatting and escapes after hard line breaks

* Avoid emitting raw newlines for multi-line link suffixes and inline HTML

* Handle updated swift-cmark source positions after hard line breaks

Newer versions of swift-cmark (swiftlang/swift-cmark@f1e8a5a2) increment subj->line and reset subj->column_offset in handle_backslash when consuming a newline after a trailing backslash hard line break, whereas older versions included via tagged swift-markdown releases do not. Compare the reported source line against currentSourceLine in InlineWordCollector so inline source slicing works with both swift-cmark versions.

* Restore testReflowCommentFindingsWithSelection removed by #1327

Restore the reflow comment selection linting test that was added in #1326 and removed when #1327 reverted #1324.

Signed-off-by: Tony Allevato <allevato@google.com>

commits.message: Read the completion settings through Config (#1769)

Release

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

ci: publish packages from GitHub Actions when a release tag is pushed (#1764)

* ci: publish packages from GitHub Actions when a release tag is pushed

Azure DevOps global PATs stop working on 1 December 2026, and the
Marketplace PAT that `vsce login` stores is one of them. Publishing moves
to a Release workflow that authenticates to every registry through OIDC
trusted publishing, so no token is stored anywhere.

- release.yml runs on vscode@*, cli@* and core@* tags, checks the tag
  against the package version, builds, then runs that package's release
  script.
- foam-vscode: vsce pinned to 4.1.0 for packaging and `publish --oidc`
  (4.1.0 is the first stable release with the fixed token exchange);
  ovsx pinned to 1.3.0 with no PAT, so it uses OIDC. Both pass
  --skip-duplicate so a re-run finishes whichever upload failed.
  vsce 4.1.0 packages the same 129 files as 3.6.0.
- foam-cli and foam-core get a repository field, which npm provenance
  checks against the repo.
- tag-release prints the exact tags to push: GitHub starts no workflow
  for a push of more than three tags.
- The root release and release-* scripts are gone; publishing no longer
  runs locally.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ci: publish only from the release environment

Registries trust a run by its workflow file name, not by its trigger, so
anyone with write access could publish by pushing a branch that runs an
edited release.yml; a tag ruleset doesn't stop that. The job now runs in
the `release` environment, which only release tags may deploy to, and
each trusted publisher names that environment. It has no reviewers, so
a tag push still publishes without approval.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ci: leave vscode tags out of the release trigger for now

The Marketplace trusted publisher for `foam` doesn't exist yet, so a run
on a vscode tag would fail at the Marketplace login. Until it does, a
vscode tag starts nothing, all of a release's tags can be pushed
together, and the docs show how to publish the extension with the
existing `vsce login`, which works until 1 December 2026. Adding
'vscode@*' back to the trigger re-enables it; the rest of the vscode
path stays in place.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Sheets: audit React, JavaScript and TypeScript (#2308)

> 💡 Check out the [PR review
guide](https://github.com/rstacruz/cheatsheets/pull/2308#issuecomment-6654681336).

### Three tiered sheets refreshed against November 2026 upstream.

## Accuracy and additions

- **React:** now covers 19.0–19.3. Added Activity, View Transitions,
`browser()`, `useOptimistic`, `useFormStatus`, ref cleanup, Fragment
refs, root error callbacks, metadata and resource hints. Corrected
removal wording and Compiler version.
- **JavaScript:** fixed locale-dependent `toLocaleString`, dynamic
default imports, `res.ok` range and promise placeholders. Added
`Promise.any`, ES2022–2026 built-ins and Temporal.
- **TypeScript:** restructured into H2/H3 and fixed invalid snippets.
Added TS 7 defaults, enums, assertions, predicates, decorators, `using`,
`satisfies`, compiler options and utility types. Basic types now splits
into Primitives and Special types tables.

## Links

All 96 external URLs return 200; 21 deep anchors and 15 internal sheet
links verified. New links use react.dev, MDN and typescriptlang.org.

## Live verification

Rendered locally in Chromium; [full evidence
comment](https://github.com/rstacruz/cheatsheets/pull/2308#issuecomment-6654659524).
`pnpm run ci` and the PR build pass.

sheet](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0b1d12d6-6aa5-4311-9545-ba387ae183ff)
| React 19.3 content renders |

sheet](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fade2714-93ab-45bc-a143-88431107526a)
| Modern built-ins and Temporal |

- `pnpm run ci` → exit 0: 160 unit tests, 22 Playwright tests, lint,
format, icons and build
- Link audit: 96 URLs, 21 anchors, 15 internal links
- Chromium capture of the built site: no console or page errors

</details>

Build: drop the Lightning CSS transformer (#2321)

### Warnings come from Lightning CSS, not Tailwind.

## Before / after

Loading any sheet in `pnpm dev`:

```js
// before: 25 warnings per page load
[vite:css][lightningcss] Unknown at rule: @reference
[vite:css][lightningcss] Unknown at rule: @apply
// after
(no output)
```

## Why

Vite hands raw CSS to Lightning CSS before `@tailwindcss/vite` resolves
`@apply` / `@reference`. Astro calls Vite's `preprocessCSS` for every
`<style>` block, so the warnings fired on each page load
([tailwindlabs/tailwindcss#14205](https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/issues/14205)).

The transformer was added to flatten nesting for Safari 16.4. Vite 8
minifies CSS with Lightning CSS, and `cssTarget` drives the same
lowering, so production output is unchanged.

Send assistant messages in Responses requests (#401)

* Send assistant messages in Responses requests

The OpenAI Responses and Open Responses builders dropped every assistant
message, so a later turn showed the model only the user's side.
Send each answer as an input item, and keep a tool round's text with its calls
so that replay sends each piece of text once, in order.

* Respect history edits when replaying assistant text

Replay used a response's metadata even after a caller edited the response,
so removed text could reach the server. Apply the metadata only to a response
that is unchanged since it was written; otherwise send its segments, and the
turn's tool rounds send only their calls.
A handoff also lost text that no tool round carried. Keep that text on the response.

* Respect history edits in Gemini and stopped structured replay

Gemini restored stored text parts and their signatures without checking the
response's current segments, so an edited answer still sent the original text.
Use stored parts only for text the segments still contain.
A stopped structured stream's JSON was both the response and the tool round's
text, so it could be sent twice or survive an edit. Treat it as the response's.

* Keep a stopped Gemini stream's text for other builders

A stopped string stream marked its response with the OpenAI metadata keys, so
Chat Completions, Responses, and Open Responses replayed an empty response and
dropped the round's text. Gemini's replay doesn't need the marker for a string
response, so leave it out. Add tests of several tool rounds in one turn.

* Keep a stopped structured stream's text only in its response

A stop returns the round's JSON as the response, but the tool round kept the
same text in its metadata. Rebuilding or removing the response discarded the
marker that replay used to clean it up, so the original text was still sent.
Don't keep the text on the round, and remove the marker and that cleanup.

fix(jats): keep tables published as an image (#5078)

* fix(jats): keep tables published as an image

A <table-wrap> that holds a <graphic> instead of a <table> was dropped
together with its label and caption, because the table content was empty
and _add_table returned before it added the caption. PMC ships many
tables this way, for example in Medicine (Wolters Kluwer) articles.

Add such a table as a picture with its label and caption, the same way as
a <fig>, so the image is also embedded when fetch_images is enabled.

Signed-off-by: Aditya Gupta <84338325+MaiAditya@users.noreply.github.com>

* test(jats): cover alternative and mixed renditions of image tables

Add a case with two <graphic> renditions in <alternatives>, which must
give one picture, and a case with both a <graphic> and a <table>, which
must stay one table and not also become a picture. Declare the xlink
namespace the same way in all cases.

Signed-off-by: Aditya Gupta <84338325+MaiAditya@users.noreply.github.com>

* test(jats): cover image tables without a caption and table-wraps without content

Signed-off-by: Aditya Gupta <84338325+MaiAditya@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(jats): keep tables published as an inline graphic

Handle the image case in the else branch of the table content selection,
so the original content check stays as it was. A <table-wrap> that holds
only an <inline-graphic>, directly or in <alternatives>, now also becomes
a picture with its label and caption, and its image is embedded when
fetch_images is enabled. Assert the position of the picture in the
Markdown and turn the test comments into docstrings.

Signed-off-by: Aditya Gupta <84338325+MaiAditya@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(jats): drop inline-graphic support for image tables

A direct <inline-graphic> child is not valid in <table-wrap> or <fig> in
JATS 1.3. Only <graphic> is. Remove the inline-graphic handling and its
tests, which also changes how <fig> images are loaded. Drop a check in
_add_tables that can no longer fail.

Signed-off-by: Cesar Berrospi Ramis <ceb@zurich.ibm.com>

* test(jats): move image table tests to the main JATS test file

Signed-off-by: Cesar Berrospi Ramis <ceb@zurich.ibm.com>

fix(asciidoc): fill a table row from the column count of the first line (#5010)

* fix(asciidoc): fill a table row from the column count of the first line

Asciidoctor takes the number of columns from the first line of a table
and fills each row with that many cells, so a row can be written over
several lines. Its basic table example writes the header on one line
and one cell per line after it. Each line became its own row, so the
two body rows of that table came out as four rows with an empty second
column.

Group the cells by that column count. A column span fills its columns
and a row span fills a column of the rows below it. A line that holds a
whole row stays one row, also when it is wider, as before.

Signed-off-by: Christopher Krah <48338417+chrikrah@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(asciidoc): count a duplicated cell once per copy when grouping rows

A "2*" factor writes a cell twice, so "2*|x |y" on the first line of a
table sets three columns in Asciidoctor. The row grouping counted it as
one cell, so the column count came out one short and every row written
over several lines after it was split in the wrong place.

Keep the factor on the cell and expand it when grouping rows, so a line
that continues the cell's text applies to every copy, as in Asciidoctor.
A stacked "2*3+" is not AsciiDoc and still reads as before.

Signed-off-by: Christopher Krah <48338417+chrikrah@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(asciidoc): place spanned table cells at their grid positions

The table grid gave every cell a span of 1 and the column index of its

fix(reading-order): skip a horizontal dilation that overlaps another element (#5131)

* fix(reading-order): skip a horizontal dilation that overlaps another element

`_do_horizontal_dilation` widens an element to the width of the element
above or below it when the two share a one-to-one vertical edge. When
the widened box overlaps another element, the element must keep its
original box. The loop wrote the widened box into the dilated copy
before the overlap check, so the check could not stop the dilation:
every widened box was kept, also when it covered part of another column.

Check the widened box first, and write it into the dilated copy only
when it overlaps no other element.

On a page with a centred title above two columns, where the right
column starts above the first paragraph of the left column, the first
right block was widened to the title. It then overlapped the left
paragraph, became a parent of the next left paragraph, and was read
between the two left paragraphs.

Signed-off-by: Zelong Wang <zew013@ucsd.edu>

* test(reading-order): add a wide caption below a column to the dilation tests

The left column ends above a caption that is wider than the column and
reaches into the right column. Widened to the caption, the last left
block overlaps the right column. If the dilation keeps that box, the
first right block becomes its parent and is read between the two left
blocks.

* fix: keep pictures whose mode cannot be written as PNG

ImageRef.from_pil() serializes to PNG, so images in CMYK, LAB or F mode
raise OSError: cannot write mode <mode> as PNG.

OSError so that a single unreadable image can never fail a conversion.

minor: Add Chat Completions ingress and native Gemini egress (#2285) ## Why FCC lacks a Chat Completions endpoint for clients. Gemini currently uses Google's Chat compatibility API, which mixes thought-tag text into content instead of exposing native thought Parts consistently. ## How Add `/v1/chat/completions` with streaming and JSON replies, and switch the Gemini provider to native GenerateContent and paginated model discovery. Connect the four client protocols to all four upstream protocols, covering sixteen combinations. Direct Chat preserves native choices and extensions, while translated paths reject unsupported controls explicitly. Preserve Chat refusal and reasoning history, accept nullable native deltas, and retain non-strict function defaults when translating to Responses. Translate Gemini thought Parts directly and preserve signed Parts, tool arguments, and provenance through subsequent turns. Save declared tool defaults with replay records so harness normalization and resumed conversations retain Google's original signed content. Integrate both new paths with the existing routing, admission, retries, history negotiation, stream cleanup, and continuation owners. Use model-appropriate Gemini thinking controls, preserve explicitly typed custom tools, object-valued tool results, and fragmented native tool calls, and prevent continuation of truncated structured output. Retain the shared classifier reasoning preparation and correction behavior, using provider defaults where native models cannot disable thinking. Responses ingress remains streaming-only. Native-only features without an equivalent translation are rejected, including strict function-tool guarantees on Gemini. Saved Google Chat compatibility signatures require a fresh conversation when switching to native Gemini.

Confidence Score: 5/5

The PR appears safe to merge; no new actionable issues remain.

Summary

commits.message:
pkg/importer: pass attributes as KeyValue pairs, not alternating strings

Object.SetAttrs and friends, and the OAuth and importers' API request
helpers, took a "keyval ...string" of alternating keys and values. An
odd count was only caught at run time, by a panic or an error, and
code that built such lists had to step through them two at a time.

Add KeyValue, a key and its value, and KV to make one, and take
...KeyValue in their place:

	o.SetAttrs(importer.KV(nodeattr.Title, title), importer.KV(nodeattr.URL, u))

KV keeps call sites short without the unkeyed fields of
importer.KeyValue{k, v}, which vet's composites check flags in other
packages.

This also fixes bluesky's checks for whether a record's attributes
already had a camliContent or title, which searched the flat list's
values as well as its keys.

pkg/importer/twitter: import X archives

The API serves only an account's most recent 3200 tweets, and charges
for each, so most of an account's tweets, its likes and its follows can
come only from the archive X makes on request. The importer could
import only archives of 2013 to about 2018, whose ZIP's file reference
had to be set on the account by hand, and fetched their media by URL.

Import archives as an archive importer: uploaded on the importer's
page, or from a file source, into the account of their account ID.
Import from the archive:
  - its tweets, with their media, stored from the archive, including
    the videos and GIFs the API gives only preview images of; for the
    tweets the API imported, add only the media they lack;
  - its likes, dated by when the tweets they're of were posted, as
    their IDs say, as the archive has no dates of them;
  - the account's profile, with its avatar and header images;
  - its follows, and, as files on the account, its follows' and
    followers' lists, of their IDs only, with the followers' count.
Older archives, of tweets by month, import as before.

Import an archive's items a batch at a time, making their nodes with
one claim on their parent, as one each serializes on it, and storing
their media many at once, read from the archive in its order: on a
development server, its tweets import about three times as fast.

Skip the images of tweets' links, on imgur and twitpic, that can't be
fetched, as twitpic is gone and imgur limits how many are, rather than
failing the run.

pkg/importer: accept X archives' ZIP quirks

X's archives of accounts failed the archive importer's ZIP checks
twice. Between the directory and its end record, they have ZIP64 end
records, though the end record has no ZIP64 values, which zip.NewReader
reads past, at the directory's offset. And they end the names of
directories with two slashes.

Allow ZIP64 end records between the directory and an end record of no
ZIP64 values only if they repeat its values exactly and a directory
header starts at its offset, as zip.NewReader then reads it there. And
trim all the trailing slashes of directories' names before checking
them, as of files' names nothing changes.

pkg/importer: let API importers take archives too

The archive import path assumed archive-only importers: once an account
had imported an archive, every later start of it, by its page, its
schedule or a resume, imported the archive again rather than running
the importer's API; archives matched accounts only by username or
email, which an API importer's accounts may not have the same, and
overwrote the identity the API gave them.

Import an archive again without being asked to only for an archive-only
importer, or to finish one that was interrupted or paused. Add
ArchiveIdentity.UserID, the provider's own ID of the owner, which
matches the account of that "userID" first, and keeps an archive from
matching another ID's account by name. For an importer that isn't
archive-only, only fill in the identity attributes its account lacks.

pkg/importer/twitter: import tweets and likes through the API v2

The Twitter importer's API runs failed: X serves the timeline and likes
only through its API v2 now ("You currently have access to a subset of
X API V2 endpoints and limited v1.1 endpoints"), and charges for each
post it returns.

Import the account's tweets through GET /2/users/:id/tweets, and, if
enabled, its likes through /2/users/:id/liked_tweets, a page of 100 at
a time, with their media by their keys, and long tweets' whole text.
An incremental run asks only for the tweets since the newest imported,
so it reads, and is charged for, only new ones. Each run logs how many
tweets the API returned.

Runs never became incremental until the server restarted, as they set
the account's completed version on a node reloaded to read attributes
set from outside the importer, not the one later runs read. Set it on
that one.

Remove the long poll, of the user stream that's long gone.
pkg/importer: say why OAuth API requests fail, from their bodies

pkg/importer: claim many objects' attributes together

Importers make a claim of each item's attributes, and, for a new item,
a permanode and a claim of its parent's camliPath: two or three schema
blobs an item, each to sign, store, verify and index, which bounds bulk
imports once their syncs are cheap.

A multi claim's children each name their permanode, so one claim can
change many objects. Add ClaimBatch, which sets many objects'
attributes with as few multi claims as hold them, keeping each
object's changes in one claim, so atomic, as Object.SetAttrs does, and
its cached attributes unchanged until that's stored; Host.NewObjects,
which stores many new permanodes together; and
Object.ChildPathObjects, which gets or makes many children together,
setting the made ones' camliPath attributes with one claim. An item of
a batch is then about one blob, its permanode, rather than three.
pkg/importer: upload importers' schema blobs in batches

Helpers owns one AppLifecycle stream per platform: the current state,

fix(security): redact secrets in the logs of every module, not only Auth (#1751)

* fix(security): redact secrets in the logs of every module, not only Auth

Move LogRedaction and RedactingLogHandler from Auth to Helpers. Every
client (Auth, AuthAdmin, Functions, PostgREST, Storage, Realtime) and
LoggerInterceptor now wraps its logger at init; the wrap is idempotent.

- LoggerInterceptor logs the request URL without its query and fragment,
  and skips body buffering when trace logging is off.
- JSON body redaction shares the key set with the log redactor and adds
  signedURL, url, and action_link.
- The redactor also masks sb_secret_ keys and apikey values.

  code, coding errors keep case and coding path, never the value.

  encode, not its payload.

Fixes SDK-2876

* fix(security): summarize URLError on Linux and add redaction keys to the spell dictionary

* fix(security): read URLError code through errorCode in the log summary

docs: add cross-module consistency rules from the v3 audit (#1750)

* docs: add cross-module consistency rules from the v3 audit

Write one rule per decision from the SDK-2588 audit into CODE_STYLE.md,
ARCHITECTURE.md, and CONTRIBUTING.md: naming, models, client
configuration, streams, the error model, the HTTP chain, logging,
concurrency, access control, and compliance declarations.

Fixes SDK-2588

* docs: allow opaque String IDs and mark log redaction as a target

fix(typegen): emit nonisolated Columns extensions for computed fields and relationships (#1748)

On Swift 6.2 and 6.3, an app module built with `.defaultIsolation(MainActor.self)`
made the generated `extension X.Columns` properties main-actor isolated. The
nonisolated `@SelectionOf` expansion and the typed query API read them, so a
selection with `@Relationship(computed:)` failed to compile.

Typegen now writes `nonisolated extension X.Columns`, matching what the
`@Relationship(computed:)` docs tell users to write by hand.
`SupabaseTypegenPostgrestTypegenOutputTests` and
`SupabaseTypegenHostileOutputTests` now build with default MainActor isolation
and `InferIsolatedConformances`, and the first one adds a selection with
foreign-key and computed embeds plus a generated function call.

fix(postgrest): make @Table, @SelectionOf, and @Function expansions compile under default MainActor isolation (#1747)

* fix(postgrest): make @Table, @SelectionOf, and @Function expansions compile under default MainActor isolation

On Swift 6.2 and 6.3, a module built with `.defaultIsolation(MainActor.self)`
made the macro-generated extension, its conformances, and its nested types
main-actor isolated. A main-actor conformance cannot satisfy the `Sendable`
requirements of the typed API, so annotated types did not compile.

The macros now emit `nonisolated extension` through a shared
`conformanceExtension` helper, and mark the nested `Columns`, `Draft`,
`Embeds`, and `CodingKeys` types `nonisolated`. `DefaultIsolationTests` now
uses the real macros instead of hand-written expansions.

Fixes SDK-2858

* ci: leave the macro plugin out of the coverage export

DefaultIsolationTests now depends on PostgrestMacros, which brings the
PostgrestMacrosPlugin sources into the iOS coverage export at 0%. The plugin
runs inside the compiler, so no test bundle can cover it.

feat(realtime): accept presence streams opened after subscribe when presence is on (#1746)

`presenceChanges()` and `presenceStates()` no longer reject every stream
opened after `subscribe()`. Following the presence spec, the core accepts
the stream when presence is on for the subscription: its joins ask for
presence, or a `track` succeeded on the live join. The stream gets events
from the next message on, and `presenceStates()` yields the current state
first. A stream opened while presence is off is still rejected.

Add `RealtimeChannelConfiguration.Presence.enabled`, which turns presence
on for the join with no stream open, as supabase-js's
`config.presence.enabled` does.

Every join of a subscription now carries the presence flag computed at
`subscribe()`, as the spec and supabase-js do. Opening or closing a
presence stream no longer changes the flag of later rejoins.

Fixes SDK-2591

Reuse parts moved between local disks in --diff-from-remote, fix #1663

A part moved by TTL TO VOLUME or MOVE PARTITION keeps its name and
hash_of_all_files, but create/upload looked it up only on the same disk
of the diff backup, so every moved part was uploaded again.

Look the part up on all disks of the diff backup, but reuse it only when
both disks are plain local disks: object disks keep object metadata and
encrypted disks keep ciphertext in the backup while hash_of_all_files is
the same. 22.9+ reports type=Local for encrypted disks, so read
system.disks.is_encrypted. The same plain-local filter now guards the
cross-disk lookup in download, and restore of a local increment does not
hardlink a required part from another disk.

Add BME680 IAQ (air quality index) to BMP sensor driver (#25175)

* Add BME680 IAQ (air quality index) to BMP sensor driver

The BME680 gas sensor reports only an ohmic resistance, not a CO2
concentration, so derive an indoor air quality index from the gas
resistance instead. The scale follows the Bosch BSEC convention of 0
(clean air) to 500 (heavily polluted air) documented in the BME680
datasheet, Sec. 4.2 and Table 4
(https://www.bosch-sensortec.com/media/boschsensortec/downloads/datasheets/bst-bme680-ds001.pdf).

The arithmetic is an adaptation of the basic open-source IAQ calculator
in thstielow/raspi-bme680-iaq (https://github.com/thstielow/raspi-bme680-iaq),
which circumvents the closed-source BSEC library by squaring the ratio
between the gas resistance and a baseline ceiling value for a steeper
slope at high air quality and rescaling the result to a 0-500 index. The
percentage-based gas quality and the baseline/drift handling are
inspired by the example in the Pimoroni bme680-python library
(https://github.com/pimoroni/bme680-python). In place of the linear
rescale IAQ = (1 - AQ/100) * 500 used there, this driver maps the
squared excess ratio through a saturating Hill function u = (k * x)^2
with IAQ = 500 * u / (1 + u), where x = R_baseline / R_gas - 1 and
resistance below the baseline is clamped to zero. A tVOC equivalent in
ppb is derived from the same excess ratio with a saturating
(Michaelis-Menten style) curve.

The metal-oxide resistance also depends on ambient humidity, so the
reading is normalized to a dry-air equivalent before it enters the
baseline and the ratio. As in the thstielow reference, absolute humidity
is derived from temperature and relative humidity with the Magnus
equation and the ideal gas law, and the resistance is scaled by
exp(ph_slope * hum_abs), with ph_slope defaulting to 0.03 per g/m3. This
keeps the index stable across humidity changes instead of drifting with
them.

The baseline is the clean-air ceiling of that compensated resistance. It
is learned as a running mean during an initial burn-in of 2880
measurements, about 96 minutes at the 2 second reading interval, and
then adapted in two directions: towards cleaner readings with an
exponential moving average of 0.005, a time constant of about 7 minutes,
and back down with a time constant of about 2.3 days to follow the slow
aging of the metal-oxide layer. Only the clean-air direction moves the
ceiling quickly, so a pollution event does not drag the reference along
with it and flatten the index.

Readings outside 1..5000 kOhm are dropped from the index, which rejects
individual sensor glitches while leaving clean, dry air well inside the
range, and a stored baseline is validated against the wider range that
the humidity compensation can produce.

MQTT and the JSON API report the raw 0-500 index and the tVOC value in
ppb. The WebUI shows the same information as a 0-100 quality percentage
where 100 is clean air, plus the tVOC in ppb, both with localized labels
from the language files. While the burn-in runs, the WebUI reports the
calibration progress instead, and no index is published until it is
based on a real baseline.

The console command BmpIaq reports, sets and resets the gas baseline:

  BmpIaq              prints the current baseline as the uncompensated
                      resistance in kOhm, directly comparable with the
                      Gas reading
  BmpIaq <1..5000>    stores the value as the calibrated clean-air
                      baseline in kOhm, normalized to dry air for the
                      ratio; values outside 1..5000 kOhm are rejected
  BmpIaq Reset        discards the learned baseline and restarts the
                      burn-in

The baseline is written to flash as soon as the burn-in completes and
again on a graceful restart or OTA update through the save-before-restart
hook. It is kept in a free area of the reserved TSettings block on
every CPU target, so the calibration survives reboots and
updates without frequent flash writes.

* bme680_iaq_baseline[4] is now a uint16_t array
holding one baseline per sensor, replacing the
single float.

* BmpIaq -> report every BME680 baseline

* BmpIaq <n>,<value> -> set baseline of sensor n
* BmpIaq Reset -> reset all sensors
* BmpIaq <n>,Reset -> reset sensor n

* Print unit "percent" after value for air quality.

fix(yy): 拦截纯音频/纯视频流，防止 B 站投稿报 21588 错误 (#1843)

* fix(yy): 拦截纯音频/纯视频流，防止 B 站投稿报 21588 错误

### 问题背景
YY 平台在直播断流重连、或者特定的网络环境下，CDN API 会返回带有 `audio-only=1` 或 `video-only=1` 参数的推流地址。
目前 biliup 会照常下载这些流，导致生成只有音频轨或只有视频轨的残缺 FLV 文件。

当 biliup 尝试将这种残缺文件投稿到 B 站时，B 站的 `bvc_check` 前置校验会直接拒绝，报错：
`code 21588: 该文件缺少视频轨，请检查文件或尝试调整文件格式后再上传。`

这不仅会导致当前分段上传失败，如果是多 P 投稿，还会导致整个稿件被 B 站打回，严重影响录制和投稿体验。

### 解决方案
在 `crates/biliup/src/downloader/live/platforms/yy.rs` 的 `check_stream` 函数中，在解析出最终的 `raw_stream_url` 之后，增加一层防御性校验：
如果 URL 中明确包含 `audio-only=1` 或 `video-only=1`，则主动阻断下载，打印警告日志，并直接返回 `LiveStatus::Offline`。

### 测试情况
- 已在本地环境下测试通过。
- 遇到 YY 断流返回纯音频流时，控制台会打印 Warn 日志，并视为未开播。不再生成垃圾文件，WebUI 也不会再报错。
- 代码通过了本地 `cargo build --release` 编译。

* ci: 不再缓存 workspace target/，保证测试运行可复现

## 问题

`Swatinem/rust-cache` 会在不同运行之间恢复整个 workspace 的 `target/` 目录。它的默认缓存 key 由 `Cargo.lock`、rustc 版本、OS/arch 和环境变量推导而来，**不包含源码 hash**。因此，一个 PR 运行可能恢复由旧 commit 产生的 `target/` 树，而 cargo 的 fingerprint 判断可能认为 `biliup-cli`（或其测试二进制）不需要重新编译。

`biliup-cli` 通过 `rust-embed` 嵌入 `out/`，而它的 `auto_clip` 测试还会在 `target/` 下写入临时文件。这两点在 `target/` 被陈旧复用时都很脆弱。实际表现是跨场景的偶发失败，例如：

* ci: 收窄 rust-cache 范围并打印 FFmpeg 版本，定位 auto_clip 测试 flaky

背景
auto_clip 相关测试在 CI 上间歇性失败，表现为两类现象：

切片边界异常：

an_oversized_upload_is_split_in_halves 输出 [120023, 120023, 120023, 120023, 120023]

transcribes_mixed_segments_and_skips_silence 输出 送转写 200121 ms（整段未切）

连锁 413：切片失效后请求体变大，撞上假 ASR 服务器（Axum）默认 2MB body limit，返回 HTTP 413 Failed to buffer the request body，导致 auto_clip::runner::tests::analyze::* 一串测试同时失败。

同一 commit 在不同 runner 上结果不同：有的 run 全绿，有的 run 挂 10 个测试。失败横跨多个不相关场景，说明问题不在业务逻辑，而在测试运行环境的不确定性。

本次改动
只改 .github/workflows/test.yml，做两件事。

1. 收窄 rust-cache 范围
在 Swatinem/rust-cache@v2 步骤加上：

with:
cache-targets: false
cache-bin: false
save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/master' }}

cache-targets: false：不再跨运行搬运 workspace 的 target/。rust-cache 默认的缓存 key 由 Cargo.lock、rustc 版本、OS/arch、环境变量推导，不包含源码 hash。PR 运行可能恢复 master 历史运行留下的 target/，其中包含旧的测试二进制和测试运行写下的临时产物。biliup-cli 又通过 rust-embed 嵌入 out/，陈旧 target/ 会让测试跑在与本次源码/前端产物脱节的二进制上。关掉 target 缓存后，每次运行都在干净的 target/ 上编译 workspace crate。

cache-bin: false：避免 ~/.cargo/bin 下的 shim 随 runner 镜像漂移。

save-if：只有 master 分支的 push 才写入缓存，PR 运行只读不写，避免多个 PR 互相覆盖同一个 key。

依赖缓存（~/.cargo/registry、~/.cargo/git）保留，大部分编译加速不受影响。实测缓存体积从约 916MB 降到约 157MB，降下来的正是 target/ 部分。

2. 打印 FFmpeg 版本
在 Install media test tools 之后新增一步：

name: Show FFmpeg version
run: |
ffmpeg -version
ffmpeg -hide_banner -encoders | head -n 20

Install media test tools 里仍是 apt-get install ffmpeg，不固定版本。新增这一步只是为了在日志中留下实际运行的 FFmpeg 版本和可用编码器，便于后续对比不同 run 的环境差异。切片边界异常高度依赖 FFmpeg 对音频时长的解析，不同 runner 镜像装到的 FFmpeg 版本可能不同，这是当前 flaky 的重点怀疑对象。

说明
本次改动不涉及业务代码，只调整 CI 配置。

打印 FFmpeg 版本用于定位问题，不解决问题。如果日志证实不同 run 的 FFmpeg 版本确实不同，后续需要在测试代码层面加固（用固定字节数据替代运行时生成的音频，或给假 ASR 服务器显式放宽 DefaultBodyLimit），可以另开 PR 处理。

由于 GitHub 对 pull_request 事件读取的是 base 分支的 workflow 文件，本 PR 自身的 CI 仍会用现有 test.yml 运行，可能仍出现 flaky。合并后，后续 PR 才会用上新配置。

验证
在包含此改动的 fork 上运行：

rust-cache 步骤日志显示缓存体积约 157MB（原约 916MB），Cache Paths 中不再包含 target/

Show FFmpeg version 步骤输出完整的版本和编码器信息

cargo test --locked --workspace 通过

* 钉住 runner 到 ubuntu-24.04，收窄 rust-cache 范围

背景
auto_clip 相关测试在 CI 上间歇性失败，表现为：

切片边界异常：an_oversized_upload_is_split_in_halves 输出 [120023, 120023, 120023, 120023, 120023]；transcribes_mixed_segments_and_skips_silence 输出 送转写 200121 ms（整段未切）

连锁 413：切片失效后请求体变大，撞上假 ASR 服务器（Axum）默认 2MB body limit，返回 HTTP 413 Failed to buffer the request body，导致 auto_clip::runner::tests::analyze::* 一串测试同时失败

同一 commit 在不同 run 上结果不同：有的全绿，有的挂 10 个测试。

已定位的根因
同一 commit 的两次运行，ffmpeg -version 输出不同：

结果	FFmpeg	libavcodec	对应镜像
失败	8.0.1-3ubuntu2	62.11.100	Ubuntu 25.10
通过	6.1.1-3ubuntu5	60.31.102	Ubuntu 24.04
两次 workflow 都写 ubuntu-latest，但 ubuntu-latest 是滚动标签，实际落到了 24.04 和 25.10 两个不同镜像上，apt 装到的 FFmpeg 跨了大版本。切片边界计算依赖 FFmpeg 对音频时长的解析，版本变化会让测试音频的时长/采样点偏移，进而触发切片异常和 413 连锁失败。

本次改动
只改 .github/workflows/test.yml，三处：

1. 钉住 runner 到 ubuntu-24.04
yaml
runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
两个 job 都从 ubuntu-latest 改为 ubuntu-24.04。该镜像的 apt 源提供 FFmpeg 6.1.1，是当前测试验证通过的版本。ubuntu-latest 的滚动切换是本次 flaky 的直接来源，钉住版本号即可消除。

2. 收窄 rust-cache 范围
yaml
- uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
  with:
    cache-targets: false
    cache-bin: false
    save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/master' }}
cache-targets: false：不再跨运行搬运 workspace 的 target/。rust-cache 默认的 key 由 Cargo.lock、rustc 版本、OS/arch、环境变量推导，不包含源码 hash。PR 运行可能恢复 master 历史运行留下的 target/，其中包含旧测试二进制和测试残留；biliup-cli 又通过 rust-embed 嵌入 out/，陈旧 target/ 会让测试跑在与本次源码/前端产物脱节的二进制上。关掉 target 缓存后，每次运行都在干净的 target/ 上编译。

cache-bin: false：避免 ~/.cargo/bin 下的 shim 随 runner 镜像漂移。

save-if：只有 master 的 push 才写入缓存，PR 只读不写，避免多个 PR 互相覆盖。

依赖缓存（~/.cargo/registry、~/.cargo/git）保留。实测缓存体积从约 916MB 降到约 157MB，降下来的正是 target/ 部分。

3. 新增 Show FFmpeg version
yaml
- name: Show FFmpeg version
  run: |
    ffmpeg -version
    ffmpeg -hide_banner -encoders | head -n 20
不固定 FFmpeg 版本，只把实际运行的版本和编码器写进日志，便于后续排查环境差异。

说明
本次改动不涉及业务代码。

钉住 ubuntu-24.04 能消除当前 flaky，但属于把环境固定下来，不是从测试代码层面根治。根治方向是让测试不再依赖 FFmpeg 版本：用固定字节数据替代运行时生成的音频，或给假 ASR 服务器显式放宽 DefaultBodyLimit。建议另开 PR 处理。

由于 GitHub 对 pull_request 事件读取 base 分支的 workflow 文件，本 PR 自身的 CI 仍会用现有 test.yml 运行，可能仍出现 flaky。合并后后续 PR 才会用上新配置。

验证
在包含此改动的 fork 上运行：

rust-cache 步骤缓存体积约 157MB（原约 916MB），Cache Paths 不再包含 target/

Show FFmpeg version 输出 ffmpeg version 6.1.1-3ubuntu5

cargo test --locked --workspace 通过，auto_clip 测试不再出现 413 连锁失败
