commits.message:
feat(edit): course-level undo timeline for manual and agent edits (#2159)

Adds one course-level undo/redo timeline to the workbench editor, covering hand edits and agent edits alike, with header buttons and keyboard shortcuts. Steps are diffs per scene, agent runs group into single steps, learner state in PBL v2 projects stays off the history, and steps that would restore reclaimed media expire after 45 minutes.

Known limitations (listed in the PR): concurrent agent writes and manual edits to the same course stay last-write-wins, and ASSET_COLLECTION_GRACE_MS below 45 minutes is unsupported.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(pbl-v3): show project outcomes in learning reports (#2205)

PBL v3 reports and share images now show what the learner built: completed milestone titles with authored goals instead of identical process-skill cards, each milestone's decision question and the learner's answer (rationale on demand), and a share card with optional course-authored result titles, workflow steps and wrapped concept labels. Cached reports are enriched on read; no migration or extra model request.

fix(pbl-v3): reduce oversized teaching tool payloads (#2204)

Keeps ordinary PBL v3 coding and review turns within the request budget: read_file returns at most 8 KiB per call for large protected files (with inclusive line ranges and a continuation offset) while full-file hashes are unchanged, and course reference documents are supplied once through the system prompt instead of being repeated in every read_next_skill result.

fix(pbl-v3): show the current milestone choice in preview (#2201)

Application previews and the assistant's product context now show only the choices submitted in the current milestone, instead of mixing in earlier milestones. Course packages can give a choice option an optional previewLabel for a contextual preview wording; the short label remains the drawer text and the fallback.

fix(pbl-v3): label the next milestone after recap (#2199)

After a recap that leads into another milestone, the PBL v3 task bar, ready hint and the button name given to the teaching agent now say "Enter next milestone" instead of a generic Continue; the final milestone and older views keep the generic action. Adds the enterMilestone key to all locales.

fix(pbl-v3): clarify quiz choices in the task drawer (#2193)

The PBL v3 quiz in the task drawer now shows numbered questions with aligned option cards, letter badges, a checkmark and a distinct focus indicator, while keeping native radio inputs for keyboard and assistive-technology support. Submission, disabled, pending and feedback behavior are unchanged.

fix(pbl-v3): preserve scroll following in Tests and Quiz (#2196)

Entering a composer-free step (Tests or Quiz) enlarges the transcript viewport and the browser clamps the scroll offset to the new bottom; the shared workbench scroll hook now ignores that clamp instead of treating it as an upward user scroll, so following continues. The hook also rebinds to the current viewport element so it survives Pro replay replacing the viewport.

feat(sandbox): let any admitted owner use sandboxes (#2191)

Removes the identity gate on sandboxes: once a deployment enables the sandbox section, any owner it admits (anonymous, shared-team, single-user or host-authenticated) can use them, and the sandbox:use role is gone. Owner isolation, admin-only settings, the caps and ACCESS_CODE are unchanged; docs warn that public anonymous deployments expose billable sandboxes up to the caps.

fix(ai): send generic thinking toggle for uncatalogued models (#2190)

Models with no catalog thinking capability (custom providers, self-hosted vLLM/sglang endpoints) now receive chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking when the thinking mode is set explicitly, so reasoning no longer leaks into content. Requests without an explicit thinking mode are unchanged.

feat(pbl-v3): support Java application previews (#2188)

Java PBL packages can now declare an application preview: the host compiles the declared Java sources with javac into a clean preview-only directory and launches the declared main class through the existing preview lifecycle. Packages declare pbl-v3-java-application@1 so older hosts reject them explicitly; sandbox templates need a JDK on PATH.

release: v1.4.1 (#2189)

Bump the root version and cut the 1.4.1 changelog section: background syncs no longer lose edits or learner progress, courses open quickly on slow connections, and PBL v3 releases deleted courses' sandboxes. Add the News item to both READMEs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(pbl-v3): reuse Pro workbench scroll following (#2178)

Long PBL v3 replies now keep following their tail with the Pro workbench's stick-to-bottom behaviour: scrolling up releases it and returning near the bottom, Latest or a new send resumes it. A viewport that shrinks no longer re-engages a released lock, and native scroll anchoring is kept.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(pbl-v3): recover teaching feedback and IDE read errors (#2173)

Recap turns can reuse feedback the learner already gave only when it covers the current goal, and failed teaching calls that later succeed for the same input and operation drop out of the default transcript. IDE read errors clear after a successful reread; the pacing rules of the teaching prompt are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(pbl-v3): reclaim sandboxes after course deletion (#2176)

## Summary

Deleting a course withdraws its packaged PBL project resources.
Background maintenance then fails while loading the study, before it can
reclaim the sandbox. Allow maintenance of an explicitly deleted course
to release its bound compute after the existing inactivity and
writer-cleanup gates, without resolving the withdrawn package.

This PR is AI-assisted (Codex). Independent subagents reviewed
lifecycle, ownership, durability, and verification behavior; confirmed
findings were fixed and reviewed again.

## Related Issues

Fixes #2172

## Changes

- Add a maintenance-only study loader for explicit course tombstones,
including deferred renewal and execution-failure reloads. Keep normal
project resolution for live courses and interactive access.
- Reuse owner/workspace checks, Agent/command/application/terminal
cleanup, release fences, and retries of the same environment identity.
- Skip package-dependent evaluation collection and final checkpointing
for deleted courses, preserving the previous checkpoint and teaching
state. Continue provider lease renewal while existing writers remain
protected by the inactivity window.
- Add PostgreSQL regressions for withdrawn/missing packages, active and
settled writers, admitted evaluation, short provider leases, uncertain
deletion, pending allocations, and owner/environment isolation. Document
the deleted-course lifecycle.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing
functionality to change)
- [x] Documentation update
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes)
- [ ] CI/CD or build changes

## Verification

### Steps to reproduce / test

1. Import a packaged PBL v3 course, prepare its sandbox, execute/read
real workspace files, and save a checkpoint.
2. Delete the course through the application, confirm its asset
references are withdrawn, and allow the configured inactivity window and
background scan to elapse.
3. Verify the provider resource is absent, the study state/revision and
previous checkpoint are unchanged, and course reads and preparation
return HTTP 404.
4. Check an undeleted course still archives before idle release and
restores matching file bytes into a new sandbox.
5. Run the real-PostgreSQL regressions, including a provider-expiry
clock that fails before the lease-ordering correction and passes
afterward.

### What you personally verified

Agent-executed verification:

- `pnpm check`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit`, and `pnpm
check:package-versions origin/main` pass. Lint reports 16 existing
warnings and no errors.
- Focused lifecycle/ownership/failure regressions: **19 passed**.
- Broader PBL/sandbox/persistence suites: **2,680 passed, 27 skipped, 3
failed**. The same three failures reproduce on unchanged `main`: two
Java-course cases on this host without a Java runtime, and a
pre-existing PBL v2 warning-format assertion. These are disclosed
baseline/environment limitations, not a claim that the entire suite
passes.
- Real-provider E2E used actual Alibaba Cloud sandboxes, the local
application's HTTP routes, an isolated PostgreSQL database, and a
separate local RustFS S3 server through the production AWS SDK
checkpoint adapter. No model calls or production deployment were
involved.
- The initial fix passed **22 real-provider assertions**, including a
before/after comparison on the same persisted resource and an undeleted
archive/restore control. The final candidate (`0f548012`) passed **12
additional real-provider assertions**, including post-deletion lease
extension before inactivity and eventual provider-confirmed deletion.
All four sandboxes across the two runs were verified absent; the
isolated databases, objects, buckets, and S3 containers were removed.
- Independent review found a premature provider-lease expiry before the
deleted-course inactivity deadline. The correction renews before the
early return; the new regression was observed failing before the
correction and passing afterward.
- Deleted courses intentionally do not receive a final checkpoint.
Already-admitted work is subject to the existing cleanup protocol; this
change does not promise immediate cancellation at deletion time. Cloud
object storage and billing accounting were not tested.

### Evidence

Redacted before/after results from the real-provider run:

| Scenario | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Unchanged `main` (`1b641161`) after real inactivity | Database and
provider both still report the deleted course's sandbox running. |
| Initial fix (`c5457f6d`) takes over the same database/resource |
Provider confirms the sandbox is absent before its lease could naturally
expire; checkpoint and teaching state are preserved. |
| Undeleted control on the initial fix | Final archive saved, idle
release succeeds, and a new real sandbox restores matching file hashes.
|
| Final candidate (`0f548012`), 2026-11-05 UTC | Course deleted at
08:12:49; provider expiry extended from 08:22:47 to 08:23:04 while still
before inactivity; provider absence and preserved state/checkpoint
confirmed by 08:14:04. Reads and preparation return 404. |

Remote CI status is reported by the checks on this PR.

- [ ] CI passes (`pnpm check && pnpm lint && npx tsc --noEmit`)
- [x] Manually tested locally
- [ ] Screenshots / recordings attached (if UI changes)

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the project's coding style
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my code
- [x] I have added/updated documentation as needed
- [x] My changes do not introduce new warnings

fix(workbench): open event streams at low priority so they stop blocking JS (#2185)

Event streams now run over a fetch-based EventSource at low priority, so on connections Chromium rates 3G or slower they no longer hold the JS chunks behind them: course load drops from about 56s to 10s and opening Edit from about 17s to under 1s. The replay watchdog now runs only while a replay can progress, and a held conversation no longer shows the previous one's transcript.

commits.message: docs: prepare 2.2.34 release

fix(usage): show a newer usage API percent in a session left idle (#767)

* fix(usage): show a newer usage API percent in a session left idle

Claude Code sends the 5-hour and weekly percents with each of a session's
API responses, and the usage widgets show those over the usage API's. A
session left idle keeps the percents from its last response, so with
`refreshInterval` its line redraws with the same numbers while other
sessions or devices use up the limits.

Once the transcript's last response is more than three minutes old (the
usage cache's lifetime), the prefetch also asks the usage API for the windows
the line shows, through the shared cache and without surfacing errors. Its
percent wins when the API sent it after that response, for the same window
and no lower, or for the next window once the payload's has reset. The
forecast history dates the 5-hour percent by its source.

* fix: retain accepted usage observation timestamps

---------

Co-authored-by: Matthew Breedlove <sirmalloc@gmail.com>

feat(thinking-effort): optional brackets and per-level colors (#777)

* feat(thinking-effort): optional brackets and per-level colors

Thinking Effort gains two options, both off by default. (b)rackets wraps
the rendered value in (), [], {} or <>. (l)evel colors opens an editor that
colors the value by effort level, with the brackets either matching the
level or keeping the widget color. With level colors on, the widget paints
only the level, and the renderer colors the rest as it colors any widget,
through a new optional Widget.colorsOnlyItsRuns().

At the 256 Color level, hex colors now render as the nearest 256-palette
color instead of a 24-bit code those terminals can't draw.

* test(tui): wait for the Thinking Effort row in the color menu's own-colors test

The line and color editor tests no longer sleep a fixed 25ms after each
render and key. They wait for the key's visible effect, and the sleep
helper flushInk is gone. The color menu test that checks the note for a
widget that sets some of its own colors still called flushInk after the
first render, so it no longer compiled. It now waits until the frame
shows the Thinking Effort row, then reads that frame as before.

feat: add an Extra Usage Today widget (#811)

* feat: label Extra Usage as spend on accounts without plan limits

On usage-based plans (Claude Enterprise) the usage API reports every
rate-limit window as null and no limits[] entries: there's no plan limit
to go over, and extra usage is the account's whole spend. The Extra
Usage widgets still called it overage ("Overage Used: $123.45"), and
their picker descriptions only mentioned pay-as-you-go overage, so
Enterprise users had no reason to think these widgets were theirs.
Searching the picker for "enterprise" or "spend" didn't find them.

The parser now flags a response that explicitly reports no plan limits
(`noPlanLimits`). The flag is kept in the usage cache and through the
merge with statusline rate_limits, and the three widgets label their
value "Spend Used", "Spend Left" and "Spend" when it's set. Only an
explicit null counts and any limits[] entry counts as a limit, so every
uncertain case keeps the "Overage" label. A cache written before this
change keeps the old label until its next refresh.

The widget descriptions now mention both Pro/Max overage and Enterprise
spend, which also makes the picker's search find them.

* refactor: share the cache file lock

Move the terminal width cache's best-effort O_EXCL lock into its own
module so other cache files can use the same read-modify-write
protection instead of copying it. No behavior change.

* feat: add a daily state file for per-day usage tracking

Some usage figures are per UTC day, but ccstatusline only ever sees the
current month-to-date totals. Keep a small state file next to the other
caches that records what was seen and when, modeled on the terminal
width cache: one JSON file, the shared lock around each
read-modify-write, an atomic temp-file rename, pruning to today and
yesterday, and injected file and clock dependencies.

* feat: track each day's starting extra usage spend

The usage API reports extra usage spent month to date only. Record the
total per login in the daily state file and work out today's spend from
where it stood when the UTC day began: the last value seen the previous
day, zero on the 1st (extra usage resets at 00:00 UTC), or otherwise the
first value seen today. A total that drops mid-day never makes today's
spend negative, and an observation that loses the state lock to another
process still reports today's spend.

* feat: work out today's extra usage spend during the usage prefetch

fetchUsageData now remembers the token fingerprint of the login it
used. When a line shows today's spend, the prefetch records the
month-to-date total for that login in the daily state file and adds
extraUsageUsedToday (cents) to the usage data. It's worked out on every
render, cache hits included, and never stored in the usage cache.

* feat: add an Extra Usage Today widget

Shows the extra usage spent since 00:00 UTC, including claude.ai and
other machines, labeled like its siblings: "Spend Today" on accounts
without plan limits, "Overage Today" otherwise. It shows nothing until a
usage fetch has run since the UTC day began, and n/a when extra usage
is off, with the same hide options, currency and cost number format as
the other Extra Usage widgets.

* fix: count a cached extra usage total for the day it was fetched

Today's spend recorded every usage prefetch as an observation at render
time, cache hits and stale fallbacks included. A total fetched at 23:58
UTC on the last day of the month and replayed from the cache at 00:01
became the 1st's first observation, so Spend Today showed the whole
previous month for up to three minutes, or for as long as the API stayed
unreachable.

fetchUsageData now reports when its data came from the API
(getUsageFetchedAt: now for a fresh fetch, the cache file's write time
for a cache hit or stale fallback), and the observation is recorded at
that time. A total fetched before midnight updates the previous day's
record, so today's spend shows nothing until a total fetched today
arrives, and an older fetch replayed after a newer one is ignored.

* test: check fetchUsageData reports the login and fetch time

Today's extra usage spend depends on fetchUsageData recording which
login and which fetch its data came from, and every other test replaces
that link with a spy. Run the real fetch in the probe harness and check
it reports the login fingerprint the usage cache is written with and the
API fetch time, and neither when there are no credentials.

* test: cover the Spend label with an edited label

Upstream's label editor (#601) gives each widget one default label,
while Extra Usage Used, Remaining and Utilization pick "Overage" or
"Spend" by account. The editor offers the Overage label, since it has
no usage data, and an edited label replaces whichever one the account
would show.

* refactor: keep the Enterprise wording, drop the Spend label detection

With the label editor (#601) in main, anyone on a usage-based Enterprise
plan can relabel the Extra Usage widgets' "Overage" to "Spend" in a few
keys, so detecting those accounts from the usage API's response shape
isn't worth its cache field and heuristics.

What stays is the wording: the three widgets' descriptions say they
cover Pro/Max overage and Enterprise spend, the docs say the same and
point at the label editor, and picker searches for "enterprise" or
"spend" list the three widgets first, which a new test checks.

* test: check the picker lists the Extra Usage widgets first, however many there are

* test: look for the Extra Usage widgets among the widgets that mention the word

* refactor(widgets): share Extra Usage Used and Remaining's code

The two widgets were the same class apart from how the amount is worked
out, and their label, name, description and preview sample. They now
extend ExtraUsageAmountWidget, the way the Tokens widgets share
TokenCountWidget. Rendering is unchanged.

* fix: drop extra usage times stamped while the clock ran ahead

Extra Usage Today ignores a fetch older than the one it last recorded,
so a cached fetch a concurrent render replays late can't move the day
back. A single render made while the system clock ran ahead defeats
that: it records a fetch stamped at a time that hasn't come yet. Once
the clock is put right, every real fetch looks older and is ignored, so
Today disappears for the rest of the day; and when the clock reaches the
stamped time, that record is taken as the day's, with the previous
day's total as its start. With $10 seen at 09:00, one render a day
ahead, then $25 and $40 later that day, Today was hidden for the rest of
the day and showed $40 the next day for at most $10 of real spend.

The usage cache that render wrote is stamped by the same clock and is
served as fresh until the clock catches up with it, so its fetch keeps
arriving with the future time and would store the same record again.

A record last seen more than a minute ahead of now is now dropped and
the day starts afresh, and a fetch stamped more than a minute ahead
isn't recorded. The minute's leeway keeps a small step back of the
clock, such as an NTP correction just after a fetch, from dropping the
day's starting point. Now is read after the state file, so a fetch
another render has just recorded is never taken for one from the
future and the replay guard still holds.

* fix(usage): remove daily.json's temp files when a write fails

updateDailyState writes daily.json through a temp file named
daily.json.<pid>.tmp and renames it into place. When the write or the
rename failed, for example a write cut short by a full disk or a rename
refused with EPERM while a Windows virus scanner or sync client holds
daily.json, the error went to the catch-all and the temp file stayed
behind. Every status line render is a new process with a new pid, so
each failing render left another orphan in ~/.cache/ccstatusline, and
nothing ever deleted them.

A failed write or rename now unlinks the temp file. A failed unlink is
ignored; as before, the state stays best-effort and the render goes on.

The same handle can be held on the temp file itself, and then it
refuses the unlink as well as the rename. So each write also removes
the other daily.json.<digits>.tmp files next to the state file once
they are a minute or more old, which no running write can still own.
While a handle stays held, only the last minute's temp files remain,
and orphans an older build left behind are cleared as well. The temp
name stays per process, so two renders never write through the same
file.

* fix(usage): keep today's extra usage spend across a token refresh

Extra Usage Today keeps each login's month-to-date total at the start of
the UTC day in daily.json, keyed by the usage cache's token fingerprint,
a hash of the refresh token. Claude Code saves a new refresh token each
time it refreshes the access token, which happens several times on a
working day. The key then changed mid-day, the new key had no record,
and today's spend started over from that moment: $15.00 at 13:00, then
$0.00 at 17:00 instead of $35.00 and $10.00 at 18:00 instead of $45.00.
The old record stayed behind until it was pruned.

The record is now kept under the account and organization the
credentials belong to. While a widget shows today's spend, ccstatusline
asks /api/oauth/profile through the usage fetch's own request, proxy
and credential code, once per token fingerprint, and keeps the answers
in ~/.cache/ccstatusline/usage-account.json. A failed lookup holds off
that fingerprint alone, for 30 seconds or a 429's Retry-After (at most
a day), and the hold-off is written before the request goes out, so
renders running side by side send one request between them.

Until the lookup answers, the record stays under the fingerprint as
before. Once the account is known, the records under its fingerprints,
written by an earlier build or while the lookup was failing, are folded
into the account's record once, so the day keeps its starting total.
A record seen while the clock ran ahead is dropped instead, as it would
be under its own key. A fingerprint that was never looked up can't be
placed with an account, so today's spend still starts over once when
an earlier build kept the record under a refresh token that has since
changed, or when a lookup outage spans a refresh.

The organization is part of the key because one account can sign in to
a personal organization and a work one, each with its own extra usage
total. The key is a hash, so neither cache file names the account.

* refactor(usage): tidy the account lookup and the record merge

mergeSpendRecord goes through an arrow, so reduce's index and array
arguments never reach it, and the account id is built before it's
fingerprinted instead of inside a nested template literal.

* refactor(usage): ask the profile endpoint once for the account email and the account key

The Claude Account Email widget (#724) and Extra Usage Today each asked
/api/oauth/profile about the same login, each with its own cache and backoff.
One request now answers both. lookUpProfile runs under the email lookup's
per-login lease and backoff files, and each caller keeps its part of the
answer in its own cache: the email in account-email-<hash>.json, the account
key in usage-account.json, which now holds only named logins. An answer that
leaves out the caller's part holds that login off as before, and the other
part is still kept.

A rate-limited lookup's Retry-After is kept within the day the backoff reader
trusts, as the account lookup did, so the email lookup no longer reads a
Retry-After further off as no backoff at all.

* docs(development): the account email and Extra Usage Today share one profile lookup

* refactor(usage): name the account id before fingerprinting it

The account key nested the id's template inside its own on one line. Build
the id first, as the account lookup did before it shared the profile
request.

* fix: enable label editing for Extra Usage Today

---------

Co-authored-by: Matthew Breedlove <sirmalloc@gmail.com>

fix: report Uninstall and Refresh Interval failures when Claude's settings.json can't be changed (#805)

* fix(install): stop Uninstall when Claude's settings.json can't be read

uninstallStatusLine caught a load failure (invalid JSON such as a
trailing comma, or a permission error), printed a warning and returned
normally. The TUI's uninstall action treats a normal return as "Claude
settings removed", so it went on to run `npm uninstall -g` or
`bun remove -g`, switched the menu to not installed and flashed
"✓ Uninstalled from Claude Code and removed global package". Nothing
had been removed from settings.json: once the file was fixed,
statusLine still ran the global binary that had just been uninstalled,
which leaves a blank status line, and the managed --hook hooks and the
installation metadata were still there. The settings-only options
reported "✓ Uninstalled from Claude Code" the same way.

The TUI only offers Uninstall when settings.json was readable at
startup, so this takes the file breaking while the TUI is open, for
example a hand edit saved with a syntax error in another window.

uninstallStatusLine now throws on that failure, as installStatusLine
already does, with the same message naming the file and the reason
from a loader the two share. The TUI's existing failure branch then
runs: it shows "✗ Uninstall failed", keeps the installed state and
skips the global package removal. settings.json, the metadata and the
hooks are left as they were.

* fix(tui): report a refresh interval that couldn't be saved

setRefreshInterval returned normally when Claude's settings.json could
not be read or parsed, and when it had no statusLine, without writing
anything. Configure Status Line sets the new value before the save and
only puts the old one back if the save rejects, so in both cases it
flashed "✓ Refresh interval updated" and kept showing the new value,
while Claude Code went on using the old one.

As with Uninstall, the menu is only enabled when settings.json was
readable and had our statusLine at startup, so this takes the file
changing while the TUI is open: a hand edit that leaves invalid JSON,
or another tool replacing the file.

setRefreshInterval now throws in both cases, the read failure with the
message install and uninstall use. The TUI's existing failure branch
then shows "✗ Failed to save refresh interval" and keeps the value
that is still in effect. The file is left unchanged.

* fix(install): stop Uninstall when the managed hooks can't be removed

uninstallStatusLine ignored any failure to remove the managed --hook
hooks. When statusLine was already gone from Claude's settings.json,
so nothing was written before that step, and the file couldn't be
written (read-only, for example), the hooks stayed in place and the
uninstall returned normally. The TUI then ran `npm uninstall -g` or
`bun remove -g` and flashed success, leaving hooks that run the binary
it had just removed. The installation metadata was cleared before the
hooks were tried, so it was gone as well.

The hook cleanup failure now rejects the uninstall, and the hooks are
removed before the metadata is cleared, so the TUI's existing failure
branch shows "✗ Uninstall failed", skips the global package removal
and leaves settings.json and the metadata as they were.

removeManagedHooks no longer rewrites settings.json when it holds none
of our hooks. An uninstall with neither statusLine nor managed hooks in
the file still goes ahead even when the file can't be written, since
nothing in it would be left pointing at the binary. It also stops
reformatting the file and refreshing its .bak copy for no change.

* fix(install): keep Uninstall working with a hand-edited hook it can't read

Removing the managed hooks assumed every hook event held a list of
objects, each with a list of hooks. A hand-edited settings.json can
break that, for example a Stop hook written as an object, a null entry,
or "hooks" set to a string. The cleanup then threw a TypeError, even when
none of the hooks were ccstatusline's, and since the previous change
that error rejects the uninstall. statusLine had already been removed in
an earlier write, so the TUI showed "Uninstall failed" with statusLine
gone, and every retry failed the same way.

Entries without the expected shape are now left as they are, since they
can't be ours. Uninstall also removes statusLine and the managed hooks
in one write, so a failure to save leaves both in place, and the .bak
copy holds the file as it was before the uninstall rather than the
halfway state between the two writes.

---------

Co-authored-by: Matthew Breedlove <sirmalloc@gmail.com>

fix(install): find programs on PATH without which, and count a symlinked PATH dir once (#804)

* fix(install): find package managers and ccstatusline on PATH without which

The TUI asked `which` whether npm, npx, bun and bunx are installed and
where ccstatusline resolves. `which` is a separate package that minimal
Linux images (Fedora, RHEL/UBI) and a base Arch install leave out.
Without it every lookup failed the way a missing tool does: the Install
screen marked all four package managers "not installed" and disabled
every option, update actions were disabled too, and Manage Installation
said ccstatusline is not resolvable on PATH.

When `which` can't be started, the lookup now searches PATH itself and
lists what `which -a` would: each file the user can run, in PATH order.
`command -v` could answer "is npm installed" but can't list every match,
which the multiple-binaries warning needs, so both checks share this one
search. The availability check now goes through the same lookup as the
ccstatusline resolution, so the two can't disagree. Where `which` exists
nothing changes, and Windows still uses `where`.

* fix(install): count a PATH directory reached through a symlink once

The "Multiple ccstatusline binaries are on PATH" warning counts the
directories `which -a` lists ccstatusline in, comparing them as text.
On merged-/usr Linux (Ubuntu 22.04+, Debian 12) /bin is a symlink to
usr/bin and the default PATH lists both, so with npm's global prefix at
/usr one installed binary shows up as /usr/bin/ccstatusline and
/bin/ccstatusline. Manage Installation and the install and update
notices then warned about a second install that doesn't exist.

Both duplicate checks now compare each directory with its symlinks
resolved, and fall back to the path as listed when it can't be
resolved. The warning still shows the paths as PATH spells them.

* fix(install): read PATH from process.env when the PATH search runs

The PATH search used when there is no `which` kept the process.env object
that existed when its module loaded. Code that replaces process.env with a
new object afterwards (a test restoring a saved environment does) left the
search reading the old object, so a PATH set on the new one was never seen.
The default search now reads process.env each time it runs.

* fix(install): list each other install once in the multiple-binaries warning

The warning counts installs by directory, with symlinks resolved, but
built its "Other matches" list from every path `which -a` printed after
the first. With a real second install on a merged-/usr system, where
/bin links to usr/bin, PATH order gives /usr/bin/ccstatusline,
/bin/ccstatusline and then the other one, so the list named
/bin/ccstatusline as another binary although it is the first match
reached a second way.

The list now takes the first path listed in each directory and leaves
out the first match's directory, so each other install appears once,
spelled as PATH lists it.

* fix(install): resolve PATH directories' letter case the same under Node and Bun

The duplicate-binary checks resolve each PATH directory with
fs.realpathSync before comparing. Where the file system ignores letter
case (macOS by default), Bun's realpathSync returns the case stored on
disk but Node's returns the case it was given. A PATH that spells one
directory two ways, such as .../bin and .../Bin, therefore showed
"Multiple ccstatusline binaries are on PATH" when the TUI ran under
Node and no warning under Bun.

The lookup now uses fs.realpathSync.native, which asks the operating
system and returns the on-disk case under both runtimes. A directory
that can't be resolved still falls back to the path as listed.

* test(install): keep the PATH search for when which is missing, not failing

The lookup searches PATH itself only when `which` can't be started
(ENOENT). When `which` runs and exits non-zero, it found nothing, and
that answer stands. No test covered this: with the ENOENT check removed,
every failed `which -a ccstatusline` would fall through to the PATH
search, and the tests still passed.

The new case has `which -a` exit with status 1 while PATH holds an
executable ccstatusline, and expects no matches.

* test(install): check that PATH directories resolve through the native realpath

The letter-case test passes under Bun with or without the native call,
because Bun's plain realpathSync already reports the on-disk case, and
it is skipped where the file system is case-sensitive. A second test
checks the call itself, so a revert fails under bun test on any system.

* refactor(install): build the default PATH search in a named helper

findAllOnPosixPath spelled its default search as an object literal inside
the parameter list, which made the signature hard to read at a glance. The
default now comes from defaultPosixPathSearch(), next to the isExecutableFile
check it uses.

A default parameter is evaluated on every call that leaves it out, so the
helper still builds a fresh search from process.env as it is when the search
runs: an env object swapped in after the module loaded is still seen.

fix(cwd): fish style keeps emoji and UNC roots, and (s)egments applies in fish mode (#803)

* fix(cwd): keep whole characters in fish-style segments

Fish style shortens each middle directory to its first character, but it
took that character with part[0] (and part[1] after a leading dot), which
index UTF-16 code units. A folder whose name starts with an emoji or other
character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane was cut in half, leaving a
lone surrogate that the terminal prints as U+FFFD: "~/🚀 rockets/sub/last"
showed as "~/�/s/last". A decomposed accented name such as "Über" lost its
combining mark, and a joined emoji such as "👨‍👩‍👧" printed as U+FFFD
too.

Take the first grapheme instead, using the getGraphemes helper the symbol
editors already use, so the abbreviation keeps one whole user-visible
character, including after the dot of a hidden directory.

* fix(cwd): keep a UNC path's root in fish style

Fish style splits the path on separators, drops the empty pieces and then
rebuilds it, putting a single separator back only when the path started
with '/'. A Windows UNC path lost its leading '\\' entirely, so
"\\server\share\team\repo" showed as the relative-looking
"server\s\t\repo", and "//server/share/team/repo" kept only one of its two
slashes.

Keep the path's leading separators as they were and join the shortened
parts after them. POSIX paths keep their '/', home and drive-letter paths
have no leading separators and come out as before.

* fix(cwd): turn fish style off when a segment count is saved

Fish style and the segment count are mutually exclusive: turning fish
style on clears the segment count, and turning on the home ~ option turns
fish style off. The (s)egments editor broke that rule. It is offered while
fish style is on, but on Enter it kept fish style and stored the count
next to it. Fish style wins when both are set, so the item still read
"(fish-style)" and the preview and status line didn't change, as if the
edit had been dropped. The hidden count then cut the path the moment fish
style was turned off.

Saving a segment count now turns fish style off, the same way the home ~
option does, so the count takes effect as soon as it is entered and the
item shows it. A blank entry still only clears the count.

Settings saved before this fix, or edited by hand, can still hold both.
Turning fish style off now drops the segment count as well, so the full
path comes back instead of a count that was never shown. Since turning
fish style on already clears the count, it can only sit next to fish
style through the old editor or a hand edit.

fix(git-remote): link plain-HTTP remotes over http (#802)

The "link to repo" option on Git Branch and the Git Origin/Upstream
widgets builds its link with buildRepoWebUrl, which always wrote
https://. For http and https remotes parseRemoteUrl keeps the port, as
the forge's web port, so an origin of
http://git.example.lan:3000/team/app.git (a Gitea or GitLab served over
plain HTTP on a LAN) linked to https://git.example.lan:3000/team/app
and .../tree/<branch>. That port speaks no TLS, so clicking the link
failed.

Take the scheme from the remote: an http:// remote links over http, and
https, ssh, git and scp-style remotes still link over https. An
http://github.com remote now links to http://github.com/..., which
GitHub redirects to https.

fix(update): Check for Updates deadline, proxy, self-managed version and re-check (#806)

* fix(update): bound the registry check with an overall deadline

Check for Updates is meant to give up on the npm registry after five
seconds, but its only timer was the request's socket timeout. That timer
starts once the socket has connected, and Bun's doesn't fire while it
connects at all. On a network that silently drops outbound HTTPS (a
firewall that expects a proxy, a captive portal), the Updates screen sat
on "Checking npm registry..." until the OS gave up on the connection:
about 75 seconds on macOS under Bun, and the same on Node 18 and older,
whose global agent has no default timeout. Node 19+ only stopped at five
seconds because its global agent's own socket timeout happens to match.

The check now arms one timer for the whole request, as the usage and
status-page requests already do. When it fires, it destroys the request
and fails the check with "npm registry request timed out after 5000ms".
The socket timeout is gone, since the deadline always fires first. The
request function can be passed in, so tests can stand in for the
network.

* fix(update): send the registry check through HTTPS_PROXY

The usage and Claude Status requests go through the proxy named by
HTTPS_PROXY unless NO_PROXY excludes the host, but Check for Updates
called https.request with no agent, and neither Node nor Bun reads the
proxy variables on its own. On a network where only the proxy gets out,
every other network widget worked while the Updates screen failed with
"npm registry request timed out after 5000ms" (and under Bun waited
about 75 seconds for the OS to give up first).

The registry request now uses the same helpers: createProxyAgent for
HTTPS_PROXY, skipped when isExcludedFromProxy matches registry.npmjs.org.
At the deadline it also closes the agent's connection to a proxy that
never answers CONNECT, which would otherwise keep the process alive. A
HTTPS_PROXY that isn't a URL fails the check with a message that says
so. The proxy docs now list the update check, and the test helper that
clears the proxy variables is shared by both suites that need it.

* fix(update): compare a self-managed global install's own version

With Claude Code's status line set to the global `ccstatusline` command
and no pinned metadata, Check for Updates compared the latest release
with the version of the TUI that was running. The README starts the TUI
with npx or bunx, so that is often a different copy from the global
package Claude Code runs. Manage Installation showed "Active PATH match:
npm global 2.2.20", yet Check for Updates said "Current: 2.2.32 ...
ccstatusline is up to date" and offered nothing, and a global already
at the latest release got an offer to reinstall it whenever the TUI was
older.

Pinned installs already use the version found on PATH. Self-managed
installs now do too when that version is known, and fall back to the
running TUI's version otherwise. The offered command already targeted
that global package's manager, so the version shown now matches what it
would update.

* fix(update): check again after a global update from the Updates screen

After "Run npm install -g ccstatusline@X" succeeded, the TUI flashed
"Global package updated" (or showed the Update Complete notice) and went
back to the Updates screen, which still held the result from before the
update: the old Current version, "An update is available." and the same
install command, which reinstalled X if picked again. Only Check again
showed that the install was up to date.

A successful update now runs the check again. It runs from an effect
once the new installation metadata has reached `settings`: calling the
check from the update's own callback would read the settings from
before the update, so a self-managed install would still show as one,
and a pinned install whose PATH version can't be read would compare
the old version. Both the flash path and the PATH-warning notice path
land on the fresh result.

* fix(update): compare a checkout status line with its own version, not PATH's

A status line that runs a local checkout (any command running
ccstatusline.ts) is classified as self-managed, the same as the bare global
`ccstatusline` command. Check for Updates then compared the latest release
with the version of whatever global `ccstatusline` sits first on PATH, a copy
Claude Code never runs for that status line. A checkout at the latest release
with an old global on PATH was told an update is available and offered
`npm install -g`; a checkout behind the latest release read as up to date
when the global was current.

The PATH version now applies only when the status line command is the global
`ccstatusline` (with or without --config). Every other self-managed command
compares this TUI's own version again, as before the self-managed change.

* fix(proxy): read an HTTPS_PROXY with no scheme as an HTTP proxy

A proxy given as host:port, such as `proxy.corp:3128` (a form curl
accepts as http://), went to HttpsProxyAgent as it was. `new URL()`
parses it without complaint but takes `proxy.corp:` as the scheme and
leaves the host empty, so the agent connected to localhost:80. Check
for Updates, which now goes through HTTPS_PROXY, then failed with only
"Unable to query npm registry", where it used to connect directly and
work wherever direct connections were allowed. The invalid-URL check
missed this form, since nothing threw.

createProxyAgent now adds `http://` when the value has no `scheme://`,
as curl does, so the request goes through the named proxy. Values that
still aren't URLs, like one with spaces, fail as before. The usage and
Claude Status requests build their agents with the same helper, so they
read the variable the same way.

* fix: close failed registry requests before clearing deadline

---------

Co-authored-by: Matthew Breedlove <sirmalloc@gmail.com>

fix: open Configure Status Line before an install, and sync hooks only from the config the status line loads (#807)

* fix(tui): open Configure Status Line before ccstatusline is installed

Configure Status Line was disabled with "(install first)" unless Claude
Code's statusLine command was one of the exact commands the installer
writes, with padding 0. A wrapper script, `bunx ccstatusline`,
`npx ccstatusline@latest` without -y, or any other padding all counted
as not installed.

That menu is the only place in the TUI to edit the Git, Custom Command
and Terminal Width cache TTLs. They are ccstatusline's own settings,
saved to its settings.json and read on every render however Claude Code
runs it. With such a status line they couldn't be changed, for example
to turn on custom command caching, which is off by default.

The menu now always opens. Only its Refresh Interval row needs the
install: Claude Code keeps that value in its statusLine setting, which
ccstatusline edits only for a status line it recognizes as its own.
Until then the row is disabled with "(install first)"; an older Claude
Code still shows its version requirement instead. The main menu's
description of the item says which part needs the install.

* fix(hooks): sync widget hooks only from the config the status line loads

Saving a config rewrote Claude Code's ccstatusline-managed hooks from
that config's widgets, whichever config it was. The installed status
line command loads one config: the path after its --config, or the
default config without one. Saving any other config, such as one opened
with `ccstatusline --config <file>` to try something out, still rewrote
the hooks to match it:

- If the status line shows Skills and the saved config doesn't, the
  Skills hooks were removed and the status line's Skills widget stopped
  updating.
- In the other direction, hooks were added that make Claude Code run
  `<command> --hook` on every prompt and Skill call, for a status line
  that doesn't need them.

Either way the TUI only said "Configuration saved".

syncWidgetHooks now works out which config the status line command
loads and leaves the hooks as they are when that isn't the config being
saved. getStatusLineConfigPath splits the command into words the way a
POSIX shell passes them on (quotes and backslash escapes; on Windows
only double quotes group), expands a leading ~ and $HOME, and resolves
the path as the --config argument is resolved at startup, through
resolveConfigPath, which initConfigPath now uses too. A command without
--config, a wrapper script included, is taken to load the default
config. Installing still syncs the hooks, since the command it writes
names the config the TUI has open.

* fix(claude-settings): start a quoted word without ??=

Node 14, the build's target, has no logical assignment operators, and the
build passes them through unchanged.

* fix: preserve config identity when syncing widget hooks

---------

Co-authored-by: Matthew Breedlove <sirmalloc@gmail.com>

fix: keep emoji whole in two text editors and in TUI rows, and align wide padding (#808)

* fix(widgets): edit Link and Custom Command text by whole characters

The Link text and URL editors and the Custom Command editor kept their
cursor as a UTF-16 index and moved or deleted one code unit at a time.
An emoji outside the Basic Multilingual Plane is two code units, so
Backspace after it, Delete before it, or an arrow key over it split the
pair:

- Backspace on "Docs 📘" saved "Docs \ud83d", which the status line
  draws as "🔗 Docs �".
- In the command "echo 🚀", Left then "x" saved "echo \ud83dx\ude80",
  so the shell received U+FFFD x U+FFFD instead of the rocket.

The cursor cell also drew value[cursor], a single code unit, so with the
cursor on an emoji a real terminal showed two replacement characters.

The Custom Text and label editors already work by grapheme through
text-cursor.ts. Its boundary lookup is now exported as
getAdjacentBoundaries, and both editors use it for Left, Right,
Backspace and Delete and to draw the whole grapheme under the cursor.
Joined, skin-toned and flag emoji now move and delete as one character,
as they do in Custom Text. Typing and pasting are unchanged.

* fix(tui): keep joined emoji whole in Edit Lines and Global Overrides rows

Each row in the line editor was a run of sibling Texts: the widget name
and its text, then one for each tag such as "(merged→)", "(label: …)",
the number style or "(no-align)". Ink lays a sibling out at the width
string-width gives the text before it, which counts a joined, skin-toned
or flag emoji (👩‍💻, 👍🏽, 🇺🇸) as two columns, but it writes every code
point of that emoji into its own cells. The text ran past its box and the
next tag overwrote the end. A Custom Text of 👩‍💻 merged into the next
widget showed as "1. Custom Text (👩‍ (merged→)", a plain 👩 with no
closing paren, and a 👍🏽 label lost its closing quote. Only the editor
list was wrong; the saved config and the status line were fine.

Global Overrides draws its Default Padding and Default Separator rows the
same way: the quoted value, then a sibling " - Press (p) to edit" hint.
A 👍🏽 padding showed as `Default Padding: "👍🏽 - Press (p) to edit`,
without its closing quote, and a 👩‍💻 padding lost its 💻 as well.

The row's name and tags are now nested Texts inside one Text, the way
the label editor already draws its value, so they print as one string
and nothing overwrites the emoji. The two Global Overrides rows nest
their value and hint the same way. The styling of each part is unchanged.

* fix(renderer): size auto-aligned columns by the padding's display width

With Powerline Align Widgets on, the shared column widths added the
default padding's string length to each widget's display width. The
renderer then pads every cell by measuring its padded text in columns.
The two only agree when every padding character is one UTF-16 unit and
one column wide.

With the ideographic space U+3000 as padding (what the space bar types
under a full-width Japanese or Chinese IME), the columns came out 2
narrower than the padded cells. On lines [A, B] and [CCCCC, D] the first
separator landed at column 7 on one line and 9 on the other. A padding
glyph from outside the Basic Multilingual Plane went the other way and
added spaces to every column.

The padding is now measured with getVisibleWidth, the same measure used
for the cells.

refactor: small cleanups to the font install, auto-align loop, GUID and root dir widgets (#809)

* refactor(powerline): drop the font install's unreachable fallback return

After the clone, installPowerlineFonts either runs install.sh (macOS and
Linux) or copies the font files (Windows), and each branch returns its
result or throws. The "Platform-specific installation not implemented"
result after them could never be returned, and an unsupported platform
already returns its own message before the clone.

* refactor(renderer): step through Powerline auto-align padding with a while loop

The padding pass jumped its for-loop counter past each merge group from
inside the body, so the loop header no longer said how it stepped. A
while loop now sets the next widget explicitly: the following one, or
the one after a merge group once the group is padded.

The output is unchanged. Two new tests pin the cases that depend on the
stepping and had no test: an auto-align exclusion on a widget merged
into the previous one is ignored and the columns after the group are
still padded, and a line rendered without column widths keeps its
natural widths.

* refactor(guid): truncate the random hex digit with Math.trunc

generateGuid dropped the fraction of Math.random() * 16 with a bitwise
"| 0". Math.trunc says that directly. For the values this sees, [0, 16),
both give the same digit: they differ only past 2^31, for NaN and for
Infinity, none of which Math.random() * 16 can produce.

New tests pin the UUID v4 shape and the digits Math.random() at 0,
1/16, 1/2 and its largest value turn into, including the variant
digit's 8 to b range.

* refactor(widgets): drop the root dir widgets' redundant separator trim

Git Root Dir and JJ Root Dir stripped trailing separators from the root
path, then split it on separators and dropped the empty parts. The split
already drops the empty parts trailing separators leave, so the strip
changed nothing:
- With a name in the path, both give the same last part.
- With no name, as for "/", the strip left an empty string and the code
  fell back to the original path, which is what the fallback now uses
  directly.

The strip's pattern also rescanned a long run of separators from every
position in it: 50,000 slashes before a name took 1.6s under Bun and
4.0s under Node. git and jj never print such a path, but the split
alone does it in about a millisecond.

An exhaustive check over every string of up to 8 characters drawn from
"/", "\", "a", ":", " " and a newline gives the same name both ways. New
tests cover trailing Windows separators in both widgets, "/" for JJ Root
Dir and a path of separators alone for Git Root Dir.

refactor(widgets): consolidate the progress-bar widgets' duplicated code (#810)

- Shared bar rendering: Block Timer, Block Reset Timer, Weekly Reset Timer,
  Extra Usage Utilization and the usage-percent widgets each built their bars
  with the same blocks. formatUsageBar in usage-display.ts now builds every
  bar mode (block, line and slider, with or without the percentage) in one
  place and returns null outside them, so each widget only adds its label.
  The time cursor is still resolved only in bar modes.
- One class for the usage-percent widgets: Block, Weekly, Weekly Sonnet,
  Weekly Opus and Fable Weekly Usage were identical apart from their kind.
  UsagePercentWidget holds the class once and each widget names its kind.
  Spend Limit Usage extends it too and keeps only its color; the class takes
  the time cursor and the API-error state from the kind.
- A shared base for the Context % widgets: Context % and Context % (usable)
  differed only in name, color, description, label prefix, preview sample
  and how they measure the used share. ContextPercentageWidgetBase holds the
  rest.

No change in behavior.

repos.name: winfunc/opcode
repos.description: A powerful GUI app and Toolkit for Claude Code - Create custom agents, manage interactive Claude Code sessions, run secure background agents, and more.

commits.message:
Merge pull request #488 from shahuldxb666-crypto/fix/462-tauri-events-esm

Fix: deliver backend events to the chat on desktop (spinner never stops, #462)

Merge pull request #487 from shahuldxb666-crypto/fix/465-project-path-underscore

Fix: resolve real project paths for paths containing _, - or . (#465)

refactor: extract the drag-drop visibility check into a helper

Move the "is this prompt on screen" check used by the drag-drop handler into
src/lib/domVisibility.ts so it can be tested without rendering the component.
No behaviour change.

fix: avoid handling a stream line twice while switching listeners

The backend emits each line on the session-scoped channel and then on the
generic one. The chat starts with generic listeners and swaps in scoped ones
after the init message; during the swap both are active, so lines arriving
then were processed twice. This path was unreachable on desktop before events
were delivered (#462).

Once a scoped listener has received an event on a channel, the generic
listener for that channel ignores it. Flags are per channel so a completion
event is never skipped.

fix: only the visible chat tab reacts to dropped files

Native drag-drop events are window-wide and every chat tab stays mounted
(inactive tabs are only hidden), so now that the drag-drop listener is
registered on desktop, dropping an image added its path to the prompt of
every open chat tab. Ignore drag-drop events in tabs whose prompt is not
visible.

refactor: import Tauri listen statically in useClaudeMessages

Replace the last require('@tauri-apps/api/event') with a static ESM import so
no component depends on require() at runtime. The hook keeps its existing
desktop/web branches; it is currently only used by
ClaudeCodeSession.refactored.tsx.

fix: restore file drag-and-drop into the prompt on desktop

FloatingPromptInput loaded getCurrentWebviewWindow with the same
require()/window.__TAURI__ pattern, so on desktop it always got a stub
without onDragDropEvent and dropping images into the prompt did nothing
(same root cause as #462).

Import it statically and register the drag-drop listener only when running
in the Tauri runtime.

fix: stream Claude output into the open chat on desktop

ClaudeCodeSession always ended up with its DOM-event fallback in the desktop
app (see previous commit), so claude-output / claude-complete events from the
backend never arrived: the chat showed a spinner until it was reopened and
cancel did nothing because the session id from the init message was never
received (#462).

Use the shared listen() from @/lib/tauriEvents. The listener call sites are
unchanged.

feat: add shared backend event listener that works on desktop and web

Components loaded Tauri's listen() with require() behind a window.__TAURI__
check. Neither works: require() does not exist in Vite's ESM bundle, and
window.__TAURI__ is only defined when withGlobalTauri is enabled (it is not),
while web mode installs a fake one, so the check is false on desktop and true
in the browser (#462).

Add src/lib/tauriEvents.ts: a static import of Tauri's listen, chosen at call
time with the same environment detection the API adapter uses for commands
(exported as isTauriRuntime), and a DOM CustomEvent fallback for web mode.
The selection logic lives in a dependency-free core module so it can be
checked without a Tauri runtime.

refactor: address clippy warnings introduced by the #465 fix

Name the project path cache type and use iter::repeat_n in a test. No
behaviour change.

fix: resolve Windows project folder names (C--Users-...) to real paths

Claude Code names a Windows project folder by replacing every non-alphanumeric
character, so C:\Users\john_doe\app becomes C--Users-john-doe-app. The
resolver only understood Unix names rooted at '/', so on Windows the same
lossy '-' -> '/' guess broke prompts (#465).

- Recognise a leading '<drive>--' as the root '<drive>:\' and walk down with
  '\' separators; UNC paths are unsupported and fall back to the guess
- Make PathProbe string-based so Windows layouts are unit-tested on any host
- Keep the last-resort guess platform-shaped (C:\a\b instead of C://a/b)

The encoder already maps '\' and ':' to '-', so no change was needed there.

fix: re-resolve saved project paths when restoring chat tabs

Chat tabs restored their project path from localStorage, so a path saved by
an older build (e.g. /home/michal/mikes/p instead of /home/michal_mikes/p)
kept breaking prompts across restarts (#465) until the user edited
localStorage by hand.

On restore, look the path up by project id in the backend's current project
list (one listing call, only when a chat tab needs restoring), use it, and
repair the saved record. Falls back to the saved path if the project is
unknown or the listing fails.

fix: report the real reason when a prompt cannot be started

When the project directory does not exist, spawning claude failed with an
opaque OS error and the UI only showed "Failed to send prompt", which made
#465 hard to diagnose.

- Validate the working directory before spawning and return
  "Project directory not found: <path>" (or "Project path is empty")
- Show the backend's message in the chat error instead of discarding it

fix: use Claude Code's folder naming wherever a project folder is computed

create_project, read_session_jsonl and the session file monitor encoded the
project path with replace('/', "-"), which leaves '_' and '.' untouched, so
they looked for (or created) folders that Claude Code never created for such
paths (#465). Use the shared encode_project_path helper, and add
session_jsonl_path so the two agents.rs lookups share one tested
implementation.

slash_commands.rs builds an internal command ID, not a project folder name,
so it is intentionally unchanged.

fix: resolve real project path in list_projects and get_project_sessions

Both commands fell back to the lossy '-' -> '/' decoder whenever the session
files had no cwd, handing a non-existent directory to the spawned claude
process ("Failed to send prompt", #465).

Add resolve_project_path: session cwd first, then the folder name resolved
against the real filesystem, then a best-effort guess. Results from the first
two are cached per project folder and invalidated by the folder's mtime, so
repeated listings skip all file reads (200 projects: ~8 ms cold, ~0.4 ms
cached). The blocking filesystem work now runs in spawn_blocking so it no
longer stalls the async runtime.

fix: resolve project folder names against the real filesystem

decode_project_path turned every '-' into '/', so folder names for paths
containing '_', '-' or '.' decoded to non-existent directories such as
/home/michal/mikes/projects (#465).

Resolve the name by walking down from the root and keeping only child
directories whose encoded name matches the front of the remaining text.
This needs one directory listing per path level (no exponential search),
allocates nothing per entry, backtracks out of dead ends and picks
deterministically (name order) when layouts encode identically. The old
'-' -> '/' guess remains only as a last resort. The filesystem is behind a
small PathProbe trait so Windows-style layouts can be tested on any host.

feat: add encode_project_path helper matching Claude Code folder naming

Claude Code names project folders by replacing every non-alphanumeric
character (including _, -, ., \ and :) with '-', per UTF-16 code unit. The
existing call sites only replaced '/', so they could not locate folders for
paths containing '_' or '.' (#465). Add a single shared, allocation-light
helper that mirrors the real rule; call sites are switched over in follow-up
commits.

fix: scan session files until a cwd is found when resolving project path

Newer Claude Code session files start with entries (last-prompt,
permission-mode) that carry no cwd. get_project_path_from_sessions only read
the first 10 lines of each file, so it often gave up and fell back to the
lossy folder-name decoder, producing paths like /home/michal/mikes/projects
and "Failed to send prompt" (#465).

- Stream up to 200 lines per file and try up to 5 files per project
- Skip lines over 1 MiB and non-UTF8 lines without buffering them
- Pre-filter on the "cwd" key to avoid JSON-parsing irrelevant lines
- Add regression tests and an ignored baseline benchmark

commits.message:
Merge branch 'feat/dual_core_claim_macro' into 'master'

feat(multicore): add ESP_NN_HAS_DUAL_CORE_CLAIM

See merge request espressif/esp-nn!87

Merge branch 'feat/bench_app' into 'master'

feat(bench_app): cycle benchmark of the kernels; test_app checks correctness only

See merge request espressif/esp-nn!78
docs: the performance tables come from bench_app
ci: expect the fc_per_ch_s8_batch_1x1 suite in the emulator runs

test(fc): time the batch scratch call in bench_app only

- The batch 1x1 test checks the outputs and the path taken, without timing.
- bench_app adds an esp_nn_scratch variant to the batched fully connected
  cases. BENCH_WARN fires when it takes over 105% of the esp_nn cycles.

ci: build bench_app for ESP32-S3, ESP32-P4 and ESP32-S31

Build only, on ESP-IDF v5.5, v6.0 and master, so the benchmark keeps
building as the kernels change. ESP32-S31 builds on master only, as a
preview target. The GitHub workflow builds it too.

test: TFLite-like quantization in the softmax and mean tests

- Softmax uses TFLite's parameters for input scale 1/16 and beta 1:
  multiplier 2^30, left shift 23, diff_min -248. The exp argument then
  spans [-15.5, 0]. Two more TFLite scalings are added: input scale 1/256
  and 0.1. The small multiplier and shift cases stay.
- Mean derives its multiplier and shift from 1 / (H * W), as TFLite does.
  The fixed 2^30 and -1 saturated every output to 127.

test(test_app): correctness only; cycles move to bench_app

- test_app prints no cycle counts: the PROFILE lines, the suite totals
  and the per-case cycle lines go. The profile hooks stay; on ESP32-P4
  and ESP32-S31 they still clear the PIE CFG before each optimized call.
- The FC performance test becomes fc_large_s8: the same six layers,
  checked bit-exact with aligned operands and at 8 mod 16. bench_app
  times them.
- run_emulator_tests.py expects fc_large_s8 and writes per-suite CSVs
  without cycle columns.

feat(bench_app): cycle benchmark of the kernels against the reference

A new app times each kernel and its ANSI C reference on hardware, and
prints one BENCH line per case and kernel variant.

- Every op has a shape table covering the published shapes, plus the
  batched fully connected shapes of small transformers.
- An op lists one or more variants of its kernel. Each variant is timed
  and checked against the reference, so another way to run the same op
  is one more table entry.
- Each case runs 9 calls per kernel, alternating two input sets with
  interrupts off, and keeps the fastest call after the first. Every
  output and the guard bytes around it are checked.
- Tensors go to PSRAM or internal RAM per case.
- Each case seeds its data from the run seed, its op and its shape.
- Cases that cannot allocate print a skip line and are counted in
  BENCH_DONE.
- The large fully connected cases warn when the aligned dispatch is
  slower than the same call with operands at 8 mod 16 (esp-nn#36).
- Softmax and mean use TFLite-like quantization parameters.
- On ESP32-P4, the bench task stack and internal buffers are in
  SIMD-capable memory.

Merge branch 'contrib/jameslavrenz/fc-batch-1x1' into 'master'

perf(fc): evaluate a zero weight zero-point batch as a 1x1 convolution (GH #46)

See merge request espressif/esp-nn!85

refactor(fc): pass the batch scratch buffer as an argument

- Add esp_nn_fully_connected_per_ch_s8_batch_scratch(), which takes the
  scratch buffer and its size. On S3, P4 and S31 it runs a qualifying
  batch as a 1x1 convolution in that buffer. Otherwise it runs the plain
  batch call.
- Remove esp_nn_set_fc_scratch_buf() and its file-static registration.
- Rename the feature flag to ESP_NN_HAS_FC_S8_BATCH_SCRATCH.
- esp_nn_fully_connected_per_ch_s8_batch() keeps its signature and runs the
  fully connected kernels only. The _ansi versions stay the portable
  reference loop.
- Move the 1x1 dispatch into esp_nn_fc_batch_conv.c, built only for the
  optimized S3 and PIE targets, and drop the ANSI borrow stubs.

fix(fc): keep the S3 preferred buffer and check output alignment

- The batched 1x1 path leaves the S3 preferred conv buffer set. The 1x1
  kernel stages its panels there, so a PSRAM fully connected buffer does
  not slow it.
- On S3 the batched 1x1 path needs an 8-byte aligned output. Other outputs
  stay on the fully connected kernel.
- The scratch borrow and restore helpers take only the scratch pointer.
- Document that the batch call swaps the conv scratch pointer and is not
  thread safe.
- Add S3 tests for a misaligned output and for a registered preferred
  buffer.

docs(fc): add batched fully connected benchmarks

- Document S3 and P4 before/after performance and core usage.
- Correct stale dual-core function reference in FC gate comment.

feat(multicore): add ESP_NN_HAS_DUAL_CORE_CLAIM

- Defined in esp_nn_multicore.h, next to the claim API.
- Callers that split work on the worker themselves, such as the
  esp-tflite-micro wrappers, check it at compile time to call
  esp_nn_dual_core_begin() and esp_nn_dual_core_end().
