repos.name: tw93/MiaoYan
repos.description: ⛷ A quiet, local-first Markdown writing app for Mac, iPhone and iPad, to help you write great sentences.

commits.message:
docs(readme): load the new composite past GitHub's image cache

The composite on miaoyan.app was rebuilt as the maintainer's pick (thinner device bezels on a wallpaper ground), but GitHub's camo proxy kept serving the previous picture, since it caches by URL and the site sends max-age=86400 with a week of stale-while-revalidate. A ?v= date on the two image URLs gives camo a new URL. AGENTS.md records the pick and the step for the next rebuild.

Verified: camo returned the old bytes before this change; checked again after the push.

Revert: git revert this commit.

docs(readme): Mac, iPad and iPhone in one picture instead of the GIF

The first screen loaded an 11 to 16 MB GIF of an interface several versions old and showed only the Mac. It is now one composite of the Mac window beside the iPad and iPhone (about 150 KB, transparent so it reads on GitHub's light and dark themes), built from the site's current shots by scripts/build-readme-shot.py on the vercel branch and loaded from miaoyan.app. The split-view screenshot, from 2026-10-11 with the old font and logo, now points at the site's current one too, so the two unused PNGs under assets/ go. The install paragraph takes the site's wording: the open-source Mac app is enough for writing on a Mac, the App Store version is for carrying on on iPhone and iPad.

Verified: all four image URLs return 200 image/webp and the composites match the vercel branch byte for byte; the README GIF rule in AGENTS.md is updated; git grep finds no other consumer of assets/split-preview*.png (the blog's hit is a heading id).

Revert: git revert this commit; the old GIFs still live in tw93/static.

docs: recommend the iPhone and iPad apps in the READMEs and release body

The READMEs only named iPhone and iPad inside the install steps, and release bodies never mentioned them, so people reading a release or the first screen of the README did not learn the App Store purchase also covers the phone and tablet. Each README's feature list gets one line linking its own App Store page, and render_release_body.sh adds an English and a Chinese sentence after the changelogs. Wording follows miaoyan.app.

Verified: the rendered V4.8.0 body differs from the published one only by those two paragraphs; bash -n and shellcheck -S error pass. No Swift or packaging changed, so the full test run on 4a770804 still stands.

Revert: git revert this commit, then re-render and gh release edit any release body that took the paragraphs.

release: V4.8.0 Brachydios

MARKETING_VERSION and CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION move to 4.8.0 in both configurations, so Sparkle's sparkle:version matches CFBundleVersion (#524). RELEASE_NOTES.md carries the seven items for this batch, Chinese and English one to one.

Verified: four version fields read 4.8.0, render_release_body.sh renders the body in V4.7.1's shape, full xcodebuild test 388 tests 0 failures on 4a770804.

Revert: git revert this commit before tagging; after V4.8.0 is published, fix forward with V4.8.1 instead, since Sparkle users already updated.

docs(incidents): record blank mind maps in exports

Row I-32 for 08bc53dc. Caught now by the two markmap runtime tests, which fail on the code before it. Verified with scripts/check_incidents.py (32 rows, 0 problems).

fix(export): mind maps no longer come out blank in PDF and PNG exports

The PDF export prints the preview's HTML in an offscreen window, which never
gets requestAnimationFrame, and neither does a preview behind other windows.
d3 steps every Markmap transition on it and caches its clock between frames,
so the map stayed at its first, empty step and printed as a blank box. On top
of that, markmap's autoLoader ran over the printed copy and redrew each drawn
map from its own SVG text, leaving one node of CSS.

- js/frame-fallback.js, loaded before d3, runs a frame callback from a 100ms
  timer when the native frame has not come; on screen the native one wins.
- index.html sets markmap's autoLoader to manual; diagram-handler.js leaves a
  map that arrives drawn alone, and redraws from source one saved mid-fit.
- data-markmap-shown now goes on only once d3 has no transition left on the
  map (fit() resolves early when another fit interrupts it), and the export
  probe waits for it or data-markmap-failed instead of data-markmap-rendered.

Verified: testMarkmapDrawsAndShowsWithoutAnimationFrames and
testADrawnMarkmapSurvivesThePageBeingLoadedAgain fail on the old code and on
each removed piece; full xcodebuild test 388 tests 0 failures, MiaoYanCore
swift test, swiftlint and swift-format strict. In the qa build a cold-launch
PDF (8 pages: image, math, Mermaid, mind map) and two PNG exports all show
the map fully drawn.

Revert: git revert this commit; export goes back to the blank mind map.

fix(ui): find matches in the editor on a green tint you can see

The editor's other find matches were drawn in sand at 35%, 1.07:1 on the
paper, so beyond the current match they could not be found by eye. They
now take Theme.searchMatch, MiaoYan green at 18% light and 22% dark, the
maintainer's pick (B) of three candidates rendered on the real editor.
The current match keeps the selection plate.

Verified: full xcodebuild test 386 passed, swiftlint and swift-format
--strict clean, and the qa build searched for "the" in light and dark,
all seven matches visible with the current one set apart.

fix(trash): Undo never moves back a different note, and says when it fails

The library Trash is shared with the iPhone and iPad (71d00a01). After
the Trash was emptied there and another note of the same name was deleted
into it, Undo on the Mac moved that other note into the first note's
folder; and an Undo that could not move a note back (the original path
taken, the file gone) failed silently after the toast had closed.

Both windows now restore through TrashReturn (Views/Toast.swift): it
reads each Trash file's identity (fileResourceIdentifierKey, cache
cleared) when the delete finishes and moves a note back only if the file
is still that one and the original path is free. A failure leaves the
note listed in the Trash and shows "Couldn't restore N note(s) from the
Trash", with plurals in en/es and the line in zh-Hans, zh-Hant and ja.

Found by a fresh review of the V4.7.1..HEAD range; a second review of
this diff found no bugs. Verified: testUndoLeavesAFileThatReplacedTheTrashedNote
failed on a first version whose identity read hit the URL cache (the same
result as no check) and passes now; full xcodebuild test 386 passed;
swiftlint and swift-format --strict clean; in the qa build Command-Z
restored a deleted note, and with the original path occupied it showed
the failure toast and left both files untouched.

Revert: git revert this commit; no stored data changes.

fix(seed): Simplified Chinese in Hong Kong gets Simplified folder names

The first-launch folders took Traditional names for any language tag that
contained HK or MO, so zh-Hans-HK and zh-Hans-MO users got 筆記 and 靈感.
An explicit script subtag now decides; a region implies Traditional only
when the tag names no script (Storage.seedsTraditionalChinese).

Found by a fresh review of the V4.7.1..HEAD range. Verified with
testSeedFolderScriptFollowsTheScriptSubtag (red on the old rule for
zh-Hans-HK and zh-Hans-MO) and the full xcodebuild test run, 386 passed.

fix(ui): warm Ink greys, 12pt list dates, one opaque floating layer style

Batch 3 of the 2026-11-06 newcomer audit, Mac side:

- Theme.textColor / secondaryTextColor were the system's cool label
  greys; they now return Theme.Ink.primary and Ink.tertiary (tertiary is
  what the shell's list dates use), so the storyboard window's list,
  sidebar, info panel and version history match the shell and Settings.
  Custom appearance keeps the user's font colour.
- List dates were 11pt, under the 12pt floor AGENTS.md names; now 12pt.
  The shell's section headers keep their 12pt (they were dateFontSize+1).
- The find bar's FloatingShadow sat on a layer that masksToBounds, so it
  never drew; the corner radius alone rounds the fill now.
- Toasts (12), the find bar and image preview (8) and the TOC (10) share
  Theme.Metrics.floatingCornerRadius = 10. The dark toast's .hudWindow
  frost becomes the same solid pill as light mode, and the image preview
  sits on the paper tone with the column hairline instead of frost.
- The export CSS's orange --primary-color is removed. It had no consumer
  in exports (the TOC is hidden there and Mermaid's line colour is set
  inline by theme-manager.js), so exports do not change.

Gates: testListDatesMeetTheTwelvePointFloor,
testFloatingLayersShareOneRadiusAndNoFrost and
testExportCSSHasNoOrangeAccent, each red on the old values.
Verified: xcodebuild test (382 before the export gate, then the gate
class 11/11), swiftlint and swift-format --strict, and the built app in
light mode: the find bar now shows its shadow and the list date reads
12pt in warm grey (before/after PDF handed to the maintainer).
Revert with git revert of this commit.

fix(l10n): license, not licence, in the Tsanger font hint

American spelling to match the rest of the English copy and the iPhone font row (newcomer audit item 50). The key is joined in TypographyPrefsViewController, so the four .strings keys change with it. Verified with plutil -lint on every Localizable.strings and a grep that no licence remains in app code or strings.

fix(i18n): plural counts, real word counts, version dates in the app language

From the same newcomer audit:

- English and Spanish showed "Move 1 note(s) to the system Trash?". The
  four counted strings now come from Localizable.stringsdict (new en.lproj
  and es.lproj) through I18n.count, which uses localizedStringWithFormat;
  the nine call sites in ViewController+Action and ShellModel switch to it.
  Chinese and Japanese keep their .strings entries, which have no plural.
- The info panel's Words counted characters, so an English sentence read
  as dozens of words. String.noteWordCount counts each CJK character as one
  and each Latin-script word as one.
- The info panel built "Words: 12" with an ASCII colon in code;
  I18n.labeled goes through the "%@: %@" key so CJK gets "：".
- Version history formatted relative dates in the system language; its
  formatters now take the app's language.

Verified: xcodebuild test (380 tests, 0 failures; LocalizationTests and
testNoteWordCountCountsWordsInLatinScriptsAndCharactersInCJK ran and
passed), swift test for MiaoYanCore (36), swiftlint and swift-format
--strict, and in the built app: "Move 2 notes to the system Trash?" in
English, 字数：59 in Chinese. Revert with git revert of this commit.

fix(l10n): native wording in zh-Hans, zh-Hant, ja and es; Settings in English

A newcomer audit (2026-11-06) read every locale against Apple's own terms
and found copy that read machine-translated or wrong:

- zh-Hans: one name per action (清理未使用的附件, 清理排版), a plain reload
  warning, full-width colons in the info panel, 设置 for 偏好设置.
- zh-Hant: 拷貝 for clipboard copy (複製 stays duplicate), 新增檔案夾,
  檔案夾 and 字體 throughout, rewritten toasts, Esc and ⌘⇧W.
- ja: the seven menu items still in English, 妙言を終了 / 妙言について,
  書き出す for export, 整形 for format, a "no note has this title" toast
  that said the opposite.
- es: Nueva carpeta, Todas las notas, Apple's sentence case on ~100
  values, three toasts rewritten; the four "(s)" plural keys move to
  Localizable.stringsdict in the next commit.
- Base: the app menu says Settings…, as macOS has since 13.
- "%@: %@" gets a full-width colon in zh-Hans, zh-Hant and ja for
  I18n.labeled.

Verified: plutil -lint on every .strings, the full xcodebuild test run
(380 tests) with the next commit, and the info panel read back in the
built app (字数：59 修改：…).

fix(ui): the sidebar's bird in grey over the empty editor

The full-colour cardinal over the empty editor sat on the same screen as
the green bird of the sidebar lockup and read as a second, different
logo. The maintainer picked, from three candidates rendered on the real
window (colour cardinal, green bird, grey bird), the sidebar's bird in
the hint's grey: the brand green stays with the lockup, the colour
cardinal stays with the alerts, and the empty state matches the line
icons around it. emptyStateBird is now the same lucide path as the
sidebar's home.svg at stroke 1.5 as a template SVG, drawn at 48pt and
tinted Theme.Ink.tertiary, with its bottom where the cardinal's was so
the line under it does not move.

Verified: Debug build; the empty folder in the qa build, light and dark
(the bird and the line share one grey in both); xcodebuild test 377
passed; swiftlint and swift-format strict on ViewController.swift.

fix(ui): draw the empty-state cardinal from full-size artwork

The empty editor showed alertIcon, a 128px image, at 88pt, so a 2x
screen stretched it to 176px and the bird read soft. emptyStateBird is
cut from the app icon's own 43.png at 88pt and 176px, with alertIcon's
margin, so the drawing keeps its size and only gets sharp. alertIcon
stays for the alert sheets. The iPhone app uses the same artwork for a
note it cannot open.

Verified: qa build, empty folder shows the bird at the same place and
size, sharper.

test(sidebar): allow pixel snapping in the brand lockup test

c46b32b9's test expected the lockup centre at 30.5pt with 0.01 slack.
Auto Layout snaps frames to device pixels, so on CI's 1x screen the
centre lands at 30.0 and all three assertions failed, while a 2x Mac
places it exactly. The slack is now half a device pixel of the main
screen (0.26pt on 2x, 0.51pt on 1x), still far below the 5pt drop the
test guards.

Verified: SidebarProjectViewTests 12 passed locally; CI run of this
commit is the 1x check.

feat(ui): Undo after a delete, an empty state, toasts sized to their text

Deleting a note now says where it went: a toast "Moved to Trash" with an
Undo button, in both the storyboard window and the SwiftUI shell, since
Command-Z is invisible to someone who never used it. The Undo is tied to
that one delete through TrashUndo, not to whatever sits on top of the
window's undo manager, which the search and title fields share; Command-Z
takes the same delete back and retires the toast. When some notes could
not be moved, the failure toast stays and no Undo toast replaces it.

An empty folder or a search with no match shows the cardinal and one
line (Press ⌘N to create a note / No results) instead of a blank editor.
The view is lifted above the layer-backed editor, re-evaluated when the
editor clears, fills or a note arrives without being opened (undo, a
file from Finder or iCloud), and creating a note hides it.

Toasts hold for a time that follows their length (1.5 to 6 s, an action
toast 5 s), stay while the pointer is over them, and fade with the
Theme.Motion durations.

Verified in the qa build: search miss and empty folder show the state,
Command-N hides it; delete then type in search then click Undo restores
the note and keeps the search text; delete then Command-Z restores it
and removes the toast. Full xcodebuild test 377 passed, swiftlint and
swift-format --strict clean. An Opus review of the diff found five
issues, all fixed here.

Revert: git revert this commit; no stored data changes.

feat(seed): localized sample folders, symbol shortcuts, miaoyan.app images

A first launch in Chinese opened on four English folders (Examples,
Guide, Ideas, Notes) holding Chinese notes; the folders now follow the
notes' language (指南, 示例, 笔记, 灵感, with 筆記 and 靈感 for a
Traditional Chinese system). The sample notes write shortcuts the way
the menus show them (⌘1, ⇧⌘N, ⌥⌘P, Esc) instead of "command + option + p",
the getting-started steps say that every note is a plain Markdown file
and how to make a folder, the welcome note adds ⌘3 for preview, and the
PPT step points at the sample deck the library already holds.

Sample images (the logo, the syntax guide pictures, the img.border
frame in base.css) move from alipay's CDN to miaoyan.app/assets/notes/,
the site repository the product controls; the files went live with the
site's own commit and were checked by md5 on the live URLs.

Verified: fresh qa libraries with -AppleLanguages zh-Hans seed the
Chinese folders and notes; the English seed was checked the same way.

Revert: git revert this commit; only affects libraries seeded after it.

fix(save): report a failing write once, and say so on Command-S

The debounced save retries every 1.5 s while typing, and each retry raised
the same Save Failed sheet again, so a folder that turned read-only or a
full disk buried the editor under sheets. A note now reports its failed
write once and re-arms after a write succeeds. Because the sheet stays
quiet after that, a deliberate Command-S that still cannot save shows a
Save Failed toast in both windows instead of saying nothing.

Verified: testFailedWriteIsReportedOnceUntilASaveSucceeds (read-only
folder, three saves, one report; restoring the folder re-arms) fails on
the always-report code with 3 vs 1; full xcodebuild test 377 passed and
swift test for MiaoYanCore 36 passed.

Revert: git revert this commit; no stored data or format changes.

fix(sidebar): give the brand lockup room under the traffic lights

The lockup sat 23pt under the traffic lights and 27pt over All Notes,
which read cramped at the top. The brand row grows by
Theme.Metrics.sidebarBrandDrop (5pt) and the bird and wordmark sit half
of it below the row's centre, so the lockup moves down the full 5pt while
the gap under it stays.

Measured on 2x captures of the storyboard window: 28pt above and 27pt
below now, and the lockup's ink centre (68.25pt) lines up with the first
note title in the list column (68.75pt). The SwiftUI shell already had
28.5pt above its lockup, so it is unchanged.

Verified: testTheBrandLockupDropsWithoutClosingTheGapUnderIt fails on the
old code (row 52, bird and wordmark 5pt higher); full xcodebuild test
(376) and swift test (36) pass; swiftlint and swift-format strict clean.

docs(incidents): I-31, the Trash row outlived a Trash emptied on the iPhone

Met in the daily build (71d00a01) during the Simulator cross-device test; fixed by 65d596eb.

test: stop leaving an empty plist in ~/Library/Preferences per run

Three tests named their UserDefaults suite with a UUID. Removing the
domain afterwards still leaves its empty plist file, so every run of the
suite added three files; 327 had piled up. Fixed names cleared at the
start leave at most one file each.

Verified: a full xcodebuild test run added no UUID-named plist; the 327
old files were all empty dictionaries and were moved to the Trash.

fix(trash): the sidebar drops the Trash row once another device empties it

The Trash row shows while the library Trash holds a note (71d00a01), but
the watcher only rebuilt the sidebar when a note arrived. When the iPhone
emptied the Trash, the Mac's Trash list went empty while its row stayed
until the next sidebar rebuild. A Trash file removed outside the app now
rebuilds the sidebar, whether the Mac had loaded that note (removeNote)
or not (refreshTrashRow, on removal and on a move away).

Verified: testTrashFilesRemovedElsewhereRefreshTheSidebar, red on the
old watcher (the expectation times out); full xcodebuild test (375, 1
pre-existing skip), MiaoYanCore swift test, swiftlint/swift-format
--strict, check_incidents. In the qa build on a scratch library, deleting
Trash/gone.md from the shell removed the Trash row within three seconds.

Revert: git revert this commit; the row then lingers until the next
sidebar rebuild, as before.

fix(trash): deleted notes go to the library's own Trash folder

The app Trash was the volume's system Trash, which for an iCloud library
is iCloud's own .Trash, while the iPhone and iPad app moves deleted notes
into <library>/Trash. A note deleted on one device never showed in the
other's Trash. Both now use <library>/Trash (maintainer 2026-11-06).

- Storage.checkLibraryTrash registers <default root>/Trash; the folder is
  made by the first note delete, not at launch. If it cannot be made
  (read-only root, a plain file named Trash) trashItem returns nil and
  Note.removeFile hands the note to the system Trash as before.
- Only notes go there. Folders and images keep going to their volume's
  system Trash (systemTrashDestination): the app Trash lists only the
  notes directly inside it, and the iPhone's Empty Trash would erase a
  folder's notes nobody saw.
- Sidebar shows the Trash row when the folder holds an unmarked note file
  on disk (trashHasNotes), since another device's deletes are never loaded.
- Extensionless names no longer get a trailing dot on collision.

Notes deleted before this update stay in the Finder or iCloud Trash.

Verified: full xcodebuild test (374, 1 pre-existing skip), MiaoYanCore
swift test, swiftlint/swift-format --strict, check_incidents. New tests
red on the old code one check at a time. Ran the qa build on a scratch
library: a note in Trash/ from "the phone" showed in the Mac Trash, a
deleted note landed in <library>/Trash intact, a deleted folder went to
~/.Trash, and a fresh library got no Trash folder or row.

Revert: git revert this commit; notes already in <library>/Trash stay
there as an ordinary hidden folder and can be moved back in Finder.

fix(preview): draw Markmap branches in the family palette

The patched render() in markmap.min.js coloured branches from a
hard-coded list of twelve stock colours (coral, turquoise, hot pink) and
passed a TsangerJinKai font option that markmap-view never reads, while
theme-config.js getMarkmapColors built a warm palette that nothing used:
diagram-handler only stored it in a data attribute.

Branches now take theme-config's colours by depth: the brand green at
the root, then the editor's title purple, link teal, bold gold and list
grey, with the dark values of the same colour assets. Because the colour
is baked into the SVG, DiagramHandler.retheme now redraws each map from
its saved source when the appearance changes, as it already does for
Mermaid and PlantUML. ppt.html loads theme-config.js so slides get the
same palette. MANIFEST.json records the new markmap.min.js hash.

Verified: testMarkmapBranchesUseTheFamilyPaletteAndFollowTheAppearance
renders a map in WebKit, reads the link colours light, then dark after
retheme, and checks one map remains. It fails on the old palette (reads
#4ECDC4) and, with only the redraw removed, fails on the dark colours.
Full xcodebuild test (370 tests), swift test for MiaoYanCore,
swiftlint and swift-format --strict, check_incidents and the review
gate tests pass. PDF and PNG export with a map were not hand-tested.

Revert: git revert this commit; the old palette needs no data change.

docs(incidents): I-30, formulas fell back to Times offline

Row for 9e65e3b5. Verified: check_incidents passes with the row.

fix(preview): bundle KaTeX's fonts so formulas typeset offline

katex.min.css declared every KaTeX font only at gw.alipayobjects.com, and
the bundle had no font files, so an offline preview, PDF or PNG set
formulas in the fallback Times while the blog told readers math needs no
network. The 20 woff2 files now sit in DownView.bundle/css/fonts, the same
bytes the CDN served (md5 checked on three) and the same files the iPhone
reader bundles, and the stylesheet points at them. The preview cache syncs
the bundle recursively on every launch, so existing installs pick them up;
exported HTML resolves them under cdn.miaoyan.app, which serves main.

Verified: testKatexFontsShipInsideThePreviewBundle red on the old
stylesheet, green now; full xcodebuild test 369 (1 skipped); with every
http request blocked in a headless page, the old stylesheet loaded no
KaTeX font (12 blocked requests) and the new one loads KaTeX_Main, Math,
AMS and Size1 with none.

fix(prefs): only the shipped app migrates the legacy MiaoYan domain

The legacy suite com.tw93.MiaoYan is, on a case-insensitive volume, the
same plist as com.tw93.miaoyan's. A build with its own bundle id
(com.tw93.miaoyan.qa for local tests) read the maintainer's real settings
through it on first launch and copied every missing key in, fonts and
library location included, which is how a "fresh" qa launch came up in
TsangerJinKai02. The migration now runs only for com.tw93.miaoyan, the id
the direct-download and App Store Mac builds share, and reads the legacy
domain's own keys rather than a suite's dictionaryRepresentation, which
also carries the global domain.

Verified: LegacyPreferencesMigrationTests red with the bundle-id guard
removed, green with it; full xcodebuild test 368 (1 skipped), swiftlint and
swift-format strict, check_incidents. A Release qa build launched on an
empty domain stored 28 keys with PingFangSC-Regular, against 66 keys and
TsangerJinKai02 before.

fix(sidebar): center folder names on their icon in the system face

The maintainer saw the selected 周刊 row's name sit below its folder
icon. The label is drawn 1.5pt lower than its frame
(sidebarStandardLabelVerticalNudge), a value tuned for TsangerJinKai02.
Since 2026-10-11 the default face is the system pairing, whose CJK ink
then sat 2pt below the icon and the selection plate's centre line.

The nudge now depends on the label's face: the system face takes -0.5,
a chosen face keeps 1.5, so TsangerJinKai02 and other picked faces draw

Verified on 2x window captures of a selected row (Release build, text
centre minus icon centre in pixels): zh system 4.0 -> 1.0, en system
("Ideas") 0.5, zh TsangerJinKai02 0.5 and en 1.0, both unchanged. A
font-metric formula was tried first and matched only the system face
(-0.45 predicted, -0.5 measured; 0.24 vs 1.25 for TsangerJinKai02), so
the values are measured ones. Full xcodebuild test (366), swift test,
swiftlint and swift-format --strict pass. risk_tier lists this file
under notes; the diff only changes where the label is drawn and touches
no save, Trash or buffer path, so no note-flow test applies.

V4.7.0 shipped on 2026-11-05 with defects that lose content (I-25, images

fix(hints): reduce collision shift threshold to prevent drift in compact lists (#2470)

In placeHints(), links aligned along the same vertical or horizontal axis
are shifted when their distance to the preceding link is under 20px. In
densely spaced lists (such as tables or sidebars with row heights between
10px and 20px), this causes hints to repeatedly get pushed downward into
the subsequent row, creating a cascading drift.

Lower the collision detection threshold from 20px to 10px so tightly
stacked items avoid triggering false vertical offsets.

Fixes #2469

Signed-off-by: Clark Wang <dearvoid@gmail.com>

commits.message:
pb_decode: fix out-of-bounds release of pointer fixed count arrays (GHSA-5v96-h584-4px4)

When all of the following conditions apply:
1) PB_ENABLE_MALLOC is used
2) There is a repeated submessage array with "(nanopb).fixed_count = true" set
   and more than one entry.
3) The submessages contain PB_POINTER fields
4) The decoded message does not contain the correct amount of entries for the array

Then pb_release() may end up calling free() on a pointer that has uninitialized value,
which can lead to either program crash or heap corruption.

This issue was independently found and reported by multiple people:
- Vladimir Kukharenko (GenProof)
- Keshava P

This commit contains the patch proposed by Keshava P in pull request #1211.
Original commit message follows:

---

For a repeated field with fixed_count and FT_POINTER, pSize points at
array_size, so pb_release_single_field() always walks array_size
entries. decode_pointer_field() grew the array one entry at a time and
never checked array_size, so when the input had fewer entries than
max_count, the pb_release() call in pb_decode_ex() read past the array,
passed the following heap data to pb_free() and wrote NULL over it.
Submessage arrays were released out of bounds in the same way, and a
string or bytes fixed count array that was absent from the message made
pb_release() dereference the NULL array pointer.

Allocate and initialize all array_size entries when the first entry is
decoded, reject extra entries with "array overflow" like static fixed
count arrays do, and skip the string/bytes release loop when the array
was never allocated. Other pointer arrays have array_size 1 and are not
affected.

Extend the fixed_count test with an empty message, a truncated array
and an over-long one.

pb_decode: fix invalid free with repeated submessages (GHSA-5v96-h584-4px4)

When all of the following conditions apply:
1) PB_ENABLE_MALLOC is used
2) There is a repeated submessage array, and the submessages contain PB_POINTER fields
3) The array itself is nested inside an oneof, or alternatively the message structure
   passed to top-level pb_decode() is uninitialized.
4) Submessage decoding fails

Then pb_release() may end up calling free() on a pointer that has uninitialized value,
which can lead to either program crash or heap corruption.

This issue was independently found and reported by multiple people:
- Vladimir Kukharenko (GenProof)
- smaeljaish771
- Keshava P

This commit contains the patch proposed by Keshava P in pull request #1213.

Fix workflows for updated Github Ubuntu GCC 15

The Github ubuntu-latest image now uses GCC15, which
required updates to apt-get commands and also purging
bazel cache.

It seems valgrind refuses to work with 32-bit binaries
on the new ubuntu, so don't use it.
pb_decode: satisfy Splint boolean check

pb_decode: Reject truncated callback streams

Track whether a tag varint consumed any bytes before callback EOF, and require length-delimited decodes to consume their full advertised size. Add regressions for truncated submessages, delimited messages, and tags while preserving clean EOF handling.

Fixes #1199.

Note: prepared with AI assistance.
Fix SCons tool availability detection

### Added (1)

- Added `ConnectionClosedError`, raised for a WebSocket request whose connection closed before it was answered.

### Changed (8)

- Fixed WebSocket requests in flight during a `serverShutdown` or the 23 h rotation timing out although the server answered them. The new connection is now opened, logged on and subscribed first; the old one is closed only after its requests are answered.
- Fixed new WebSocket requests being sent on a connection that was shutting down or being replaced.
- WebSocket requests whose connection closes now return `{error: connection_closed}` at once instead of `{error: timeout}` after 20 s. Like a timeout, the request may still have been executed: check an order with `order.status` or its `newClientOrderId` before sending it again.
- WebSocket API requests now wait for `ConfigurationWebSocketAPI.timeout` (default 5000 ms) instead of a fixed 20 s. WebSocket Streams requests still wait 20 s.
- The session of a replaced WebSocket API connection is now logged out before the connection is closed.
- When a connection cannot be replaced, the old one is kept in use and the replacement is tried again after 60 s.
- Fixed REST requests opening a new connection every time when `https_agent` was set: the adapter is now mounted once per session, so keep-alive connections are reused.
- WebSocket API connections now pass `aiohttp.ClientWSTimeout` to `ws_connect`, fixing the `aiohttp` deprecation warning for a `float` timeout.

commits.message: Upgrade version to 2.8.0 (#1658)
Fix default R2 target order for time-series scores (#1654)

fix: isolate inline Spark trials from the Spark joblib backend (#1657)

Type: bugfix

## Summary
Prevent forest probability prediction from resolving n_jobs=-1 to zero under
an inherited Spark joblib backend when tuning falls back to one driver-side
trial worker. Add regression coverage and document nested parallelism.

## Prompting Intent
Fix the library-side ZeroDivisionError affecting forest probability prediction
during Spark-backed AutoML and submit a pull request to microsoft/FLAML.
Address the execution-context bug rather than requiring notebook-only n_jobs
changes, and preserve trial-level parallelism.

## Linked Sources
- Spark integration guidance: https://microsoft.github.io/FLAML/docs/Examples/Integrate%20-%20Spark#parallel-spark-jobs
- Joblib single-worker execution: https://github.com/joblib/joblib/blob/1.4.2/joblib/parallel.py#L1819-L1850
- Spark joblib backend and nested execution: https://github.com/joblib/joblib-spark
- Forest worker partitioning: https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/blob/1.6.1/sklearn/ensemble/_base.py#L165-L175

## Rationale
Keep the existing Parallel instance bound to Spark, but activate a local
threading backend while it collects trial results. This isolates inline
estimator operations without changing the configured Spark concurrency,
forcing all learners to n_jobs=1, or adding another evaluation wrapper.
Context managers restore the caller's backend even when evaluation fails.
Deterministic tests cover real concurrent execution, both forest learners,
and complete AutoML cross-validation without requiring a Spark cluster.

commits.message:
Report a failed ASIF disk resize only once (#1413)

performASIFResize threw its "Failed to resize ASIF disk image" error
inside the do block that's meant to catch a failure to start diskutil,
so the catch wrapped it again and tart set --disk-size printed
"Failed to execute diskutil resize: Failed to resize ASIF disk image:
...". Only wrap the error from process.run().

Report why a lock file can't be opened (#1414)

FileLock didn't check the result of open(2), so locking a path that
doesn't exist failed later in flock(2) with "Bad file descriptor". For
example, tart run --disk with a mistyped disk image path reported
"failed to lock ...: Bad file descriptor". Throw the open(2) error from
the initializer instead, like PIDLock does.

commits.message:
rust/lib: merge CachedInput and Input into a concrete Input<'a> type

Replace the `Input` trait and internal `CachedInput<I>` wrapper with a
concrete `Input<'a>` struct backed by either a `std::fs::File` (with
lazy prefix/suffix caching) or an in-memory `Cow<'a, [u8]>`.

Previously, `CachedInput<&[u8]>` started in the `Partial` state and
allocated/copied slices into `Box<[u8]>` buffers on read, and `stdin`
buffers in the pipeline were copied a second time. Using `Cow<'a, [u8]>`
for in-memory inputs avoids these allocations and copies, and removes
generic monomorphization over `I: Input` across resolvers, custom rules,
and feature extraction.

Assisted-by: Gemini <gemini@google.com>

tree, code search and manifest view looked in the wrong directory.
